label: 2-Chlorophenothiazine
source_file: _document_ - Neuroprotective Actions of Methylene Blue and Its Derivatives.md
description: 2-Chlorophenothiazine, which consists of the phenothiazine nucleus without the amine side chains of methylene blue, acts as a direct free-radical scavenger independent of mitochondria and NADH. In the cell-free mitochondrial lysate oxidation assay it significantly reduced DCF fluorescence both with and without mitochondria/NADH, unlike MB which required both. Despite potent nanomolar neuroprotection against glutamate, IAA, and rotenone toxicity, it had no effect on oxygen consumption, anaerobic glycolysis, or the complex I-III electron shunt, and it did not upregulate complex IV expression, revealing a mechanism distinct from MB.

label: Reactive Oxygen Species
source_file: _document_ - Neuroprotective Actions of Methylene Blue and Its Derivatives.md
description: 2-Chlorophenothiazine, which consists of the phenothiazine nucleus without the amine side chains of methylene blue, acts as a direct free-radical scavenger independent of mitochondria and NADH. In the cell-free mitochondrial lysate oxidation assay it significantly reduced DCF fluorescence both with and without mitochondria/NADH, unlike MB which required both. Despite potent nanomolar neuroprotection against glutamate, IAA, and rotenone toxicity, it had no effect on oxygen consumption, anaerobic glycolysis, or the complex I-III electron shunt, and it did not upregulate complex IV expression, revealing a mechanism distinct from MB.

label: Acetate
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP.md
description: Acetate is converted intracellularly into acetyl-CoA by ACSS2 and is not membrane-permeable acetyl-CoA itself. Acetate supplementation increases global nuclear acetylation including H3K27ac and induces expression of pro-inflammatory genes including IL6, IL8, IL1B and CCL2 without affecting cell cycle regulators p16 and p21. In mitochondria-depleted senescent cells, acetate increases histone acetylation and partially restores a subset of the mitochondrial-dependent SASP programme. However, acetate-induced SASP gene expression is suppressed by the STING inhibitor SN011, showing that chromatin accessibility alone cannot drive SASP transcription without innate immune activation.

label: SASP
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP.md
description: Cellular senescence is a key response to various cellular stresses characterized by a permanent cell cycle arrest and the secretion of a pro-inflammatory cocktail of factors known as the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Senescence serves protective roles in embryonic development, tumour suppression and tissue repair, but persistent SASP activation leads to chronic inflammation contributing to tissue dysfunction, ageing and a broad spectrum of age-related diseases including cancer. This dual nature makes SASP a focal point for understanding both the protective and detrimental effects of senescence.

label: Acetyl-CoA
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP.md
description: Acetyl-CoA is the obligate donor for protein acetylation, including histone acetylation, a modification associated with chromatin relaxation and increased accessibility to transcriptional machinery. In senescent cells, acetyl-CoA availability determines H3K27ac deposition at SASP gene loci: enhancing acetyl-CoA levels promotes SASP gene expression while depleting it limits the programme. Acetate supplementation, converted intracellularly into acetyl-CoA by ACSS2, increases nuclear acetylation and induces pro-inflammatory genes IL6, IL8, IL1B and CCL2 without affecting cell cycle regulators, linking mitochondrial metabolism to the epigenetic regulation of inflammatory genes.

label: Histone Acetylation
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP.md
description: SIRT1 removes acetyl groups from histones, promoting a repressive/condensed chromatin state at target loci.

label: Acid ceramidase
description: Acid ceramidase (ACase, encoded by ASAH1) is the lysosomal enzyme that breaks down ceramide into sphingosine and free fatty acids. By controlling ceramide levels, ACase affects the abundance of many lipid species relevant to cell fate decisions, including sphingomyelin, ceramide-1-phosphate, and free fatty acids. In the context of replicative senescence, this ceramide catabolism releases free saturated and monounsaturated fatty acids that feed polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) and PUFA-phospholipid synthesis, remodeling the membrane lipid profile.

label: ACSL4
description: Acid ceramidase (ACase) inhibition reduces PL-PUFA levels and lipid peroxidation without altering expression of ACSL4, the acyl-CoA synthetase that canonically drives PUFA incorporation into phospholipids during ferroptosis. After ACase knockdown, ACSL4 protein remained high, indicating that the decrease in PL-PUFAs is driven by reduced supply of saturated/monounsaturated fatty acids for Lands-cycle exchange (due to decreased ceramide lipolysis) rather than by changes in ACSL4. Both ACase and ACSL4 knockdown protect senescent cells against RSL3, but through supply-side versus incorporation-side mechanisms respectively.

label: GPX4
description: The anti-ferroptotic protection conferred by acid ceramidase (ACase) knockdown is independent of the GPX4/glutathione (GSH) axis. Senescent cells had higher basal GSH and elevated GPX4 protein, yet ACase silencing reduced GPX4 expression while still protecting against RSL3-induced cell death. Even when GSH was depleted with buthionine sulfoximine (BSO), ACase knockdown conferred strong resistance to RSL3. The GSH/GPX4 changes therefore appear to be consequences of attenuated ferroptotic pressure rather than the protective mechanism itself, placing ACase upstream of these classic ferroptosis elements.

label: Iron
description: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent cell death pathway in which the accumulation of lipid peroxides becomes toxic to cells. Pam Maher, the Salk senior author, discovered the pathway and named it (originally 'oxytosis') in 2001. Healthy cells keep lipid peroxides at steady levels with the help of glutathione, an antioxidant that can stave off ferroptosis. Ferroptosis has been increasingly linked to neurodegeneration - Maher's lab recently reported that chronic iron overexposure in neurons makes them less resilient over time and more vulnerable to neurodegeneration - and targeting the pathway has become a promising therapeutic strategy for age-related diseases alongside senescence research.

label: Ceramide
description: Acid ceramidase (ACase, encoded by ASAH1) is the lysosomal enzyme that breaks down ceramide into sphingosine and free fatty acids. By controlling ceramide levels, ACase affects the abundance of many lipid species relevant to cell fate decisions, including sphingomyelin, ceramide-1-phosphate, and free fatty acids. In the context of replicative senescence, this ceramide catabolism releases free saturated and monounsaturated fatty acids that feed polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) and PUFA-phospholipid synthesis, remodeling the membrane lipid profile.

label: PUFA
description: Acid ceramidase (ACase) over-expression increases the polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) content of membrane phospholipids, promoting a pro-ferroptotic lipid profile. Mechanistically, ACase-mediated ceramide breakdown releases free saturated and monounsaturated fatty acids that, via the Lands cycle, are exchanged into sn-2 PUFA-containing phospholipids (PL-PUFAs) - the substrates of lipid peroxidation. ACase knockdown in senescent cells decreased the most abundant PL-PUFA species (including PC-AA, PG-DHA, PG-DPA), thereby reducing the lipid peroxidation substrate pool and conferring ferroptosis resistance.

label: Senolytic Drug Target
source_file: _document_ - Could this enzyme help remove "zombie" cells from our tissues?.md
description: Acid ceramidase is a druggable, near-term, testable senotherapeutic target for clearing senescent cells. Experimental drugs targeting acid ceramidase have already been developed for other therapeutic purposes, demonstrating that the enzyme is targetable and lighting the way toward future innovation that could extend healthspans. Because elevated acid ceramidase makes senescent cells more susceptible to ferroptosis, inhibitors of the enzyme could selectively eliminate senescent 'zombie' cells while keeping neighboring cells healthy. The Salk team calls this a big milestone in the public health effort to support healthy aging, with the next steps being pathway completion, animal translation, and clinical trials.

label: Cellular Senescence
source_file: _document_ - Could this enzyme help remove "zombie" cells from our tissues?.md
description: SIRT1 inhibits cellular senescence and apoptosis in c-Myc- and PML-driven cancers by deacetylating and inactivating p53 and proapoptotic FOXO transcription factors and by sequestering Bax via deacetylated Ku70. These actions blunt the tumor-suppressive programs that would otherwise eliminate premalignant cells. The directionality is that SIRT1 activity is upstream of senescence suppression, protecting cells from growth arrest. Consequently, SIRT1 inhibitors are frequently anticancer on their own and sensitize cancer cells to anticancer agents or oxidative stress.

label: IL-6
description: IL6 is a representative SASP gene whose expression is suppressed upon mitochondrial clearance, with coordinated decreases in chromatin acetylation at its locus and mRNA expression. Acetate supplementation induces expression of IL6 alongside IL8, IL1B and CCL2, while MPC1 deletion or SLC25A1 inhibition reduces these factors. In aged mice, CTPI2 treatment reduces expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines including Il6 and Il1b in skeletal muscle, and their expression negatively correlates with muscle strength, indicating that mitochondrial acetyl-CoA-dependent histone acetylation gates the secretion of IL-6 as part of the senescent inflammatory programme.

label: IL-8
description: Interleukin-8 (IL-8) is one of the best-known cytokines of the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), along with IL-6. Secreted by senescent cells, IL-8 reshapes local tissue microenvironments and exerts paracrine effects on neighboring cells. In this study, recombinant IL-8 (combined with IL-6 at a 1:2 ratio) induced acid ceramidase expression in proliferative cells, reproduced by senescent-cell co-culture, resulting in elevated lipid peroxidation and sensitization of bystander cells to ferroptosis.

label: ARN14794
description: ARN14794 is a specific chemical inhibitor of acid ceramidase (ACase). Treatment with ARN14794 protected proliferative and senescent WI-38 cells, as well as neuronal-derived murine HT22 cells (a well-studied ferroptosis model), against RSL3-induced ferroptosis. Because ACase inhibitors already exist as drug candidates developed for other indications, ACase represents a tractable senolytic/senomorphic target for attenuating the deleterious effects of senescent cells during aging - a potential 'two birds with one stone' strategy that eliminates senescent cells while keeping neighboring cells healthy.

label: Senescent Cells
description: Targeting mitochondrial citrate metabolism suppresses inflammation across tissues and improves tissue function and healthspan during ageing without detectable changes in p16 or p21 expression, consistent with SASP modulation rather than senolytic clearance of senescent cells. In aged muscle, senescent-like nuclei defined by the CoreScence gene signature are present at similar abundance and distribution across conditions despite reduced SASP-associated transcription and chromatin accessibility at loci such as Ccl2 and Igfbp4. In the liver, the abundance of p16-positive and/or p21-positive cells remains unchanged while their nuclear histone acetylation is reduced by CTPI2 treatment.

label: Sphingosine
source_file: _document_ - Could this enzyme help remove "zombie" cells from our tissues?.md
description: Acid ceramidase catalyzes the breakdown of ceramides into sphingosine and free fatty acids, directly producing sphingosine in the cell. This enzymatic hydrolysis is a key branch point in sphingolipid metabolism, and in senescent cells the resulting reshaping of membrane lipid composition pushes membranes toward a pro-ferroptotic profile rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), the preferred substrates for lipid peroxidation. Because the excess sphingosine and free fatty acids generated by elevated acid ceramidase feed the lipid-peroxidation cascade, the enzyme serves as a mechanistic link between the cellular programs of senescence and ferroptosis, and its removal protects cells from ferroptotic death.

label: Ferroptosis
source_file: _document_ - Could this enzyme help remove "zombie" cells from our tissues?.md
description: SIRT6 silencing can overcome sorafenib resistance by promoting ferroptosis in gastric cancer, suggesting a therapeutic strategy for resistant malignancies. Directionally, SIRT6 loss sits upstream of ferroptotic cell death and restored drug sensitivity. By triggering this iron-dependent form of cell death, SIRT6 depletion bypasses the resistance mechanisms that allow gastric cancer cells to survive sorafenib treatment. This reveals an unexpected pro-survival role for SIRT6 in this context, where its activity protects cells from ferroptosis.

label: Lipid Peroxidation
source_file: _document_ - Could this enzyme help remove "zombie" cells from our tissues?.md
description: Ferroptosis is a regulated cell death pathway driven by the toxic accumulation of lipid peroxides. Cells die in ferroptosis when they lose the ability to regulate fats, and polyunsaturated fatty acids in membranes become the substrates for peroxidative damage. Healthy cells keep lipid peroxides at steady levels with the help of glutathione, an antioxidant that staves off ferroptosis. The pathway is iron-dependent and has been linked to aging and neurodegeneration, including Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease. Understanding lipid-peroxide accumulation as the central executioner mechanism explains why membrane lipid remodeling - such as that caused by acid ceramidase - can sensitize cells to ferroptosis.

label: ACLY
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP.md
description: ACLY (ATP-citrate lyase) catalyzes the downstream conversion of mitochondria-derived citrate exported to the cytosol into acetyl-CoA, the principal substrate for cytosolic acetyl-CoA production and histone acetylation. ACLY expression is increased across multiple senescence models, and its silencing reduces both H3K27ac levels and SASP gene expression in irradiation-induced and replicative senescence. Conversely, citrate supplementation increases histone acetylation and induces pro-inflammatory gene expression in proliferating cells, confirming that increasing citrate availability is sufficient to drive the acetylation-dependent inflammatory programme.

label: Advanced Glycation End Products
source_file: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md
description: Aminoguanidine, also developed as pimagedine by Alteon/Synvista Therapeutics, is the first identified inhibitor of advanced glycation end products (AGEs). By trapping reactive carbonyl species, it prevents the cross-linking of tissue proteins that is proposed to drive many features of aging. Most anti-aging research has been carried out using a hydrochloride (HCL) derivative, which is more soluble and less irritating than the bicarbonate form, and aminoguanidine has a half-life of only 4 hours, so dosages of 150-300 mg per day are best administered in split doses.

label: Aging
source_file: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md
description: Aging is associated with declining SIRT3 activity and rising SIRT4, which narrows the hormetic window and increases vulnerability to mitochondrial stressors. Directionally, aging sits upstream of the altered ratio. This shift favors oxidant stress and metabolic inflexibility, and restoring the ratio, for example via caloric restriction or NAD+ precursors, is a proposed anti-aging strategy. By reducing the protective SIRT3/SIRT4 balance, aging impairs mitochondrial quality control and stress adaptation. This association links mitochondrial sirtuin biology to the functional decline of aging tissues.

label: Thymic Involution
description: Age-associated thymic involution results in diminished thymopoiesis: reduction of the thymic epithelial space causes loss of T cell receptor gene rearrangement and decreased output of naive T cells to the periphery. Using single joint T cell receptor excision circle analysis (sjTREC), a molecular marker for active thymopoiesis, researchers measured a steady three-log decline in circulating naive T cells across an 80-year human lifespan. Similar decreases in sjTREC per milligram of thymus tissue were observed in aging BALB/c mice from 6 to 90 weeks. Thus involution reduces both the quantity and quality of T cells exported across the lifespan.

label: Age-Related Diseases
description: Aging is the sum of all age-related diseases, pre-diseases and pre-pre-diseases, which limit lifespan, and since humans die from age-related diseases rather than from healthy aging, a drug indicated for all age-related diseases must be an anti-aging drug in that it targets the common driver of these diseases, namely aging itself. Standard medicine extends lifespan mostly by preventing death from overt diseases, extending the unhealthy phase of life, whereas anti-aging medicine increases both healthspan and lifespan and is most effective at the stage of pre-diseases before complications and organ damage occur.

label: Alagebrium
source_file: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md
description: Alagebrium (ALT-711), a thiazolium salt developed by the Alteon Corporation and in stage II trials, is claimed to break existing cross-links rather than merely prevent them. Aminoguanidine and other agents such as carnosine and acetyl-L-carnitine have been shown to help prevent cross-linking, whereas ALT-711 is claimed to break existing links. If this is substantiated, alagebrium could be a major anti-aging medicine of the future, complementing AGE inhibitors that only block formation of new cross-links.

label: Cross-linking
source_file: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md
description: Aminoguanidine prevents the cross-linking of tissue proteins by trapping reactive carbonyl species and by binding to sugars, thus preventing them from binding to the lysine groups of proteins. Glucose can react with protein amino groups in a process called glycation to form glucose/protein combinations that eventually cause active cross-links, and this continuous cross-linking may be prevented by glycation inhibitors whose primary use is to stabilize glucose metabolism. Aminoguanidine joins up with substances that cause links and stops cross-links from developing, protecting the proteins that make up the body from aging damage.

label: Aminoguanidine
source_file: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md
description: Aminoguanidine, also developed as pimagedine by Alteon/Synvista Therapeutics, is the first identified inhibitor of advanced glycation end products (AGEs). By trapping reactive carbonyl species, it prevents the cross-linking of tissue proteins that is proposed to drive many features of aging. Most anti-aging research has been carried out using a hydrochloride (HCL) derivative, which is more soluble and less irritating than the bicarbonate form, and aminoguanidine has a half-life of only 4 hours, so dosages of 150-300 mg per day are best administered in split doses.

label: Lysine
source_file: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md
description: Aminoguanidine acts to bind to sugars, thus preventing them from binding to the lysine groups of proteins, which is the mechanism by which it blocks the formation of glucose-derived cross-links. Glucose is found in every cell of the body and is relatively stable, but it can join with protein to form a glucose/protein combination that continues through a number of steps to eventually cause active cross-links. The formation process is reversible, and glycation inhibitors stabilize glucose metabolism, but glucose/protein substances can stay in the body for months or even years, cross-linking with the proteins around them.

label: Nitric Oxide
description: Under normal conditions nitric oxide is a crucial signaling molecule that relaxes vascular smooth muscle via activation of soluble guanylyl cyclase and cGMP production. However, during severe inflammation, injury, or shock, overproduction of NO - primarily by inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) - leads to excessive vasodilation, vascular leakage, and tissue damage. This is the pathway targeted by both aminoguanidine, which blocks NO synthesis at iNOS (upstream), and methylene blue, which blocks NO action at sGC (downstream).

label: Histamine Intolerance
description: Aminoguanidine is a strong inhibitor of diamine oxidase (DAO), the enzyme that breaks down histamine in the gut. By blocking intestinal DAO, oral aminoguanidine can dramatically increase sensitivity to dietary histamine, potentially triggering severe acute histamine intolerance; consuming normal amounts of histamine-rich foods - aged cheeses, cured meats, fermented foods - may cause headaches, flushing, hives, and tachycardia. This is a major safety consideration for oral aminoguanidine use in supplement or experimental settings.

label: Albuminuria
source_file: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md
description: Trials conducted by the Alteon Corporation indicate that aminoguanidine can significantly reduce albuminuria, proteins present in urine usually as a result of kidney disease, delay the onset of end-stage renal disease, and improve the cholesterol profiles of diabetic patients. Diabetic clinical trials have also highlighted aminoguanidine's ability to prevent oxidative modification of LDL and inhibit the formation of atherosclerotic plaques. A number of studies with diabetic rats indicate that aminoguanidine-administered rats have significantly superior survival rates than untreated animals.

label: Survival
source_file: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md
description: A number of different studies with diabetic rats indicate that aminoguanidine-administered rats have significantly superior survival rates than untreated animals. Aminoguanidine prolongs survival in azotemic-induced diabetic rats, and it prevents age-related arterial stiffening and cardiac hypertrophy in animals. Human trials indicate aminoguanidine has very low toxicity and appears safe to use at normal dosages, with side effects limited to nausea and headache, although there is still relatively little human data and clinical trials, and broad anti-aging claims rest largely on animal and early human data rather than definitive clinical outcomes.

label: Diamine Oxidase
description: Aminoguanidine is a strong inhibitor of diamine oxidase (DAO), the intestinal enzyme that breaks down histamine. By blocking gut DAO, oral aminoguanidine can dramatically increase sensitivity to dietary histamine, potentially triggering severe acute histamine intolerance; consuming normal amounts of histamine-rich foods (aged cheeses, cured meats, fermented foods) may cause headaches, flushing, hives, and tachycardia. This histamine-sensitivity risk is a major safety consideration for oral use of aminoguanidine.

label: Inducible Nitric Oxide Synthase
description: Aminoguanidine (Pimagedine) is primarily known as a selective inhibitor of inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS), the enzyme responsible for producing high levels of nitric oxide during inflammation. By blocking iNOS, aminoguanidine prevents the overproduction of nitric oxide from the start of the inflammatory cascade, acting upstream of NO signaling. Because it selectively targets the inducible form rather than the healthy endothelial form (eNOS), it is considered a way to halt the inflammatory cascade without completely shutting down normal blood pressure regulation.

label: Cataract
source_file: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md
description: Aminoguanidine is able to join up with substances that cause links and stop cross-links from developing, and therefore it may help alleviate or prevent senile cataract, thickening of the arteries, kidney failure, thinning bones, osteoarthritis, skin wrinkles and many other signs of aging. One animal study showed that aminoguanidine prevented age-related cardiac enlargement, reduced the membrane surface area of the rats by 30%, and increased the collagen content of their arterial walls by 24-30%, improving overall heart and arterial condition by decreasing AGE-induced cross-linking of the extracellular matrix.

label: Collagen
source_file: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md
description: Aminoguanidine has the potential to slow the aging process by protecting the proteins that make up the human body, such as the skin proteins collagen and elastin, eye lens protein, nerve protein and kidney proteins, from aging damage. One animal study showed aminoguanidine increased the collagen content of arterial walls by 24-30%, and it decreases AGE-induced cross-linking of the extracellular matrix. Aminoguanidine is able to combat some of the adverse effects of diabetes and improve the quality and duration of life, protecting proteins that deteriorate with advancing age and more so in diabetes.

label: Very Low Density Lipoprotein
source_file: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md
description: Studies conducted at the University of Milan over 25 years showed that aminoguanidine reduces the ability of very low density lipoprotein (VLDL), the bad form of cholesterol, to bind itself to blood vessel walls, in tests on animals. In turn, blood platelets are less likely to coagulate and form dangerous clots. Aminoguanidine's role in reducing VLDL cholesterol and its ability to stabilize glucose metabolism indicate it has a wide-reaching ability to help prevent and treat a number of aging disorders.

label: Endothelial Nitric Oxide Synthase
description: Aminoguanidine selectively inhibits only the inducible form of nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) rather than the healthy endothelial form (eNOS). This selectivity is considered advantageous because it can halt the inflammatory overproduction of nitric oxide - which causes excessive vasodilation, vascular leakage, and tissue damage - without completely shutting down normal blood-pressure regulation maintained by eNOS-derived NO. This contrasts with non-selective NOS inhibition, making aminoguanidine a theoretically more targeted anti-inflammatory intervention.

label: Diabetic nephropathy
description: Aminoguanidine, under the developmental name Pimagedine, was evaluated in phase III clinical trials for diabetic nephropathy as a long-term chronic therapy aimed at preventing the slow, progressive formation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs) that damage blood vessels and kidneys in diabetics. It was ultimately not approved for widespread clinical use due to safety concerns, including a risk of autoimmune reactions and vitamin B6 depletion. Today it is primarily used as an experimental tool in laboratory settings.

label: Atherosclerosis
source_file: _document_ - Aminoguanidine An AGE Product Inhibitor  Antiaging Systems Articles.md
description: SIRT6 protects against endothelial dysfunction, vascular smooth muscle cell senescence, and atherosclerosis in mice through multiple mechanisms, including deacetylation of H3K9 at inflammatory gene promoters and suppression of NF-kappaB signaling. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of vascular homeostasis. By restraining inflammatory gene expression and maintaining endothelial and smooth muscle function, SIRT6 resists the cellular changes that drive atherogenesis. This places SIRT6 among the key sirtuins defending the vasculature against age-related dysfunction.

label: Androgen Receptor
description: Enzalutamide (Xtandi) is a second-generation androgen receptor (AR) antagonist that blocks AR nuclear translocation.

label: Antioxidants
description: Antioxidants did not extend lifespan in any clinical trials and were detrimental in some: in two very large randomized controlled trials, antioxidants increased the incidence of cancer, especially lung cancer in smokers, and increased all-cause mortality, leading both trials to be stopped earlier than planned. Antioxidants also accelerate cancer progression and promote metastasis. The idea that free radicals cause aging was based on circumstantial evidence, and although excessive ROS can shorten lifespan, organisms normally die from mTOR-driven age-related diseases before ROS can kill them, so antioxidant supplementation is described as worse than useless for life extension.

label: Longevity
description: An SNP in SIRT3 (rs11555236, in linkage with a putative enhancer) is associated with increased longevity, male-specific in some cohorts and whole-population in the TRELONG study, with homozygotes showing higher SIRT3 expression, supporting a role for SIRT3 variation in human lifespan. Directionally, the genetic variant is associated with longevity through increased SIRT3 expression. By raising SIRT3 levels, the variant may enhance mitochondrial function and stress resistance. These genetic associations complement the animal data linking SIRT3 to healthspan and position SIRT3 as a candidate human longevity gene.

label: Apigenin
description: Apigenin (4',5,7-trihydroxyflavone) is a major plant flavone belonging to the flavonoid subclass flavones within the polyphenols. It is a yellow crystalline powder with the molecular formula C15H10O5 and a molecular weight of 270.24 Da, bearing hydroxyl groups at C-5 and C-7 of the A-ring and C-4' of the B-ring. Structurally it is related to biapigenin and naturally occurs as apigenin-7-O-glucoside and acylated derivatives. Its classification as a flavone underpins its shared antioxidant and anti-inflammatory pharmacology with other plant polyphenols such as quercetin and kaempferol.

label: Cognitive Decline
description: Apigenin improved cognitive and affective outcomes in prematurely aged mice following whole-body irradiation: Y-maze spontaneous alternation tests showed basic recovery of short-term working memory in apigenin-treated aged animals, and open-field assays showed prolonged exploration of the central zone, indicating reduced anxiety-like behavior. These findings suggest that SASP suppression by apigenin can counteract neurobehavioral deficits associated with premature aging.

label: Frailty
description: In humans, lower serum SIRT1 levels are associated with frailty compared with non-frail individuals, suggesting circulating sirtuins as a non-invasive frailty marker. Directionally, the association is correlative: reduced SIRT1 tracks frail phenotype. A caveat is that this is a biomarker correlation, not proof of causality.

label: PRDX6
description: Apigenin directly binds peroxiredoxin 6 (PRDX6), identified as its bona fide molecular target through two affinity-based approaches: biotin-tagged apigenin pull-down (Bio-APIG) and drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS). Binding was confirmed by cellular thermal shift assay, surface plasmon resonance (KD ~ 0.237 uM) and microscale thermophoresis (Kd ~ 916 nM). In silico modelling indicates direct hydrogen bonds with Cys91 and Glu210 of PRDX6; mutating either residue weakens binding ~10-fold and mutating both abolishes it. This is the primary upstream molecular interaction underlying apigenin's senomorphic activity.

label: Cell Cycle Arrest
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: SIRT1 governs cell-cycle checkpoints by deacetylating p53 (reducing its transcriptional activity) and RB, supporting DNA-repair-coupled arrest rather than apoptosis or premature senescence; age-related SIRT1 decline biases G1/S and G2/M responses toward senescence (reviewed in the source review).

label: HER2
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: Cancer is driven by HER2. Cancer is a family of diseases driven by the stepwise acquisition of mutations and epimutations that confer proliferative autonomy, survival, and dissemination. HER2 (ERBB2) is a receptor tyrosine kinase that, when amplified, drives aggressive breast cancer and is the target of trastuzumab. The directionality runs from HER2 toward Cancer, so HER2 is the active agent and Cancer the recipient of the effect. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: HSPA8
description: Apigenin specifically abrogates the interaction of HSPA8 (heat shock cognate protein 70, HSC70), a shared interactor of both ATM and p38 MAPK identified from proteome-scale interactor profiling (19 proteins shared by ATM and p38 MAPK). Co-immunoprecipitation shows that apigenin attenuates HSPA8's direct binding to p-ATM and to p38 MAPK, whereas the related interactor NPM1 is unaffected, demonstrating target specificity. HSPA8 is a chaperone involved in chaperone-mediated autophagy and NF-κB activation, and its inhibition with the selective drug VER155008 phenocopies apigenin's dampening of SASP factors, p38 MAPK activation, and PI3K/Akt engagement.

label: Bioavailability
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: Fisetin suffers from intrinsically poor bioavailability that restricts its clinical translation. Its water solubility is very low (below 10 ug/mL), and the compound is sensitive to light, heat, and oxidative degradation. After oral administration fisetin is rapidly metabolized in the gut and liver to glucuronide and sulfate conjugates, so systemic exposure of the parent compound is minimal. The review documents that oral fisetin has short half-life and low plasma concentrations, and it attributes these problems to the BCS class II/IV characteristics of fisetin, motivating the development of macro- and nano-formulations to improve its absorption.

label: Apoptosis
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: By deacetylating p53, SIRT1 lowers p53's transcriptional activation of BH3-only proteins and other apoptotic effectors, suppressing programmed cell death after oxidative or genotoxic stress. This creates a survival bias that helps cells tolerate damage but can also protect incipient cancer cells from elimination. The directionality is that SIRT1 activity on p53 is upstream of reduced apoptosis. A caveat is that chronic suppression of p53-dependent apoptosis is a double-edged sword: protective in normal tissue but potentially tumor-promoting.

label: Autophagy
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: Mitophagy is a form of selective autophagy in which damaged and dysfunctional mitochondrial fragments are engulfed by double-membraned autophagosomes and delivered to the lysosome for degradation by hydrolytic enzymes. It is triggered by cues that mark mitochondrial damage, such as imbalance in mitochondrial fission-fusion dynamics, and is mediated either by specific outer mitochondrial membrane receptors such as BNIP3, BNIP3L/NIX and FUNDC1, or by ubiquitin molecules conjugated to mitochondrial surface proteins. Mitophagy is a core mitochondrial quality control mechanism closely related to cell fate decisions including senescence, apoptosis and necroptosis.

label: CK2
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: Apigenin is a potent inhibitor of casein kinase 2 (CK2), a serine/threonine kinase that is elevated in many cancers. In prostate cancer, apigenin inhibited CK2 activity in both hormone-responsive LNCaP and hormone-refractory PC-3 cells, though apoptosis was induced only in LNCaP. In colon cancer cells, apigenin together with DRB inhibited CK2 expression and synergistically sensitized cells to TNF-alpha-mediated apoptosis. In cervical cancer stem-like cells, apigenin suppressed self-renewal by downregulating CK2-alpha, and in pancreatic cancer it stabilized the transcription factor Ikaros by downregulating CK2 to restore T-cell homeostasis.

label: COX-2
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: Apigenin suppresses cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), the enzyme that converts arachidonic acid into prostaglandins and whose overexpression drives carcinogenesis. It inhibits UVB-induced increases in COX-2 protein and mRNA in mouse and human keratinocytes, reduces COX-2 expression in colon and gastric cancer models, and downregulates inducible COX-2 in HCEC colon cells more potently than quercetin or tricin. In non-melanoma skin cancer models, COX-2 inhibition by apigenin prevents tumor development, and apigenin also suppresses UVB-induced cutaneous angiogenesis by maintaining endogenous TSP1 levels.

label: Fatty Acid Synthase
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: Apigenin inhibits fatty acid synthase (FASN), an enzyme that catalyzes long-chain fatty acid synthesis and is overexpressed in many cancers. Brusselmans and colleagues showed that plant flavonoids including apigenin induce apoptosis in prostate and breast carcinoma cells specifically through their ability to block fatty acid synthase activity, and this effect on lipogenesis was also observed in osteosarcoma cells where apigenin and luteolin downregulated FASN and acetyl-CoA carboxylase. By depriving cancer cells of de novo lipid synthesis, apigenin curbs cancer cell growth and survival through a metabolic route complementary to its effects on signaling kinases.

label: HDAC1
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: Apigenin acts as a histone deacetylase inhibitor, directly targeting HDAC1 and HDAC3, which increases global histone acetylation and produces localized hyperacetylation of histone H3 on the p21/Waf1 promoter. In triple-negative breast cancer cells this drives histone H3 acetylation, decreasing cyclin A and cyclin B and increasing p21/Waf1/Cip1. Apigenin can additionally function as a dual epigenetic inhibitor that reverses both DNA methylation and trimethylation of lysine 27 on histone H3, qualifying it as an epigenetic modulator relevant to chemoprevention.

label: HIF-1α
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: SIRT6 represses hypoxia-inducible factor 1alpha (HIF-1alpha) as a co-repressor (Zhong et al., 2010), suppressing downstream glycolytic and lipogenic programs and opposing the Warburg-like shift seen in cancer and aging. By limiting HIF-1alpha target transcription, SIRT6 favors oxidative metabolism and genomic stability, complementing its repression of c-MYC and its deacetylation of H3K9 and H3K56 at glycolytic promoters. Loss of SIRT6, seen in many cancer cell lines, derepresses glycolytic metabolism and supports tumor growth.

label: MAPK
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: Cancer is driven by MAPK. Cancer is a family of diseases driven by the stepwise acquisition of mutations and epimutations that confer proliferative autonomy, survival, and dissemination. The mitogen-activated protein kinase cascades relay extracellular signals to transcriptional programs governing proliferation and stress responses. The directionality runs from MAPK toward Cancer, so MAPK is the active agent and Cancer the recipient of the effect. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: NF-κB
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: SIRT1 deacetylates the NF-kB subunit RelA/p65 at Lys310 (Yeung 2004 PMID 15152190), preventing optimal DNA binding and transcriptional activation, and licenses p65 for ubiquitin-proteasomal degradation, lowering both NF-kB activity and protein levels. This suppresses pro-inflammatory cytokines including TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, and IL-6. SIRT6 cooperates in constraining p65, and loss of SIRT1 or its decline with age allows NF-kB activity and chronic low-grade inflammation to rise, positioning the SIRT1-NF-kB axis as a key node in inflammaging and a mediator of resveratrol's anti-inflammatory and cardiovascular benefits.

label: PI3K
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: IRS1 is the upstream insulin receptor substrate in the mTOR-PI3K signaling cascade: the IRS receptor upstream of the pathway is activated by binding reversibly to insulin, and active IRS1 promotes the activation of PI3K by phosphorylation. PI3K in turn activates mTORC2 by phosphorylation and activates IRS1 indirectly via AKT, forming a positive feedback loop. Active IRS1 is inactivated by phosphorylation by S6K1/2, closing a negative feedback arm. IRS1 therefore sits at the hub of the incoherent bivalent motif, and the backward reaction from the target toward IRS1 is central to the hormetic response.

label: STAT3
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: SIRT1 deacetylates STAT3 as part of its broad anti-inflammatory and metabolic regulatory functions, altering STAT3-driven transcription. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically tunes STAT3. Because STAT3 drives proliferation and inflammation, its deacetylation influences cytokine signaling and cell growth, and the effect is relevant to both cancer and chronic inflammation. The evidence for this regulation carries moderate confidence, reflecting incomplete characterization. By modifying STAT3, SIRT1 provides another route to restrain inflammatory and growth-promoting transcription, complementing its actions on NF-κB.

label: Flavone
description: Apigenin (4',5,7-trihydroxyflavone) is a naturally occurring flavone belonging to the class of dietary flavonoids found in fruits and vegetables. It is historically recognized for antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antiviral and anticancer activities, and it reduces reactive oxygen species production while raising glutathione and mitochondrial ATP to protect oocyte quality during aging. Its canonical downstream anti-inflammatory actions include suppressing the SASP partially by inhibiting IL-1α signaling through IRAK1/IRAK4, p38 MAPK and NF-κB, which reduces the aggressiveness of human breast cancer cells.

label: Flavones
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: Apigenin (4',5,7-trihydroxyflavone) is a major plant flavone belonging to the flavonoid subclass flavones within the polyphenols. It is a yellow crystalline powder with the molecular formula C15H10O5 and a molecular weight of 270.24 Da, bearing hydroxyl groups at C-5 and C-7 of the A-ring and C-4' of the B-ring. Structurally it is related to biapigenin and naturally occurs as apigenin-7-O-glucoside and acylated derivatives. Its classification as a flavone underpins its shared antioxidant and anti-inflammatory pharmacology with other plant polyphenols such as quercetin and kaempferol.

label: Senomorphic
description: Apigenin is a dietary flavone flavonoid identified by screening a 66-compound natural product library against bleomycin-senescent PSC27 human prostate stromal cells. It functions as a senomorphic agent: it suppresses the pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) without killing senescent cells or forcing them back into the cell cycle, in contrast to senolytics such as ABT-263 or procyanidin C1, which preferentially lyse senescent cells. Because it leaves the growth arrest intact, apigenin is classified specifically as a natural senomorphic rather than a senolytic, aligning with the ideal profile for SASP-restraining geroprotective therapy.

label: Parsley
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: Apigenin is a major dietary flavone enriched in a range of fruits and vegetables, with parsley being the richest documented source. Dried parsley was reported to contain up to 45,035 ug/g apigenin, far exceeding dried chamomile flowers (3,000-5,000 ug/g), celery seeds (786.5 ug/g), vine spinach (622 ug/g), and Chinese celery (240.2 ug/g). It is also found in chamomile tea, red wine, and beer, and is a signature component of the Mediterranean diet, whose intake has been associated epidemiologically with lower rates of several human diseases including cancer.

label: UGT1A1
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: In the intestine and liver, apigenin is extensively conjugated by UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 1A1 (UGT1A1), the key enzyme converting it into glucuronide and sulfate derivatives that are more readily transported in blood and excreted in bile or urine, and apigenin itself induces UGT1A1 transcription in colon cells. Combined treatment with sulforaphane synergistically increased UGT1A1 mRNA induction, although apigenin did not induce GSTA1. This phase II metabolism underlies apigenin's rapid clearance and low plasma bioavailability after oral dosing, while its slow systemic elimination may allow peripheral tissue accumulation that supports chemopreventive efficacy.

label: Senescence
description: Apigenin is not senolytic and does not reverse cellular senescence: SA-β-Gal staining profiles and mitotic inactivity remain essentially unchanged in senescent cells treated with apigenin, both in vitro and in xenografts and whole-body-irradiated mouse tissues. It also fails to downregulate the core senescence markers p16^INK4a and p21^CIP1 in vivo. Instead of eliminating senescent cells, apigenin curtails their pathological secretory output. This property is considered pharmacologically favorable because rejuvenating or removing cells is not required to blunt the harmful paracrine effects of the SASP, and retained senescent cells may still contribute beneficial functions such as t...

label: Chemotherapy
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: Survivin confers resistance to Chemotherapy. Survivin (BIRC5) is a bifunctional IAP that inhibits apoptosis and is required for chromosomal passenger complex function in mitosis, making it a tumor-selective antigen. Chemotherapy uses cytotoxic agents to kill rapidly dividing cells, and its efficacy is limited by innate and acquired resistance mechanisms. The relationship is directional, with Survivin acting as the operative agent upon Chemotherapy rather than the reverse. This restraint is biologically significant because it modulates the threshold at which the affected process engages, and when co-opted by tumors it fosters survival and treatment resistance that must be overcome therapeutically.

label: ovarian cancer
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: BRCA predisposes to ovarian cancer. BRCA1 and BRCA2 are tumor suppressors that orchestrate homology-directed repair of DNA double-strand breaks and genome stability. High-grade serous ovarian cancer is characterized by frequent BRCA1/2 dysfunction and exquisite sensitivity to platinum and PARP inhibition. The relationship is directional, with BRCA acting as the operative agent upon ovarian cancer rather than the reverse. Such relationships underscore how inherited or intrinsic factors shape cancer susceptibility and inform risk-stratified screening and prevention.

label: Mitoxantrone
description: In a preclinical NOD-SCID xenograft model combining PC3 prostate cancer cells with senescent PSC27 stroma, co-administration of apigenin with the chemotherapy agent mitoxantrone (MIT) produced additional tumor reduction beyond MIT alone: MIT alone shrank tumors 57.8%, and the combination achieved an additional 51.1% reduction, for a total 74.9% decrease versus placebo. Apigenin reversed circulating SASP factors (amphiregulin/AREG, epiregulin/EREG) and enhanced DNA damage (γH2AX) and cleaved-caspase-3 apoptosis in tumors.

label: p53
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: SIRT1 deacetylates p53 at multiple lysine residues, dampening p53's transcriptional activation of pro-apoptotic and senescence genes and promoting cell survival under stress. The modification reduces p53's DNA-binding affinity and coactivator recruitment at target promoters, so SIRT1 effectively restrains the tumor-suppressive output of the protein. This dual role—protective in normal tissue by limiting excessive apoptosis, yet potentially oncogenic by shielding damaged cells—is a defining feature of SIRT1 biology.

label: p21
source_file: _document_ - Plant flavone apigenin An emerging anticancer agent.md
description: Therapy-Induced Senescence is enforced by p21. Therapy-induced senescence is the durable arrest imposed on tumor cells by genotoxic treatments, with both tumor-suppressive and relapse-promoting consequences. p21 (CDKN1A) is a p53-inducible CDK inhibitor that enforces G1 arrest during senescence and DNA-damage responses. The directionality runs from p21 toward Therapy-Induced Senescence, so p21 is the active agent and Therapy-Induced Senescence the recipient of the effect. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor
description: Kynurenine and its derivatives activate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR), promoting regulatory T cell (Treg) differentiation and suppressing effector T/NK cells. This metabolite-driven AhR signaling is the second major mechanism of IDO1-mediated immunosuppression alongside local tryptophan depletion, and together they create an immunosuppressive microenvironment in tissues such as tumors, placenta and inflamed sites. The context-dependent nature of this pathway is notable: it is protective via tolerance induction in autoimmunity but potentially detrimental when overactive in metabolic inflammation, where elevated KP activity links to insulin resistance and chronic low-grade inflammation.

label: Regulatory T cells
description: SIRT1 in dendritic cells modulates the balance between pro-inflammatory Th1 and anti-inflammatory Foxp3+ regulatory T (Treg) cells; its knockout restrains Treg generation. Directionally, DC SIRT1 sits upstream of Treg differentiation. This shapes peripheral tolerance and limits autoimmunity, and DC-specific SIRT1 loss drives Th1 polarization and promotes inflammation. It links sirtuins to immune homeostasis beyond metabolism, showing that SIRT1 activity in antigen-presenting cells influences the outcome of T-cell responses. This immunoregulatory role is relevant to autoimmune disease, where tipping the balance toward Tregs is protective.

label: Aspirin
description: Aspirin not only reduces inflammation, a hallmark of aging, it also reduces the risk of cardiovascular disease, thrombosis and cancer; low-dose aspirin prevents one-third of colorectal, gastric and esophageal cancers. Millions of people take aspirin daily to prevent cardiovascular disease and cancer, and it was calculated that the benefits of aspirin are greater than its risks despite side effects including life-threatening gastric bleeding. The author argues that the benefits of the anti-aging effects of rapamycin and everolimus may be even greater, and that aspirin can be combined with rapamycin in an anti-aging formulation.

label: Cancer
description: SIRT3 exerts context-dependent roles in cancer: as a tumor suppressor it stabilizes chromosomal integrity via OGG1-mediated DNA repair potentiation, facilitates H3K56 deacetylation for NHEJ fidelity, destabilizes HIF-1alpha to attenuate the Warburg effect, and deacetylates IDH2 at K143 to suppress ROS-mediated mutagenesis. Yet it can be oncogenic (pyroline-5-carboxylate reductase 1 Lys228, SHMT2 Lys95, glycine decarboxylase Lys514 deacetylation) and enables chemoresistance in CLL via ROS buffering.

label: ATFS-1
description: ATFS-1 (Activating Transcription Factor associated with Stress-1) is the transcription factor required for activation of the mitochondrial unfolded protein response (UPRmt) in C. elegans. Uniquely, it possesses both a mitochondrial targeting sequence and a nuclear localization signal: in the absence of stress it is imported into mitochondria and rapidly degraded, whereas under mitochondrial dysfunction its import is impaired and it translocates to the nucleus to orchestrate a broad transcriptional response, including induction of mitochondrial chaperones. Nuclear ATFS-1 thereby couples mitochondrial status directly to nuclear gene expression.

label: Mitochondrial Unfolded Protein Response
description: ATFS-1 (Activating Transcription Factor associated with Stress-1) is the transcription factor required for activation of the mitochondrial unfolded protein response (UPRmt) in C. elegans. Uniquely, it possesses both a mitochondrial targeting sequence and a nuclear localization signal: in the absence of stress it is imported into mitochondria and rapidly degraded, whereas under mitochondrial dysfunction its import is impaired and it translocates to the nucleus to orchestrate a broad transcriptional response, including induction of mitochondrial chaperones. Nuclear ATFS-1 thereby couples mitochondrial status directly to nuclear gene expression.

label: Nucleus
description: In C. elegans, mitochondrial dysfunction caused by protein misfolding alters the subcellular localization of the transcription factor ATFS-1. In healthy mitochondria, ATFS-1 is imported into the organelle and degraded by the Lon protease. During stress, ATFS-1 instead traffics to the nucleus to drive transcription of genes involved in the coordinated UPRmt response. This import-versus-nuclear-translocation decision makes protein import a readout of mitochondrial health, a paradigm the review argues is extended in mammals by mechanisms involving DELE1 processing and PINK1 accumulation.

label: Biphasic Dose-Response Curve
description: For a network to produce a biphasic dose-response curve, the probability is highly increased if one of the bivalent interactions of the inhibited target operates in the saturated enzymatic regime, i.e., a Michaelis-Menten interaction with high affinity towards its substrate whose reaction speed does not depend on substrate amount. Specifically, the Michaelis-Menten constant K21 of the backward interaction from Target to Input must be significantly low. Fixing K21 to a low value raises the percentage of hormetic parameter sets from about 6% to 80%, a roughly ten-fold increase in the probability of observing hormesis.

label: Saturated Enzymatic Regime
description: For a network to produce a biphasic dose-response curve, the probability is highly increased if one of the bivalent interactions of the inhibited target operates in the saturated enzymatic regime, i.e., a Michaelis-Menten interaction with high affinity towards its substrate whose reaction speed does not depend on substrate amount. Specifically, the Michaelis-Menten constant K21 of the backward interaction from Target to Input must be significantly low. Fixing K21 to a low value raises the percentage of hormetic parameter sets from about 6% to 80%, a roughly ten-fold increase in the probability of observing hormesis.

label: BNIP3
source_file: _document_ - The role of mitochondrial dynamics in disease.md
description: BNIP3 (BCL-2/adenovirus E1B interacting protein 3) is an outer mitochondrial membrane mitophagy receptor that interacts directly with LC3 to promote engulfment of damaged mitochondria, functioning independently of Parkin. NIX/BNIP3-mediated mitophagy is induced through hypoxia and stabilization of HIF-1alpha. BNIP3 also interacts with OPA1 to induce mitochondrial fragmentation and with FUNDC1 under the control of OPA1 and DRP1, and its protein levels are upregulated at early premalignant stages of several human solid cancers but frequently decrease when tumors become invasive.

label: Mitophagy
source_file: _document_ - The role of mitochondrial dynamics in disease.md
description: SIRT3 promotes mitophagy by deacetylating FOXO3a, which induces BNIP3 and triggers clearance of damaged mitochondria to maintain homeostasis. Directionally, SIRT3 activates FOXO3a, which promotes mitophagy. This removes dysfunctional organelles that would otherwise fuel ROS and inflammation, and it is a key quality-control function of SIRT3. By coupling mitochondrial sirtuin activity to the mitophagic program, SIRT3 ensures that damaged mitochondria are selectively eliminated. This regulation is essential for preserving mitochondrial health in tissues with high energy demand, such as heart and muscle.

label: Branched-Chain Amino Acids
description: High circulating branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) levels - leucine, isoleucine, and valine - are associated with obesity, insulin resistance, and mortality in humans. High-BCAA diets promote obesity, insulin resistance, inflammation, and decreased lifespan in rodents, whereas dietary restriction of BCAAs promotes metabolic health, reduces frailty, and extends lifespan, recapitulating many benefits of protein restriction. BCAA restriction reduces mTORC1 signaling, induces Fgf21, reduces hepatic cellular senescence, and in human studies improves insulin sensitivity and glucose/insulin homeostasis while increasing circulating FGF21. Although BCAAs are often considered as a group, each individual BCAA plays distinct roles in aging.

label: Insulin Resistance
description: When it is over-activated by nutrients and insulin, mTOR acts via S6K1 to inhibit insulin signaling, thereby causing insulin resistance. Acute treatment with rapamycin abrogates insulin resistance in cells and animals including humans, and one study shows chronic treatment with rapamycin may also prevent insulin resistance. However, in some rodent models chronic rapamycin treatment can cause glucose intolerance and insulin resistance, which is interpreted as a benevolent starvation pseudo-diabetes (SPD), a reversible condition that does not lead to complications and resembles the metabolic state of prolonged fasting.

label: Caloric Restriction
description: In yeast, the replicative lifespan extension conferred by caloric restriction is abolished when the SIR2 gene is deleted, establishing Sir2 as a required mediator of the CR response. This dependence reflects the fact that CR raises the NAD+/nicotinamide ratio, which relieves nicotinamide feedback inhibition and boosts Sir2 deacetylase activity. The relationship is directional: CR acts upstream and Sir2 is the necessary downstream effector in this genetic pathway. A caveat is that in higher organisms the requirement is distributed across multiple sirtuins and redundant pathways, so SIR2/SIRT1 is necessary but not solely sufficient.

label: CD38
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial Drivers Stem Cell Aging Inflammaging Bautista 2026.md
description: Inhibiting CD38, a major consumer of NAD+ that generates nicotinamide and cADPR, preserves cellular NAD+ pools by reducing their catabolic drain. Directionally, CD38 inhibition sits upstream of higher NAD+ availability. Because all sirtuins require NAD+ as an obligate co-substrate, preserving NAD+ indirectly sustains sirtuin activity across the family. This is a leading strategy to reverse age-related NAD+ decline, and CD38 expression rises with age, further depleting NAD+ and compromising sirtuin function. Pharmacologic CD38 inhibitors such as 78c restore NAD+ and sirtuin activity, and in aged male mice extend lifespan.

label: NAD+
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial Drivers Stem Cell Aging Inflammaging Bautista 2026.md
description: Inhibiting CD38, a major consumer of NAD+ that generates nicotinamide and cADPR, preserves cellular NAD+ pools by reducing their catabolic drain. Directionally, CD38 inhibition sits upstream of higher NAD+ availability. Because all sirtuins require NAD+ as an obligate co-substrate, preserving NAD+ indirectly sustains sirtuin activity across the family. This is a leading strategy to reverse age-related NAD+ decline, and CD38 expression rises with age, further depleting NAD+ and compromising sirtuin function. Pharmacologic CD38 inhibitors such as 78c restore NAD+ and sirtuin activity, and in aged male mice extend lifespan.

label: Neurodegenerative Diseases
source_file: _document_ - Could this enzyme help remove "zombie" cells from our tissues?.md
description: Senescent cells are linked to many age-related conditions, including osteoarthritis, poor wound healing, and neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's, according to senior author Pam Maher. The harmful factors senescent cells release (the SASP) promote tissue dysfunction and disease development in surrounding tissue. Because senescence and ferroptosis are both independently linked to age-related dysfunction, the discovery that elevated acid ceramidase makes senescent cells more susceptible to ferroptosis offers a two-birds-with-one-stone strategy: eliminating senescent cells while keeping neighboring cells healthy. Clearing senescent cells is considered a promising therapeutic approach for a multitude of age-related diseases and disorders.

label: Osteoarthritis
source_file: _document_ - Could this enzyme help remove "zombie" cells from our tissues?.md
description: Senescent cells are linked to many age-related conditions, including osteoarthritis (arthritis), poor wound healing, and neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's or Parkinson's. The pro-inflammatory factors that senescent cells secrete into surrounding tissues promote tissue dysfunction and disease development, contributing to the joint degeneration seen in arthritis. The Salk findings suggest that making senescent cells vulnerable to ferroptosis through acid ceramidase could provide a novel target for therapeutics applicable to a multitude of diseases and disorders, including arthritis. Senescent cells are considered a hallmark of aging, and clearing them is a major goal of senolytic research for extending healthspan.

label: Senescence-Messaging Secretome
source_file: _document_ - Could this enzyme help remove "zombie" cells from our tissues?.md
description: Senescent cells - often called 'zombie' cells - are a hallmark of aging: they do not completely die but also are not quite alive, and while sometimes harmless, they release harmful factors called the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) into surrounding tissues. This secretory phenotype is pro-inflammatory and can promote the development of diseases or disorders, including cancer, and accelerates aging by driving tissue dysfunction. Because senescent cells are linked to many age-related conditions including arthritis, poor wound healing, and neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's, clearing them - as proposed through acid ceramidase-mediated ferroptosis sensitization - is a major strategy for extending healthspan.

label: Ferroptosis Susceptibility
source_file: _document_ - Could this enzyme help remove "zombie" cells from our tissues?.md
description: Vulnerable senescent cells are able to pass their ferroptosis vulnerability on to neighboring cells, helping explain why only a few senescent cells can turn into more and ultimately impact a larger tissue over time. This paracrine transmission of ferroptosis sensitivity means that a small number of senescent cells can spread susceptibility to ferroptotic death across a tissue, and it represents one mechanism by which the Salk team found ferroptosis and senescence to be connected during aging. The researchers describe the target as eliminating senescent cells while keeping neighboring cells healthy for longer, and the finding underpins the therapeutic rationale for targeting acid ceramidase.

label: cGAS-STING Pathway
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP.md
description: In senescence and ageing, mitochondrial dysfunction promotes the cytosolic release of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), which activates cGAS-STING signalling and drives inflammatory responses and the SASP. Cytosolic mtDNA levels were unchanged in senescent MRC5 and IMR90 fibroblasts following SLC25A1 inhibition, indicating that metabolic regulation of histone acetylation restrains SASP independently of mtDNA release. STING inhibition with SN011 suppresses SASP gene expression without affecting histone acetylation, showing that mtDNA-driven innate immune signalling and mitochondrial control of histone acetylation are independent but complementary inputs that converge to enable full SASP expression.

label: Chlorpromazine
source_file: _document_ - Neuroprotective Actions of Methylene Blue and Its Derivatives.md
description: Chlorpromazine, a phenothiazine carrying an amine side chain on its 10-nitrogen, was the only compound among those tested that failed to protect HT-22 cells in the rotenone neurotoxicity model. The 10-N substitution causes a roughly 1000-fold loss of potency relative to methylene blue in glutamate, IAA, and rotenone assays, and abolishes the complex I-to-cytochrome c electron shunt, oxygen consumption enhancement, and glycolysis suppression. In the lysate oxidation assay chlorpromazine increased DCF fluorescence with or without mitochondria and NADH, behaving as a pro-oxidant and explaining its weak neuroprotection.

label: Rotenone
source_file: _document_ - Neuroprotective Actions of Methylene Blue and Its Derivatives.md
description: Methylene blue (MB) protects HT-22 cells against rotenone-induced neurotoxicity. Rotenone inhibits mitochondrial complex I (NADH oxidase), reducing oxidative phosphorylation and generating excess ROS. When HT-22 cells were exposed to 5 uM rotenone for 24 hours, MB increased cell viability at concentrations from 10 nM to 10 uM, and MB-treated groups maintained significantly higher oxygen consumption even under rotenone challenge. This protection reflects MB's alternative electron-transfer shunt that bypasses the rotenone-blocked complex I, preserving electron flow to cytochrome c.

label: Creatine
description: Creatine supplementation is one of the most effective and best-documented ergogenic aids for improving performance in high-intensity, short-duration activities. By increasing muscle phosphocreatine stores, creatine enhances the capacity to regenerate ATP during repeated bouts of maximal exercise, increasing power output, strength gains during resistance training, and work performed in repeated sprint protocols. Meta-analyses consistently show moderate improvements in measures such as maximal strength, sprint performance, and lean body mass, with benefit most pronounced in activities relying on the phosphocreatine energy system. These well-established performance effects are the context in which the trace asks whether creatine also influences cancer outcomes.

label: Sarcopenia
description: The results of the PEARL study, a trial of low-dose intermittent rapamycin given for 48 weeks to adults aged 50-85, appear to confirm the possibility of pharmacological modulation of age-related inconveniences. Significant improvements in lean body mass, reduction of pain symptoms in women, and improvements in self-assessment of health and emotional well-being in both sexes were observed. Sarcopenia, defined as progressive loss of muscle mass and strength leading to physical deterioration and increased fall risk, is one of the key conditions targeted, and an ongoing randomized placebo-controlled study is testing intermittent sirolimus at 6 mg/week combined with a training program for sarcopenia prevention in the elderly.

label: Homocysteine
description: Creatine supplementation has been reported to lower plasma homocysteine, an effect that may reduce cardiovascular disease risk. Because homocysteine is methylated back to methionine by enzymes that require the same methyl-donor pool (S-adenosyl methionine) used for creatine synthesis, supplying exogenous creatine spares methyl groups that would otherwise be consumed in endogenous creatine formation, thereby lowering homocysteine production. Studies in individuals adhering to vegan diets (who tend to have elevated homocysteine) reported that creatine supplementation reduced homocysteine levels and improved systemic microvascular endothelial function, supporting creatine's role in cardiovascular health beyond its direct effects on muscle bioenergetics.

label: Toll-like Receptor
description: Creatine down-regulates the expression of toll-like receptors, including TLR-2, TLR-3, TLR-4, and TLR-7, in a mouse macrophage cell line (RAW 254.7). This downregulation could reduce the ability to sense some infections in immunocompromised individuals, but TLR-4 downregulation may also alter Parkinson's disease pathology and inhibit neuronal death as the disease progresses. Creatine's influence on toll-like receptors is one component of its broader immunomodulatory effects, which also include altering cytokine production, possibly through the NF-kB signaling pathway, thereby affecting cytokines, receptors, and growth factors that shape immune responses and inflammation.

label: Cognition
description: Creatine supplementation increases brain phosphocreatine content by 5-15% and enhances brain bioenergetics, which is thought to underlie its cognitive benefits. Studies report that creatine attenuates mental fatigue and improves cognition, executive function, working memory, and processing speed, especially in older adults and during sleep deprivation. Examples include improved working memory and processing speed after 5 g/day for 6 weeks, better maintenance of mood, balance, and reaction time after sleep deprivation, and improved long-term memory and random number generation in elderly participants. While not all studies show benefit, the evidence supports creatine as a modest cognitive enhancer, particularly under metabolic or cognitive stress.

label: Exercise
description: Exercise raises both BDNF and NAD+ levels, and SIRT1 may mediate exercise-induced BDNF upregulation in the hippocampus. Directionally, exercise sits upstream of BDNF and NAD+ elevation. Higher NAD+ fuels SIRT1, which then supports BDNF, and this provides a mechanistic bridge between physical activity, sirtuins, and brain health. By raising NAD+, exercise engages the sirtuin pathway that promotes BDNF expression and mitochondrial function. This axis is central to the well-established cognitive benefits of exercise and to the geroscience concept of exercise as medicine.

label: Methylglyoxal (MG)
description: Creatine augments the anticancer efficacy of the metabolite methylglyoxal (MG). Creatine content and energy availability are low in several types of malignant cells and in the T cells that mediate immune responses against cancer, and the creatine transporter SLC6A8 is markedly increased in tumor-infiltrating immune cells. Patra et al. reported that MG efficacy is significantly augmented in the presence of creatine, and combined administration of creatine, methylglyoxal, and ascorbic acid provided greater efficacy and eliminated visible signs of tumor growth. Creatine and creatine kinase, very low in sarcoma tissue, were significantly elevated with concomitant regression of tumor cells.

label: Antioxidant Properties
description: Creatine is reported to exert antioxidant effects, scavenging reactive oxygen and nitrogen species and stabilizing membranes, effects that are proposed to protect tissues from oxidative damage. Some studies suggest creatine supplementation reduces markers of oxidative stress and muscle damage after intense exercise, and experimental work indicates creatine can directly scavenge superoxide and peroxynitrite in vitro. Because oxidative stress contributes to DNA damage and tumor promotion, creatine's antioxidant capacity is cited in the trace as one possible mechanism for an anti-cancer effect, although direct evidence linking creatine's antioxidant action to cancer prevention in humans is lacking.

label: Exercise Performance
description: Creatine supplementation is one of the most effective and best-documented ergogenic aids for improving performance in high-intensity, short-duration activities. By increasing muscle phosphocreatine stores, creatine enhances the capacity to regenerate ATP during repeated bouts of maximal exercise, increasing power output, strength gains during resistance training, and work performed in repeated sprint protocols. Meta-analyses consistently show moderate improvements in measures such as maximal strength, sprint performance, and lean body mass, with benefit most pronounced in activities relying on the phosphocreatine energy system. These well-established performance effects are the context in which the trace asks whether creatine also influences cancer outcomes.

label: Glycemic Control
description: Creatine supplementation supports healthy glucose management by enhancing glucose uptake and insulin sensitivity. Mechanistically, creatine prevents the decline of GLUT4 during muscle disuse, increases GLUT4 during rehabilitation, and co-ingestion with carbohydrate or protein augments muscle creatine and glycogen. In individuals with type 2 diabetes, creatine supplementation during exercise training improved glucose tolerance to a standard meal, increased GLUT4 translocation, and lowered HbA1c, with AMPK signaling implicated in these effects. Creatine uptake into tissue is itself influenced by glucose and insulin, establishing a bidirectional relationship between creatine status and glycemic physiology that supports creatine as an adjunct for metabolic health.

label: GLUT4
description: Creatine supplementation influences glucose handling in skeletal muscle, in part by upregulating the GLUT4 glucose transporter. Creatine prevents declines in GLUT4 during immobilization and increases GLUT4 by about 40% during rehabilitation after atrophy, and co-ingestion with carbohydrate and protein enhances creatine uptake and muscle glycogen. In type 2 diabetic patients, 12 weeks of creatine supplementation during training improved glucose tolerance, increased GLUT4 translocation, and significantly reduced HbA1c, with changes in AMPK signaling related to GLUT4 translocation and HbA1c. These findings indicate creatine enhances glucose uptake and supports glucose management, especially when combined with exercise.

label: Muscle Mass
description: Creatine supplementation increases muscle creatine and phosphocreatine stores and, particularly when combined with resistance training, promotes gains in lean tissue mass and strength. Randomized trials in older adults show greater gains in muscle mass and isometric strength with creatine plus heavy resistance training compared to training alone, and meta-analyses confirm larger gains in muscle mass and upper-body strength in older individuals supplementing creatine during resistance exercise. Creatine also decreases protein breakdown and can preserve muscle mass during energy-restricted weight loss, making it a broadly useful strategy for maintaining muscle across the lifespan and in clinical rehabilitation populations.

label: Nutraceuticals
description: Creatine is a naturally occurring nitrogen-containing compound that is synthesized endogenously in the liver, kidney, and pancreas and is also obtained from dietary sources, particularly red meat and fish. Around 95 percent of the body's creatine is stored in skeletal muscle, approximately one-third of it in the phosphorylated form creatine phosphate. In the muscle it is converted to creatine phosphate, which donates its high-energy phosphate group to regenerate ATP from ADP, supporting short-duration, high-intensity exercise. Because of its role in ATP regeneration, creatine is one of the most widely used sports supplements and is increasingly examined for additional therapeutic effects, including possible anti-cancer properties.

label: Red Meat
description: Dietary creatine is obtained almost exclusively from animal-derived foods, with red meat and fish being the richest sources. Cooking does not destroy creatine, and an omnivorous diet typically supplies one to two grams of creatine per day, which complements the roughly one gram synthesized endogenously per day. Vegetarians have lower muscle creatine stores and show larger increases in response to supplementation than meat-eaters, reflecting the lower baseline intake. This dietary origin is relevant to epidemiologic questions about meat consumption and cancer risk, because creatine is often discussed alongside other meat-derived compounds when considering diet-cancer associations.

label: Creatine Phosphate
description: Within cells, creatine is phosphorylated by the enzyme creatine kinase to form creatine phosphate (phosphocreatine), which serves as a rapidly mobilizable reserve of high-energy phosphate. The reaction creatine plus ATP yields creatine phosphate plus ADP, and the reverse reaction regenerates ATP during bursts of high energy demand, such as muscle contraction. The phosphocreatine pool is the immediate energy buffer that sustains ATP levels for the first several seconds of maximal effort, before glycolysis and oxidative metabolism fully contribute. This conversion of creatine to creatine phosphate is the mechanistic heart of the creatine-phosphocreatine energy system.

label: Phosphocreatine (PCr)
description: Roughly two-thirds of the body's creatine pool is phosphorylated and stored as phosphocreatine (PCr), with the remainder held as free creatine. The creatine kinase (CK) reaction interconverts creatine and PCr, and the energy liberated by breaking PCr down into phosphate and creatine (about 10.3 kcal) is used to resynthesize ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate. This PCr/CK system is the rapid, phosphagen-based buffer that maintains ATP availability during intense exercise, ischemia, hypoxia, and high metabolic demand. Creatine supplementation raises muscle creatine and PCr stores, expanding this reserve and thereby enhancing high-intensity exercise capacity and training adaptations.

label: Dietary Supplement
description: Creatine monohydrate is among the most extensively studied dietary supplements and is generally regarded as safe when used at recommended doses over periods of many years. Long-term supplementation studies report no consistent adverse effects on renal, hepatic, or cardiovascular function in healthy individuals, and creatine is approved for use by many sports organizations.
