label: SK61_2
description: mTORC1, the complex formed when mTOR binds to raptor, activates the ribosomal protein S6 kinases S6K1/S6K2 (S6K1/2) by phosphorylation. Active S6K1/2 in turn inactivates IRS1 by phosphorylation, forming a negative feedback loop that regulates insulin signaling, and also deactivates mTORC2. In the mass-action model of the mTOR-PI3K pathway, the Michaelis-Menten constant for the activation of S6K1/2 by mTORC1 is significantly smaller on average than other pathway constants, correlating with the low backward-reaction constant that increases the rate of hormesis in rapamycin-treated networks.

label: mTORC2
description: Active PI3K (phosphoinositide 3-kinase) activates mTORC2 by phosphorylation in the mass-action model of the insulin signaling cascade. mTORC2 is the chosen output node of the pathway because it drives cell cycle progression and survival via AKT and regulates mitochondrial physiology, metabolism and integrity; mTORC2 activity increases with age and its elimination alleviates aging progression. Principal component analysis of hormetic parameter sets shows that the most important parameters correspond to the phosphorylation and dephosphorylation of PI3K, suggesting that PI3K levels are relevant to the mechanisms that induce the hormetic response of rapamycin.

label: Cell Proliferation
description: mTORC2 is the downstream readout of the rapamycin model since it drives cell cycle progression and survival via AKT, and also regulates mitochondrial physiology, metabolism and integrity. mTORC2 activity has been shown to increase with age, and its elimination has been shown to alleviate aging progression. In the simulations, the typical dose-response curve shows a clear decrease in mTORC2 activity at intermediate rapamycin concentrations, followed by reduced sensitivity at higher doses, while short-term rapamycin exposure increases mTORC2 activity and long-term exposure obstructs its assembly.

label: N-Formylkynurenine
description: N-formylkynurenine is the immediate product of IDO1's oxidative cleavage of the tryptophan indole ring at the 2,3-position; it is then rapidly converted to kynurenine (Kyn). Kynurenine is the central metabolite of the kynurenine pathway from which downstream neuroactive and NAD+-linked metabolites are derived. The kynurenine pathway leads to metabolites including kynurenic acid, 3-hydroxykynurenine, quinolinic acid (a neurotoxin and NAD+ precursor), and ultimately NAD+, and accounts for roughly 95% of tryptophan degradation outside protein synthesis and serotonin production.

label: Sirtuins
description: Sirtuins are class III histone deacetylases whose catalytic mechanism absolutely requires NAD+ as a co-substrate, coupling deacetylation to the cellular redox and energy state. Each turnover hydrolyzes one NAD+ molecule into nicotinamide and 2'-O-acetyl-ADP-ribose while removing an acetyl group from a lysine residue on the target protein. This strict NAD+ dependence means sirtuin activity rises when the NAD+/NADH ratio is high, as occurs during caloric restriction, exercise, or fasting, and falls when NAD+ is depleted. A caveat is that this dependency creates competition with other NAD+-consuming enzymes such as CD38 and PARPs for the same limited co-substrate pool.

label: Nano-formulation
source_file: _document_ - Fisetin—In Search of Better Bioavailability—From Macro to Nano Modifications A Review.md
description: Nano-sized formulations of fisetin, including polymeric nanoparticles, lipid nanoparticles, nanoemulsions, and nanocrystals, have been developed to overcome its poor solubility and low oral bioavailability. These systems increase fisetin's dissolution rate, protect it from degradation and first-pass conjugation, and can enable sustained release and improved tissue targeting, including brain delivery. Studies summarized in the review report several-fold increases in fisetin peak plasma concentration and area under the curve for nanoformulations compared with free fisetin suspension, and enhanced efficacy in tumor and neuroprotection models, although clinical data remain limited.

label: Fisetin Bioavailability
source_file: _document_ - Fisetin—In Search of Better Bioavailability—From Macro to Nano Modifications A Review.md

label: Neutral Red
source_file: _document_ - Neuroprotective Actions of Methylene Blue and Its Derivatives.md
description: Neutral red (NR), a phenazine formed by substituting nitrogen for the position-5 sulfur of the phenothiazine nucleus, retained the ability to increase cellular oxygen consumption (OCR) in Seahorse assays, similar to methylene blue and toluidine blue O, and these three compounds share similar negative redox potentials. However, NR had markedly weaker neuroprotective potency than MB in the glutamate, rotenone, and IAA assays and does not function as an alternative electron-transfer carrier in mitochondria, indicating that oxygen-consumption enhancement alone does not confer neuroprotection and that electron-shunt activity is the key protective feature.

label: Nicotinamide Riboside
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial Drivers Stem Cell Aging Inflammaging Bautista 2026.md
description: Restoring NAD+ with nicotinamide riboside (NR) reactivated mitochondrial metabolism, upregulated prohibitin proteins, and induced UPRmt, delaying stem cell senescence and extending lifespan in aged contexts. In aged muscle stem cells, neural stem cells and melanocyte stem cells, NAD+ depletion leads to senescence, loss of quiescence and diminished regenerative capacity, and NR treatment reverses this by restoring mitochondrial function. NR is a key NAD+ repletion strategy alongside NMN that restores sirtuin activity, enhances the mitochondrial unfolded protein response, and improves mitochondrial membrane potential, thereby supporting regeneration and resilience in aged stem cell c...

label: Stem Cells
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial Drivers Stem Cell Aging Inflammaging Bautista 2026.md
description: Restoring NAD+ with nicotinamide riboside (NR) reactivated mitochondrial metabolism, upregulated prohibitin proteins, and induced UPRmt, delaying stem cell senescence and extending lifespan in aged contexts. In aged muscle stem cells, neural stem cells and melanocyte stem cells, NAD+ depletion leads to senescence, loss of quiescence and diminished regenerative capacity, and NR treatment reverses this by restoring mitochondrial function. NR is a key NAD+ repletion strategy alongside NMN that restores sirtuin activity, enhances the mitochondrial unfolded protein response, and improves mitochondrial membrane potential, thereby supporting regeneration and resilience in aged stem cell c...

label: Hypotension
description: Massive nitric oxide release during septic shock, anaphylaxis, or post-cardiopulmonary bypass vasoplegia causes excessive vasodilation and life-threateningly low blood pressure (hypotension). NO overproduction is driven largely by the inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) enzyme during the inflammatory response. Therapeutic strategies target this cascade at different levels: aminoguanidine inhibits iNOS to block NO synthesis upstream, while methylene blue inhibits soluble guanylyl cyclase to block NO signaling downstream and restore blood pressure when vasopressors fail.

label: Vasodilation
description: Under normal conditions nitric oxide is a crucial signaling molecule that relaxes vascular smooth muscle via activation of soluble guanylyl cyclase and cGMP production. However, during severe inflammation, injury, or shock, overproduction of NO - primarily by inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) - leads to excessive vasodilation, vascular leakage, and tissue damage. This is the pathway targeted by both aminoguanidine, which blocks NO synthesis at iNOS (upstream), and methylene blue, which blocks NO action at sGC (downstream).

label: NLRP3
description: The NLRP3 inflammasome, a large protein complex whose assembly is triggered by stimuli including uric acid and lipopolysaccharide, is primed by mitochondrial reactive oxygen species. Mitochondrial ROS inhibitors block priming, but not activation, of the NLRP3 inflammasome. Activation of the inflammasome results in enzymatic activation of caspase-1 and subsequent proteolytic cleavage of pro-interleukin-1beta into its mature, secreted form, linking mitochondrial oxidant signaling to the innate immune inflammatory response.

label: NMN
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial Drivers Stem Cell Aging Inflammaging Bautista 2026.md
description: In intestinal stem cells, a high mtDNA mutation burden reduces LGR5+ cell function and organoid-forming capacity, mediated by ATF5-driven UPRmt activation, and this is reversible with NMN supplementation. NMN is an NAD+ precursor that restores NAD+ levels, thereby supporting sirtuin-dependent resilience and mitochondrial function in aged stem cell compartments. Alongside nicotinamide riboside, NMN represents a leading NAD+ repletion strategy for restoring stem cell regenerative potential and delaying senescence. The reversibility of mtDNA-mutation-associated stem cell dysfunction with NMN demonstrates that NAD+ replenishment can functionally counteract age-related mitochondrial decline.

label: Intestinal Stem Cell
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial Drivers Stem Cell Aging Inflammaging Bautista 2026.md
description: In intestinal stem cells, a high mtDNA mutation burden reduces LGR5+ cell function and organoid-forming capacity, mediated by ATF5-driven UPRmt activation, and this is reversible with NMN supplementation. NMN is an NAD+ precursor that restores NAD+ levels, thereby supporting sirtuin-dependent resilience and mitochondrial function in aged stem cell compartments. Alongside nicotinamide riboside, NMN represents a leading NAD+ repletion strategy for restoring stem cell regenerative potential and delaying senescence. The reversibility of mtDNA-mutation-associated stem cell dysfunction with NMN demonstrates that NAD+ replenishment can functionally counteract age-related mitochondrial decline.

label: NRF2
description: SIRT1 activates the transcription factor Nrf2 by modifying the structure of its cytoplasmic repressor Keap1, permitting Nrf2 nuclear translocation and induction of antioxidant genes. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of Nrf2 activation. This boosts expression of phase-II detoxifying and antioxidant enzymes, providing broad protection against oxidative and electrophilic stress. It is a major cytoprotective pathway engaged by SIRT1, complementing its deacetylation of FOXO and PGC-1α. Because Nrf2 coordinates hundreds of protective genes, SIRT1-dependent Nrf2 activation is central to SIRT1's stress-resistance and longevity-associated phenotypes.

label: OMA1
description: The proteolytic processing of OPA1 is mediated by several mitochondrial proteases, including the metalloendopeptidase OMA1, the ATP-dependent zinc metalloprotease YME1L1, the rhomboid protease PARL, paraplegin and the mAAA protease complex. Under stress conditions such as mitochondrial depolarization, the S1 site of OPA1 is cleaved by YME1L1 or OMA1 to produce the short form S-OPA1, which lacks a membrane anchor but can modulate fusion by complexing with membrane-bound L-OPA1. DRP1-mediated zinc influx into the matrix causes membrane depolarization, resulting in OMA1 activation and OPA1 inactivation to enable clearance of damaged mitochondrial fragments by mitophagy.

label: Dominant Optic Atrophy
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial Fusion and Fission The fine-tune balance for cellular homeostasis.md
description: Dominant optic atrophy (DOA) is directly caused by heterozygous mutations in the mitochondrial fusion-related gene OPA1, which encodes the inner mitochondrial membrane fusion GTPase optic atrophy 1. OPA1 mutations and improper OPA1 processing induce mitochondrial fragmentation, resulting in severe cardiomyopathy and ultimately heart failure in addition to optic atrophy. In a mouse DOA model, adeno-associated virus delivery of wild-type OPA1 alleviates retinal ganglion cell degeneration, demonstrating the therapeutic potential of restoring fusion capacity in OPA1-mutant disease.

label: Parasympathetic Nervous System
description: The parasympathetic nervous system is the rest, digest, and repair branch of the autonomic nervous system, controlled heavily by the vagus nerve. When active, it signals the body to calm down, digest food, and repair cells, allowing for more fluctuation between heartbeats and thereby raising HRV. A high HRV indicates strong vagal tone, meaning the parasympathetic system can quickly hit the brakes on stress. HRV reflects the tug-of-war between the sympathetic and parasympathetic systems, and recovery after stressors allows the parasympathetic branch to rebound and push HRV back to or above baseline.

label: Parkin
source_file: _document_ - The role of mitochondrial dynamics in disease.md
description: In healthy mitochondria, PINK1 (PTEN-induced putative kinase 1) is continuously imported into the inner membrane, cleaved and degraded by PARL and mitochondrial processing peptidases. When mitochondrial membrane potential becomes abnormal or import is impaired, PINK1 stabilizes and accumulates on the outer mitochondrial membrane, where its kinase domain phosphorylates outer membrane proteins and recruits and activates the E3 ubiquitin ligase Parkin (PRKN). PINK1 phosphorylation of MFN2 acts as a Parkin receptor that facilitates Parkin recruitment, and activated Parkin polyubiquitinates outer membrane proteins, marking damaged mitochondria for autophagic degradation.

label: PGC-1α
description: PGC-1α is the master coactivator controlling mitochondrial biogenesis, stimulating transcription of nuclear-encoded respiratory-chain subunits and coordinating with mitochondrial DNA replication. Its activation by SIRT1, through deacetylation, and by AMPK, through phosphorylation, increases mitochondrial number and oxidative capacity in response to energy demand. Directionally, PGC-1α sits upstream of new mitochondrion formation, partnering with NRF1, NRF2, ERRα, and TFAM to execute the program.

label: Photobiomodulation
description: Photobiomodulation, applied as daily morning sunlight or targeted red and near-infrared light therapy, directly stimulates cytochrome c oxidase (Complex IV) in the mitochondria, enhancing ATP production. It is listed among the light, temperature, and environmental exposures that act as mitohormetic stressors. Cold exposure similarly activates brown adipose tissue and induces uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) leading to increased mitochondrial density, while sauna heat exposure induces heat shock proteins that repair misfolded proteins and support mitochondrial function.

label: Sedentary Behaviour
description: Total physical activity during the day can be limited by sedentary behaviour, and in some doubly labelled water studies the elevated energy expenditure from a structured exercise session was partly offset by a reduction in non-exercise physical activity elsewhere in the day. Speakman notes that the extent of this compensation varies between individuals, so the net effect of a training program on total daily energy expenditure is the sum of the exercise cost, the excess post-exercise oxygen consumption, and any changes in spontaneous activity and appetite. This interaction helps explain why measured increases in total daily energy expenditure with training are often smaller than the energy cost of the training sessions themselves.

label: Doubly Labelled Water
description: The doubly labelled water (DLW) technique is the gold-standard method for measuring total daily energy expenditure and the physical activity component of the energy budget in free-living humans. Subjects drink water labeled with the stable isotopes deuterium and oxygen-18; carbon dioxide production is calculated from the differential loss rates of the two isotopes, and energy expenditure is derived using standard equations. In the studies reviewed by Speakman, DLW has been used to quantify total daily energy expenditure (TEE) over 7-14 day periods, showing that within-individual day-to-day variability of TEE is small even when physical activity varies.

label: Daily Energy Expenditure
description: Physical activity and exercise are the components of daily energy expenditure that are most amenable to voluntary modification, in contrast to resting metabolic rate and thermic effect of food which are largely fixed by body size and composition. Speakman reviews doubly labelled water studies of total daily energy expenditure in adults to argue that although activity levels vary widely between individuals, the day-to-day variability of total daily energy expenditure is surprisingly small, around 2-3 percent. This suggests energy intake is tightly matched to expenditure over the long term, and that exercise-induced elevations in expenditure are generally not fully compensated by reductions elsewhere in the daily energy budget.

label: PINK1
source_file: _document_ - The role of mitochondrial dynamics in disease.md
description: In healthy mitochondria, PINK1 (PTEN-induced putative kinase 1) is continuously imported into the inner membrane, cleaved and degraded by PARL and mitochondrial processing peptidases. When mitochondrial membrane potential becomes abnormal or import is impaired, PINK1 stabilizes and accumulates on the outer mitochondrial membrane, where its kinase domain phosphorylates outer membrane proteins and recruits and activates the E3 ubiquitin ligase Parkin (PRKN). PINK1 phosphorylation of MFN2 acts as a Parkin receptor that facilitates Parkin recruitment, and activated Parkin polyubiquitinates outer membrane proteins, marking damaged mitochondria for autophagic degradation.

label: PP2A
description: PP2A (protein phosphatase 2A) is the main phosphatase that counteracts the effect of mTORC1 in the activation of S6K1/2 within the mass-action model of the mTOR-PI3K pathway. It is one of the two key phosphatases in the cascade, alongside PTEN which indirectly inactivates PI3K. The signaling pathway is designed as a chain of kinase-phosphatase opposing pairs, and the balance between these antagonistic reactions at key nodes is a structural feature that shapes the dose-response behavior of the network under rapamycin inhibition.

label: Peroxiredoxin
description: Peroxiredoxin 6 is a unique 1-Cys member of the peroxiredoxin family, which comprises six highly conserved antioxidant enzymes (PRDX1-PRDX6) featuring a cysteine residue involved in peroxide reduction. Uniquely among peroxiredoxins, PRDX6 possesses three activities: peroxidase, acidic calcium-independent phospholipase A2 (aiPLA2), and lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferase (LPCAT). It is important for lipid peroxidation repair, inflammatory signaling, and antioxidant damage responses, and it is extensively studied in brain disorders such as Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease.

label: Arachidonic acid
description: Through its phospholipase A2 (PLA2) activity, PRDX6 generates arachidonic acid from membrane phospholipids; arachidonic acid is a precursor of pro-inflammatory eicosanoids and is often a driver of inflammation. This places PRDX6's aiPLA2 activity at the interface between redox homeostasis and inflammatory signaling. Apigenin suppresses this activity, and the selective PRDX6 PLA2 inhibitor MJ33 lowers canonical SASP factor expression in a concentration-dependent manner, functionally linking the PLA2-dependent arachidonic acid axis to the senescent secretory phenotype. This mechanism is independent of PRDX6's peroxidase function, which is only modestly inhibited by apigenin.

label: Epigenome
description: Protein restriction alters the epigenome, one of its six hallmarks. Aging is accompanied by erosion of the epigenetic landscape - DNA methylation and post-translational modifications of histone tails - that promotes hallmarks of aging including cellular senescence. PR in pregnant rodents leads to loci-specific changes in histone methylation and gene expression, and dietary levels of specific amino acids regulate histone post-translational modifications, linking nutrient sensing to the epigenome. Methionine is the precursor of S-adenosyl methionine, the universal methyl donor, so dietary methionine deprivation may affect physiology through changes in histone methylation due to decreased methyl-donor availability, with cells preserving heterochromatic stability through upregulation of H3K9 methylation in the liver.

label: Glucose Homeostasis
description: Protein restriction improves glucose homeostasis and insulin sensitivity in both rodents and humans. In young and aged rodents, PR reduces body weight and fat mass, increases energy expenditure, and improves glucose handling even when initiated late in life. Randomized controlled trials in humans show low-protein diets reduce body weight, fat mass, and fasting blood glucose, improve insulin sensitivity, and lower hemoglobin A1C and kidney disease outcomes in diabetic patients. BCAA restriction similarly improves insulin sensitivity and glucose/insulin homeostasis in humans, and methionine restriction improves glucose homeostasis in humans on strict vegan diets. These metabolic benefits contrast with high-protein diets associated with increased diabetes risk.

label: Energy Expenditure
description: Several single-nucleotide polymorphisms in the human SIRT1 gene are significantly associated with systemic energy expenditure in Finnish cohorts, suggesting that SIRT1 variation influences metabolic rate. These variants may alter SIRT1 expression or activity, shifting how individuals burn fuel at rest and during activity. Directionally, genetic SIRT1 variation is linked to an energy-expenditure phenotype. As with most genetic-association findings, effect sizes are modest and context-dependent, and replication in other populations is needed.

label: Adiposity
description: Protein restriction reduces adiposity while increasing energy expenditure, an effect that occurs despite increased food intake. In young and aged rodents, PR reduces body fat, increases energy expenditure, and improves glucose homeostasis, with effects most pronounced in males but also present in females, and it remains effective when initiated late in life (18-20 months). These metabolic benefits are largely mediated by FGF21, which promotes energy expenditure through UCP1-dependent thermogenic beiging of white adipose tissue and increases thermogenesis in brown adipose tissue, shifting brain signaling toward protein appetite. Randomized controlled trials confirm low-protein diets reduce body weight and fat mass in humans despite increased caloric intake.

label: Proton Leak
description: Mitochondrial proton leak, the passive return of protons across the inner mitochondrial membrane that bypasses ATP synthase, is a significant component of resting metabolic rate and of the energy expenditure of skeletal muscle. Because proton leak uncouples oxygen consumption from ATP production, it dissipates a portion of the proton gradient as heat and is estimated to account for roughly 20 percent of resting oxygen consumption in mammals. Speakman discusses how variations in proton leak, partly set by the expression of uncoupling proteins such as UCP3 in muscle, contribute to inter-individual differences in metabolic rate and, potentially, to differences in exercise-induced energy expenditure.

label: PTEN
description: PTEN is the main phosphatase that indirectly inactivates PI3K in the mTOR-PI3K signaling cascade, providing the antagonistic deactivating arm that balances PI3K activation. Alongside PP2A, which counteracts the effect of mTORC1 in the activation of S6K1/2, PTEN is one of the two key phosphatases modeled as kinase-phosphatase opposing pairs. The balance between activating and deactivating reactions at key nodes, such as the positive correlation between activation and deactivation of mTORC2, is consistent with the requirement for opposite reactions to underlie biphasic dose-responses.

label: Rapamycin
source_file: _document_ - The Mechanistic Target of Rapamycin (mTOR) Pathway as a Target of Anti-aging Therapies The Role of Rapamycin and Its Analogs in the Regulation of Cellular Processes and Their Impact on Longevity.md
description: Rapamycin, also called sirolimus, is an organic chemical compound produced by Streptomyces hygroscopicus, isolated from soil samples taken on Easter Island Rapa Nui by Georges Nogrady in the late 1960s. At the molecular level it acts as a specific inhibitor of mTOR by forming a complex with the immunophilin FKBP12, which then binds to mTOR and suppresses its kinase activity. As a result, rapamycin downregulates protein synthesis, cell growth, and anabolic metabolism while promoting autophagy, shifting the cell from anabolic to maintenance and repair processes, a key mechanism underlying its longevity-promoting effects.

label: Stomatitis
description: While aspirin may cause gastric ulceration and bleeding, rapamycin may cause stomatitis and mucositis, ulceration of the mucous membranes of the mouth and digestive tract, when used at high doses or chronically. A rare side effect of rapamycin is noninfectious interstitial pneumonitis, and by inhibiting neutrophil function rapamycin may increase the severity of bacterial infections. These side effects require rapamycin's discontinuation, but for anti-aging purposes rapamycin may be used intermittently (e.g., once a week) or at low daily doses and can be discontinued if any unpleasant effects occur.

label: Cardiovascular System
source_file: _document_ - The Mechanistic Target of Rapamycin (mTOR) Pathway as a Target of Anti-aging Therapies The Role of Rapamycin and Its Analogs in the Regulation of Cellular Processes and Their Impact on Longevity.md
description: In a study of 24 middle-aged companion dogs, echocardiography showed improvements in both diastolic and systolic measures of age-related cardiac function (E/A ratio, fractional shortening, and ejection fraction) in dogs treated with rapamycin. Rapamycin also stimulates the breakdown of damaged cytoplasmic elements, reduces oxidative stress, and supports tissue regeneration in cardiac tissue, and induces production of growth factors IGF1 and VEGF while reducing IL-1beta and TNF-alpha to support cardiac regeneration after infarction. Cardiovascular diseases are the main cause of death in the elderly, making mTOR inhibitors a promising direction for cardioprotective research.

label: Oxidative Phosphorylation
source_file: _document_ - The Mechanistic Target of Rapamycin (mTOR) Pathway as a Target of Anti-aging Therapies The Role of Rapamycin and Its Analogs in the Regulation of Cellular Processes and Their Impact on Longevity.md
description: Rapamycin improves the NAD+/NADH redox balance, which supports normal oxidative phosphorylation and reduces cellular pseudohypoxia associated with mTOR hyperactivity and HIF-1alpha accumulation. As a result, lactate production is reduced and cellular energy efficiency improves. In addition, inhibition of mTOR promotes mitochondrial biogenesis and increases the expression of key regulators such as PGC-1alpha and mitochondrial transcription factor A (TFAM), leading to renewal of mitochondrial populations and improved fatty acid metabolism in senescent tissues including the myocardium and brown adipose tissue.

label: Proteostasis
source_file: _document_ - The Mechanistic Target of Rapamycin (mTOR) Pathway as a Target of Anti-aging Therapies The Role of Rapamycin and Its Analogs in the Regulation of Cellular Processes and Their Impact on Longevity.md
description: The mTORC1 pathway controls mRNA translation, and its overactivity increases the rate of protein synthesis at the expense of protein quality. Inhibition of mTORC1 by rapamycin reduces translation, improves its accuracy, and promotes longer life by reducing genetic code reading errors and the accumulation of abnormal proteins, a mechanism confirmed in Drosophila and C. elegans models. Rapamycin also inhibits cap-dependent translation of mRNA, supporting alternative stress-resistant translation that increases production of stress-response and mitochondrial-protection proteins such as HSP70 and TFAM, and by activating ATF4 and producing hydrogen sulfide it increases resistance to oxidative stress.

label: Glucose Intolerance
source_file: _document_ - Rapamycin for longevity the pros, the cons, and future perspectives.md
description: Chronic rapamycin treatment is associated with metabolic disturbances including glucose intolerance and hyperlipidemia in both mice and humans administered rapamycin for prevention of immunosenescence. Mechanistically these effects are attributed not only to mTORC1 inhibition but also to unintended suppression of mTORC2, which induces insulin resistance - a mechanistic trade-off between metabolic side effects and longevity benefits. Houde et al. showed chronic rapamycin causes glucose intolerance and hyperlipidemia by upregulating hepatic gluconeogenesis and impairing lipid deposition in adipose tissue.

label: Hyperlipidemia
source_file: _document_ - Rapamycin for longevity the pros, the cons, and future perspectives.md
description: Chronic rapamycin or everolimus use is associated with elevated cholesterol and triglyceride levels (hyperlipidemia), alongside mucosal ulcers, impaired wound healing, delayed tissue repair, and increased infection risk. These metabolic disturbances were common in the EXIST-3 trial and other cohorts, along with stomatitis, infections, and cytopenias. The mechanisms are attributed to both mTORC1 inhibition and unintended mTORC2 suppression, which induces insulin resistance.

label: Rapalogs
description: Rapamycin is a natural anti-fungal antibiotic produced by soil bacteria of Eastern Island whose patent has expired, and pharmacological companies have developed other rapalogs such as everolimus. The term rapalogs encompasses rapamycin, everolimus and any other analogs, and at equipotent doses rapamycin and everolimus exert almost identical therapeutic and adverse effects, although everolimus is weaker and has a shorter half-life. All current rapalogs exhibit the same side effects as rapamycin and everolimus, and their real side effects are mTORC1-dependent.

label: CYP3A4
source_file: _document_ - Rapamycin for longevity the pros, the cons, and future perspectives.md
description: Rapamycin and its analogs are metabolized by the cytochrome P450 enzyme CYP3A4 and are therefore sensitive to pharmacokinetic drug interactions. Cannabidiol (CBD) is a potent CYP3A inhibitor that increases circulating levels of mTOR inhibitors, raising the risk of toxicity - a clinically relevant interaction given the widespread use of CBD and other cannabis products. This has been documented in patients with tuberous sclerosis complex (cannabidiol elevates mechanistic target of rapamycin inhibitor levels) and in a phase 1 healthy volunteer trial of coadministered everolimus and CBD.

label: Colorectal Cancer
source_file: _document_ - The Mechanistic Target of Rapamycin (mTOR) Pathway as a Target of Anti-aging Therapies The Role of Rapamycin and Its Analogs in the Regulation of Cellular Processes and Their Impact on Longevity.md
description: SIRT5 contributes to colorectal carcinogenesis by enhancing glutaminolysis in a deglutarylation-dependent manner, promoting cancer cell metabolism and proliferation. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of enhanced glutamine catabolism in colorectal cancer. By supporting the use of glutamine as a fuel and carbon source, SIRT5 provides tumor cells with the metabolic flexibility required for rapid growth. This oncogenic function illustrates that sirtuins can promote as well as suppress cancer, depending on the tissue and the specific metabolic demands of the tumor. Inhibiting SIRT5 may therefore be a strategy to starve colorectal cancer cells of the glutamine-dependent metabolism they rely on.

label: mTORopathies
source_file: _document_ - Rapamycin for longevity the pros, the cons, and future perspectives.md
description: The success of rapamycin in mTORopathy models stems from clearly defined molecular etiology and robust biomarkers: highly penetrant mutations driving mTOR hyperactivation render the pathway an actionable target. In TSC and GATOR1-related models such as Nprl3 knockout mice, rapamycin prevented seizures, reduced mortality, and rescued neuropathology, including when delivered in utero or postnatally. Everolimus is used as precision therapy in GATOR1-related epilepsies.

label: Athletes
description: Athletes in heavy training display elevated resting metabolic rates compared with untrained individuals, largely because their higher fat free mass increases the metabolic load of lean tissues. Speakman notes that RMR measured in endurance athletes can be elevated by about 5-10 percent beyond the prediction for their body composition alone, an effect attributed to increased protein turnover, elevated sympathetic tone, and continued recovery processes in muscle. However, the review stresses that the majority of the difference in total daily energy expenditure between athletes and non-athletes arises from the energy cost of training itself, not from chronic elevation of RMR.

label: Thyroid Hormones
description: Resting metabolic rate is modulated by thyroid hormones, which set the metabolic tone of the body by regulating mitochondrial oxygen consumption and cellular sodium-potassium ATPase activity in most tissues. Speakman reviews that both hypothyroid and hyperthyroid states shift RMR substantially, and that within the normal range thyroid status contributes to inter-individual variability in resting metabolic rate. However, training-induced changes in RMR are generally not mediated by changes in thyroid hormone levels, and short-term exercise does not consistently alter circulating thyroid hormone concentrations, indicating that the post-exercise RMR elevation is driven by other factors.

label: Ribosomal Protein S6
source_file: _document_ - Rapamycin for longevity the pros, the cons, and future perspectives.md
description: Phosphorylated ribosomal protein S6 (phospho-S6) is used as a surrogate marker of mTORC1 activation, having been applied to resected brain tissue specimens and experimental models for mTOR pathway hyperactivation in TSC and other mTORopathies. However, phospho-S6 has not proven a consistent clinical biomarker, making it difficult to determine how the extent of mTOR inhibition, rapamycin blood levels, and seizure reduction correlate. In many aging studies, surrogate biomarkers of mTORC1 inhibition are underreported or inconsistently applied, making it hard to confirm outcomes truly reflect effective mTOR inhibition - a key gap in the rapamycin longevity literature.

label: Super-enhancer
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP.md
description: Many SASP-associated genes are linked to super-enhancer-like regions that are particularly sensitive to changes in histone acetylation, and such loci probably require sustained acetyl-CoA availability to maintain high transcriptional output, rendering them especially vulnerable to interventions that limit acetyl-CoA supply. SLC25A1 inhibition reduces chromatin accessibility at these SASP loci both in vitro and in vivo, selectively suppressing inflammatory gene expression. This positions mitochondrial metabolism as an upstream determinant of chromatin accessibility in senescent cells, aligning with previous reports linking citrate metabolism to SASP regulation.

label: H3K27ac
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP.md
description: ChIP-seq analysis of histone H3 acetylation at lysine 27 (H3K27ac) showed that loci gaining acetylation during senescence are markedly reduced following mitochondrial clearance, and these regions are enriched for inflammatory and interleukin signalling pathways central to the SASP. A 51-gene SASP signature induced during senescence is suppressed upon mitochondrial removal, with genes such as IL6 and CCL2 showing coordinated decreases in chromatin acetylation and mRNA expression. Multiple nodes of the mitochondrial citrate-acetyl-CoA axis converge to control H3K27ac at SASP loci, selectively modulating inflammatory gene expression without affecting the senescence-associated cell cycle arrest.

label: SIRT1
description: SIRT1 is the predominant nuclear sirtuin and is enriched at euchromatic regions, where it deacetylates both histones and many transcriptional regulators to shape gene expression. Its nuclear residence allows it to directly access chromatin and nuclear factors such as p53, FOXO, NF-κB, and PGC-1α. Subcellular localization is dynamic and can shift toward DNA double-strand break foci during genotoxic stress, reflecting its role in DNA repair. A caveat is that a fraction of SIRT1 is also cytosolic, so 'nuclear' describes its dominant but not exclusive compartment.

label: SIRT3
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial Drivers Stem Cell Aging Inflammaging Bautista 2026.md
description: SIRT3 is the principal mitochondrial sirtuin, imported into the matrix where it removes acetyl, succinyl, and other acyl modifications from respiratory-chain and metabolic enzymes. Its activity is governed by the mitochondrial NAD+/NADH ratio, which links the cell's energy state directly to enzyme function, so SIRT3 serves as a metabolic sensor within the organelle. Because of its mitochondrial residence, SIRT3 is positioned to sense and tune local metabolism, driving oxidative phosphorylation, antioxidant defense, and fatty-acid oxidation.

label: sjTREC
description: Single joint T cell receptor excision circle (sjTREC) analysis is a molecular marker for active thymopoiesis. Using sjTREC, researchers reported a steady three-log decline in circulating naive T cells across an 80-year human lifespan, and a significant decrease of sjTREC per milligram of mouse thymus tissue with increasing age in BALB/c mice (6-90 weeks), demonstrating gradual decrease in thymopoiesis with age similar to humans. The sjTREC assay was also used to show that ghrelin administration to aged mice increases the number of recent thymic emigrants exported to the periphery. It is thus a quantitative readout of thymic output used across species.

label: Citrate
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP.md
description: SLC25A1, the mitochondrial citrate carrier, exports citrate from the mitochondrial matrix to the cytosol, where it can be converted to acetyl-CoA. SLC25A1 expression is significantly increased at both mRNA and protein levels in multiple senescence contexts, and this citrate export sustains the nucleocytosolic acetyl-CoA pool required for histone acetylation. Genetic ablation of SLC25A1 does not alter CDK inhibitor expression or cell cycle arrest but markedly reduces SASP gene expression, and inhibition with the third-generation inhibitor CTPI2 selectively suppresses SASP-associated inflammation without clearing senescent cells.

label: SOCS3
description: IDO1 is controlled post-translationally: phosphorylation of its ITIM motifs recruits SOCS3, leading to ubiquitination and degradation of IDO1 as a negative feedback mechanism. This degradation pathway limits IDO1 activity and terminates its immunosuppressive effects, representing a key regulatory checkpoint. IDO1 can also mediate non-enzymatic signaling such as PI3K activation. IDO2 may compete for heme and act as a negative regulator in some settings. These regulatory layers are important for therapeutic targeting of IDO1, as they influence the durability and magnitude of tryptophan depletion and kynurenine production in the tumor microenvironment.

label: Solid Dispersion
source_file: _document_ - Fisetin—In Search of Better Bioavailability—From Macro to Nano Modifications A Review.md
description: Solid dispersions of fisetin are prepared by dispersing the drug in a hydrophilic polymer matrix such as polyvinylpyrrolidone or hydroxypropyl methylcellulose, converting crystalline fisetin into an amorphous form that dissolves much faster. The review describes how fisetin solid dispersions markedly increase the dissolution rate and apparent solubility relative to the free drug, leading to improved oral absorption and higher plasma concentrations in pharmacokinetic studies. Because dissolution is the limiting step in fisetin absorption, solid dispersion technology is one of the most straightforward and widely explored macro- to micro-scale strategies for improving its bioavailability.

label: Fisetin Dissolution
source_file: _document_ - Fisetin—In Search of Better Bioavailability—From Macro to Nano Modifications A Review.md
description: Solid dispersions of fisetin are prepared by dispersing the drug in a hydrophilic polymer matrix such as polyvinylpyrrolidone or hydroxypropyl methylcellulose, converting crystalline fisetin into an amorphous form that dissolves much faster. The review describes how fisetin solid dispersions markedly increase the dissolution rate and apparent solubility relative to the free drug, leading to improved oral absorption and higher plasma concentrations in pharmacokinetic studies. Because dissolution is the limiting step in fisetin absorption, solid dispersion technology is one of the most straightforward and widely explored macro- to micro-scale strategies for improving its bioavailability.

label: Sulforaphane
description: Sulforaphane, found abundantly in broccoli sprouts, is highlighted as a potent activator of NRF2 and an upregulator of Phase II detoxification enzymes. NRF2 is one of the key stress-response pathways activated by the acute ROS pulse that defines mitohormesis, alongside AMPK, PGC-1alpha, and SIRT1. Cruciferous vegetables are therefore recommended in the dietary protocol as polyphenol-rich xenohormetins and NRF2 activators that support the hormetic response.

label: Sympathetic Nervous System
description: The sympathetic nervous system is the fight, flight, or freeze branch of the autonomic nervous system. It releases adrenaline and cortisol to prepare the body for action during events such as a HIIT workout, cold plunge, or fasting. When the SNS is active, it forces the heart to beat faster and more rhythmically, thereby lowering HRV. Chronic sympathetic dominance keeps the system stuck in the on position, producing a chronically depressed HRV that signals under-recovery and overtraining rather than adaptation.

label: TAK1
description: TAK1, a key cytoplasmic kinase in modulation of the SASP, is rapidly phosphorylated upon genotoxic stress and functionally participates in the transition of the acute stress-associated phenotype (ASAP) towards the SASP through dual feedforward mechanisms. Phosphorylation and activation of p38 MAPK occurs downstream of TAK1, followed by engagement of the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway that supports the chronic secretory phenotype. Apigenin does not block ATM or TAK1 phosphorylation but abrogates the sequential molecular events downstream, acting through the HSPA8 hub to dampen p38 MAPK and downstream PI3K/Akt/mTOR engagement.

label: TFEB
description: SIRT2 directly binds the 3'UTR of transcription factor EB (TFEB) and enhances its mRNA stability, raising TFEB protein availability. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of stabilized TFEB message. TFEB then drives lysosomal and autophagic gene programs, so SIRT2 promotes autophagy and lysosomal biogenesis through this post-transcriptional mechanism. This reveals an RNA-binding facet of SIRT2's regulation of autophagy, distinct from its enzymatic deacetylation of other substrates. By stabilizing TFEB mRNA, SIRT2 supports cellular clearance of damaged components, linking sirtuin activity to lysosomal quality control.

label: Rag GTPases
description: TFEB binds Rag GTPases as part of the amino acid-sensing machinery at the lysosomal surface, and this interaction is modulated by post-translational modification: oxidation of cysteine 212 inhibits TFEB's binding to Rag GTPases (PMID 31826695). The Rag GTPase complex is central to nutrient sensing, recruiting mTORC1 and its substrate machinery to the lysosome when amino acids are abundant, and TFEB's association with this complex links TFEB localization to nutrient availability. Oxidation at C212, by disrupting this binding, represents a redox-responsive mechanism that influences TFEB's cellular localization and activity, coupling oxidative stress to the regulation of the autophagy-lysosome pathway.

label: ACAT1
description: The acetyltransferase ACAT1 acetylates TFEB at multiple lysine residues with opposing functional outcomes: acetylation at K116 hinders TFEB binding to DNA (PMID 30059277), while acetylation at K91, K103, and K430 promotes nuclear translocation and DNA binding. These site-specific acetylation events modulate TFEB's ability to interact with chromatin and activate transcription of lysosomal and autophagic genes. The K116 acetylation that inhibits DNA binding is reversed by SIRT1 deacetylation, which enhances TFEB transcriptional activity. Together these marks show that acetylation acts as a dynamic post-translational switch controlling TFEB's DNA-binding capacity and thus its gene-regulatory output.

label: GCN5
description: SIRT6 deacetylates the acetyltransferase GCN5, one of its direct non-histone substrates, altering the chromatin acetylation balance at metabolic and growth promoters and complementing SIRT6's histone deacetylation at H3K9/H3K56. In hepatocytes, SIRT6 also engages GCN5 to acetylate and inhibit PGC-1alpha and thereby restrain gluconeogenesis, so the same enzyme-substrate pair can be tuned in different directions depending on cellular context.

label: calcineurin
description: Calcineurin dephosphorylates TFEB at S211 and S142, promoting nuclear translocation of the transcription factor (PMID 26043755). This dephosphorylation reverses the cytoplasmic-retention effect imposed by mTORC1 (S211) and ERK2/mTORC1 (S142) phosphorylation, allowing TFEB to enter the nucleus and activate lysosomal biogenesis and autophagy genes. Calcineurin is a calcium/calmodulin-dependent phosphatase, so this pathway couples calcium signaling to the TFEB-mediated cellular clearance program. It forms the dephosphorylation arm of TFEB regulation alongside PP2A, providing a calcium-sensitive route to activate the autophagy-lysosome pathway under stress conditions.

label: ERK2
description: ERK2 phosphorylates TFEB at serine 142, producing cytoplasmic retention and nuclear export of the transcription factor (PMID 21617040, 29992949). Phosphorylation at this site, shared with mTORC1 and CDK4/CDK6, keeps TFEB out of the nucleus and thereby represses its transcriptional program for lysosomal and autophagic genes. This places TFEB under the control of mitogen/extracellular-signal-regulated kinase (ERK) signaling in addition to nutrient sensing, integrating growth factor cues into the control of lysosome biogenesis and autophagy. Dephosphorylation of S142 by calcineurin reverses this effect and promotes TFEB translocation to the nucleus.

label: GSK3
description: GSK3beta phosphorylates TFEB at serine 138, promoting lysosomal localization and nuclear export (PMID 27617930, 29992949), and at S134 promoting lysosomal localization. Phosphorylation of TFEB by GSK3beta modulates its subcellular distribution, controlling access of the transcription factor to its nuclear targets. The S138 site is particularly notable because it is also subject to O-GlcNAc glucosylation that blocks TFEB nuclear export, illustrating cross-talk between phosphorylation and glycosylation at the same residue. GSK3beta regulation of TFEB links glycogen synthase kinase signaling to the control of lysosomal biogenesis and autophagy.

label: PKC
description: Protein kinase C beta (PKCbeta) phosphorylates TFEB at S466 and the cluster S461/S462 and S468, promoting its stability (PMID 23599343). Phosphorylation at S466 is shared with AMPK, which phosphorylates the same site to enhance transcriptional activity, while PKCbeta-mediated phosphorylation stabilizes the TFEB protein. By stabilizing TFEB, PKCbeta signaling can raise the cellular pool of the transcription factor available for nuclear translocation when other activating signals arrive. This illustrates how post-translational phosphorylation by multiple kinases converges on TFEB to control its abundance, localization, and activity, integrating diverse cellular signaling inputs into the regulation of lysosomal and autophagic gene expression.

label: Cytosol
description: TFEB is retained in the cytosol when it is phosphorylated at cytoplasmic-retention sites. Phosphorylation of S211 by mTORC1 or p38 MAPK, of S142 by mTORC1 or ERK2, of S122 by mTORC1, of S467 by Akt, and of S3 by MAP4K3 all promote cytoplasmic retention of TFEB, keeping the transcription factor away from its nuclear target genes. This phosphorylation-dependent cytosolic sequestration is the primary mechanism by which nutrient-rich and growth-factor-rich conditions suppress the lysosomal and autophagic transcriptional program. Dephosphorylation of these sites by calcineurin or PP2A relieves the retention and permits TFEB to translocate to the nucleus.

label: STUB1
description: The E3 ubiquitin ligase STUB1 ubiquitinates TFEB, and this ubiquitination enhances TFEB activity (PMID 28754656). Rather than simply marking TFEB for degradation, ubiquitination by STUB1 in this case increases the transcription factor's functional output, consistent with the growing appreciation that ubiquitination can serve non-proteolytic regulatory functions. This adds TFEB to the set of proteins whose activity is tuned by ubiquitin conjugation. The finding illustrates the diversity of post-translational modifications - including ubiquitination, PARsylation, and SUMOylation in addition to phosphorylation and acetylation - that regulate TFEB's localization, stability, and transcriptional activity in the control of lysosomal biogenesis and autophagy.

label: Toluidine Blue O
source_file: _document_ - Neuroprotective Actions of Methylene Blue and Its Derivatives.md
description: Toluidine blue O (TB), the 3,7-dimethyl analog of methylene blue, is the most potent of the tested phenothiazine derivatives, with EC50s of 1.75 nM for viability, 0.11 nM for ROS reduction, and 1.54 nM for preserving mitochondrial membrane potential in the HT-22 glutamate assay. Like MB, TB significantly increased the rate of cytochrome c reduction in the complex I-III assay with NADH as electron donor, enhanced cellular oxygen consumption, and decreased lactate production, sharing MB's alternative electron-transfer-carrier function but with greater potency.

label: UCP3
description: Uncoupling protein 3 (UCP3) is expressed primarily in skeletal muscle and is a candidate mediator of the proton leak that contributes to resting metabolic rate and exercise-related energy expenditure. Speakman cites evidence that UCP3 mRNA is elevated after exercise and that its expression, together with UCP2, may account for a fraction of the exercise-induced rise in metabolic rate. The functional importance of UCP3 in mediating proton leak remains debated, because knockout studies in mice do not show gross changes in resting metabolic rate, but its induction by training and by lipids keeps it a focus for understanding inter-individual differences in energy expenditure.

label: Urolithin A
source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial Drivers Stem Cell Aging Inflammaging Bautista 2026.md
description: Urolithin A is a potent inducer of mitophagy, the clean-up process that recycles old, damaged mitochondria so new ones can take their place, and is described as a core mitohormetic mechanism. It is recommended to be taken with the first fat-containing meal of the day, as co-ingesting with healthy fats such as eggs, avocado, or yogurt can enhance its absorption. By supporting mitochondrial recycling, Urolithin A complements the energy production and renewal pathways targeted by the overall mitohormesis protocol.

label: Valine
description: Valine metabolism involves conversion to succinyl-CoA, which enters the TCA cycle to produce ATP, making valine a gluconeogenic and anaplerotic amino acid. Restricting valine alone reduces body weight, improves metabolic health, reduces hepatic senescence, and extends lifespan of male mice, while in female mice valine restriction is protective in Alzheimer's disease progression. Dysregulated valine catabolism (via 3-hydroxyisobutyrate) contributes to insulin resistance in diabetic rats. Human plasma analysis found reduced circulating valine is associated with aging and moderate cognitive impairment, but valine supplementation worsens glucose tolerance and induces gut inflammation and hepatic lipid deposition, suggesting the role of valine in healthy aging may vary between species.

label: TCA cycle
description: Valine metabolism involves conversion to succinyl-CoA, which enters the TCA cycle to produce ATP, making valine a gluconeogenic and anaplerotic amino acid. Restricting valine alone reduces body weight, improves metabolic health, reduces hepatic senescence, and extends lifespan of male mice, while in female mice valine restriction is protective in Alzheimer's disease progression. Dysregulated valine catabolism (via 3-hydroxyisobutyrate) contributes to insulin resistance in diabetic rats. Human plasma analysis found reduced circulating valine is associated with aging and moderate cognitive impairment, but valine supplementation worsens glucose tolerance and induces gut inflammation and hepatic lipid deposition, suggesting the role of valine in healthy aging may vary between species.

label: Vitamin C
description: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) exhibits reducing properties similar to methylene blue and can serve as an alternative treatment for methemoglobinemia, though with significant limitations. Ascorbic acid reduces methemoglobin through a slower, nonenzymatic pathway that often requires multiple doses over several hours to achieve a significant effect. Although case reports demonstrate successful treatment with high-dose vitamin C, it is unlikely to be effective in a resuscitation situation. Vitamin C is most appropriate when methylene blue is contraindicated, such as in patients with G6PD deficiency, or when methylene blue is unavailable.

label: Xenohormesis
description: Xenohormesis is the hypothesis that naturally occurring plant compounds - often synthesized when plants are under environmental stress such as drought - act as cross-species signaling molecules that induce a hormetic response when consumed by animals. These compounds are proposed to prepare the recipient organism for presumed worsening environmental conditions (famine for the animal, drought for the plant). This concept extends the hormesis framework to dietary phytochemicals and may help explain the medicinal value of certain plant-derived molecules.

label: Zone 2 Cardio
description: Zone 2 cardio performed 3 to 4 times per week for 45-60 minutes builds the aerobic base, increases mitochondrial volume, and improves fat oxidation efficiency, and is the recommended low-intensity alternative when HRV is significantly below baseline and heavy stressors must be skipped. It is positioned as the aerobic foundation of the training protocol, complementing HIIT and sprint interval training done 1-2 times per week that generate the acute ROS spike and lactate accumulation to trigger PGC-1alpha, the master regulator of mitochondrial biogenesis.

label: HMGB1
description: HMGB1 is a chromatin protein released as a damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) from dying or stressed cells.

label: Damage-associated molecular pattern
description: HMGB1 is a chromatin protein released as a damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) from dying or stressed cells.

label: TLR4
description: Extracellular disulfide-HMGB1 signals through TLR4 on antigen-presenting cells to drive inflammatory and antitumor immune responses.

label: RAGE
description: HMGB1 engages the receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE/AGER), promoting inflammation, migration and metastasis.

label: Ivermectin
description: Avermectin B1a is the natural macrocyclic-lactone precursor of ivermectin (22,23-dihydroavermectin B1a), the semi-synthetic lead derivative developed for human and veterinary medicine.

label: Immunogenic cell death
description: HMGB1 release is a hallmark DAMP of immunogenic cell death, necessary for anticancer immune priming.

label: Metastasis
description: EMT enables Metastasis. Epithelial-mesenchymal transition is a developmental program co-opted by carcinomas to lose polarity, gain motility, and acquire stem-like properties for invasion. Metastasis is the multistep dissemination of tumor cells to distant organs and the principal cause of cancer mortality. The relationship is directional, with EMT acting as the operative agent upon Metastasis rather than the reverse. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: HSP27
description: HSP27 (HSPB1) is a small heat-shock protein that buffers stress and inhibits apoptosis, contributing to chemoresistance.

label: Multidrug Resistance
description: Cancer overcomes Multidrug Resistance. Cancer is a family of diseases driven by the stepwise acquisition of mutations and epimutations that confer proliferative autonomy, survival, and dissemination. Multidrug resistance is the cross-resistance of tumors to structurally unrelated drugs, most classically mediated by ATP-dependent efflux pumps. The relationship is directional, with Cancer acting as the operative agent upon Multidrug Resistance rather than the reverse. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: Renal Cell Carcinoma
description: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is the most common malignant kidney tumor, usually clear-cell subtype.

label: Antiangiogenic therapy
description: RCC is treated with VEGF-pathway inhibitors (e.g., sunitinib) and mTOR inhibitors; chemotherapy is largely ineffective.

label: Fenbendazole
description: Fenbendazole binds the colchicine site of beta-tubulin, preventing polymerization and destabilizing microtubules (Dogra & Mukhopadhyay, Sci Rep 2018).

label: Mebendazole
description: Mebendazole is a benzimidazole anthelmintic in the same class as fenbendazole and albendazole.

label: Tubulin
description: SIRT2 is the first identified tubulin deacetylase, with α-tubulin as its most characterized substrate; deacetylation regulates microtubule stability and dynamics. Directionally, SIRT2 enzymatically tunes α-tubulin acetylation. Reduced α-tubulin acetylation is linked to neurodegeneration, explaining why SIRT2 inhibitors protect neurons, and it is the mechanistic basis for SIRT2's mitotic and axonal roles. By deacetylating tubulin, SIRT2 influences microtubule dynamics during cell division and in axons, where acetylation stabilizes microtubules. This substrate specificity distinguishes SIRT2 from other sirtuins and underpins its distinct pharmacology.

label: Microtubule
description: alpha/beta-tubulin heterodimers polymerize into microtubules, the dynamic polymers of the mitotic spindle and cytoskeleton.

label: SIRT2
description: SIRT2 is the predominantly cytoplasmic sirtuin and is most abundant in the cytosol, where it deacetylates α-tubulin and a range of metabolic and regulatory proteins. Its localization is cell-cycle regulated, with SIRT2 accumulating and being hyperphosphorylated as cells transit the G2/M boundary. The cytoplasmic residence underpins its roles in microtubule dynamics, mitosis, and cytoplasmic autophagy regulation rather than direct chromatin modification. Note that SIRT2 can also shuttle to the nucleus under certain stress conditions, so localization is not absolute.

label: Paclitaxel
description: Paclitaxel stabilizes microtubules by binding polymerized tubulin, arresting mitosis (contrast to benzimidazole destabilizers).

label: Microtubule inhibitors
description: Tubulin is the target of microtubule-interfering agents including benzimidazoles, taxanes and vinca alkaloids.

label: Enzalutamide
description: Enzalutamide (Xtandi) is a second-generation androgen receptor (AR) antagonist that blocks AR nuclear translocation.

label: Prostate Cancer
description: Enzalutamide is approved for castration-resistant prostate cancer.

label: Docetaxel
description: Cancer is treated by docetaxel. Cancer is a family of diseases driven by the stepwise acquisition of mutations and epimutations that confer proliferative autonomy, survival, and dissemination. Docetaxel is a taxane that stabilizes microtubules, arresting mitosis and inducing cell death in a range of carcinomas. The directionality runs from docetaxel toward Cancer, so docetaxel is the active agent and Cancer the recipient of the effect. Clinically, this positions the object as a therapeutic modality against the subject, though efficacy is shaped by biomarker selection and the eventual emergence of resistance.

label: Anti-androgen
description: Enzalutamide is a nonsteroidal anti-androgen used in endocrine therapy of prostate cancer.

label: Glioblastoma
description: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most malignant primary brain tumor in adults (grade IV astrocytoma).

label: Cancer Stem Cells
description: Cancer Stem Cells drive Chemotherapy Resistance. Cancer stem cells are self-renewing subpopulations that seed tumors, resist therapy, and are enriched by EMT and inflammatory signaling. Chemotherapy resistance denotes the failure of cytotoxic drugs to kill tumor cells, arising through efflux, death-pathway suppression, and stem-cell states. The relationship is directional, with Cancer Stem Cells acting as the operative agent upon Chemotherapy Resistance rather than the reverse. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: Temozolomide
description: MGMT expression confers temozolomide resistance in a subset of GBM.

label: Adrenochrome
description: Adrenochrome semiquinone radical generates ROS through redox cycling. The autoxidation/redox cycling pathway produces superoxide, amplifying oxidative stress.

label: Indoles
description: Adrenochrome is a cyclic amino ketone pigment classified as a member of indoles. It bears the core indoline-5,6-dione scaffold, a fused bicyclic ring system derived from the cyclized catecholamine backbone. This indole classification reflects adrenochrome's origin as an oxidation product of the catecholamine epinephrine, whose benzene ring and amine side chain fold into a five-membered nitrogen-containing ring during intramolecular cyclization. As an indole quinone, adrenochrome sits at the intersection of catecholamine and pigment biochemistry, connecting the chemistry of adrenaline to downstream reactive electrophiles. Its indole structure underlies both its characteristic pink color and its tendency to undergo further reactions, including polymerization into melanins. This classification is central to understanding adrenochrome's behavior as an electron-deficient quinone that forms adducts with cellular nucleophiles.

label: Epinephrine
description: COMT is the primary clearance route for epinephrine (~60-70% via O-methylation). Competition with the oxidative cyclization pathway determines adrenochrome formation.

label: C9H9NO3
description: Adrenochrome has the molecular formula C9H9NO3, corresponding to nine carbon atoms, nine hydrogen atoms, one nitrogen atom, and three oxygen atoms, with a computed molecular weight of 179.17 g/mol and a monoisotopic mass of 179.0582 Da. The three oxygen atoms reflect the two carbonyl groups of the quinone ring (the 5,6-dione) and a single hydroxyl group at the 3-position of the indoline ring. The single nitrogen atom is the methylated amine that becomes part of the five-membered ring after epinephrine cyclizes. With one hydrogen bond donor and four hydrogen bond acceptors and no rotatable bonds, the formula describes a rigid, compact, oxygen-rich heterocycle whose composition is consistent across PubChem identifiers CID 5898, ChEMBL1314174, and CHEBI:166544. These structural parameters explain adrenochrome's high polarity and reactivity as an electrophilic quinone.

label: 179.17 g/mol
description: Adrenochrome has a molecular weight of 179.17 g/mol, computed by PubChem for the formula C9H9NO3. This relatively low molecular mass places adrenochrome among small bioactive molecules that can diffuse through tissues and interact with intracellular targets. The mass is consistent with the monoisotopic value of 179.0582 Da and reflects the compact indoline-5,6-dione scaffold assembled from the oxidation and cyclization of epinephrine. As a small, polar electrophile, adrenochrome's mass underlies its ability to cross cell membranes, reach nuclear DNA, and form covalent adducts with proteins, contributing to its documented toxicity. Knowledge of its molecular weight is also essential for analytical detection by HPLC and mass spectrometry, methods that have been used to search for adrenochrome in biological fluids.

label: 3-hydroxy-1-methyl-2,3-dihydroindole-5,6-dione
description: The IUPAC name of adrenochrome is 3-hydroxy-1-methyl-2,3-dihydroindole-5,6-dione, which encodes the complete structure of the molecule: an indole (indoline) bicyclic core, a hydroxyl group at the 3-position, an N-methyl group on the ring nitrogen, and two ketone carbonyls at the 5- and 6-positions of the benzo ring. The 5,6-dione motif makes adrenochrome a quinone, while the 3-hydroxyl and N-methyl groups are the vestiges of the epinephrine side chain after oxidative cyclization. Alternative names such as indoline-5,6-dione refer to the same compound. The name captures the duality of adrenochrome: a rigid indole ring system that is simultaneously an electron-deficient quinone, explaining both its stability within the indole class and its electrophilic reactivity toward biological nucleophiles.

Adrenochrome has a computed XLogP3-AA partition coefficient of -1.3, indicating that the molecule is substantially more hydrophilic than lipophilic. The negative logP value arises from the polar indoline-5,6-dione core with its two carbonyl oxygens, one hydroxyl group, and four hydrogen bond acceptors, giving adrenochrome limited ability to partition into lipid membranes. This water solubility is consistent with its behavior as a blood- and tissue-dissolved oxidation product of the hydrophilic catecholamine epinephrine rather than a membrane-accumulating species. The polarity also shapes its toxicology: adrenochrome remains in aqueous compartments such as serum and cytosol where it can encounter proteins, DNA, and small-molecule nucleophiles. The low partition coefficient is relevant to questions about whether and where the compound can form and persist in biological fluids.

label: Acute oral toxicity
description: Adrenochrome is classified under the Globally Harmonized System (GHS) with hazard statement H302, meaning it is harmful if swallowed, with acute oral toxicity category 4 (Acute Tox. 4, 100% of notifications). The signal word is Warning with an irritant pictogram. This regulatory classification reflects experimental evidence that ingestion of adrenochrome can produce adverse effects, complementing mechanistic studies showing that adrenochrome, as an electrophilic quinone, readily forms covalent adducts with proteins and DNA and is cardiotoxic, capable of causing cell necrosis, arrhythmias, and coronary artery constriction. The GHS designation provides a formal toxicological endpoint that supports the view of adrenochrome as a biologically reactive molecule rather than an inert pigment, though its clinical significance in human disease remains debated.

label: Pigment
description: Adrenochrome is a pigment obtained by the oxidation of epinephrine, exhibiting a characteristic pink-to-red color in aqueous solution that has been recognized since its first description in 1856. The pink color results from the conjugated indoline-5,6-dione chromophore that forms when the catecholamine ring is oxidized and cyclized. As a pigment, adrenochrome is an intermediate in the melanin pathway, because its further polymerization produces dark brown and black melanin pigments; the visible reddening of adrenaline solutions left exposed to air is the classic demonstration of this chemistry. Beyond its color, the pigment identity connects adrenochrome to histochemical and forensic contexts, where oxidation products of catecholamines are used as stains, and to pathology, where it represents an oxidative transformation of adrenaline linked to cellular damage.

label: o-quinone
description: Epinephrine is a catecholamine built from a benzene ring carrying two hydroxyl groups (a catechol) plus an amine side chain. Under oxidative stress, or simply in the presence of oxygen in a test tube, the two hydroxyl groups lose hydrogen atoms or electrons, transforming the stable catechol ring into a highly reactive o-quinone. This oxidation is the trigger of the entire adrenochrome pathway: the o-quinone intermediate is electron-poor and unstable, and it immediately seeks stabilization by cyclization. Because no enzyme is needed for the oxidation step, epinephrine can autoxidize spontaneously in vitro, and in vivo the reaction becomes significant only when antioxidant defenses are overwhelmed. The catechol-to-quinone conversion is the same chemistry that underpins the oxidation of dopamine and other catecholamines.

label: MAO
description: Monoamine oxidase (MAO) is an intracellular mitochondrial enzyme that oxidatively deaminates monoamines including epinephrine, producing aldehydes and hydrogen peroxide. Along with COMT-mediated methylation, MAO-mediated oxidative deamination is one of the two dominant routes for terminating adrenaline signaling. Because these enzymes clear adrenaline rapidly, the direct oxidation of epinephrine to adrenochrome remains a minor side pathway under normal conditions. Blocking MAO, especially together with COMT inhibition, elevates catecholamine levels and gives excess epinephrine more opportunity to undergo autoxidation or radical-mediated conversion to adrenochrome.

label: COMT
description: Fisetin is a mixed-type COMT inhibitor with IC50 2.6-5.8 µM. It is also a COMT substrate — itself O-methylated to geraldol — making inhibition concentration-dependent and genotype-sensitive.

label: Ascorbic Acid
description: Ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is a reducing agent that acts as an electron donor to prevent catecholamine oxidation. If a molecule of epinephrine starts to oxidize into a quinone, ascorbic acid immediately donates an electron, converting the o-quinone intermediate back into stable epinephrine and thereby preventing the intramolecular cyclization that would produce adrenochrome. This is why ascorbic acid can block or delay the reddening of adrenaline solutions exposed to air. Alongside glutathione and sodium metabisulfite, ascorbic acid is a classic example of a sacrificial antioxidant that intercepts the quinone intermediate at the earliest step of the adrenochrome pathway. The reversibility of the catechol-quinone redox couple is what makes electron-donating agents so effective at suppressing this oxidative transformation.

label: Sodium Metabisulfite
description: Sodium metabisulfite is a reducing agent commonly added to pharmaceutical epinephrine solutions as a sacrificial antioxidant. Because epinephrine slowly oxidizes in the presence of air, the sulfite compound donates electrons to any quinone intermediate that forms, converting it back to stable epinephrine and preventing the pink-red adrenochrome discoloration that indicates oxidation. This is why many injectable epinephrine formulations used in emergency devices such as autoinjectors contain sodium metabisulfite: it extends the shelf life of the catecholamine by intercepting the very first oxidation step of the adrenochrome pathway. The practice illustrates how chemical formulation, not just biology, exploits the catechol-quinone redox equilibrium to suppress adrenochrome formation and preserve drug potency.

label: Transition Metals
description: Transition metals such as iron and copper catalyze the oxidation of epinephrine by accelerating electron transfer to oxygen. In the presence of these metals, the catechol hydroxyls of epinephrine lose electrons more readily, generating the reactive o-quinone that proceeds to cyclize into adrenochrome. This metal-dependent acceleration is why pharmaceutical epinephrine solutions and laboratory preparations are vulnerable to autoxidation unless protected. The catalytic role of transition metals explains the utility of chelating agents such as EDTA, which bind the metals and render them inert, drastically slowing epinephrine autoxidation and therefore adrenochrome formation. Metal-catalyzed oxidation is likewise a recognized mechanism by which oxidative stress in tissues, where iron and copper can be released from proteins, promotes catecholamine oxidation in vivo.

label: EDTA
description: EDTA (ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid) is a chelating agent that binds transition metal ions such as iron and copper, making them inert and drastically slowing the autoxidation of epinephrine. Because these metals catalyze electron transfer from the catechol ring to oxygen, their removal suppresses the formation of the o-quinone intermediate that leads to adrenochrome. The strategy of metal chelation is therefore a key chemical defense against the oxidative conversion of adrenaline into its reactive oxidation product. EDTA exemplifies the broader class of chelating agents used to stabilize catecholamines in pharmaceutical and analytical settings, and it highlights the general principle that transition metal availability controls the rate at which the adrenochrome pathway can proceed in solution.

label: UV Light
description: Ultraviolet light generates reactive oxygen species (ROS) that drive the oxidation of catecholamines such as epinephrine. Because ROS can steal electrons from the catechol hydroxyls, producing the o-quinone intermediate, light exposure accelerates the pathway that converts adrenaline into adrenochrome. This photochemical sensitivity is why pharmaceutical epinephrine is stored in amber vials away from light: preventing light-induced ROS formation slows the oxidation and cyclization reactions that degrade the drug. The same principle applies more broadly to catecholamine biochemistry, where photo-oxidation can convert adrenaline solutions pink. Temperature and light, as factors governing kinetic energy and radical generation, are therefore environmental controls that determine whether epinephrine remains stable or proceeds toward adrenochrome and its toxic downstream chemistry.

label: Melanins
description: Adrenochrome is inherently very unstable and, as a highly reactive electrophile, rapidly undergoes further reactions once formed. Chief among these is polymerization: adrenochrome molecules condense together to produce melanins, the black and brown pigments responsible for the darkening of oxidized adrenaline solutions and related to the pigment chemistry of skin and hair. This polymerization is part of why adrenochrome has only a fleeting existence in aqueous solution, with a half-life ranging from minutes to hours depending on temperature, pH, and the presence of nucleophiles. The melanin-forming instability also means that adrenochrome sits on the oxidative pathway connecting catecholamines to the pigment melanin, linking adrenaline oxidation to pigmentation biochemistry and to the tissue discoloration seen in oxidized catecholamine environments.

label: Minutes to hours
description: Adrenochrome is a very unstable molecule in aqueous solution, with a half-life ranging from minutes to hours depending on temperature, pH, and the presence of nucleophiles. The instability arises because adrenochrome is a highly reactive electrophilic quinone that rapidly undergoes further reactions, principally polymerization into melanins and covalent adduct formation with proteins and DNA. This transience is a central reason why adrenochrome has proven difficult to detect in biological fluids despite decades of interest in its possible role in disease: it does not persist long enough to accumulate. The short half-life also frames the clinical controversy around the compound, since any effect it exerts must occur quickly after formation, and its fleeting nature makes measurement of the relevant intermediate states technically challenging.

label: Electrophile
description: Adrenochrome is a highly reactive electrophile, an electron-poor species that seeks electrons from other molecules. As a quinone, its electron-deficient carbonyl system readily bonds with nucleophilic sites on proteins, DNA, and other cellular structures, forming covalent adducts, and this reactivity is why the molecule is considered toxic to cells. The electrophilic character also drives adrenochrome's self-reactivity: it rapidly polymerizes into melanin pigments rather than persisting in solution. This electron-poor nature is the mechanistic basis for adrenochrome's reported cardiotoxic effects, including cell necrosis, arrhythmias, and coronary artery constriction, because covalent modification of cellular macromolecules disrupts their function. Electrophilicity therefore unifies adrenochrome's instability, its adduct-forming toxicity, and its position as the central reactive intermediate of the adrenaline oxidation pathway.

label: DNA
description: 8-oxo-2'-deoxyguanosine is the most abundant oxidative lesion in DNA, with roughly 10^3 to 10^6 lesions per cell per day arising from normal metabolism and extrinsic insults. Its prevalence reflects both high formation rate and efficient but imperfect repair. The directionality is oxidation of guanine to the dominant adduct. A caveat is that the steady-state level integrates formation and repair, so it is an indirect rather than instantaneous measure of ROS flux. The steady-state 8-oxodG level is influenced by both the rate of oxidation and the efficiency of OGG1-mediated repair, so it reflects the balance between insult and defense.

label: Superoxide Dismutase
description: Superoxide dismutase (SOD) catalyzes the dismutation of two superoxide radicals into hydrogen peroxide and oxygen, accelerating a reaction that is already spontaneous to near diffusion-limited rates. Three isoforms partition the task: Cu/Zn-SOD in cytosol and extracellular space, Mn-SOD in mitochondria, and extracellular SOD in the interstitium. The directionality is detoxification of a precursor radical into a more diffusible but less reactive species. A caveat is that the H2O2 product still requires removal by catalase or glutathione peroxidase, so SOD activity shifts rather than eliminates oxidative burden.

label: Superoxide anion
description: The adrenochrome semiquinone radical is a highly reactive one-electron reduction product of adrenochrome. It rapidly donates its unpaired electron to molecular oxygen, generating superoxide anion and regenerating adrenochrome; the reaction proceeds at approximately 9 x 10^8 M-1 s-1 in some studies.
