label: TNFα
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: SIRT6 promotes secretion of the pro-inflammatory cytokine TNF-alpha via deacylation of a target, distinct from its anti-inflammatory chromatin roles; this illustrates that SIRT6 can both stimulate and suppress inflammatory outputs depending on substrate and context. Directionally, SIRT6 promotes TNF-alpha secretion through a specific substrate. This context-dependence is a defining feature of SIRT6 biology, and it cautions against simple interpretations of SIRT6 as purely anti-inflammatory. By understanding when SIRT6 promotes versus suppresses inflammation, researchers can better predict the effects of SIRT6-targeted therapies.

label: Superoxide
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: NADPH oxidase is a complex of enzymes activated downstream of AGE-RAGE interaction that produces superoxide, an important reactive oxygen species. When this complex is upregulated, it increases intracellular oxidative stress, and the resulting oxidant burst can activate NF-kB, further amplifying inflammatory gene expression. NADPH oxidase therefore serves as a molecular bridge between receptor-mediated AGE signaling and oxidative damage. This NADPH oxidase-derived superoxide production is a key reason advanced glycation end products behave as pro-oxidant agents, contributing to the oxidative stress component of diabetic complications and aging.

label: Vascular Dementia
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Accumulation of advanced glycation end products in aging persons is associated not only with diabetes complications but also with chronic diseases including vascular dementia. Bar and colleagues demonstrated differential increases of AGE products in Alzheimer's dementia and vascular dementia compared with controls. Because vascular dementia is driven by cerebrovascular dysfunction and impaired perfusion, the ability of AGEs to stiffen vessels, drive endothelial dysfunction, and promote inflammation offers a plausible mechanistic link. These findings place glycation among the modifiable biochemical processes associated with cognitive decline in the elderly.

label: Low-Density Lipoprotein
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Advanced glycation end products damage the cardiovascular system in part by glycating low-density lipoproteins (LDL) on both the apolipoprotein B and phospholipid components of the particle. Glycated LDL is more susceptible to crosslinking with collagen on the arterial wall than non-glycated LDL, and it is not taken up into cells through the normal receptor pathway, so it accumulates in the vessel wall. Macrophage uptake of these modified LDL particles leads to foam cell formation and the development of atheroma. This glycoxidative modification of LDL is thus a direct route through which AGEs promote atherosclerosis.

label: Foam Cells
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Glycated low-density lipoprotein is taken up by macrophages in the arterial wall, and this uptake of modified LDL leads to foam cell formation. Because glycation reduces LDL uptake by the normal cell receptor pathway, modified LDL accumulates, and its subsequent engulfment by macrophages produces lipid-laden foam cells, the hallmark cells of atherosclerotic plaques. The formation of foam cells from modified LDL represents an initiating step of atheroma development and explains why AGE-mediated modification of LDL is considered pro-atherogenic. This pathway links glycation chemistry directly to the cellular pathology of atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease.

label: eNOS
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Resveratrol-activated endothelial SIRT1 increases eNOS expression and deacetylates and activates it, enhancing nitric-oxide production and promoting vasodilation. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of eNOS activation in the endothelium. Improved NO bioavailability lowers vascular tone, protects against endothelial dysfunction, and reduces platelet aggregation and smooth-muscle proliferation. This underlies resveratrol's cardiovascular and French-paradox associations, and SIRT1's regulation of eNOS is one of its best-established vascular mechanisms, linking sirtuin activity directly to blood-vessel health and blood-pressure control.

label: CML
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: CML (N-epsilon-carboxymethyl-lysine) has been reported as one of the most abundant advanced glycation end products in vivo and was one of the first AGEs to be characterized in foods, particularly milk and milk products. Because of its abundance and relative ease of measurement, CML is chosen in most studies as a marker of AGEs in both foods and in vivo. It is a glycoxidation product of lysine residues and accumulates in long-lived proteins. CML is the basis of a food database of approximately 500 items and is widely used as a biomarker linking dietary and circulating AGE burden to health outcomes.

label: Hyperglycemia
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Chronic hyperglycemia suppresses SIRT3 expression in the hippocampus, contributing to cognitive deficits through mitochondrial Ca2+ overload and neuronal apoptosis. SIRT3 is also consistently downregulated in clinical diabetic tissues, where its deficiency correlates with insulin resistance, and in skeletal muscle its deficiency impairs insulin-stimulated glucose translocation, aggravating peripheral insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes.

label: Hemoglobin A1c
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Hemoglobin A1c is the most widely recognized early glycation product, an Amadori product formed when glucose attaches non-enzymatically to the amino terminus of hemoglobin in red blood cells. It is used clinically as an indicator of blood glucose management in people with diabetes because its level reflects average glycemia over the preceding weeks. As an Amadori product, hemoglobin A1c is a reversible early intermediate on the pathway to irreversible advanced glycation end products. Its clinical utility demonstrates that even early, reversible glycation products are valuable biomarkers of glycation burden.

label: Chronic Kidney Disease
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: SIRT6 is markedly downregulated in chronic kidney disease and vascular calcification patients, and it suppresses osteogenic transdifferentiation of vascular smooth muscle cells via runt-related transcription factor 2. MSC exosomes inhibit high-phosphate aortic calcification through SIRT6-HMGB1 deacetylation, and proximal tubule-specific SIRT6 knockout aggravates UUO fibrosis. SIRT6 thereby protects the kidney and vasculature in CKD.

label: Cigarette Smoke
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Exposure to cigarette-smoke extract disrupts the SIRT1–RelA/p65 complex, diminishing deacetylation of RelA and leaving NF-κB in a more active, pro-inflammatory state. The consequence is heightened expression of inflammatory mediators in airway and other cells exposed to smoke. The directionality is that the environmental insult (smoke) reduces a protective protein–protein interaction, increasing inflammation. This provides a mechanistic link between smoking, impaired sirtuin function, and chronic inflammatory lung disease.

label: Glycotoxins
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Cigarette smoking is an exogenous source of glycation compounds. The curing of tobacco leaves has been proposed as the source of compounds that can readily increase in vivo AGEs; Cerami and colleagues found that glycotoxins from cigarettes are inhaled into the alveoli, then transported to the bloodstream or to lung cells where they interact with other glycation products and contribute to AGE formation. Smoking thus adds to the body's AGE burden beyond diet and endogenous production. This exogenous route of AGE generation helps explain the accelerated tissue aging and cardiovascular risk observed in smokers.

label: Dietary AGEs
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: It was estimated using an AGE-specific enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay that approximately 10% of ingested immunoreactive advanced glycation end products are transported into the circulation, two-thirds of which remain in the body and are incorporated covalently into tissues, while only one-third is excreted via the kidneys. Dietary intake is therefore an important contributor to the body's AGE pool, and studies in healthy subjects, diabetic patients, and renal failure patients have found significant correlations between ingested AGEs and plasma AGE levels. Restricting dietary AGEs reduces circulating AGE concentrations, supporting the view that diet modulates systemic glycation burden.

label: Circulation
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: It was estimated using an AGE-specific enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay that approximately 10% of ingested immunoreactive advanced glycation end products are transported into the circulation, two-thirds of which remain in the body and are incorporated covalently into tissues, while only one-third is excreted via the kidneys. Dietary intake is therefore an important contributor to the body's AGE pool, and studies in healthy subjects, diabetic patients, and renal failure patients have found significant correlations between ingested AGEs and plasma AGE levels. Restricting dietary AGEs reduces circulating AGE concentrations, supporting the view that diet modulates systemic glycation burden.

label: Melanoidins
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Melanoidins are the final Maillard reaction products formed in food science, found in bread crust, bakery products, and coffee. Ames and colleagues found that melanoidins increased the number of anaerobes, clostridia, and bifidobacteria in cultures of human fecal bacteria, and Borrelli and colleagues found that bread crust melanoidins can promote growth of some bifidobacterial strains, indicating a possible prebiotic effect. These findings show that not all Maillard products are detrimental, and that some dietary glycation products may support gut bacteria considered health-beneficial, in contrast to the pro-inflammatory effects of other AGEs.

label: Bifidobacterium
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) can selectively stimulate the growth of beneficial gut bacteria such as Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus. These genera are associated with improved gut health, including prevention of diarrhea, improved gut barrier function, reduced inflammation, and immune system support. NAD+ precursors modulate gut microbiota by providing an energy source for beneficial bacteria, activating sirtuins, and improving gut barrier function. NMN and NR thereby reverse gut dysbiosis and promote beneficial effects at both intestinal and extraintestinal levels, linking dietary NAD+ precursor intake to a healthier gut microbial community.

label: Plasma AGEs
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Uribarri and colleagues estimated dietary AGE intake from three-day food records in 90 healthy subjects using a database of the AGE content of foods and found a significant correlation between ingested AGEs and plasma levels; a subgroup exposed to dietary restriction of AGEs showed decreased plasma levels as well. Similar results were reported in patients with diabetes and renal failure. These findings support the view that the intake of dietary AGEs is an important contributor to the body's AGE pool, and that reducing dietary AGE intake lowers circulating AGE concentrations even in healthy individuals.

label: Pyrraline
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Pyrraline is an advanced glycation end product that is absorbed by the peptide transporter hPEPT1, according to the first study addressing the absorption mechanism of individual AGEs. In a bioavailability study, pretzel sticks were found to be a rich source of pyrraline and pentosidine; after ingestion of these foods, urinary excretion of pyrraline and pentosidine increased, with recovery in urine of about 50% for pyrraline and 60% for pentosidine. Although the metabolic fate of these compounds is unknown, their absorption via peptide transporters such as hPEPT1 explains how dietary AGEs enter the circulation.

label: hPEPT1
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Pyrraline is an advanced glycation end product that is absorbed by the peptide transporter hPEPT1, according to the first study addressing the absorption mechanism of individual AGEs. In a bioavailability study, pretzel sticks were found to be a rich source of pyrraline and pentosidine; after ingestion of these foods, urinary excretion of pyrraline and pentosidine increased, with recovery in urine of about 50% for pyrraline and 60% for pentosidine. Although the metabolic fate of these compounds is unknown, their absorption via peptide transporters such as hPEPT1 explains how dietary AGEs enter the circulation.

label: AGER1
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Several enzymes, including glyoxalase I, glyoxalase II, and carbonyl reductase, together with the receptor AGER1, have been shown to be part of a detoxification and counterregulation system against the prooxidant effects of glycation. AGER1 helps oppose the pro-inflammatory actions of advanced glycation end products, functioning as an endogenous check on AGE-mediated signaling. With aging and in some pathological conditions, there is an imbalance in this steady state, due to increased endogenous production or increased exogenous intake combined with lower renal AGE clearance, leading to the AGE accumulation observed in older populations.

label: Glomerular Filtration Rate
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Vlassara and colleagues studied 325 healthy participants and 66 participants with kidney disease and found that serum CML and methylglyoxal were higher in the older participants, and that serum CML correlated negatively with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and positively with age. Because declining kidney function reduces AGE clearance, the inverse relationship between CML and eGFR indicates that the kidney is central to regulating circulating AGE levels. This correlation supports the view that age-related decline in renal function contributes to the progressive accumulation of advanced glycation end products in the elderly.

label: Dietary AGE Restriction
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Intervention studies in mice show that reduced dietary AGEs attenuate insulin resistance, increase prevention of diabetes, and, in diabetic mice, reduce diabetic vascular and renal complications and improve impaired wound healing. The positive outcomes of caloric restriction in mice may be explained in part by a decrease in AGE intake and a concomitant decrease in oxidative stress. These findings indicate that the glycation load of the diet is not merely a bystander but can modulate insulin sensitivity and metabolic health, reinforcing the idea that dietary AGE restriction is a viable intervention against metabolic dysfunction.

label: Wound Healing
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Dietary advanced glycation end products are exogenous glycotoxins absorbed from food that trigger organ dysfunction and tissue aging. In genetically diabetic mice, adverse effects of dietary glycotoxins on wound healing have been demonstrated, and dietary AGEs also accelerate endothelial dysfunction and arterial aging with prolonged exposure. Because AGEs promote inflammation via RAGE and cross-link extracellular matrix proteins, dietary glycotoxins burden the body in addition to endogenous glycation. Restricting dietary AGEs reduces circulating AGE levels and may protect against AGE-related tissue damage.

label: High dietary AGE intake
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Sebekova and colleagues found that long-term consumption of advanced glycation end products in rats leads to a dose-dependent increase in proteinuria that over time could induce renal damage. High long-term consumption of AGEs has also been associated with higher levels of fasting glucose, insulin, and serum AGEs, as well as increased AGE localization and RAGE staining in the ovarian tissue of rats. These results show that chronic dietary AGE excess can reproduce in animals some of the renal and metabolic features seen in aging and diabetes, supporting the toxicity of a high-AGE diet.

label: Proteinuria
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Sebekova and colleagues found that long-term consumption of advanced glycation end products in rats leads to a dose-dependent increase in proteinuria that over time could induce renal damage. High long-term consumption of AGEs has also been associated with higher levels of fasting glucose, insulin, and serum AGEs, as well as increased AGE localization and RAGE staining in the ovarian tissue of rats. These results show that chronic dietary AGE excess can reproduce in animals some of the renal and metabolic features seen in aging and diabetes, supporting the toxicity of a high-AGE diet.

label: High-AGE diet
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: In a study of three groups of mice fed a caloric restriction (CR) diet, a regular diet, or a CR diet high in AGEs, CR mice lived longer than regular or CR-high mice, with median and maximal survival increased by 13.2% and 6%, respectively. Survival in CR-high mice was shorter than in regular-fed mice, and the CR-high group showed significantly increased oxidative stress and accelerated aging-related cardiovascular and renal disease. High dietary AGEs thus compete with the benefits of caloric restriction, indicating that the AGE content of the diet modulates lifespan.

label: Lifespan
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: BRASTO mice overexpress SIRT1 in the dorsomedial and lateral hypothalamus, raising physical activity and oxygen consumption, preserving skeletal-muscle mitochondrial morphology and body-temperature homeostasis, and extending median lifespan ~11% with delayed cancer-related death in both sexes. The mechanism is SIRT1 upregulating OX2R via NKX2-1 deacetylation, recapitulating calorie restriction. Notably, global SIRT1 overexpression does not extend lifespan, so the effect is brain-specific and dose-dependent.

label: Orlistat
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Orlistat, a lipase inhibitor, reduced serum AGEs after a high-AGE meal in 21 women with polycystic ovary disease compared with 15 women without PCOS, by decreasing AGE absorption. A six-month study evaluating the effect of calorie restriction and orlistat found serum AGE reductions in both PCOS and obese groups, independent of changes in body mass index. By interfering with lipid absorption, orlistat also reduces the absorption of fat-associated dietary AGEs, since foods rich in protein and fat have the highest AGE content. Orlistat therefore illustrates how modulating intestinal absorption can lower postprandial glycation load.

label: Intestinal Absorption
source_file: _document_ - Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products and Aging.md
description: Orlistat, a lipase inhibitor, reduced serum AGEs after a high-AGE meal in 21 women with polycystic ovary disease compared with 15 women without PCOS, by decreasing AGE absorption. A six-month study evaluating the effect of calorie restriction and orlistat found serum AGE reductions in both PCOS and obese groups, independent of changes in body mass index. By interfering with lipid absorption, orlistat also reduces the absorption of fat-associated dietary AGEs, since foods rich in protein and fat have the highest AGE content. Orlistat therefore illustrates how modulating intestinal absorption can lower postprandial glycation load.

label: Glyoxalase System
description: The glyoxalase system, composed of GLO1 and GLO2, is the primary defense system against dicarbonyl stress. Methylglyoxal, glyoxal, and 3-deoxyglucosone are highly reactive dicarbonyl intermediates generated during glycolysis and lipid peroxidation, and if left unchecked they form irreversible AGE crosslinks on cysteine, lysine, and arginine residues. The glyoxalase system neutralizes these precursors, and maintaining GLO1 activity is a primary target for reducing endogenous AGE accumulation. Dysfunction of this system is therefore linked to increased dicarbonyl stress and accelerated protein glycation, with consequences for aging, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease.

label: Methylglyoxal
description: DJ-1 is a glutathione-independent glyoxalase that stereospecifically detoxifies methylglyoxal into L-lactate, bypassing the glutathione requirement of the canonical glyoxalase system.

label: GLO1
description: GLO1 (glyoxalase I) is the rate-limiting enzyme of the glyoxalase system. It catalyzes the conversion of hemithioacetals, formed spontaneously from methylglyoxal and glutathione, into S-D-lactoylglutathione. Because methylglyoxal is one of the most reactive dicarbonyl precursors of advanced glycation end products, GLO1 activity is critical for preventing dicarbonyl stress from damaging proteins. Enhancing or maintaining GLO1 function is considered a primary target for reducing endogenous AGE accumulation and for protecting against age-related pathologies in which glycation plays a role.

label: S-D-lactoylglutathione
description: GLO1 (glyoxalase I) is the rate-limiting enzyme of the glyoxalase system. It catalyzes the conversion of hemithioacetals, formed spontaneously from methylglyoxal and glutathione, into S-D-lactoylglutathione. Because methylglyoxal is one of the most reactive dicarbonyl precursors of advanced glycation end products, GLO1 activity is critical for preventing dicarbonyl stress from damaging proteins. Enhancing or maintaining GLO1 function is considered a primary target for reducing endogenous AGE accumulation and for protecting against age-related pathologies in which glycation plays a role.

label: GLO2
description: GLO2 (glyoxalase II) is the second enzyme of the glyoxalase system. It converts S-D-lactoylglutathione into D-lactate, regenerating glutathione in the process. Because glutathione is both the cofactor for GLO1 and a major cellular antioxidant, GLO2 activity sustains the capacity of the glyoxalase system to detoxify methylglyoxal and other dicarbonyls. The conversion of reactive dicarbonyl intermediates into lactate thereby prevents them from forming irreversible AGE crosslinks on proteins, making GLO2 an integral component of the body's defense against glycation stress.

label: D-lactate
description: GLO2 (glyoxalase II) is the second enzyme of the glyoxalase system. It converts S-D-lactoylglutathione into D-lactate, regenerating glutathione in the process. Because glutathione is both the cofactor for GLO1 and a major cellular antioxidant, GLO2 activity sustains the capacity of the glyoxalase system to detoxify methylglyoxal and other dicarbonyls. The conversion of reactive dicarbonyl intermediates into lactate thereby prevents them from forming irreversible AGE crosslinks on proteins, making GLO2 an integral component of the body's defense against glycation stress.

label: PARK7
description: PARK7 mutations (L166P, M26I) cause early-onset autosomal recessive Parkinson's disease. DJ-1-deficient neurons show fragmented mitochondria, Complex I impairment, and accelerated α-synuclein aggregation.

label: Glycolic acid
description: PARK7 (DJ-1) detoxifies the reactive dicarbonyl species glyoxal and methylglyoxal in a glutathione-independent manner, converting glyoxal into glycolic acid and methylglyoxal into L-lactate. This stereospecific conversion removes dicarbonyls before they can form irreversible AGE crosslinks on protein residues. Because glyoxal is a major product of glucose and lipid oxidation, PARK7-dependent conversion of glyoxal to glycolic acid is an important route for limiting dicarbonyl stress. Loss of PARK7 activity is associated with tissue-specific accumulation of novel AGEs and, in humans, is linked to early-onset Parkinson's disease.

label: Aldo-Keto Reductases
description: Aldo-keto reductases (AKRs) and aldehyde dehydrogenases (ALDHs) are enzyme families that assist in reducing or oxidizing reactive aldehydes and dicarbonyls, such as 3-deoxyglucosone and methylglyoxal, into less toxic alcohols or carboxylic acids. By converting these reactive species into less harmful products, AKRs prevent them from participating in glycation cascades that form advanced glycation end products. This enzymatic detoxification is one of the three lines of defense against AGE accumulation, operating alongside the glyoxalase system and PARK7. Impaired AKR or ALDH function would be expected to increase dicarbonyl burden and accelerate protein glycation.

label: Aldehyde Dehydrogenases
description: Aldehyde dehydrogenases (ALDHs), together with aldo-keto reductases, help neutralize reactive aldehydes and dicarbonyls such as 3-deoxyglucosone and methylglyoxal by oxidizing them into less toxic carboxylic acids. This prevents these highly reactive species from participating in glycation cascades that form advanced glycation end products. ALDH activity therefore contributes to the body's first line of enzymatic defense against dicarbonyl stress, operating alongside the glyoxalase system and PARK7. Reduced ALDH function would be expected to increase the pool of reactive dicarbonyls available to damage proteins, promoting AGE accumulation.

label: Fructosamine-3-kinase
description: Fructosamine-3-kinase (FN3K) is an intracellular enzyme that initiates protein deglycation by phosphorylating fructosamine, the Amadori residues on glycated proteins, converting them into fructosamine-3-phosphate. This phosphorylated compound is highly unstable and spontaneously decomposes, regenerating the original, undamaged amino acid and releasing 3-deoxyglucosone, which is then neutralized by detoxifying enzymes. By repairing early glycation intermediates before they progress to irreversible AGEs, FN3K provides the repair arm of the enzymatic defense against AGE accumulation, complementary to prevention by dicarbonyl detoxification.

label: Fructosamine
description: Fructosamine-3-kinase (FN3K) is an intracellular enzyme that initiates protein deglycation by phosphorylating fructosamine, the Amadori residues on glycated proteins, converting them into fructosamine-3-phosphate. This phosphorylated compound is highly unstable and spontaneously decomposes, regenerating the original, undamaged amino acid and releasing 3-deoxyglucosone, which is then neutralized by detoxifying enzymes. By repairing early glycation intermediates before they progress to irreversible AGEs, FN3K provides the repair arm of the enzymatic defense against AGE accumulation, complementary to prevention by dicarbonyl detoxification.

label: 3-deoxyglucosone
description: Fructosamine-3-kinase (FN3K) phosphorylates Amadori (fructosamine) residues on glycated proteins to form fructosamine-3-phosphate, a highly unstable compound that spontaneously decomposes. The decomposition regenerates the original amino acid, repairing the glycated protein, and releases 3-deoxyglucosone, a reactive dicarbonyl that is then neutralized by detoxifying enzymes such as the glyoxalase system. FN3K therefore reverses early-stage glycation but generates a dicarbonyl byproduct that must be cleared, illustrating how the prevention and repair arms of AGE defense work together to limit the accumulation of advanced glycation end products.

label: Fructosyl-Amino Acid Oxidases
description: Fructosyl-amino acid oxidases (FAOD), also known as amadoriases, are enzymes found primarily in fungi and bacteria, such as Aspergillus species, that catalyze the oxidation of Amadori products. The reaction yields an unmodified amino acid, a glucosone, and hydrogen peroxide. Because they deglycate early glycation intermediates, FAOD are actively researched for therapeutic and cosmetic applications, and some research explores pairing FAOD with fructosamine-3-kinase to synergistically deglycate damaged structural proteins such as skin collagen. These enzymes represent a repair-based strategy for reducing AGE accumulation.

label: Cathepsin D
description: Lysosomal proteases are responsible for degrading glycated proteins intracellularly. Cathepsin D, an aspartic protease, and Cathepsin B, a cysteine protease, are major enzymes that break down AGE-modified proteins after they are directed to lysosomes for degradation. A decrease in Cathepsin D expression or activity, which occurs during aging and UV exposure, directly correlates with the accumulation of AGEs such as N-epsilon-carboxymethyl-lysine (CML). Cathepsin-dependent lysosomal degradation therefore represents the third line of defense against AGE accumulation, removing established glycated proteins that prevention and repair enzymes cannot handle.

label: AGE-modified proteins
description: Lysosomal proteases are responsible for degrading glycated proteins intracellularly. Cathepsin D, an aspartic protease, and Cathepsin B, a cysteine protease, are major enzymes that break down AGE-modified proteins after they are directed to lysosomes for degradation. A decrease in Cathepsin D expression or activity, which occurs during aging and UV exposure, directly correlates with the accumulation of AGEs such as N-epsilon-carboxymethyl-lysine (CML). Cathepsin-dependent lysosomal degradation therefore represents the third line of defense against AGE accumulation, removing established glycated proteins that prevention and repair enzymes cannot handle.

label: Cathepsin B
description: Cathepsin B is a lysosomal cysteine protease that, together with cathepsin D, is a major enzyme responsible for breaking down AGE-modified proteins. Glycated proteins are directed to lysosomes for degradation, and these cathepsins ensure that proteins damaged by non-enzymatic glycation are cleared rather than allowed to accumulate. The activity of such lysosomal proteases declines with age and under UV exposure, which correlates with accumulation of AGEs such as N-epsilon-carboxymethyl-lysine (CML). Maintaining lysosomal cathepsin function is therefore important for proteolytic clearance of glycated material and limiting AGE burden.

label: N-(carboxymethyl)-lysine
description: N-(carboxymethyl)-lysine (CML) is a prominent advanced glycation end product formed from glycated proteins. There is a marked correlation between the serum concentration of CML and vessel stiffness in elderly individuals, reflecting the role of AGE accumulation and ECM cross-linking in arterial stiffening. CML also accumulates in heart tissue with age, and dietary CML-enriched protein induces functional arterial aging in a RAGE-dependent manner in mice. Serum CML is therefore used as a biomarker of glycation burden and age-related vascular pathology.

label: Matrix Metalloproteinases
description: In the extracellular matrix, matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) such as MMP-1 and MMP-2 are involved in remodeling collagen and elastin that have been stiffened by glycation. Because AGE crosslinks make these long-lived structural proteins resistant to normal turnover, MMP-mediated remodeling helps manage matrix that has accumulated glycation damage, though MMP activity can become dysregulated under high-AGE conditions. MMPs thereby act as a degradative countermeasure to AGE-induced matrix stiffening, balancing crosslink formation and matrix turnover in vascular and connective tissue, although excessive or dysregulated MMP activity contributes to matrix destruction.

label: Glucosepane
description: Glucosepane is the most abundant and stubborn protein-protein AGE crosslink in human structural tissues, driving the systemic stiffening associated with aging and diabetes. Humans lack endogenous enzymes capable of directly breaking the glucosepane ring without destroying the surrounding collagen. Because of its abundance and stability, glucosepane is considered a major molecular target for anti-glycation therapies. Its crosslinks accumulate in long-lived proteins such as collagen and elastin, and are a principal cause of the extracellular matrix stiffening that contributes to arterial stiffening and age-related loss of tissue compliance.

label: HemF-like
description: Through functional metagenomics, researchers identified soil bacteria enzymes capable of utilizing synthetic glucosepane as a nutrient source, including the biocatalysts HemF-like (coproporphyrinogen III oxidase-like), BluB-like (5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole synthase-like), and QueE-like (7-carboxy-7-deazaguanine synthase-like). Remarkably, the human homolog of HemF, alongside homologous bacterial proteins found in the human microbiome, was shown to catalyze the cleavage of glucosepane in vitro, releasing citrulline as a byproduct. These glucosepane-cleaving enzymes represent a promising frontier for therapeutic interventions against age-related vascular stiffness and diabetic complications.

label: Adrenochrome monoaminoguanidine
description: Adrenochrome is an intermediate for adrenochrome monoaminoguanidine, a hemostatic agent formed when aminoguanidine reacts with the freshly generated adrenochrome. This hydrazone derivative both stabilizes the chemically unstable adrenochrome and serves as a useful medicine. Adrenochrome monoaminoguanidine obtained by the bismuth-catalyzed persulfate process is far less colored than that prepared by the method using potassium ferricyanide, and its identity is confirmed by UV absorption maxima at 348 nm and 445 nm.

label: Guanylhydrazone
description: Adrenochrome monoaminoguanidine (AMM), historically known as S-Adchnon or adrenochrome guanylhydrazone, is formed by reacting adrenochrome, an oxidation product of epinephrine containing an indoline-5,6-dione core, with aminoguanidine, a nucleophilic hydrazine derivative. The reaction forms a stable guanylhydrazone linkage at one of the carbonyl groups of the dione structure. AMM therefore combines a redox-active indoline core with an established anti-glycation agent, providing a dual-action glyco-oxidative modulator designed to simultaneously target oxidative stress and protein crosslinking by advanced glycation end products.

label: indoline-5,6-dione
description: Adrenochrome is chemically an indoline-5,6-dione, formally 3-hydroxy-1-methyl-2,3-dihydro-1H-indole-5,6-dione. The molecule features a fused bicyclic system in which a six-membered benzene ring (oxidized to a quinone at positions 5 and 6) is fused to a five-membered nitrogen-containing ring bearing a hydroxy substituent and an N-methyl group. This structure arises when oxidized epinephrine undergoes intramolecular cyclization, in which the side-chain nitrogen attacks the electrophilic o-quinone ring (a Michael addition), closing the second ring. The quinone moiety and its o-quinone character account for much of adrenochrome's reactivity, including its ability to undergo redox cycling and one-electron reduction to the semiquinone radical.

label: Hemostatics
description: Carbazochrome (adrenochrome monosemicarbazone) is known as a hemostatic agent, one of two hydrazine derivatives of adrenochrome described in the patent, the other being adrenochrome monoaminoguanidine. These hydrazine derivatives serve both for the stabilization of adrenochrome and for the preparation of useful medicines that act to stop bleeding. In the patented process, semicarbazide is added to the adrenochrome solution at 0 to 15 degrees C at pH 5 to 7 to form carbazochrome, which is then isolated by filtration and purified.

label: Hematopoietic Stem Cell
description: Adult stem cells such as hematopoietic stem cells spend most of their lives in quiescence to protect the genome and preserve self-renewal capacity. By remaining in a low-activity state, these cells limit DNA replication-associated damage and metabolic stress, maintaining their regenerative potential over a lifetime and resisting stem cell exhaustion. Quiescence therefore serves as a protective mechanism that balances stem cell maintenance with the need to respond rapidly to hematopoietic demand.

label: Prodrug
description: For adrenochrome monoaminoguanidine to act as an active AGE inhibitor despite its hydrazine group being locked in a hydrazone bond, it must either retain sufficient nucleophilicity through its remaining guanidine nitrogens, act as a prodrug that undergoes controlled in vivo hydrolysis to slowly release free aminoguanidine, or work via alternative pathways such as chelating transition metals that catalyze glycoxidation. The prodrug hypothesis is plausible because the conjugate is stable for clinical use yet could hydrolyze to release aminoguanidine over time. Whether the bound aminoguanidine retains dicarbonyl-scavenging activity remains unresolved.

label: oxidation product of epinephrine
description: Adrenochrome is a chemical compound formed by the oxidation of epinephrine (adrenaline), a catecholamine stress hormone. In humans it arises as a minor oxidative metabolite or byproduct rather than through a dedicated biosynthetic pathway. Oxidation converts the catechol ring of adrenaline to an o-quinone followed by internal cyclization to an indoline-5,6-dione structure. This process occurs in vivo, driven by reactive oxygen species such as superoxide anion and hydrogen peroxide, and in vitro. Because the reaction competes with the primary COMT and MAO degradation routes, adrenochrome formation becomes more prominent under oxidative stress, inflammation, and conditions where adrenaline levels are high, and it is considered a marker of failed homeostasis rather than a normal abundant product.

label: Adrenochrome formation
description: Oxidative stress drives adrenochrome formation because high levels of superoxide and H2O2 favor oxidation and cyclization of adrenaline to the neurotoxic quinone adrenochrome. This pathway has been implicated in psychosis models and redox-linked neuronal injury. The directionality is catecholamine oxidation to adrenochrome. A caveat is that adrenochrome formation in vivo is contested, and adrenochrome can also be detoxified or further metabolized, so its pathological relevance remains debated. The pathway is also relevant to catecholamine-driven cardiotoxicity during stress and to hypotheses linking redox state to neuropsychiatric phenomena.

label: Liver microsomes
description: Liver microsomes are subcellular fractions of hepatic endoplasmic reticulum enriched in oxidative enzymes. In the presence of NADPH and oxygen, hepatic microsomal enzymes can oxidize epinephrine to adrenochrome, and the rate is modulated by high oxygen tension or inhibitors such as cyanide. This demonstrates that hepatic microsomal oxidases contribute to adrenaline oxidation alongside the well-known neutrophil and myocardial routes. The microsomal pathway represents an enzymatic or semi-enzymatic route of catecholamine oxidation that may be more relevant when oxidative stress or drug-induced enzyme activity is elevated, though it remains a minor pathway relative to COMT- and MAO-mediated metabolism.

label: Metanephrine
description: Metanephrine is the principal COMT-derived metabolite of epinephrine, formed when catechol-O-methyltransferase methylates one of the catechol hydroxyl groups of adrenaline using S-adenosylmethionine as the methyl donor. Together with MAO-mediated oxidative deamination, this conversion is the primary route of adrenaline breakdown in the body. Because COMT and MAO clear adrenaline rapidly, the alternative oxidative pathway that yields adrenochrome is normally a minor side route. Metanephrine measurements are also clinically useful as markers of catecholamine production, and elevated levels reflect increased release of epinephrine from the adrenal medulla.

label: COMT Inhibitors
description: COMT inhibitors such as entacapone, tolcapone, and opicapone block catechol-O-methyltransferase, one of the principal enzymes that degrades catecholamines by methylation. Inhibiting COMT therefore increases synaptic and circulating levels of dopamine, norepinephrine, and epinephrine, and this is exploited clinically in Parkinson's disease, often combined with MAO inhibitors and levodopa, to prolong dopaminergic effects and reduce off time. The resulting higher catecholamine levels, together with inhibition of MAO-mediated clearance, provide more substrate for oxidative conversion to adrenochrome, though this effect is mostly theoretical in clinical use and benefits are generally judged to outweigh risks.

label: Catecholamines
description: Catecholamines, dopamine, norepinephrine, and epinephrine, are a subclass of catechols, meaning they each contain the 1,2-dihydroxybenzene (catechol) ring that makes them substrates for COMT. This shared structural motif is the recognition site for O-methylation, which explains why all three monoamines are inactivated by COMT-catalyzed methyl transfer. Their classification as catechols is foundational to understanding COMT substrate specificity and why catechol-bearing drugs and flavonoids also interact with the enzyme. It also underlies the shared metabolic handling of these signaling molecules.

label: Smoking
description: Cigarette, cigar, and wood smoke contain enormous amounts of free radicals and oxidants (cigarette smoke alone carries on the order of 10^17 oxidant molecules per puff). These external oxidants directly increase reactive oxygen species, deplete antioxidants such as vitamin C and glutathione, and cause systemic oxidative stress. Smoke also activates sympathetic nervous system responses and inflammation, further raising endogenous ROS production. This oxidative environment promotes the oxidation of adrenaline to adrenochrome and supports the redox cycle by which adrenochrome generates more superoxide, linking smoking to increased catecholamine oxidation and oxidative damage.

label: Neuromelanin formation
description: Adrenochrome and related aminochromes serve as intermediates in the synthesis of neuromelanin, the dark pigment that accumulates in catecholaminergic neurons of the substantia nigra and locus coeruleus. When catecholamines such as dopamine, norepinephrine, and adrenaline are oxidized, they generate reactive quinones and aminochromes that polymerize into melanin-like pigments. In the brain, this process is tied to iron- and metal-catalyzed autoxidation, and the oxidative metabolism of catecholamines into quinone compounds contributes to the age-dependent buildup of neuromelanin. Adrenochrome-like structures are thus chemically upstream of neuromelanin formation, with neuromelanin granules accumulating progressively from birth to middle-to-late adulthood.

label: Dopamine
description: COMT metabolizes dopamine by catalyzing the transfer of a methyl group from S-adenosylmethionine to the catechol ring, producing 3-methoxytyramine, which is further oxidized by monoamine oxidase. This O-methylation is the primary route of dopamine inactivation in the prefrontal cortex, where the dopamine transporter is sparse and clearance depends on extracellular enzymes. By controlling the duration and magnitude of extracellular dopamine, COMT activity directly influences dopaminergic tone in cognition, mood, and reward. The Val158Met polymorphism, by altering enzyme activity, modulates the efficiency of this degradation.

label: Carbazochrome
description: Adrenochrome is an intermediate for adrenochrome monosemicarbazone (carbazochrome), which is known as a hemostatic agent. In the patented process, semicarbazide reacts with the freshly produced adrenochrome to form carbazochrome, stabilizing the unstable quinoid intermediate and yielding a useful medicine. The carbazochrome obtained by the bismuth-catalyzed persulfate method is far less colored than that prepared using the potassium ferricyanide method, and its identity is confirmed by UV absorption at 354 nm and characteristic infrared absorptions.

label: Low pH
description: Acidic conditions strongly slow or prevent the cyclization step of adrenochrome formation, because at low pH the side-chain amine of the oxidized epinephrine intermediate is protonated and reduced in nucleophilicity, so it cannot easily attack the quinone ring. In highly acidic solutions the open-chain quinone form is favored and more stable, while neutral-to-alkaline pH accelerates cyclization and oxidation. This pH dependence explains why pharmaceutical epinephrine solutions are kept acidic (pH 3-5) with antioxidants to minimize oxidation and adrenochrome formation, and it is the most important factor in controlling the reaction rate.

label: Bisulfite
description: Bisulfite (sodium bisulfite or metabisulfite) is a reducing agent added to pharmaceutical epinephrine injections to prevent oxidation of the catechol and thereby inhibit adrenochrome formation. By scavenging oxygen and reactive oxygen species and reducing oxidized intermediates, bisulfite keeps adrenaline solutions stable and usable for extended periods, preventing the pink-to-red discoloration that signals adrenochrome accumulation. This practical application reflects the general principle that the epinephrine-to-adrenochrome oxidation can be slowed by antioxidants, acidic pH, low temperature, and protection from light. Without such stabilizers, adrenaline auto-oxidizes visibly within days to weeks.

label: Elastin
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: Advanced glycation end products accumulate within the extracellular matrix and cross-link elastic fibers as well as collagen. This cross-linking of extracellular proteins reduces the elasticity of connective tissues such as blood vessels, skin, and tendons, affecting especially vascular function. Glycated modifications alter the balance between ECM synthesis and degradation, accelerating skin aging and increasing skin stiffness. AGE-elastin cross-linking is one of the three major mechanisms by which AGEs injure tissues, alongside intracellular glycation and RAGE-mediated inflammatory signaling.

label: protein function
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: Glycation is a spontaneous non-enzymatic reaction of reducing sugars with free amino groups of proteins, DNA, and lipids that leads to loss of protein function and impaired elasticity of tissues such as blood vessels, skin, and tendons. The process is highly accelerated in the presence of hyperglycemia and tissue oxidative stress, implicating it in diabetic complications and aging. Intracellular AGE modification of signaling molecules can impair cellular functions and gene expression, and glycation of antioxidant enzymes such as catalase, glutathione peroxidase, and glutathione reductase reduces their activity, further increasing cellular oxidative stress.

label: diabetic complications
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: Advanced glycation end products accumulate in tissues and organs during diabetes and contribute to the pathogenesis of diabetic complications. AGE formation and accumulation in diabetic patients results in vascular alterations leading to diabetic vasculopathy, and glycation is implicated in diabetic renal, retinal, and neural complications. Because the glycation reaction is accelerated by hyperglycemia and oxidative stress, poor glycemic control exacerbates AGE burden. AGE inhibitors such as aminoguanidine were shown to prevent diabetic complications by inhibiting AGE formation, supporting the causal role of glycation in diabetic pathology.

label: Reactive Oxygen Species generation
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: RAGE is the receptor for advanced glycation end products that regulates cell processes including inflammation, apoptosis, ROS signaling, proliferation, autophagy, and aging. Activation of RAGE by AGEs leads to ROS generation and downstream inflammatory signaling, providing a receptor-mediated route by which glycated proteins damage cells. This ROS generation contributes to oxidative stress in diabetes, renal failure, and aging. The AGE-RAGE axis is therefore a key molecular link between glycation and oxidative damage, and blocking RAGE signaling is a potential therapeutic strategy against AGE-mediated pathology.

label: ECM
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: Advanced glycation end products accumulate within the extracellular matrix (ECM), such as in collagen and elastic fibers, and cross-link with ECM components. This accumulation and cross-linking cause a decrease in connective tissue elasticity, alter ECM structure and function, and impair vascular function, facilitating plaque formation and basement membrane hyperplasia. AGE accumulation in the ECM is one of the three major mechanisms by which AGEs contribute to aging, alongside intracellular glycation and RAGE-mediated signaling. ECM glycation is strongly implicated in arterial stiffening, skin aging, and age-related stiffness of tendons and cartilage.

label: Glycated proteins
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: Glycated proteins are normally removed from cells via ubiquitin-dependent 20S proteasome-mediated proteolysis, an important quality control pathway for damaged proteins. AGE modifications can disturb this proteolytic degradation, contributing to a further increase in the cellular content of glycated proteins. The resulting accumulation of glycated proteins is a hallmark of aging and is associated with loss of cellular function. Proteasomal degradation of glycated proteins is thus a key cellular defense against glycation stress, and its impairment creates a feed-forward loop of AGE accumulation.

label: Pentosidine
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: Pentosidine is a cross-linking advanced glycation end product that accumulates in skin with age, together with argpyrimidine. It is also found to increase with age in the lamina cribrosa, lung collagen, patellar tendon, vitreous body, oocytes, intervertebral disk, and cartilage. Pentosidine is formed from the reaction of sugars with lysine and arginine residues and functions as a fluorescent AGE marker of cumulative glycation. Its age-dependent accumulation in skin and other connective tissues reflects the progressive cross-linking and stiffening of the extracellular matrix during aging.

label: Skin

label: Heart
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: N-(carboxymethyl)-lysine (CML) is an advanced glycation end product that increases with age in heart tissue. It is one of the most abundant AGEs and is also a biomarker of glycation burden, with serum CML correlating with vessel stiffness in elderly individuals. CML accumulation results from the non-enzymatic glycation of proteins by glucose and other carbonyls, and it contributes to the cross-linking and functional impairment of extracellular matrix proteins. Heart CML accumulation is part of the broader age-related AGE buildup that affects cardiovascular tissues.

label: Dietary Advanced Glycation End Products
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: Food is an important source of exogenous advanced glycation end products, since significant AGE generation occurs when sugars are cooked with proteins via the Maillard reaction. In a mouse model, feeding an AGE-rich diet for 16 weeks promoted a 53% increase in serum AGE levels. In renal failure patients, an AGE-rich diet produced a 29% increase in blood CML, while a low-AGE diet produced a 34% reduction. These findings suggest that a diet restricting AGEs is an effective way to reduce the AGE burden in the human body.

label: Endothelial dysfunction
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: Alpha-lipoic acid improves endothelial dysfunction, as confirmed in meta-analyses showing improved flow-mediated dilation and markers of oxidative stress in diabetic and metabolic patients. By restoring GSH and reducing NF-kappaB, it ameliorates NO bioavailability. The directionality is antioxidant supplementation to vascular benefit. A caveat is that trial results are heterogeneous and benefits are most consistent in established endothelial dysfunction rather than primary prevention. Lipoic acid also chelates redox-active metals, which may reduce the metal-catalyzed generation of hydroxyl radicals in the vascular wall.

label: Advanced Glycation End Products formation
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: Aminoguanidine was the first agent introduced as an AGE inhibitor. It and related inhibitors such as pyridoxamine prevent AGE accumulation by interacting with highly reactive carbonyl species and acting as carbonyl traps. Aminoguanidine prevented diabetic renal, retinal, and neural complications through the inhibition of AGE formation in animal models. However, it cannot be used clinically due to safety concerns including pro-oxidant activities and inhibition of nitric oxide synthase, so its role is now primarily as a research tool and reference compound.

label: Pyridoxamine
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: Pyridoxamine is a synthetic AGE inhibitor that prevents AGE accumulation by interacting with highly reactive carbonyl species and acting as a carbonyl trap, similar to aminoguanidine. By scavenging carbonyl intermediates, pyridoxamine blocks the formation of advanced glycation end products and is considered a candidate for preventing glycation-mediated pathology. Unlike aminoguanidine, pyridoxamine (a vitamin B6 derivative) has a more favorable safety profile. AGE inhibitors and carbonyl-trapping agents remain an active area of research for reducing AGE burden in diabetes and aging.

label: Epicatechin
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: Epicatechin, a flavanol, demonstrates potent AGE-breaking properties in vitro and in vivo. It destroyed preformed glycated serum albumin in vitro and decreased AGE accumulation in retinal tissues of rats injected with exogenous AGE. Mechanistically, side chains attached to the pyrrole ring carbons of AGE structures are susceptible to nucleophilic attack, and because C6 and C8 on the A-ring of epicatechin are nucleophilic, epicatechin can attack and destroy AGE cross-links. These findings position epicatechin as a naturally occurring AGE breaker with potential for preventing AGE-mediated tissue damage.

label: glycated serum albumin

label: Kaempferol
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: Kaempferol is a flavonoid polyphenol reported to possess anti-glycation properties. Along with other flavonoids such as genistein, quercitrin, and quercetin, kaempferol inhibits the glycation process in vitro, and several herbal polyphenols have anti-glycation activities similar to or stronger than aminoguanidine. These compounds act partly through their antioxidant capacity, which reduces the ROS-driven acceleration of protein glycation. Flavonoid-rich herbs and dietary plants are therefore considered promising, relatively safe agents for the prevention of glycation and AGE formation during aging.

label: Quercetin
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: High-catechol flavonoids such as quercetin, fisetin, and luteolin can inhibit COMT, leading to catecholamine accumulation and worrier-type symptoms during a bulk phase. Slow-COMT individuals are especially advised to avoid these during high catecholamine turnover to prevent adrenochrome pathway fueling.

label: Genistein
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: Genistein is a type of flavonoids, specifically an isoflavone found abundantly in soy, and it shares the redox and signaling properties of the broader flavonoid class. Its structure includes a phenolic A ring that confers antioxidant activity. The directionality is subclass membership within the flavonoid family. A caveat is that genistein also has estrogen-receptor modulatory activity distinct from its antioxidant effects. Genistein's antioxidant actions are complemented by estrogen-receptor signaling, tyrosine-kinase inhibition, and effects on eNOS and NOX, making it a multitarget isoflavone.

label: antioxidant enzyme expression
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: Moderate physical exercise induces the expression of antioxidant enzymes, leading to the reduction of oxidative stress. Exercise effectively inhibits ROS generation and improves the activities of antioxidant enzymes, and because the protein glycation reaction is driven and accelerated by ROS, the inhibition of AGE formation by regular exercise is attributed mainly to exercise-associated antioxidant activity. Physical exercise also decreases oxidative stress in rodent models and is reported to improve systemic antioxidant activity in humans. These antioxidant effects link exercise to reduced AGE accumulation and healthier aging.

label: AGE inhibition
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: The inhibition of AGE formation and accumulation in tissues can lead to an increase in lifespan, as concluded from extensive evidence that AGE accumulation accompanies aging and age-related diseases. Because there are no enzymes to remove glycated products, AGEs accumulate as metabolic waste and contribute to tissue senescence. Inhibiting the glycation process and removing existing glycation products may prolong lifespan, and dietary herbal supplements or physiological exercise are advantageous in reducing the AGE burden in the body.

label: AGE-restricted diet
source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
description: A diet restricting advanced glycation end products can effectively reduce the AGE burden in the human body. In renal failure patients, a low-AGE diet produced a 34% reduction in blood CML levels, while an AGE-rich diet increased CML by 29%. Because significant AGE generation occurs when sugars are cooked with proteins, dietary intake is an important exogenous source of glycotoxins. Restricting dietary AGEs is therefore proposed as an effective way to reduce circulating AGE levels and protect against AGE-related organ dysfunction and tissue aging.
