description: PERO1 functions as a sensor of oleic acid accumulation on damaged peroxisomes, triggering autophagic removal of these defective organelles. By detecting lipid imbalance indicative of peroxisomal dysfunction, PERO1 initiates quality-control degradation that prevents the propagation of impaired organelles. This lipid-sensing mechanism links metabolic state to organelle surveillance. The pathway exemplifies how selective autophagy integrates metabolic cues to maintain peroxisome integrity.

label: Oleic acid accumulation
description: PERO1 functions as a sensor of oleic acid accumulation on damaged peroxisomes, triggering autophagic removal of these defective organelles. By detecting lipid imbalance indicative of peroxisomal dysfunction, PERO1 initiates quality-control degradation that prevents the propagation of impaired organelles. This lipid-sensing mechanism links metabolic state to organelle surveillance. The pathway exemplifies how selective autophagy integrates metabolic cues to maintain peroxisome integrity.

label: Selective Autophagy
description: Selective autophagy targets damaged peroxisomes for degradation through a process termed pexophagy, in which ubiquitin tagging of peroxisomal proteins and recruitment of ESCRT (endosomal sorting complex required for transport) machinery mark the organelle for autophagic engulfment. This cargo-specific pathway contrasts with bulk autophagy by requiring receptor proteins that bridge the peroxisome to the autophagosomal membrane. Pexophagy protects cells from the oxidative and metabolic damage caused by defective peroxisomes. Its failure leads to accumulation of aberrant organelles and disease.

label: Damaged peroxisomes
description: Selective autophagy targets damaged peroxisomes for degradation through a process termed pexophagy, in which ubiquitin tagging of peroxisomal proteins and recruitment of ESCRT (endosomal sorting complex required for transport) machinery mark the organelle for autophagic engulfment. This cargo-specific pathway contrasts with bulk autophagy by requiring receptor proteins that bridge the peroxisome to the autophagosomal membrane. Pexophagy protects cells from the oxidative and metabolic damage caused by defective peroxisomes. Its failure leads to accumulation of aberrant organelles and disease.

label: PEX1
description: PEX1 is an ATPase essential for peroxisome membrane assembly and matrix protein import, operating as part of the peroxisomal AAA (ATPases associated with diverse cellular activities) machinery. Loss of PEX1 causes a complete lack of functional peroxisomes, as import and biogenesis cannot proceed. This essential role makes PEX1 mutations among the most common causes of peroxisome biogenesis disorders. The gene thus sits at the foundation of peroxisome formation and metabolic competence.

label: Peroxisome membrane assembly
description: PEX1 is an ATPase essential for peroxisome membrane assembly and matrix protein import, operating as part of the peroxisomal AAA (ATPases associated with diverse cellular activities) machinery. Loss of PEX1 causes a complete lack of functional peroxisomes, as import and biogenesis cannot proceed. This essential role makes PEX1 mutations among the most common causes of peroxisome biogenesis disorders. The gene thus sits at the foundation of peroxisome formation and metabolic competence.

label: ABCD1
description: Mutations in ABCD1, encoding a peroxisomal ATP-binding cassette transporter for very-long-chain fatty acids (VLCFAs), cause X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD). Impaired ABCD1 disrupts VLCFA import into peroxisomes for beta-oxidation, leading to toxic accumulation of VLCFAs in adrenal cortex and central nervous system white matter. The resulting demyelination and adrenal insufficiency define the clinical syndrome. The disorder illustrates how peroxisomal transport defects produce severe neurodegeneration and underscores the importance of peroxisomal lipid homeostasis.

label: Adrenoleukodystrophy
description: Mutations in ABCD1, encoding a peroxisomal ATP-binding cassette transporter for very-long-chain fatty acids (VLCFAs), cause X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD). Impaired ABCD1 disrupts VLCFA import into peroxisomes for beta-oxidation, leading to toxic accumulation of VLCFAs in adrenal cortex and central nervous system white matter. The resulting demyelination and adrenal insufficiency define the clinical syndrome. The disorder illustrates how peroxisomal transport defects produce severe neurodegeneration and underscores the importance of peroxisomal lipid homeostasis.

label: Zellweger syndrome
description: Zellweger syndrome, the most severe form of the Zellweger spectrum of peroxisome biogenesis disorders, is caused by mutations in PEX genes required for peroxisome assembly and matrix protein import. Affected individuals lack functional peroxisomes, leading to accumulation of very-long-chain fatty acids, bile acid intermediates, and pipecolic acid, with profound neurologic, hepatic, and skeletal abnormalities. The spectrum's severity correlates with the degree of residual peroxisomal function. These disorders highlight the non-redundant essentiality of peroxisomes in human development.

label: PEX gene mutations
description: Zellweger syndrome, the most severe form of the Zellweger spectrum of peroxisome biogenesis disorders, is caused by mutations in PEX genes required for peroxisome assembly and matrix protein import. Affected individuals lack functional peroxisomes, leading to accumulation of very-long-chain fatty acids, bile acid intermediates, and pipecolic acid, with profound neurologic, hepatic, and skeletal abnormalities. The spectrum's severity correlates with the degree of residual peroxisomal function. These disorders highlight the non-redundant essentiality of peroxisomes in human development.

label: Lysosomal biogenesis
source_file: _document_ - From the regulatory mechanism of TFEB to its therapeutic implications - Cell Death Discovery.md
description: TFEB is a master transcriptional regulator of lysosomal biogenesis, and its overexpression drives coordinated activation of numerous lysosomal genes encoding membrane proteins, hydrolases, and v-ATPase subunits. This global upregulation increases both the number and functional capacity of lysosomes, expanding degradative reserve. As the central node of the CLEAR network, TFEB integrates diverse stress signals into a unified lysosomal expansion program. Its master-regulator status makes it a prime target for therapies aimed at enhancing cellular clearance.

label: TFE3 at S321
description: mTORC1 phosphorylates TFE3 at serine 321, an analog of the TFEB S211 site, thereby promoting cytosolic retention and inhibiting TFE3's transcriptional activity under nutrient-replete conditions. This parallel modification ensures that both MiT/TFE family master regulators are coordinately repressed by mTORC1. Upon starvation or mTORC1 inhibition, dephosphorylation permits TFE3 nuclear entry and activation of lysosomal genes. The conserved regulatory logic highlights the unified control of the degradative program.

label: Lipid catabolism
description: TFEB regulates lipid catabolism by upregulating genes involved in fatty acid import, beta-oxidation, lysosomal acid lipase (LAL)-mediated lipophagy, and the transcriptional coactivators PGC-1α and PPAR-α. Through these targets, TFEB coordinates the mobilization and oxidation of stored lipids during fasting and stress. This lipid-catabolic program complements TFEB's role in protein and organelle turnover, rendering it a comprehensive metabolic regulator. Enhanced TFEB activity improves lipid handling and protects against hepatic steatosis.

label: Mitochondrial stress
source_file: _document_ - From the regulatory mechanism of TFEB to its therapeutic implications - Cell Death Discovery.md
description: TFEB is activated in response to mitochondrial stress, a process requiring mitophagy machinery including PINK1, Parkin, Atg9A, and Atg5 to signal and enable TFEB nuclear translocation. As damaged mitochondria are selected for autophagic removal, TFEB coordinates a compensatory lysosomal and autophagic response that restores organelle quality. This coupling ensures that mitochondrial turnover is matched by degradative capacity. The axis links mitochondrial quality control to the broader autophagy-lysosomal network and to metabolic homeostasis.

label: ER stress
description: TFE3 is activated in response to endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress through a pathway that is mTORC1-independent but requires the ER stress sensor PERK. Under unfolded protein accumulation, PERK signaling promotes TFE3 nuclear translocation, engaging lysosomal and autophagic genes to alleviate proteotoxic burden. This distinct trigger allows TFE3 to contribute to the integrated stress response without relying on nutrient sensing. The mechanism expands the repertoire of stressors that can recruit the MiT/TFE degradative program.

label: Immune response
source_file: _document_ - From the regulatory mechanism of TFEB to its therapeutic implications - Cell Death Discovery.md
description: TFEB regulates innate and adaptive immune responses, becoming activated during dendritic cell maturation to enhance antigen processing and presentation via expanded lysosomal and MHC-related machinery. By boosting degradative capacity, TFEB improves the efficiency of antigen degradation and epitope loading, strengthening T cell priming. TFEB activity also influences macrophage polarization and immune cell metabolism. These roles position the autophagy-lysosomal master regulator as an important modulator of immunity.

label: PGC1-alpha
source_file: _document_ - From the regulatory mechanism of TFEB to its therapeutic implications - Cell Death Discovery.md
description: TFEB and the mitochondrial biogenesis coactivator PGC-1α form a positive feedback loop: PGC-1α modulates mitophagy by regulating TFEB expression, while TFEB induces PGC-1α transcription, reinforcing mitochondrial turnover and biogenesis. This reciprocal regulation couples lysosomal-autophagic clearance with mitochondrial network expansion under stress. The loop ensures coordinated enhancement of both degradative and biosynthetic mitochondrial programs. Its disruption impairs metabolic adaptation and is relevant to aging and myopathy.

label: MALAT1 in renal carcinoma
source_file: _document_ - From the regulatory mechanism of TFEB to its therapeutic implications - Cell Death Discovery.md
description: In a subset of translocation renal cell carcinomas (t(6;11) RCC), the TFEB gene is fused with the long non-coding RNA locus MALAT1, producing a MALAT1-TFEB fusion that drives overexpression of intact TFEB. The fusion places TFEB under the strong promoter activity of MALAT1, leading to constitutive activation of the lysosomal-autophagic and proliferative programs. This genetic rearrangement defines a distinct clinicopathologic entity of RCC with characteristic biphasic histology. The finding established TFEB as an oncogene when deregulated by chromosomal translocation.

label: Xp11 translocation RCC
description: TFE3 is recurrently involved in Xp11.2 translocation renal cell carcinomas, in which it fuses with partner genes such as ASPSCR1, PRCC, or SFPQ, creating chimeric transcription factors that drive tumorigenesis. These gene fusions define a distinct subset of RCC, often arising in children and young adults, with characteristic clear-cell or papillary features. The fusion proteins typically retain the TFE3 DNA-binding domain and are constitutively active, deregulating MiT/TFE target genes. Detection of TFE3 rearrangement is important for correct diagnosis and classification of these tumors.

label: mTORC1 activation
description: The lysosome serves as the physical platform for mTORC1 activation, hosting the recruitment of mTORC1 via Rag GTPases and Ragulator and its encounter with the activator Rheb at the lysosomal surface. Amino-acid sensing, growth-factor inputs, and calcium signals all converge at this organelle to determine mTORC1 activity. By colocalizing mTORC1 with its upstream regulators, the lysosome functionally couples nutrient detection to the control of autophagy and anabolism. This spatial organization is essential for the rapid, reversible regulation of the pathway.

label: Longevity in C. elegans
description: HLH-30 regulates longevity in C. elegans, as its overexpression extends lifespan while loss of hlh-30 shortens it and suppresses the longevity of other mutants. By inducing autophagy, lysosomal biogenesis, and lipid mobilization, HLH-30 preserves proteostasis and metabolic homeostasis that decline with age. Its activity integrates insulin, mTOR, and dietary signals into a pro-longevity transcriptional program. The worm findings provide a conserved model for how TFEB orthologs promote healthspan in higher organisms.

label: Arterial aging
description: Spermidine reverses features of arterial aging, including large elastic artery stiffening, and restores nitric-oxide-mediated endothelial function in aged vessels. These vascular benefits are linked to spermidine-induced autophagy, which clears damaged mitochondria and reduces vascular oxidative stress and inflammation. By improving endothelial-dependent vasodilation, spermidine counteracts the stiffening that drives systolic hypertension and cardiovascular risk with age. The findings support spermidine as a candidate intervention for vascular rejuvenation.

label: Adaptive autophagy
description: Moderate caloric restriction induces adaptive autophagy—a beneficial, hormetic form of the pathway that enhances cellular clearance and resilience without causing damage. This adaptive response, driven by AMPK activation and mTORC1 inhibition, contributes substantially to the lifespan and healthspan extension observed with CR. Unlike pathological autophagy, adaptive autophagy is precisely regulated and supports rather than threatens cell survival. It represents the mechanistic core of CR's pro-longevity effects.

label: Excessive autophagy
description: Prolonged or severe caloric restriction can drive excessive autophagy that crosses into autophagic cell death, particularly when degradative flux outpaces biosynthetic capacity. This maladaptive extreme underscores the biphasic, hormetic nature of autophagy, where too little or too much is detrimental. The balance between adaptive and excessive autophagy determines whether CR is protective or harmful. Understanding this threshold is important for safely translating CR-mimetic strategies.

label: ATG4B
source_file: _document_ - The Beneficial and Adverse Effects of Autophagic Response to Caloric Restriction and Fasting.md
description: Starvation induces SIRT2 activity, which deacetylates ATG4B, a cysteine protease required for LC3 processing and autophagy induction. Directionally, SIRT2 enzymatically activates ATG4B. This is necessary for proper autophagosome formation during nutrient deprivation, and it adds SIRT2 to the sirtuin network controlling autophagy. By promoting LC3 processing, SIRT2 supports the elongation of autophagosome membranes during starvation. This nutrient-responsive regulation connects SIRT2 to the cellular adaptation to fasting, complementing the roles of SIRT1 in autophagy regulation.

label: Insulin signaling
description: Insulin signaling inhibits autophagy by activating the PI3K-Akt axis, which in turn activates mTORC1 and promotes phosphorylation of ULK1 and TFEB that suppress autophagic initiation and lysosomal gene expression. Through this cascade, the fed-state hormone maintains an anabolic, autophagy-off condition in peripheral tissues. The relief of insulin signaling during fasting or caloric restriction is therefore prerequisite for autophagic induction. This relationship is a primary reason why nutrient excess and insulin resistance are associated with impaired autophagy and metabolic disease.

label: Chemotherapy sensitivity
description: Caloric restriction increases the sensitivity of tumor cells to chemotherapy by creating a differential stress resistance in which normal cells enter a protective, autophagy-dependent quiescent state while cancer cells remain vulnerable. CR additionally stimulates CD8+ T cell-mediated anti-tumor immunity and enhances apoptotic priming of malignant cells. The improved therapeutic index allows lower effective doses and reduced toxicity. These effects position CR and its mimetics as adjuncts to conventional cancer therapy.

label: FOXO1
description: SIRT1 deacetylates the forkhead factor FOXO1, redirecting its transcriptional program toward metabolic homeostasis and stress resistance while tempering apoptosis. Deacetylated FOXO1 cooperates with C/EBPα to induce adiponectin and with PGC-1α to support oxidative metabolism, gluconeogenesis, and antioxidant gene expression. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically modifies FOXO1 to reshape its target-gene output. This regulation is central to SIRT1's control of glucose handling and insulin sensitivity, and the two proteins form a positive feedback loop in which FOXO1 also activates the SIRT1 promoter, amplifying stress-resistance and metabolic-adaptation programs across tissues.

label: Akt inhibits autophagy
description: Akt phosphorylates and inhibits the FOXO1/FOXO3 transcription factors, which normally promote autophagy and stress-resistance gene expression, thereby indirectly suppressing autophagy downstream of insulin/PI3K signaling. The reciprocal interaction reflects the broader antagonism between growth-factor-driven anabolism (via Akt-mTOR) and the autophagy-promoting FOXO program. When Akt is inactive during fasting, FOXO factors are de-repressed and contribute to autophagic and longevity pathways. This axis embeds autophagy control within the insulin-signaling network that also regulates mTORC1.

label: Ketogenic Diet
description: Ketogenic diets, characterized by high fat and very low carbohydrate intake, activate autophagy by lowering insulin and glucose while elevating ketone bodies and AMPK activity. The metabolic shift toward fatty-acid oxidation and mild energy stress mimics aspects of caloric restriction, engaging the autophagic machinery. This activation contributes to the reported healing and neuroprotective effects of ketogenic regimens in epilepsy, neurodegeneration, and metabolic disease. The diet thus provides a non-fasting nutritional strategy to recruit autophagic clearance.

label: Cancer treatment
description: During cancer treatment, autophagy plays a dual role that depends on context: it can protect tumor cells from chemotherapy- and radiation-induced damage, limiting therapeutic efficacy, yet it can also promote therapy-induced cell death when excessive or when it facilitates terminal differentiation and antigen presentation. In normal tissues, treatment-induced autophagy is generally cytoprotective and reduces toxicity, widening the therapeutic window. The opposing outcomes necessitate careful stratification of when to inhibit versus enhance autophagy in the clinic. This duality mirrors autophagy's broader role in cancer initiation versus progression.

label: S130 enhances CR effect
source_file: _document_ - The Beneficial and Adverse Effects of Autophagic Response to Caloric Restriction and Fasting.md
description: The small-molecule ATG4B inhibitor S130 blocks the cysteine protease required for LC3 processing and autophagosome maturation; when combined with caloric restriction, this inhibition shifts the balance toward apoptotic death in colorectal cancer cells. By preventing autophagic protection of tumor cells while CR imposes metabolic stress, S130 sensitizes malignancy to cell death. The synergy illustrates a therapeutic strategy of pairing CR or CR-mimetics with targeted autophagy inhibition in cancer. The approach exploits the reliance of some tumors on basal autophagy for survival.

label: P300
source_file: _document_ - The Beneficial and Adverse Effects of Autophagic Response to Caloric Restriction and Fasting.md
description: SIRT1 inhibits the coactivator p300 by deacetylation, dampening p300-dependent transcriptional programs.

label: ATG4B inhibiting autophagy
source_file: _document_ - The Beneficial and Adverse Effects of Autophagic Response to Caloric Restriction and Fasting.md
description: The acetyltransferase p300 acetylates ATG4B, an modification that inhibits its proteolytic activity required for LC3 lipidation and autophagosome formation, thereby restraining autophagy under normal conditions. This acetylation-dependent repression adds a transcriptional coactivator-derived control layer to core autophagy machinery beyond the well-studied phosphorylation circuits. Relief of p300-mediated acetylation during stress can de-repress ATG4B and facilitate autophagic flux. The finding situates autophagy regulation within the broader acetylome governed by p300/CBP.

label: Hallmarks of Cancer
description: Cancer is characterized by Hallmarks of Cancer. Cancer is a family of diseases driven by the stepwise acquisition of mutations and epimutations that confer proliferative autonomy, survival, and dissemination. The Hallmarks of Cancer are the enabling biological capabilities acquired during tumorigenesis, including sustained proliferation, evasion of death, and metastasis. The directionality runs from Hallmarks of Cancer toward Cancer, so Hallmarks of Cancer is the active agent and Cancer the recipient of the effect. Together these facts situate the relationship within the broader architecture of cancer biology, clarifying how the two entities connect as part of the hallmark or taxonomic framework.

label: Metabolic Reprogramming
description: Cancer undergoes Metabolic Reprogramming. Cancer is a family of diseases driven by the stepwise acquisition of mutations and epimutations that confer proliferative autonomy, survival, and dissemination. Metabolic reprogramming is the rewiring of nutrient uptake and bioenergetics that supplies building blocks and redox balance to proliferating tumors. The relationship is directional, with Cancer acting as the operative agent upon Metabolic Reprogramming rather than the reverse. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: Angiogenesis
description: Cancer induces Angiogenesis. Cancer is a family of diseases driven by the stepwise acquisition of mutations and epimutations that confer proliferative autonomy, survival, and dissemination. Angiogenesis is the sprouting of new vessels from preexisting vasculature that tumors must recruit to grow beyond a few millimeters and to metastasize. The relationship is directional, with Cancer acting as the operative agent upon Angiogenesis rather than the reverse. label: Wnt
description: β-catenin (Wnt pathway) transcriptionally represses the SIRT2 promoter, and SIRT2 reciprocally deacetylates β-catenin to destabilize it, so Wnt signaling opposes SIRT2 pathway activity and vice versa in intestinal and cancer cell contexts (BBA Mol Cell Res 2021).

label: JAK2

JAK2 is a cytokine-receptor-associated tyrosine kinase that phosphorylates STATs and is constitutively active in several myeloproliferative neoplasms. The directionality runs from JAK2 toward Cancer, so JAK2 is the active agent and Cancer the recipient of the effect. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: EGFR
description: Cancer is driven by EGFR. Cancer is a family of diseases driven by the stepwise acquisition of mutations and epimutations that confer proliferative autonomy, survival, and dissemination. EGFR is a receptor tyrosine kinase whose activating mutations and overexpression couple extracellular cues to proliferative and survival signaling. The directionality runs from EGFR toward Cancer, so EGFR is the active agent and Cancer the recipient of the effect. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: BRCA
description: Cancer is suppressed by BRCA. Cancer is a family of diseases driven by the stepwise acquisition of mutations and epimutations that confer proliferative autonomy, survival, and dissemination. BRCA1 and BRCA2 are tumor suppressors that orchestrate homology-directed repair of DNA double-strand breaks and genome stability. The directionality runs from BRCA toward Cancer, so BRCA is the active agent and Cancer the recipient of the effect. This restraint is biologically significant because it modulates the threshold at which the affected process engages, and when co-opted by tumors it fosters survival and treatment resistance that must be overcome therapeutically.

label: Ki-67
description: Ki-67 is expressed in all active phases of the cell cycle and absent in quiescent cells, making it a robust immunohistochemical readout of proliferation. A high Ki-67 labeling index correlates with aggressive biology and, in some tumors, informs adjuvant therapy decisions. The relationship is directional as a biomarker: proliferation evidences the tumor's growth fraction rather than causing it. It is particularly integrated into grading of breast and neuroendocrine neoplasms.

label: trastuzumab
description: Cancer is treated by trastuzumab. Cancer is a family of diseases driven by the stepwise acquisition of mutations and epimutations that confer proliferative autonomy, survival, and dissemination. Trastuzumab is a monoclonal antibody against HER2 that inhibits signaling and recruits immune effector mechanisms in HER2-positive breast cancer. The directionality runs from trastuzumab toward Cancer, so trastuzumab is the active agent and Cancer the recipient of the effect. Clinically, this positions the object as a therapeutic modality against the subject, though efficacy is shaped by biomarker selection and the eventual emergence of resistance.

label: melittin
description: Cancer is treated by melittin. Cancer is a family of diseases driven by the stepwise acquisition of mutations and epimutations that confer proliferative autonomy, survival, and dissemination. Melittin is the principal peptide of honeybee venom that permeabilizes membranes and suppresses oncogenic receptors and checkpoints. The directionality runs from melittin toward Cancer, so melittin is the active agent and Cancer the recipient of the effect. label: Nutlins
description: Cancer is treated by Nutlins. Cancer is a family of diseases driven by the stepwise acquisition of mutations and epimutations that confer proliferative autonomy, survival, and dissemination. Nutlins are cis-imidazoline small molecules that block the MDM2-p53 interface, stabilizing p53 to enforce arrest or apoptosis. The directionality runs from Nutlins toward Cancer, so Nutlins is the active agent and Cancer the recipient of the effect. Clinically, this positions the object as a therapeutic modality against the subject, though efficacy is shaped by biomarker selection and the eventual emergence of resistance.

label: BH3 mimetics
description: Cancer is treated by BH3 mimetics. Cancer is a family of diseases driven by the stepwise acquisition of mutations and epimutations that confer proliferative autonomy, survival, and dissemination. BH3 mimetics are small molecules that occupy the hydrophobic groove of anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 proteins, freeing Bax/Bak to kill tumor cells. The directionality runs from BH3 mimetics toward Cancer, so BH3 mimetics is the active agent and Cancer the recipient of the effect. Clinically, this positions the object as a therapeutic modality against the subject, though efficacy is shaped by biomarker selection and the eventual emergence of resistance.

label: BET inhibitors
description: Cancer is treated by BET inhibitors. Cancer is a family of diseases driven by the stepwise acquisition of mutations and epimutations that confer proliferative autonomy, survival, and dissemination. BET inhibitors displace bromodomain proteins such as BRD4 from acetylated chromatin, silencing MYC and inflammatory transcription programs. The directionality runs from BET inhibitors toward Cancer, so BET inhibitors is the active agent and Cancer the recipient of the effect. Clinically, this positions the object as a therapeutic modality against the subject, though efficacy is shaped by biomarker selection and the eventual emergence of resistance.

label: Integrins
description: FAK is activated by Integrins. Focal adhesion kinase transduces integrin and growth-factor signals into survival, migration, and angiogenesis and is overexpressed in many solid tumors. Integrins are transmembrane receptors that connect the extracellular matrix to the cytoskeleton and intracellular survival kinases. The directionality runs from Integrins toward FAK, so Integrins is the active agent and FAK the recipient of the effect. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: Intrinsic Pathway
description: Apoptosis has the pathway Intrinsic Pathway. Apoptosis is a genetically programmed, caspase-dependent form of cell death that dismantles cells without provoking inflammation. The intrinsic (mitochondrial) apoptotic pathway is initiated by intracellular damage and is gated at the outer mitochondrial membrane by the Bcl-2 family. The relationship is directional, with Apoptosis acting as the operative agent upon Intrinsic Pathway rather than the reverse. Together these facts situate the relationship within the broader architecture of cancer biology, clarifying how the two entities connect as part of the hallmark or taxonomic framework.

label: Extrinsic Pathway
description: Apoptosis has the pathway Extrinsic Pathway. Apoptosis is a genetically programmed, caspase-dependent form of cell death that dismantles cells without provoking inflammation. The extrinsic (death-receptor) apoptotic pathway is triggered by extracellular ligands engaging cell-surface death receptors and proceeds through the DISC. The relationship is directional, with Apoptosis acting as the operative agent upon Extrinsic Pathway rather than the reverse. Together these facts situate the relationship within the broader architecture of cancer biology, clarifying how the two entities connect as part of the hallmark or taxonomic framework.

label: Endoplasmic Reticulum Pathway
description: Apoptosis has the pathway Endoplasmic Reticulum Pathway. Apoptosis is a genetically programmed, caspase-dependent form of cell death that dismantles cells without provoking inflammation. The endoplasmic-reticulum stress pathway of apoptosis is initiated by unfolded-protein accumulation and engages CHOP and caspase-12. The relationship is directional, with Apoptosis acting as the operative agent upon Endoplasmic Reticulum Pathway rather than the reverse. Together these facts situate the relationship within the broader architecture of cancer biology, clarifying how the two entities connect as part of the hallmark or taxonomic framework.

label: Common Pathway
description: Apoptosis converges at Common Pathway. Apoptosis is a genetically programmed, caspase-dependent form of cell death that dismantles cells without provoking inflammation. The common execution phase of apoptosis is the point at which all initiation routes converge on effector caspases that proteolyze the cellular proteome. The relationship is directional, with Apoptosis acting as the operative agent upon Common Pathway rather than the reverse. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: Inhibitor of Apoptosis Proteins
description: Apoptosis is inhibited by Inhibitor of Apoptosis Proteins. Apoptosis is a genetically programmed, caspase-dependent form of cell death that dismantles cells without provoking inflammation. Inhibitor of Apoptosis Proteins (IAPs) are endogenous caspase-suppressor proteins that block cell death and are frequently co-opted by tumors. The directionality runs from Inhibitor of Apoptosis Proteins toward Apoptosis, so Inhibitor of Apoptosis Proteins is the active agent and Apoptosis the recipient of the effect. This restraint is biologically significant because it modulates the threshold at which the affected process engages, and when co-opted by tumors it fosters survival and treatment resistance that must be overcome therapeutically.

label: Bcl-2
source_file: _document_ - Apoptosis in cancer from pathogenesis to treatment.md
description: Anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 inhibits apoptosis, thereby opposing SIRT5's pro-survival species; in Table 3 Bcl-2 is listed among negative regulators of the SIRT5 pathway in contexts where SIRT5's effects depend on cell survival/Apoptosis signaling.

label: TRAIL
description: Apoptosis is induced by TRAIL. Apoptosis is a genetically programmed, caspase-dependent form of cell death that dismantles cells without provoking inflammation. TRAIL (TNFSF10) is a death ligand that engages DR4 and DR5 to initiate extrinsic apoptosis with relative selectivity for malignant cells. The directionality runs from TRAIL toward Apoptosis, so TRAIL is the active agent and Apoptosis the recipient of the effect. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: Gossypol
description: Apoptosis is induced by Gossypol. Apoptosis is a genetically programmed, caspase-dependent form of cell death that dismantles cells without provoking inflammation. Gossypol is a natural BH3-mimetic derived from cottonseed that, unusually, also engages Mcl-1. The directionality runs from Gossypol toward Apoptosis, so Gossypol is the active agent and Apoptosis the recipient of the effect. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: Bcl-2 family
description: Intrinsic Pathway is regulated by Bcl-2 family. The intrinsic (mitochondrial) apoptotic pathway is initiated by intracellular damage and is gated at the outer mitochondrial membrane by the Bcl-2 family. The Bcl-2 protein family comprises pro-apoptotic effectors (Bax, Bak) and BH3-only activators balanced against anti-apoptotic guardians (Bcl-2, Bcl-xL, Mcl-1, Bcl-w) that set the mitochondrial death threshold. The directionality runs from Bcl-2 family toward Intrinsic Pathway, so Bcl-2 family is the active agent and Intrinsic Pathway the recipient of the effect. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: MOMP
description: Intrinsic Pathway relates to MOMP through the relation involves. The intrinsic (mitochondrial) apoptotic pathway is initiated by intracellular damage and is gated at the outer mitochondrial membrane by the Bcl-2 family. Mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP) is the committed, largely irreversible step of intrinsic apoptosis that releases intermembrane-space proteins. The interaction is specific and directional within the cancer context. Understanding this link contributes to the broader map of tumor biology and potential intervention points.

label: Apoptosome
description: Intrinsic Pathway activates Apoptosome. The intrinsic (mitochondrial) apoptotic pathway is initiated by intracellular damage and is gated at the outer mitochondrial membrane by the Bcl-2 family. The apoptosome is a heptamer of Apaf-1, cytochrome c, and dATP that recruits and activates initiator caspase-9. The relationship is directional, with Intrinsic Pathway acting as the operative agent upon Apoptosome rather than the reverse. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: Caspase-9
description: Caspase-9, activated within the apoptosome, cleaves and activates executioner caspase-3 in the intrinsic (mitochondrial) apoptosis pathway. Directionally, caspase-9 sits upstream of caspase-3 activation. This propagates the death signal following mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilization, when cytochrome c is released to assemble the apoptosome. It is central to the intrinsic apoptotic cascade, which is regulated by the Bcl-2 family and by sirtuins that modulate pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins. The intrinsic pathway is the primary target of many cancer chemotherapies and of cytoprotective interventions.

label: XIAP
description: Intrinsic Pathway is inhibited by XIAP. The intrinsic (mitochondrial) apoptotic pathway is initiated by intracellular damage and is gated at the outer mitochondrial membrane by the Bcl-2 family. XIAP is the most potent mammalian IAP, directly inhibiting caspases-9, -3, and -7 and stabilized by survival kinases. The directionality runs from XIAP toward Intrinsic Pathway, so XIAP is the active agent and Intrinsic Pathway the recipient of the effect. This restraint is biologically significant because it modulates the threshold at which the affected process engages, and when co-opted by tumors it fosters survival and treatment resistance that must be overcome therapeutically.

label: DISC
description: Extrinsic Pathway forms DISC. The extrinsic (death-receptor) apoptotic pathway is triggered by extracellular ligands engaging cell-surface death receptors and proceeds through the DISC. The death-inducing signaling complex assembles on ligand-bound death receptors and converts procaspase-8/10 into active initiator caspases. The relationship is directional, with Extrinsic Pathway acting as the operative agent upon DISC rather than the reverse. The directness of this molecular event makes it a precise, often druggable point of control whose perturbation can decisively shift cell fate in cancer.

label: Caspase-8
description: Extrinsic Pathway activates Caspase-8. The extrinsic (death-receptor) apoptotic pathway is triggered by extracellular ligands engaging cell-surface death receptors and proceeds through the DISC. Caspase-8 is the initiator caspase of the extrinsic pathway and also gates the intrinsic pathway through Bid cleavage. The relationship is directional, with Extrinsic Pathway acting as the operative agent upon Caspase-8 rather than the reverse. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: SRC kinase
description: Extrinsic Pathway is suppressed by SRC kinase. The extrinsic (death-receptor) apoptotic pathway is triggered by extracellular ligands engaging cell-surface death receptors and proceeds through the DISC. SRC is a non-receptor tyrosine kinase that promotes survival and, notably, phosphorylates and inactivates caspase-8 and Bik. The directionality runs from SRC kinase toward Extrinsic Pathway, so SRC kinase is the active agent and Extrinsic Pathway the recipient of the effect. This restraint is biologically significant because it modulates the threshold at which the affected process engages, and when co-opted by tumors it fosters survival and treatment resistance that must be overcome therapeutically.

label: SHP1
description: Extrinsic Pathway is restored by SHP1. The extrinsic (death-receptor) apoptotic pathway is triggered by extracellular ligands engaging cell-surface death receptors and proceeds through the DISC. SHP1 is a protein tyrosine phosphatase that dephosphorylates and reactivates caspase-8, restoring death-receptor-induced apoptosis. The directionality runs from SHP1 toward Extrinsic Pathway, so SHP1 is the active agent and Extrinsic Pathway the recipient of the effect. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: Bak
description: MOMP is driven by Bak. Mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP) is the committed, largely irreversible step of intrinsic apoptosis that releases intermembrane-space proteins. Bak is a pro-apoptotic Bcl-2 effector anchored at the mitochondrial outer membrane that cooperates with Bax to execute MOMP. The directionality runs from Bak toward MOMP, so Bak is the active agent and MOMP the recipient of the effect. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: Mcl-1
description: MOMP is inhibited by Mcl-1. Mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP) is the committed, largely irreversible step of intrinsic apoptosis that releases intermembrane-space proteins. Mcl-1 is a labile anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family protein whose rapid turnover makes it a frequent, difficult-to-target resistance determinant in cancer. The directionality runs from Mcl-1 toward MOMP, so Mcl-1 is the active agent and MOMP the recipient of the effect. This restraint is biologically significant because it modulates the threshold at which the affected process engages, and when co-opted by tumors it fosters survival and treatment resistance that must be overcome therapeutically.

label: Smac DIABLO
description: MOMP releases Smac-DIABLO. Mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP) is the committed, largely irreversible step of intrinsic apoptosis that releases intermembrane-space proteins. Smac/DIABLO is released from mitochondria during MOMP and unleashes caspases by binding the BIR domains of IAPs. The relationship is directional, with MOMP acting as the operative agent upon Smac-DIABLO rather than the reverse. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: Bim
description: MOMP is inhibited by Bim. Mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP) is the committed, largely irreversible step of intrinsic apoptosis that releases intermembrane-space proteins. Bim is a sentinel BH3-only protein sequestered at microtubules that is released by stress to directly activate Bax/Bak. The directionality runs from Bim toward MOMP, so Bim is the active agent and MOMP the recipient of the effect. This restraint is biologically significant because it modulates the threshold at which the affected process engages, and when co-opted by tumors it fosters survival and treatment resistance that must be overcome therapeutically.

label: Bid
description: MOMP is inhibited by Bid. Mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP) is the committed, largely irreversible step of intrinsic apoptosis that releases intermembrane-space proteins. Bid is a BH3-only protein cleaved by caspase-8 into truncated Bid, physically linking the extrinsic and intrinsic apoptotic routes. The directionality runs from Bid toward MOMP, so Bid is the active agent and MOMP the recipient of the effect. This restraint is biologically significant because it modulates the threshold at which the affected process engages, and when co-opted by tumors it fosters survival and treatment resistance that must be overcome therapeutically.

label: Apaf-1
description: Apoptosome is composed of Apaf-1. The apoptosome is a heptamer of Apaf-1, cytochrome c, and dATP that recruits and activates initiator caspase-9. Apaf-1 is the scaffolding adaptor of the apoptosome, containing CARD, NB-ARC, and WD40 domains that bind cytochrome c and recruit procaspase-9. The directionality runs from Apaf-1 toward Apoptosome, so Apaf-1 is the active agent and Apoptosome the recipient of the effect. Together these facts situate the relationship within the broader architecture of cancer biology, clarifying how the two entities connect as part of the hallmark or taxonomic framework.

label: Fas
description: DISC is formed by Fas. The death-inducing signaling complex assembles on ligand-bound death receptors and converts procaspase-8/10 into active initiator caspases. Fas (CD95) is a death receptor whose ligation by FasL initiates the extrinsic apoptotic pathway through DISC assembly. The directionality runs from Fas toward DISC, so Fas is the active agent and DISC the recipient of the effect. The directness of this molecular event makes it a precise, often druggable point of control whose perturbation can decisively shift cell fate in cancer.

label: DR4
description: DISC is formed by DR4. The death-inducing signaling complex assembles on ligand-bound death receptors and converts procaspase-8/10 into active initiator caspases. DR4 (TRAIL-R1) is a death receptor that binds TRAIL and nucleates the DISC to initiate extrinsic apoptosis. The directionality runs from DR4 toward DISC, so DR4 is the active agent and DISC the recipient of the effect. The directness of this molecular event makes it a precise, often druggable point of control whose perturbation can decisively shift cell fate in cancer.

label: DR5
description: DISC is formed by DR5. The death-inducing signaling complex assembles on ligand-bound death receptors and converts procaspase-8/10 into active initiator caspases. DR5 (TRAIL-R2) is a death receptor that binds TRAIL and nucleates the DISC to initiate extrinsic apoptosis, often more prominently than DR4. The directionality runs from DR5 toward DISC, so DR5 is the active agent and DISC the recipient of the effect. The directness of this molecular event makes it a precise, often druggable point of control whose perturbation can decisively shift cell fate in cancer.

label: FADD
description: DISC uses FADD. The death-inducing signaling complex assembles on ligand-bound death receptors and converts procaspase-8/10 into active initiator caspases. FADD is the core death-adaptor protein of the DISC that bridges death receptors to procaspase-8 via its death domain and DED. The relationship is directional, with DISC acting as the operative agent upon FADD rather than the reverse. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: Puma
description: Bcl-2 family includes Puma. The Bcl-2 protein family comprises pro-apoptotic effectors (Bax, Bak) and BH3-only activators balanced against anti-apoptotic guardians (Bcl-2, Bcl-xL, Mcl-1, Bcl-w) that set the mitochondrial death threshold. Puma is a p53-inducible BH3-only protein that binds and neutralizes essentially all anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 relatives to license mitochondrial death. The relationship is directional, with Bcl-2 family acting as the operative agent upon Puma rather than the reverse. Together these facts situate the relationship within the broader architecture of cancer biology, clarifying how the two entities connect as part of the hallmark or taxonomic framework.

label: Noxa
description: Bcl-2 family includes Noxa. The Bcl-2 protein family comprises pro-apoptotic effectors (Bax, Bak) and BH3-only activators balanced against anti-apoptotic guardians (Bcl-2, Bcl-xL, Mcl-1, Bcl-w) that set the mitochondrial death threshold. Noxa is a p53-inducible BH3-only protein with selective affinity for Mcl-1 and A1, sensitizing cells to mitochondrial apoptosis. The relationship is directional, with Bcl-2 family acting as the operative agent upon Noxa rather than the reverse. Together these facts situate the relationship within the broader architecture of cancer biology, clarifying how the two entities connect as part of the hallmark or taxonomic framework.

label: Lamins
description: Caspase-3 cleaves Lamins. Caspase-3 is the principal executioner caspase that cleaves hundreds of substrates to produce the apoptotic phenotype. Lamins are the intermediate-filament proteins of the nuclear lamina whose cleavage by caspases drives nuclear collapse during apoptosis. The relationship is directional, with Caspase-3 acting as the operative agent upon Lamins rather than the reverse. The directness of this molecular event makes it a precise, often druggable point of control whose perturbation can decisively shift cell fate in cancer.

label: ICAD
description: Caspase-3 cleaves ICAD. Caspase-3 is the principal executioner caspase that cleaves hundreds of substrates to produce the apoptotic phenotype. ICAD is the inhibitor of caspase-activated DNase that, upon caspase-3 cleavage, releases CAD to fragment nuclear DNA. The relationship is directional, with Caspase-3 acting as the operative agent upon ICAD rather than the reverse. The directness of this molecular event makes it a precise, often druggable point of control whose perturbation can decisively shift cell fate in cancer.

label: LYN
description: Caspase-8 is inhibited by LYN. Caspase-8 is the initiator caspase of the extrinsic pathway and also gates the intrinsic pathway through Bid cleavage. LYN is a Src-family kinase that, like SRC and FYN, can phosphorylate and inactivate caspase-8 to promote cell survival. The directionality runs from LYN toward Caspase-8, so LYN is the active agent and Caspase-8 the recipient of the effect. This restraint is biologically significant because it modulates the threshold at which the affected process engages, and when co-opted by tumors it fosters survival and treatment resistance that must be overcome therapeutically.

label: c-ABL
description: Caspase-9 is activated by c-ABL. Caspase-9 is the mitochondrial initiator caspase activated by the apoptosome to launch the execution phase. c-ABL is a tyrosine kinase that, upon genotoxic stress, can phosphorylate and activate caspase-9 to promote apoptosis. The directionality runs from c-ABL toward Caspase-9, so c-ABL is the active agent and Caspase-9 the recipient of the effect. This directional link makes the interaction a meaningful node in tumor biology, with implications for understanding disease progression and for identifying therapeutic or biomarker opportunities.

label: Caspase-7
description: Inhibitor of Apoptosis Proteins relates to Caspase-7 through the relation inhibit. Inhibitor of Apoptosis Proteins (IAPs) are endogenous caspase-suppressor proteins that block cell death and are frequently co-opted by tumors. Caspase-7 is an executioner caspase closely related to caspase-3 that contributes to the proteolytic demolition of the cell. The interaction is specific and directional within the cancer context. Understanding this link contributes to the broader map of tumor biology and potential intervention points.

label: TBK1
description: XIAP is degraded by TBK1. XIAP is the most potent mammalian IAP, directly inhibiting caspases-9, -3, and -7 and stabilized by survival kinases. TBK1 is a kinase of the innate immune pathway that phosphorylates XIAP to trigger its autoubiquitination and degradation. The directionality runs from TBK1 toward XIAP, so TBK1 is the active agent and XIAP the recipient of the effect. This restraint is biologically significant because it modulates the threshold at which the affected process engages, and when co-opted by tumors it fosters survival and treatment resistance that must be overcome therapeutically.

label: miR-24
description: XIAP is downregulated by miR-24. XIAP is the most potent mammalian IAP, directly inhibiting caspases-9, -3, and -7 and stabilized by survival kinases. miR-24 is a microRNA that targets several anti-apoptotic and cell-cycle mRNAs, including XIAP, to lower the death threshold. The directionality runs from miR-24 toward XIAP, so miR-24 is the active agent and XIAP the recipient of the effect. This restraint is biologically significant because it modulates the threshold at which the affected process engages, and when co-opted by tumors it fosters survival and treatment resistance that must be overcome therapeutically.

label: miR-7
description: XIAP is downregulated by miR-7. XIAP is the most potent mammalian IAP, directly inhibiting caspases-9, -3, and -7 and stabilized by survival kinases. miR-7 is a microRNA with tumor-suppressive roles that downregulates survival proteins such as XIAP and EGFR signaling. The directionality runs from miR-7 toward XIAP, so miR-7 is the active agent and XIAP the recipient of the effect. This restraint is biologically significant because it modulates the threshold at which the affected process engages, and when co-opted by tumors it fosters survival and treatment resistance that must be overcome therapeutically.

label: Survivin
description: In a mouse liver cancer model, increased SIRT6 expression reduces survivin expression by deacetylating H3K9Ac at the survivin promoter, and this induces apoptosis during cancer initiation. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of survivin suppression and prevention of tumor initiation. By silencing survivin, an anti-apoptotic factor, SIRT6 removes a key block to programmed cell death in early tumor cells. This allows damaged or transformed cells to undergo apoptosis rather than expand into tumors. The finding links SIRT6's epigenetic control of a critical survival gene to its tumor-suppressive activity in the liver.

label: MDM2
description: p53 is inhibited by MDM2. p53 is the archetypal tumor-suppressor transcription factor that integrates stress signals into cell-cycle arrest, senescence, or apoptosis. MDM2 is the principal E3 ubiquitin ligase and transcriptional antagonist that keeps p53 quiescent in unstressed cells. The directionality runs from MDM2 toward p53, so MDM2 is the active agent and p53 the recipient of the effect.
