IRAK4 then phosphorylates IRAK1/IRAK2, propagating the signal toward TRAF6 and TAK1 activation. This recruitment is a conserved early event in TLR/IL-1R pathways and is essential for downstream NF-kB and AP-1 signaling. In senescence it initiates the cascade that licenses SASP transcription, making IRAK4 a potential target for dampening IL-1-driven inflammation and the myddosome architecture ensures rapid, robust signal propagation.

label: IRAK1
description: Active IRAK4 phosphorylates IRAK1, which then recruits TRAF6 through its C-terminal TRAF6-binding motifs, extending the myddosome signaling complex. This step connects the receptor-proximal kinases to E3 ubiquitin ligase activity and TAK1 activation, ultimately driving NF-kB and MAPK signaling. In senescence, IRAK1 is required for full SASP establishment, linking the IL-1R pathway to the secretome. The relationship is a standard component of IL-1R/TLR signal propagation and is well validated biochemically.

label: Myddosome
description: MyD88 assembles into the helical oligomeric myddosome with IRAK4 and IRAK1/2, serving as the scaffolding platform that activates downstream kinases such as TAK1 and transcription factors such as NF-kB. This supramolecular complex is the mechanistic core of IL-1R/TLR signaling and is assembled through death-domain homotypic interactions. In senescence, myddosome formation underlies IL-1alpha-driven SASP, translating IL-1 receptor engagement into inflammatory transcription. The assembly is a defining structural feature of MyD88-dependent signaling and a validated drug target.

label: Senescent Cells to Macrophages
description: Senescent-cell surface IL-1alpha engages IL-1R on macrophages, recruiting MyD88 to activate NF-kB and amplify SASP both in the sender cell through autocrine signaling and in recruited immune cells through paracrine signaling. This bridges the senescent cell and the macrophage through IL-1R/MyD88 signaling, propagating inflammation across the tissue. The relationship situates MyD88 at the interface of senescence and innate immunity and explains how local senescence ignites broader inflammatory responses. It is a key mechanism of SASP-driven immune amplification.

label: Myeloid-Derived Suppressor Cells
description: Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) are a heterogeneous population of immature myeloid cells with potent immunosuppressive activity, expanded under pathological stress including cancer and chronic inflammation. Their classification reflects an arrested differentiation state rather than a single lineage, with polymorphonuclear and monocytic subsets recognized. In senescence contexts, MDSCs are recruited by SASP factors and blunt anti-tumor and anti-senescence immunity, shifting the immune balance away from clearance. They represent a key immunosuppressive cell type bridging aging, inflammation, and cancer.

label: Immature Myeloid Cell
description: Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) are a heterogeneous population of immature myeloid cells with potent immunosuppressive activity, expanded under pathological stress including cancer and chronic inflammation. Their classification reflects an arrested differentiation state rather than a single lineage, with polymorphonuclear and monocytic subsets recognized. In senescence contexts, MDSCs are recruited by SASP factors and blunt anti-tumor and anti-senescence immunity, shifting the immune balance away from clearance. They represent a key immunosuppressive cell type bridging aging, inflammation, and cancer.

label: GM-CSF
description: The SASP factor GM-CSF stimulates myeloid expansion and biases differentiation toward immunosuppressive MDSCs, recruiting them into senescent and tumor tissues. GM-CSF thereby shapes the myeloid compartment to be tolerogenic and arrest-promoting, exemplifying SASP-driven paracrine reprogramming of immune lineage fate. The relationship links a specific SASP cytokine to myeloid suppressor accumulation and is a recognized driver of MDSC expansion in inflammation and cancer. Blocking GM-CSF signaling can reduce MDSC generation.

label: Caspase-5
description: Caspase-5 (human) is the inducible noncanonical effector caspase that cleaves IL-1alpha and gasdermin D to drive SASP and pyroptosis. Its activation is essential for the noncanonical inflammasome's role in senescence, and its expression is induced by interferons and controlled upstream by the cGAS-STING pathway. The relationship positions caspase-5 as the enzymatic executor of the pathway in human cells. It is supported by cleavage-site and loss-of-function studies showing reduced SASP after CASP5 knockdown.

label: Caspase-11
description: Caspase-11 (mouse) is the noncanonical effector caspase that cleaves IL-1alpha and gasdermin D, paralleling human caspase-4/5. It is activated by cytosolic LPS and drives SASP establishment in murine senescence models, and it is required for SASP-driven immune clearance of senescent hepatocytes in vivo. The relationship establishes the species-specific executor of the noncanonical pathway in mice. It is a well-supported component of senescence inflammasome biology, with genetic deficiency of the enzyme blunting IL-1alpha processing and downstream secretome output.

label: Gasdermin D
description: Active caspase-4/5/11 cleave gasdermin D between its N-terminal pore-forming domain and C-terminal inhibitory domain, releasing the N-terminal fragment to form plasma-membrane pores. This drives inflammatory cell death (pyroptosis) and IL-1alpha release in senescent and responding cells, and the pores also permit release of IL-1beta and IL-18 prior to membrane rupture. The relationship is the canonical execution step of noncanonical inflammasome signaling and links the pathway to both cell death and SASP amplification, creating a feed-forward inflammatory loop in senescent tissue.

label: LPS
description: The hexa-acylated lipid A of LPS binds directly to the CARD domain of caspase-4/5/11, inducing their dimerization and activation, the defining trigger of the noncanonical inflammasome. While classically microbial, this mechanism can be engaged in senescence-associated inflammatory contexts. The relationship is the canonical activation mode of the pathway and links Gram-negative sensing to caspase activation. Because the caspases themselves are the sensors, no upstream receptor is required for this pathway.

label: Paracrine Reprogramming
description: Paracrine reprogramming is the biological process by which SASP factors alter the differentiation status and fate of neighbouring cells, pushing them toward stemness, EMT, or altered lineage commitment. Distinct from paracrine senescence, which induces growth arrest, it remodels recipient identity and is dose- and time-dependent, with acute exposure promoting plasticity and chronic exposure driving fibrosis and cancer stemness. The process is mediated by cytokines such as IL-6, TGFbeta, and VEGF family members. It expands the non-cell-autonomous influence of senescent cells beyond growth arrest.

label: Biological Process
description: Paracrine reprogramming is the biological process by which SASP factors alter the differentiation status and fate of neighbouring cells, pushing them toward stemness, EMT, or altered lineage commitment. Distinct from paracrine senescence, which induces growth arrest, it remodels recipient identity and is dose- and time-dependent, with acute exposure promoting plasticity and chronic exposure driving fibrosis and cancer stemness. The process is mediated by cytokines such as IL-6, TGFbeta, and VEGF family members. It expands the non-cell-autonomous influence of senescent cells beyond growth arrest.

label: Stemness
description: IL-6 is a central driver of in vivo reprogramming toward pluripotency and stemness via JAK/STAT3 signaling, promoting a dedifferentiated, stem-like state in recipient cells. This underlies both wound-healing plasticity and, pathologically, cancer stemness, with STAT3 transcriptionally sustaining stemness factors such as OCT4, NANOG, and SOX2. The relationship links a core SASP cytokine to cell-fate reprogramming and is supported by reprogramming and cancer-stemness studies. Blocking IL-6/JAK/STAT3 signaling can interrupt this reprogramming.

label: Chronic SASP
description: Chronic SASP, through IL-6 and IL-8 via JAK/STAT3, promotes cancer stem-cell traits and expands the CSC pool in neighbouring epithelial and tumour cells, enhancing tumour initiation and relapse potential. By driving stemness and survival, the persistent secretome fosters malignant progression and therapy resistance. The relationship is a key mechanism by which senescence can become tumor-promoting and is supported by cancer-stemness and senescence co-culture studies. It motivates the one-two punch strategy of senescence induction followed by senolytic clearance.

label: Myeloid Differentiation
description: GM-CSF and CCL2 skew myeloid differentiation toward immunosuppressive MDSCs and specific macrophage phenotypes, reshaping the myeloid compartment in senescence and cancer. This biases haematopoiesis away from inflammatory resolution toward tolerance and suppression, exemplifying SASP-driven paracrine reprogramming of immune lineage fate. The relationship links SASP factors to myeloid lineage outcomes and is supported by myeloid-differentiation and tumor-immunology studies. Targeting these factors can restore protective myeloid responses.

label: VEGFc
description: VEGF-C is a member of the VEGF family of cysteine-knot growth factors, structurally related to VEGF-A but with distinct receptor usage and lymphatic specificity. Its classification situates it among the growth-factor arm of the SASP, and in senescence it is an early-induced angiogenic and lymphangiogenic factor. The family membership underpins its receptor interactions, particularly with VEGFR-3 and, after proteolytic processing, VEGFR-2. This dual receptor capacity distinguishes its vascular functions from other family members.

label: VEGF Family
description: VEGF-C is a member of the VEGF family of cysteine-knot growth factors, structurally related to VEGF-A but with distinct receptor usage and lymphatic specificity. Its classification situates it among the growth-factor arm of the SASP, and in senescence it is an early-induced angiogenic and lymphangiogenic factor. The family membership underpins its receptor interactions, particularly with VEGFR-3 and, after proteolytic processing, VEGFR-2. This dual receptor capacity distinguishes its vascular functions from other family members.

label: VEGFR3
description: VEGF-C signals primarily through VEGFR-3 on lymphatic endothelium, promoting lymphangiogenesis and lymphatic vessel sprouting. This receptor usage distinguishes VEGF-C from VEGF-A's preferential VEGFR2 engagement and underlies its role in lymphatic remodeling around senescent tissue. In the SASP, VEGF-C-VEGFR3 signaling contributes to lymphatic vessel formation and potentially to immune cell trafficking routes. The relationship is a canonical VEGF-C function well established in lymphatic biology.

label: VEGFR2
description: At higher concentrations or after proteolytic processing, VEGF-C also engages VEGFR2 on blood vascular endothelium, supporting angiogenesis in addition to its lymphatic actions. This dual receptor usage broadens its angiogenic potential within the SASP and explains how VEGF-C can drive both blood- and lymphatic-vessel formation, depending on the local processing environment. The relationship is supported by receptor-binding and processing studies, and it positions processed VEGF-C as a shared ligand across the two receptor systems with distinct downstream signaling outputs.

label: Lymphangiogenesis
description: Full-length VEGF-C preferentially activates VEGFR-3 and promotes lymphatic vessel sprouting, driving lymphangiogenesis. In senescence, this contributes to lymphatic remodeling and potentially to immune cell trafficking routes, shaping how immune cells access senescent tissue. The relationship is the canonical lymphangiogenic function of VEGF-C and expands the vascular consequences of the SASP beyond blood vessels. It is supported by studies of lymphatic development and tumor-associated lymphangiogenesis.

label: DNA Replication Stress
source_file: _document_ - Small molecule compounds that induce cellular senescence.md
description: Constitutive oncogenic RAS signaling pushes cells into hyper-replication, where DNA replication forks are initiated at excessive frequency and become stalled or collapsed. This generates single-stranded DNA gaps and replication stress that activate checkpoint kinases ATR and ATM, converging on p53 stabilization. The relationship is a central mechanism linking oncogene activation to senescence-inducing damage and is well established in OIS biology. It explains how proliferative overload is converted into a senescence signal.

label: ATR
source_file: _document_ - Small molecule compounds that induce cellular senescence.md
description: Stalled or collapsed replication forks generate single-stranded DNA gaps that engage the ATR-CHK1 cascade, activating a checkpoint that senses replication stress. In oncogene-induced senescence, ATR signaling contributes to arrest and senescence establishment by stabilizing p53 and enforcing cell-cycle exit. The relationship is a canonical DNA-damage-checkpoint response and links oncogene-driven hyper-replication to cell-cycle enforcement. ATR is considered the primary sensor of replication stress.

label: CDKN2A
description: OIS derepresses the CDKN2A locus to upregulate p16INK4A, reinforcing the p16/Rb cell-cycle arrest that locks the benign lesion in a permanent frozen, tumor-suppressive state. This p16-mediated arrest is the mechanistic backbone of the protective benign nevus.

label: Sir2 (yeast)
description: Sir2 (silent information regulator 2) is the founding member of the sirtuin family, first identified in Saccharomyces cerevisiae as a regulator of mating-type locus silencing and replicative lifespan. The seven mammalian paralogues SIRT1–SIRT7 evolved from this ancestral NAD+-dependent deacetylase, retaining the conserved catalytic core while diversifying in subcellular localization and substrate repertoire. This phylogenetic continuity means insights from yeast Sir2 historically informed mammalian sirtuin biology, although the mammalian enzymes acquired lineage-specific regulatory domains. The relationship is directional: yeast Sir2 is the evolutionary precursor, not a downstream effector, of the SIRT1–7 family.

label: Sirtuins (SIRT1–7)
description: Sir2 (silent information regulator 2) is the founding member of the sirtuin family, first identified in Saccharomyces cerevisiae as a regulator of mating-type locus silencing and replicative lifespan. The seven mammalian paralogues SIRT1–SIRT7 evolved from this ancestral NAD+-dependent deacetylase, retaining the conserved catalytic core while diversifying in subcellular localization and substrate repertoire. This phylogenetic continuity means insights from yeast Sir2 historically informed mammalian sirtuin biology, although the mammalian enzymes acquired lineage-specific regulatory domains. The relationship is directional: yeast Sir2 is the evolutionary precursor, not a downstream effector, of the SIRT1–7 family.

label: Mono-ADP-ribosyl transferases
description: Beyond deacetylation, several sirtuins catalyze mono-ADP-ribosylation, transferring the ADP-ribose moiety of NAD+ onto target proteins without removing an acetyl group. SIRT4 and SIRT6 prominently display this mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activity, with SIRT6 using it to recruit heterochromatin proteins such as KAP1/HP1α. The directionality is that NAD+ is the donor and the target lysine (or other residue) is the acceptor, producing a mono-ADP-ribosylated product rather than free OAADPr. Biologically, ADP-ribosylation allows sirtuins to regulate processes—such as DNA repair and LINE-1 repression—distinct from their deacetylase functions.

label: Sirtuin deacetylation reaction
description: During the sirtuin-catalyzed deacetylation of a lysine, NAD+ is cleaved between its nicotinamide and ADP-ribose moieties, and the acetyl group is transferred to the ADP-ribose to generate 2'-O-acetyl-ADP-ribose (OAADPr) plus free nicotinamide. OAADPr is a stoichiometric by-product, released in equimolar amounts with the deacetylated substrate on every catalytic cycle. This molecule is not merely waste: it binds and activates the TRPM2 cation channel, linking sirtuin activity to calcium signaling and cellular stress responses. A caveat is that OAADPr accumulation can itself feed back on cellular metabolism, and its levels reflect the integrated deacetylase flux of the cell.

label: OAADPr (2'-O-acetyl-ADP-ribose)
description: During the sirtuin-catalyzed deacetylation of a lysine, NAD+ is cleaved between its nicotinamide and ADP-ribose moieties, and the acetyl group is transferred to the ADP-ribose to generate 2'-O-acetyl-ADP-ribose (OAADPr) plus free nicotinamide. OAADPr is a stoichiometric by-product, released in equimolar amounts with the deacetylated substrate on every catalytic cycle. This molecule is not merely waste: it binds and activates the TRPM2 cation channel, linking sirtuin activity to calcium signaling and cellular stress responses. A caveat is that OAADPr accumulation can itself feed back on cellular metabolism, and its levels reflect the integrated deacetylase flux of the cell.

label: OAADPr
description: OAADPr (2'-O-acetyl-ADP-ribose) binds to the cytoplasmic N-terminal domain of the TRPM2 non-selective cation channel, promoting its opening and calcium influx into the cytosol. Because OAADPr is generated directly by sirtuin deacetylase activity, TRPM2 activation acts as a sensor of cellular sirtuin flux and NAD+ utilization. The directionality is unidirectional under basal conditions: sirtuin activity produces OAADPr, which then gates TRPM2, rather than TRPM2 regulating sirtuins. This coupling provides a mechanistic link between metabolic state, redox stress, and calcium-dependent processes such as insulin secretion and apoptotic signaling.

label: TRPM2
description: OAADPr (2'-O-acetyl-ADP-ribose) binds to the cytoplasmic N-terminal domain of the TRPM2 non-selective cation channel, promoting its opening and calcium influx into the cytosol. Because OAADPr is generated directly by sirtuin deacetylase activity, TRPM2 activation acts as a sensor of cellular sirtuin flux and NAD+ utilization. The directionality is unidirectional under basal conditions: sirtuin activity produces OAADPr, which then gates TRPM2, rather than TRPM2 regulating sirtuins. This coupling provides a mechanistic link between metabolic state, redox stress, and calcium-dependent processes such as insulin secretion and apoptotic signaling.

label: Nucleus (euchromatin)
description: SIRT1 is the predominant nuclear sirtuin and is enriched at euchromatic regions, where it deacetylates both histones and many transcriptional regulators to shape gene expression. Its nuclear residence allows it to directly access chromatin and nuclear factors such as p53, FOXO, NF-κB, and PGC-1α. Subcellular localization is dynamic and can shift toward DNA double-strand break foci during genotoxic stress, reflecting its role in DNA repair. A caveat is that a fraction of SIRT1 is also cytosolic, so 'nuclear' describes its dominant but not exclusive compartment.

label: Cytoplasm
description: SIRT2 is the predominantly cytoplasmic sirtuin and is most abundant in the cytosol, where it deacetylates α-tubulin and a range of metabolic and regulatory proteins. Its localization is cell-cycle regulated, with SIRT2 accumulating and being hyperphosphorylated as cells transit the G2/M boundary. The cytoplasmic residence underpins its roles in microtubule dynamics, mitosis, and cytoplasmic autophagy regulation rather than direct chromatin modification. Note that SIRT2 can also shuttle to the nucleus under certain stress conditions, so localization is not absolute.

label: SIRT4
description: SIRT4 resides in the mitochondrial matrix and acts mainly as a mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase on metabolic enzymes such as GDH and MTPα rather than as a conventional deacetylase. Its mitochondrial localization enables direct control of amino-acid and fatty-acid fueling of the TCA cycle, braking anaplerosis and oxidative catabolism. Directionally, SIRT4 is positioned to restrain mitochondrial anabolism, reducing nutrient-driven ATP generation and insulin secretion under replete conditions. This braking role complements SIRT3, which promotes oxidative catabolism, so the SIRT3/SIRT4 balance determines whether mitochondria oxidize or conserve fuel.

label: SIRT5
description: SIRT5 localizes to the mitochondrial matrix and is specialized for removing lysine succinyl, malonyl, and glutaryl groups from metabolic enzymes including CPS1, HMGCS2, and enzymes of β-oxidation and the TCA cycle. Its mitochondrial residence makes it a key regulator of catabolic flux during fasting, coordinating nitrogen clearance, ketogenesis, and fatty-acid oxidation. Through desuccinylation it optimizes energy production and redox balance, activating urea-cycle and lipid-catabolism machinery when nutrient supply demands it.

label: Nucleus (heterochromatin)
description: SIRT6 is a nuclear sirtuin enriched at heterochromatic and telomeric regions, where it deacetylates H3K9 and H3K56 and performs mono-ADP-ribosylation of KAP1. Its heterochromatin association is critical for genome stability, telomere maintenance, and suppression of repetitive elements such as LINE-1. SIRT6 thus integrates chromatin regulation with metabolic control of glycolysis, DNA repair, and inflammation. Loss of SIRT6 produces a pronounced premature-aging phenotype, highlighting its non-redundant role in the nucleus.

label: SIRT7
description: SIRT7 is concentrated in the nucleolus, the site of ribosomal DNA transcription and ribosome biogenesis, where it deacetylates histone H3K18 and regulates RNA polymerase I. Its nucleolar residence positions it to control rRNA synthesis and, consequently, protein synthetic capacity and growth. SIRT7 also deacetylates extra-nucleolar targets such as GATA4 and SMAD3, linking it to cardiac and fibrotic pathways. Deficiency of SIRT7 yields extensive myocardial fibrosis and cardiomyopathy, revealing its importance in stress responses of the heart.

label: Nucleolus
description: SIRT7 is concentrated in the nucleolus, the site of ribosomal DNA transcription and ribosome biogenesis, where it deacetylates histone H3K18 and regulates RNA polymerase I. Its nucleolar residence positions it to control rRNA synthesis and, consequently, protein synthetic capacity and growth. SIRT7 also deacetylates extra-nucleolar targets such as GATA4 and SMAD3, linking it to cardiac and fibrotic pathways. Deficiency of SIRT7 yields extensive myocardial fibrosis and cardiomyopathy, revealing its importance in stress responses of the heart.

label: ADP-ribosylation
description: SIRT4 functions principally as a mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase, using NAD+ to attach a single ADP-ribose group to target lysines rather than removing acetyl marks. Its best-characterized ADP-ribosylation target is glutamate dehydrogenase, whose activity it inhibits to dampen amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion. This enzymatic orientation means SIRT4 generally acts as a metabolic suppressor within mitochondria, opposing anabolic and growth signals. A caveat is that SIRT4's deacetylase activity is weak in vitro, so ADP-ribosylation is its physiologically dominant modality.

label: Drosophila melanogaster
description: Dietary restriction in Drosophila extends lifespan and, as in yeast, this benefit requires the dSir2 (Sir2) gene, indicating evolutionary conservation of the sirtuin-mediated CR pathway. The effect is thought to operate through improved protein homeostasis, stress resistance, and metabolic efficiency rather than simple calorie shortage. Directionally, reduced nutrient signaling upstream engages dSir2 to produce the longevity phenotype. Caveats include that the magnitude and requirement vary with sex, genetic background, and the precise restriction paradigm used.

label: SIRT1 expression
description: In rodents, caloric restriction raises SIRT1 levels in multiple tissues, and this elevation is linked to reduced inflammatory and oxidative responses. Higher SIRT1 expression translates into enhanced deacetylation of targets such as NF-κB, FOXO, and PGC-1α, promoting stress resistance and metabolic health. The directionality is that CR is the upstream stimulus and increased SIRT1 abundance/activity the downstream mediator. This adaptation is considered a key explanation for the anti-aging and disease-protective effects of CR in mammals.

label: NAD+/nicotinamide ratio (brain)
description: Caloric restriction elevates the brain NAD+/nicotinamide ratio, which both supplies more co-substrate for sirtuins and relieves nicotinamide-mediated feedback inhibition of SIRT1. The resulting gain in sirtuin activity supports neuronal stress resistance, mitochondrial function, and suppression of neuroinflammatory signaling. The relationship is directional: CR shifts the ratio upward, which then potentiates sirtuin-dependent protective programs. This mechanism is frequently invoked to explain CR's protective effects against age-related cognitive decline and neurodegenerative pathology.

label: SIR2 overexpression (yeast)
description: Integration of an extra SIR2 copy in yeast increases replicative lifespan by up to about 30%, implicating Sir2 dosage directly in longevity. The mechanism involves reinforced silencing at rDNA repeats, which reduces spurious recombination and the accumulation of extrachromosomal rDNA circles that drive aging. This is a gain-of-function, directional relationship: more Sir2 yields longer lifespan, though the effect saturates and very high doses can be detrimental. The finding established the foundational idea that boosting sirtuin activity can extend lifespan in a simple eukaryote.

label: sir-2.1 overexpression (C. elegans)
description: A chromosomal duplication that increases sir-2.1 dosage in C. elegans extends lifespan by up to approximately 50%, paralleling the yeast finding in a multicellular organism. The longevity effect depends on intact insulin/IGF-1-like signaling, because sir-2.1 acts downstream of the DAF-2 pathway to promote stress resistance. The relationship is directional: elevated sir-2.1 produces the lifespan gain. A key caveat is that the requirement for DAF-16 (FOXO) ties sirtuin longevity to the conserved FOXO transcription-factor network.

label: sir-2.1 lifespan extension
description: The lifespan extension produced by sir-2.1 overexpression in C. elegans is strictly dependent on the forkhead transcription factor DAF-16, the worm FOXO ortholog. DAF-16 is the downstream effector that induces stress-resistance and xenobiotic-detoxification genes once sir-2.1 releases it from repression. Mechanistically, sir-2.1 deacetylates and cooperates with DAF-16 to drive the longevity transcriptional program. Thus the directionality is sir-2.1 → DAF-16 → lifespan, and removing DAF-16 abolishes the benefit.

label: DAF-16 (FOXO)
description: The lifespan extension produced by sir-2.1 overexpression in C. elegans is strictly dependent on the forkhead transcription factor DAF-16, the worm FOXO ortholog. DAF-16 is the downstream effector that induces stress-resistance and xenobiotic-detoxification genes once sir-2.1 releases it from repression. Mechanistically, sir-2.1 deacetylates and cooperates with DAF-16 to drive the longevity transcriptional program. Thus the directionality is sir-2.1 → DAF-16 → lifespan, and removing DAF-16 abolishes the benefit.

label: dSir2 overexpression (Drosophila)
description: Ubiquitous overexpression of the Drosophila Sir2 ortholog (dSir2) extends female lifespan by about 29%, with a more modest or absent effect in males. The sexually dimorphic response reflects differences in nutrient sensing and reproductive physiology between the sexes, and it mirrors the pattern seen in worm and yeast models. Directionally, increased dSir2 acts upstream to produce the longevity phenotype, consistent with a conserved sirtuin-caloric-restriction axis. As in C. elegans and S. cerevisiae, the effect depends on genetic background, dietary conditions, and the level of expression achieved.

label: Histone H1 (Lys9, Lys26)
description: SIRT1 removes acetyl groups from Lys9 and Lys26 of linker histone H1, a modification that influences higher-order chromatin compaction and gene accessibility. Deacetylated H1 is generally associated with a more condensed, transcriptionally repressed chromatin state at SIRT1-target loci. The relationship is directional: SIRT1 acts enzymatically on H1 to remodel chromatin and silence specific programs. Because H1 links nucleosomes, this action helps SIRT1 enforce long-range repression independently of core histone modifications.

label: H3K14
description: SIRT1 deacetylates Lys14 of histone H3 (H3K14ac), a mark associated with active transcription, thereby contributing to gene silencing at targeted promoters. Loss of H3K14ac reduces promoter accessibility and cooperates with other repressive modifications to restrain transcription, making this a mechanism of chromatin-level control. Directionally, SIRT1 acts enzymatically to remove the acetyl mark and shift chromatin toward repression. This histone-targeting activity complements SIRT1 deacetylation of non-histone substrates and helps explain how a single sirtuin coordinates broad transcriptional programs across the genome.

label: SIRT1 deacetylation of p53
description: By deacetylating p53, SIRT1 lowers p53's transcriptional activation of BH3-only proteins and other apoptotic effectors, suppressing programmed cell death after oxidative or genotoxic stress. This creates a survival bias that helps cells tolerate damage but can also protect incipient cancer cells from elimination. The directionality is that SIRT1 activity on p53 is upstream of reduced apoptosis. A caveat is that chronic suppression of p53-dependent apoptosis is a double-edged sword: protective in normal tissue but potentially tumor-promoting.

label: HIC1
description: HIC1 (hypermethylated in cancer 1) is a tumor suppressor that binds the SIRT1 promoter via its POZ domain and directly represses SIRT1 transcription. Because p53 transactivates HIC1, a negative feedback loop exists: p53 induces HIC1, which then restrains SIRT1, preventing excessive p53 deacetylation and preserving p53 tumor-suppressive capacity. The directionality is HIC1 → SIRT1 repression, upstream of SIRT1's inhibition of p53. Disruption of this loop in cancer can unleash SIRT1 to silence p53.

label: SIRT1 promoter
description: HIC1 (hypermethylated in cancer 1) is a tumor suppressor that binds the SIRT1 promoter via its POZ domain and directly represses SIRT1 transcription. Because p53 transactivates HIC1, a negative feedback loop exists: p53 induces HIC1, which then restrains SIRT1, preventing excessive p53 deacetylation and preserving p53 tumor-suppressive capacity. The directionality is HIC1 → SIRT1 repression, upstream of SIRT1's inhibition of p53. Disruption of this loop in cancer can unleash SIRT1 to silence p53.

label: HIC1 transcription
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: p53 directly activates transcription of HIC1, a tumor suppressor that in turn represses the SIRT1 promoter, forming a negative feedback loop that restrains SIRT1 abundance. This loop ensures that p53 activity is not indefinitely suppressed by SIRT1-mediated deacetylation, because sustained p53 signaling drives HIC1 to limit SIRT1 expression. Directionally, p53 is the transcription factor and HIC1 the induced target gene, with SIRT1 sitting downstream of both. The biological significance is genome protection: by inducing HIC1, p53 prevents SIRT1 from over-deacetylating and silencing p53 itself, preserving the capacity for apoptosis and senescence in response to damage.

label: Ku70
description: SIRT1 deacetylates Ku70 (Cohen 2004), the DNA-repair factor and Ku-complex subunit that also binds and inhibits the pro-apoptotic protein Bax. Deacetylation increases Ku70's affinity for Bax, sequestering Bax away from mitochondria and preventing outer-membrane permeabilization, coupling DNA-damage signaling to cell-survival decisions. This links SIRT1's genome-maintenance functions to a direct anti-apoptotic program; in some cancers the same axis helps tumor cells evade death, showing how a survival pathway can be co-opted in oncogenesis.

label: Deacetylated Ku70
description: Once deacetylated by SIRT1, Ku70 binds the BH3 domain of the pro-apoptotic protein Bax and retains it in the cytosol, preventing Bax translocation to and permeabilization of mitochondria. This sequestration blocks the intrinsic apoptosis cascade downstream of many stress signals, including DNA damage and oxidative stress. Directionally, deacetylated Ku70 is the binding partner that neutralizes Bax, converting a DNA-repair factor into an anti-apoptotic scaffold. The net effect is cytoprotection, though as with p53 suppression this can also shield damaged cells in oncogenic contexts, where the Ku70–Bax interaction becomes a target for restoring apoptosis in cancer therapy.

label: Bax (pro-apoptotic)
description: Once deacetylated by SIRT1, Ku70 binds the BH3 domain of the pro-apoptotic protein Bax and retains it in the cytosol, preventing Bax translocation to and permeabilization of mitochondria. This sequestration blocks the intrinsic apoptosis cascade downstream of many stress signals, including DNA damage and oxidative stress. Directionally, deacetylated Ku70 is the binding partner that neutralizes Bax, converting a DNA-repair factor into an anti-apoptotic scaffold. The net effect is cytoprotection, though as with p53 suppression this can also shield damaged cells in oncogenic contexts, where the Ku70–Bax interaction becomes a target for restoring apoptosis in cancer therapy.

label: E2F1
description: The E2F1 transcription factor binds directly to the SIRT1 promoter and activates its transcription, particularly under proliferative or DNA-damage signals. This positions SIRT1 as a downstream effector of E2F1-driven programs that balance cell-cycle progression with survival. Directionally, E2F1 acts upstream of SIRT1 gene activation, linking growth signals to increased sirtuin abundance. Notably, the relationship is reciprocal, because SIRT1 then feeds back to deacetylate and inhibit E2F1's apoptotic function, creating a regulatory loop in which E2F1 both induces its own regulator and is constrained by it—a circuit relevant to tumor suppression and the DNA-damage response.

label: FOXO3a
description: SIRT1 deacetylates FOXO3a in multiple cell types, including neurons and fibroblasts, shifting its target-gene program toward stress resistance and away from apoptosis. Deacetylated FOXO3a induces antioxidant enzymes such as SOD2 and catalase, promotes autophagy and mitophagy through BNIP3, and reduces death-gene expression, biasing cells toward repair and survival. Directionally, SIRT1 modifies FOXO3a, and the altered transcription follows downstream. This stress-resistant switch is central to SIRT1-mediated protection in aging and neurodegeneration, and it links sirtuin activity to redox homeostasis and cellular quality control.

label: FOXO4
description: SIRT1 deacetylates FOXO4, which reverts FOXO4-mediated suppression and enhances cellular defenses against oxidative stress. Deacetylation of FOXO4 boosts expression of DNA-repair and antioxidant genes such as GADD45 while suppressing caspase activation, steering cells toward genome maintenance rather than death. The relationship is directional: SIRT1 enzymatically licenses FOXO4 to drive protective transcription. This contributes to SIRT1's broad role in genomic maintenance and resilience to damage, and parallels SIRT1's regulation of other FOXO family members, with the balance among FOXO1, FOXO3a, and FOXO4 shaping tissue-specific stress responses and survival decisions.

label: RelA/p65 (NF-κB subunit)
description: SIRT1 deacetylates the RelA/p65 subunit of NF-κB, particularly at Lys310, reducing its ability to recruit the transcriptional machinery and activate pro-inflammatory genes. This post-translational modification dampens NF-κB target genes such as TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, and also licenses p65 for ubiquitin-proteasomal degradation, further lowering inflammatory output. Directionally, SIRT1 acts enzymatically on RelA to inhibit inflammatory transcription. Because NF-κB drives chronic inflammation implicated in aging and disease, SIRT1's action is a key anti-inflammatory node, and loss of SIRT1 or its decline with age allows NF-κB activity to rise and perpetuate low-grade systemic inflammation.

label: SIRT1 deacetylation of RelA/p65
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Deacetylation of RelA/p65 by SIRT1 lowers NF-κB transactivation, thereby reducing expression of cytokines, chemokines, and adhesion molecules that propagate inflammation. This directly opposes the pro-inflammatory program and underlies many of SIRT1's protective effects in metabolic, cardiovascular, and neurodegenerative contexts. The directionality is SIRT1 deacetylation → suppressed NF-κB signaling. A caveat is that excessive NF-κB suppression could impair host defense, so the effect is beneficial within physiological ranges.

label: NF-κB pro-inflammatory signalling
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Deacetylation of RelA/p65 by SIRT1 lowers NF-κB transactivation, thereby reducing expression of cytokines, chemokines, and adhesion molecules that propagate inflammation. This directly opposes the pro-inflammatory program and underlies many of SIRT1's protective effects in metabolic, cardiovascular, and neurodegenerative contexts. The directionality is SIRT1 deacetylation → suppressed NF-κB signaling. A caveat is that excessive NF-κB suppression could impair host defense, so the effect is beneficial within physiological ranges.

label: SIRT1 and RelA/p65
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Exposure to cigarette-smoke extract disrupts the SIRT1–RelA/p65 complex, diminishing deacetylation of RelA and leaving NF-κB in a more active, pro-inflammatory state. The consequence is heightened expression of inflammatory mediators in airway and other cells exposed to smoke. The directionality is that the environmental insult (smoke) reduces a protective protein–protein interaction, increasing inflammation. This provides a mechanistic link between smoking, impaired sirtuin function, and chronic inflammatory lung disease.

label: RNA Polymerase I transcription
description: SIRT7 activates RNA polymerase I-mediated transcription of ribosomal DNA, driving ribosome biogenesis and protein synthetic capacity in proliferating cells. It does so in part through deacetylation of histone H3K18 at rDNA loci and by stabilizing the Pol I transcriptional apparatus, ensuring sufficient ribosome output for growth. Directionally, SIRT7 acts upstream to enhance rRNA production and ribosome biogenesis. By sustaining this biosynthetic capacity, SIRT7 supports cell growth and proliferation, which underlies its roles in development and in cancer, where ribosome biogenesis is frequently upregulated.

label: RNA Polymerase I transcription (via TAFI68 deacetylation)
description: SIRT1 deacetylates TAFI68, a subunit of the RNA polymerase I transcription factor complex, decreasing its DNA-binding activity and thereby repressing rRNA transcription. This contrasts with SIRT7, which activates Pol I, illustrating divergent sirtuin control of ribosome biogenesis within the same family. Directionally, SIRT1 acts on TAFI68 to repress Pol I output. By limiting ribosome production, SIRT1 can restrain growth and oppose the biosynthetic programs favored in cancer and pathological hypertrophy, positioning the SIRT1/SIRT7 balance as a rheostat that determines whether cells commit to growth-oriented or maintenance-oriented metabolism.

label: Glioma tumour formation
description: SIRT2 resides in a genomic region frequently deleted in human gliomas, and re-expression of SIRT2 markedly reduces colony formation by glioma cells, indicating tumor-suppressor function. Its activity deacetylates substrates such as α-tubulin and HNF4α that govern mitotic fidelity and metabolism, helping to preserve genomic stability during division. Directionally, SIRT2 loss permits gliomagenesis while SIRT2 restoration suppresses it. A caveat is that SIRT2 can act as either a tumor suppressor or a promoter depending on tissue and context—stabilizing oncogenes like c-Myc in some settings—so its role in cancer is highly context-dependent and cell-type-specific.

label: Histone H4
description: SIRT2 deacetylates Lys16 on histone H4 (H4K16ac), a modification linked to chromatin condensation during the G2/M transition of mitosis. Removing H4K16ac promotes a more compact mitotic chromatin state compatible with chromosome segregation and mitotic fidelity. Enzymatically, SIRT2 directly deacetylates H4K16 to remodel chromatin at division, complementing its actions on α-tubulin and mitotic regulators. This chromatin function, together with SIRT2's peak expression at G2/M, couples deacetylation to cell-cycle control, and its loss is associated with mitotic defects, genomic instability, and, in some cancers, tumor progression.

label: SIRT2 expression
description: SIRT2 protein levels rise dramatically as cells enter mitosis, and the enzyme is hyperphosphorylated at the G2/M boundary, timing its activity to chromosome condensation and division. This cell-cycle coupling links SIRT2 to proper mitotic progression and genomic stability, with the enzyme regulating both tubulin dynamics and chromatin state during division. Directionally, the G2/M transition drives SIRT2 upregulation and activation, and at mitotic exit the phosphatase CDC14B dephosphorylates SIRT2 to trigger its degradation. Loss or dysregulation of this mitotic peak is associated with aneuploidy, mitotic defects, and, in some cancers, genomic instability.

label: Mitosis (G2/M phase)
description: SIRT2 protein levels rise dramatically as cells enter mitosis, and the enzyme is hyperphosphorylated at the G2/M boundary, timing its activity to chromosome condensation and division. This cell-cycle coupling links SIRT2 to proper mitotic progression and genomic stability, with the enzyme regulating both tubulin dynamics and chromatin state during division. Directionally, the G2/M transition drives SIRT2 upregulation and activation, and at mitotic exit the phosphatase CDC14B dephosphorylates SIRT2 to trigger its degradation. Loss or dysregulation of this mitotic peak is associated with aneuploidy, mitotic defects, and, in some cancers, genomic instability.

label: SIRT6 knockout mice
description: Mice lacking SIRT6 develop a striking premature-aging syndrome with reduced size, loss of subcutaneous fat, lymphopenia, colitis, and spinal curvature, dying early in life. The phenotype reflects defective base-excision repair, genomic instability, and metabolic and inflammatory dysregulation, demonstrating that SIRT6 is essential for maintaining genome integrity and metabolic homeostasis. Directionally, SIRT6 deficiency produces multisystem premature aging. This makes SIRT6 one of the clearest single-gene links between sirtuins and mammalian longevity, and it positions SIRT6 among the strongest candidates for translating sirtuin biology into interventions that delay age-related decline.

label: Premature aging phenotype
description: Mice lacking SIRT6 develop a striking premature-aging syndrome with reduced size, loss of subcutaneous fat, lymphopenia, colitis, and spinal curvature, dying early in life. The phenotype reflects defective base-excision repair, genomic instability, and metabolic and inflammatory dysregulation, demonstrating that SIRT6 is essential for maintaining genome integrity and metabolic homeostasis. Directionally, SIRT6 deficiency produces multisystem premature aging. This makes SIRT6 one of the clearest single-gene links between sirtuins and mammalian longevity, and it positions SIRT6 among the strongest candidates for translating sirtuin biology into interventions that delay age-related decline.

label: Tat (HIV-1 protein)
description: SIRT1 deacetylates Lys50 of the HIV-1 transactivator Tat, a modification that increases Tat's affinity for the viral LTR and its ability to recruit the transcription machinery. This enzymatic action therefore activates, rather than suppresses, the viral protein, promoting robust expression of viral genes from the proviral genome. Directionally, SIRT1 modifies Tat and thereby enhances viral transcription, revealing an unexpected pro-viral role for the otherwise cytoprotective SIRT1. Because deacetylated Tat is a more potent transactivator, the interaction represents a host factor that HIV exploits, making SIRT1–Tat a candidate target for antiviral strategies.

label: SIRT1 deacetylation of Tat
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Because deacetylated Tat is a more potent transactivator, SIRT1-mediated deacetylation at Lys50 boosts HIV-1 transcription from the proviral LTR. The relationship is directional: SIRT1 acts on Tat to amplify viral gene expression and reactivate latent proviruses. This positions host SIRT1 as a cofactor that HIV exploits, a caveat to the generally beneficial reputation of SIRT1 activation. Targeting this interaction is of interest for antiviral strategies, particularly for the shock-and-kill approach to HIV latency, where compounds that modulate the SIRT1–Tat axis could either silence or purge the latent reservoir depending on the therapeutic goal.

label: HIV-1 viral transcription

label: White adipose tissue
description: In white adipose tissue, SIRT1 promotes lipolysis and fat mobilization by repressing adipogenic transcription factors such as PPAR-γ and aP2 and by co-ordinating catabolic gene programs. This shifts storage tissue from lipid accumulation toward fatty-acid release for oxidation in muscle and liver, supporting metabolic flexibility. Directionally, SIRT1 acts to repress adipogenesis and enhance fat mobilization. These actions contribute to the lean phenotype and metabolic health seen under caloric restriction, and reduced SIRT1 in visceral adipose stem cells from obese individuals is associated with enhanced adipogenic capacity and visceral fat expansion.

label: PPAR-γ (adipogenesis)
description: SIRT1 represses PPAR-γ, the master regulator of adipogenesis, by deacetylating it and interfering with its co-activator interactions, thereby inhibiting differentiation of preadipocytes into fat cells. Pharmacological SIRT1 activation or overexpression recapitulates this repression and blocks adipogenesis, while SIRT1 knockdown promotes adipogenic differentiation. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of PPAR-γ suppression, limiting fat-cell formation. By restraining adipogenesis, SIRT1 prevents excessive white-fat accumulation and contributes to the metabolic benefits of caloric restriction, although its role in mature adipocytes and lipid mobilization is more complex.

label: UCP2 (Uncoupling Protein 2)
description: SIRT1 transcriptionally represses UCP2, a mitochondrial inner-membrane uncoupler that dissipates the proton gradient and reduces ATP yield. In SIRT1 knockout mice, UCP2 is upregulated, lowering ATP production in pancreatic β-cells and impairing glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. Directionally, SIRT1 suppresses UCP2 expression to preserve the mitochondrial membrane potential needed for efficient ATP generation. By keeping UCP2 low, SIRT1 maintains bioenergetic efficiency in β-cells and other tissues, linking sirtuin activity to glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and protection against the β-cell dysfunction that characterizes type 2 diabetes.

label: SIRT1 repression of UCP2
description: Repression of UCP2 by SIRT1 preserves mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP synthesis in pancreatic β-cells, which raises the ATP/ADP ratio and closes KATP channels to trigger insulin release. Mice overexpressing SIRT1 in β-cells show enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, while SIRT1 loss elevates UCP2 and impairs the response. Directionally, SIRT1-mediated UCP2 downregulation leads to stronger insulin secretion. This links SIRT1 to improved glucose homeostasis and protection against diabetes, and it is consistent with the observation that caloric restriction, which raises SIRT1, preserves β-cell function and insulin sensitivity in aging organisms.

label: Glucose-stimulated insulin secretion
description: Repression of UCP2 by SIRT1 preserves mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP synthesis in pancreatic β-cells, which raises the ATP/ADP ratio and closes KATP channels to trigger insulin release. Mice overexpressing SIRT1 in β-cells show enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, while SIRT1 loss elevates UCP2 and impairs the response. Directionally, SIRT1-mediated UCP2 downregulation leads to stronger insulin secretion. This links SIRT1 to improved glucose homeostasis and protection against diabetes, and it is consistent with the observation that caloric restriction, which raises SIRT1, preserves β-cell function and insulin sensitivity in aging organisms.

label: AceCS2 (mitochondrial acetyl-CoA synthetase)
description: SIRT3 deacetylates and activates acetyl-CoA synthetase 2 (AceCS2) in the mitochondrial matrix, enabling it to convert acetate into acetyl-CoA for the TCA cycle and lipogenesis. Deacetylation relieves autoinhibition, increasing AceCS2's catalytic efficiency and allowing mitochondria to use acetate as an alternative carbon source. Directionally, SIRT3 activates AceCS2 to drive mitochondrial acetyl-CoA production. This supports metabolic flexibility during fasting and alcohol metabolism, when acetate is abundant, and parallels SIRT1's activation of the cytoplasmic isoform AceCS1, demonstrating that sirtuins broadly license acetate salvage across both mitochondrial and cytosolic compartments.

label: AceCS1 (cytoplasmic acetyl-CoA synthetase)
description: SIRT1 deacetylates and activates acetyl-CoA synthetase 1 (AceCS1) in the cytoplasm, analogous to SIRT3's activation of the mitochondrial AceCS2, permitting acetate utilization outside the mitochondrion. Activated AceCS1 supplies cytosolic acetyl-CoA for chromatin modification, fatty-acid synthesis, and other biosynthetic reactions. Directionally, SIRT1 activates AceCS1 to feed cytosolic acetyl-CoA metabolism. Together with SIRT3, this shows sirtuins broadly license acetate salvage across compartments, coupling nutrient availability and redox state to acetyl-CoA pools that influence both bioenergetics and the epigenetic regulation of gene expression.

label: Reactive oxygen species production
description: SIRT3 lowers mitochondrial ROS by deacetylating and activating antioxidant enzymes such as MnSOD and components of the electron-transport chain, while also reducing mitochondrial membrane potential in a manner that limits superoxide leak. Higher SIRT3 activity therefore shifts the mitochondrial redox balance toward less oxidative damage. The directionality is SIRT3 activity upstream of reduced ROS. This antioxidant function is a major basis for SIRT3's protective roles in heart, liver, and aging.

label: Cold exposure (brown adipose tissue)
description: Cold exposure induces SIRT3 in brown adipose tissue, where it promotes expression of mitochondrial genes and supports thermogenic programs. The induction enhances oxidative metabolism and uncoupled respiration needed for heat production, with SIRT3 acting upstream of UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Directionally, a cold stimulus triggers SIRT3 upregulation, which in turn drives thermogenic mitochondrial biogenesis. This ties SIRT3 to adaptive thermogenesis and the metabolic benefits of cold exposure, and conversely SIRT3 is reduced in brown adipose tissue of obese mice, linking obesity to impaired thermogenic capacity and blunted cold-induced mitochondrial function.

label: GDH (Glutamate Dehydrogenase)
description: SIRT4 mono-ADP-ribosylates glutamate dehydrogenase (GDH), inhibiting its oxidative deamination of glutamate to α-ketoglutarate and thereby slowing anaplerotic carbon entry into the TCA cycle. This restrains amino-acid-derived ATP production and insulin secretion in pancreatic β-cells, limiting nutrient-driven hormonal output. Directionally, SIRT4 enzymatically inhibits GDH, acting as a mitochondrial brake on amino-acid catabolism. This opposes anabolic fueling of secretion, and because SIRT4 also inhibits MTPα, glutamine metabolism, and PPARα signaling, it broadly curbs mitochondrial oxidative capacity while promoting lipid conservation under nutrient-replete conditions.

label: SIRT4 inhibition of GDH
description: By inhibiting GDH, SIRT4 blunts the ability of amino acids such as leucine to stimulate insulin release from pancreatic β-cells, because less α-ketoglutarate is generated to elevate ATP and trigger secretion. The relationship is directional: SIRT4-mediated GDH inhibition reduces amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion, restraining the nutrient-dependent arm of insulin release. This positions SIRT4 as a physiological negative regulator of nutrient-stimulated insulin secretion, complementary to SIRT1's positive effects on glucose-stimulated secretion.

label: Amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion
description: By inhibiting GDH, SIRT4 blunts the ability of amino acids such as leucine to stimulate insulin release from pancreatic β-cells, because less α-ketoglutarate is generated to elevate ATP and trigger secretion. The relationship is directional: SIRT4-mediated GDH inhibition reduces amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion, restraining the nutrient-dependent arm of insulin release. This positions SIRT4 as a physiological negative regulator of nutrient-stimulated insulin secretion, complementary to SIRT1's positive effects on glucose-stimulated secretion.

label: β-amyloid toxicity
description: SIRT1 protects neurons from β-amyloid-induced toxicity, in part by inhibiting NF-κB signaling in microglia and reducing neuroinflammation, and by supporting neuronal stress-resistance pathways. This limits the inflammatory and oxidative damage that accompany amyloid pathology and preserves synaptic function. Directionally, SIRT1 activity sits upstream of reduced neuronal injury. The effect dovetails with observations that caloric restriction, which raises SIRT1, protects against Alzheimer's-like neuropathology in mouse models, and that SIRT1 promotes non-amyloidogenic processing of APP through the α-secretase ADAM10, reducing production of the toxic β-amyloid peptide itself.

label: PGC-1α regulation
description: SIRT1 confers neuroprotection partly through deacetylation and activation of PGC-1α, which drives mitochondrial biogenesis and antioxidant defenses in neurons. Enhanced PGC-1α activity counters the energetic and oxidative deficits underlying neurodegeneration, and PGC-1α knockout mice are markedly more sensitive to toxins such as MPTP and kainic acid. Directionally, SIRT1 activates PGC-1α to build neuronal resilience. This axis is a leading explanation for how SIRT1 activation benefits Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, and other neurodegenerative models, and it connects sirtuin biology to mitochondrial health as a central determinant of neuronal survival in aging.

label: Resveratrol (high-calorie diet mice)
description: In mice on a high-calorie diet, resveratrol increases mitochondrial number and function, an effect accompanied by elevated SIRT1 and PGC-1α activity. This shift counters diet-induced metabolic dysfunction by improving oxidative capacity, increasing endurance, and protecting against the metabolic consequences of overnutrition. Directionally, resveratrol activates SIRT1/PGC-1α to drive mitochondrial biogenesis. The finding, from Baur and Sinclair's 2006 study in Cell, helped popularize resveratrol as a caloric-restriction mimetic against diet-induced obesity and demonstrated that a small molecule could reproduce key metabolic benefits of dietary restriction in mammals.

label: Blood glucose and insulin
description: Resveratrol treatment lowers blood glucose and circulating insulin in animals on a high-calorie diet, improving glycemic control and insulin sensitivity. These metabolic benefits are linked to SIRT1/AMPK activation and improved insulin signaling in liver and muscle, together with reduced hepatic steatosis. Directionally, resveratrol activates SIRT1/AMPK to lower glycemia. Caveats include that human trials have been inconsistent, likely owing to the compound's poor oral bioavailability, short half-life, and extensive first-pass metabolism, which limit the translation of preclinical efficacy to physiological exposures achievable through dietary or supplement intake in people.

label: SIRT3 gene variant (intron 5 enhancer)
description: A polymorphism in an intron-5 enhancer of the SIRT3 gene is associated with exceptional longevity, specifically survival beyond 90 years in men. The variant is thought to alter SIRT3 expression or regulation, conferring enhanced mitochondrial stress resistance and antioxidant capacity. Directionally, the genetic variation is associated with, and putatively causal of, prolonged lifespan. As a correlation it supports—but does not prove—that higher SIRT3 activity promotes human longevity, and it is consistent with separate findings linking SIRT3 single-nucleotide polymorphisms to longevity in other cohorts, including the TRELONG study, reinforcing SIRT3 as a candidate human longevity gene.

label: Male longevity beyond 90 years

The variant is thought to alter SIRT3 expression or regulation, conferring enhanced mitochondrial stress resistance and antioxidant capacity. Directionally, the genetic variation is associated with, and putatively causal of, prolonged lifespan. As a correlation it supports—but does not prove—that higher SIRT3 activity promotes human longevity, and it is consistent with separate findings linking SIRT3 single-nucleotide polymorphisms to longevity in other cohorts, including the TRELONG study, reinforcing SIRT3 as a candidate human longevity gene.

label: SIRT1 allele variants
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Several single-nucleotide polymorphisms in the human SIRT1 gene are significantly associated with systemic energy expenditure in Finnish cohorts, suggesting that SIRT1 variation influences metabolic rate. These variants may alter SIRT1 expression or activity, shifting how individuals burn fuel at rest and during activity. Directionally, genetic SIRT1 variation is linked to an energy-expenditure phenotype. As with most genetic-association findings, effect sizes are modest and context-dependent, and replication in other populations is needed.

label: Androgen receptor (Lys630)
description: SIRT1 binds the androgen receptor and deacetylates it at Lys630 within its lysine-rich motif, repressing AR transcriptional activity and its oncogenic signaling in prostate tissue. This enzymatic modification dampens AR-driven proliferative and survival programs, opposing androgen-dependent growth. Directionally, SIRT1 acts upstream to inhibit AR function. This axis is relevant to prostate cancer, where SIRT1 can oppose androgen-dependent tumor growth, and it suggests that sirtuin activators might complement androgen-deprivation therapies. The interaction also illustrates SIRT1's broader capacity to restrain nuclear-receptor signaling in steroid-responsive tissues.

label: HOXA10 (homeobox transcription factor)
description: SIRT2 interacts with HOXA10, a conserved homeobox transcription factor critical for embryonic cell-type determination and adult tissue homeostasis, including reproductive and hematopoietic development. The interaction suggests SIRT2 influences HOXA10-dependent transcriptional programs, though the precise deacetylation outcome is less well characterized than for other SIRT2 substrates. Directionally, SIRT2 engages HOXA10 as a partner and potential substrate. This connection links SIRT2 to developmental regulation and possibly to differentiation defects in disease, and is consistent with SIRT2's broader roles in controlling transcription-factor activity and cell-fate decisions across tissues.

label: Hes1 and Hey2 (bHLH repressors)
description: SIRT1 physically interacts with the bHLH transcriptional repressors Hes1 and Hey2 both in vitro and in vivo, modulating their ability to repress target promoters. Deacetylation by SIRT1 can alter the DNA-binding or co-repressor recruitment of these factors, tuning the strength of Notch-and-Hes-coupled gene silencing. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically modulates Hes1/Hey2 repression. This intersects with Notch and VEGF signaling and with SIRT1's neuroprotective regulation of BDNF, since Hes1 is a repressor of the BDNF promoter and SIRT1 relieves that repression through Hes1 deacetylation, linking this interaction to neuronal survival and cognitive function.

label: Developmental defects
description: SIRT1-null mice are markedly smaller, grow slowly, and show defects in eye morphogenesis and cardiac septation, revealing SIRT1's role in normal development. These phenotypes indicate that SIRT1 is not merely a stress-response protein but is required for organogenesis and systemic growth. Directionally, SIRT1 deficiency causes structural developmental abnormalities. The perinatal lethality of many SIRT1 knockout strains limited study of the complete phenotype, prompting the development of tissue-specific conditional models that have since clarified SIRT1's contributions to metabolism, circadian rhythm, fertility, and stress resistance in the adult organism.

label: Sterility
description: Surviving SIRT1 knockout mice of both sexes are sterile: males have low sperm counts and females fail to ovulate, implicating SIRT1 in gametogenesis and reproductive endocrine control. The defect reflects failed differentiation and stress responses in gonadal tissues, where SIRT1 normally supports germ-cell survival and maturation. Directionally, SIRT1 loss leads to reproductive failure. This shows SIRT1 is essential for germ-cell development and fertility, and it is consistent with SIRT1's broader role in integrating nutrient status with reproductive function—a link relevant to the well-known dependence of fertility on metabolic state in mammals.

label: Nmnat (NAD+ biosynthetic enzyme)
description: Nmnat, the NAD+-biosynthetic enzyme, protects axons from Wallerian degeneration largely by raising NAD+ and thereby activating SIRT1, which supports axonal survival after injury. The protection is upstream of SIRT1-dependent maintenance of mitochondrial and chromatin function in neurons, preserving axon integrity when the soma is damaged. Directionally, Nmnat increases NAD+, which activates SIRT1 to provide axonal protection. This established a key NAD+/sirtuin axis in neuronal resilience, informed subsequent studies of SARM1-mediated NAD+ depletion in axonal degeneration, and helped motivate the use of NAD+ precursors such as NMN and NR to protect neurons.

label: Axonal/Wallerian degeneration (via SIRT1)
description: Nmnat, the NAD+-biosynthetic enzyme, protects axons from Wallerian degeneration largely by raising NAD+ and thereby activating SIRT1, which supports axonal survival after injury. The protection is upstream of SIRT1-dependent maintenance of mitochondrial and chromatin function in neurons, preserving axon integrity when the soma is damaged. Directionally, Nmnat increases NAD+, which activates SIRT1 to provide axonal protection. This established a key NAD+/sirtuin axis in neuronal resilience, informed subsequent studies of SARM1-mediated NAD+ depletion in axonal degeneration, and helped motivate the use of NAD+ precursors such as NMN and NR to protect neurons.

label: Smad7 (Lys60, Lys70)
description: SIRT1 deacetylates Smad7 at Lys60 and Lys70, which enhances Smad7's recognition by the E3 ligase Smurf1 and targets it for ubiquitin-proteasomal degradation. This accelerates turnover of the TGF-β inhibitory Smad, modulating the intensity and duration of TGF-β pathway signaling. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically marks Smad7 for destruction. The consequence is context-dependent regulation of TGF-β signaling rather than simple inhibition: by limiting the negative-feedback inhibitor Smad7, SIRT1 can fine-tune TGF-β responses in kidney, where this mechanism protects glomerular cells from TGF-β-dependent apoptosis during injury.

label: SIRT1 deacetylation of Smad7
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: By promoting degradation of Smad7, SIRT1 deacetylation tempers TGF-β signaling in glomerular mesangial cells and protects them from TGF-β-dependent apoptosis. The relationship is directional: SIRT1 acts on Smad7 to relieve a pro-apoptotic TGF-β output in the kidney. This renoprotective mechanism is relevant to diabetic nephropathy and other glomerulopathies, where excessive TGF-β drives mesangial injury and fibrosis. It illustrates how sirtuin control of a single substrate can determine cell fate during injury, and it complements SIRT1's broader antifibrotic actions that suppress TGF-β1-induced apoptosis, fibrosis, and CTGF expression in renal tissue.

label: TGF-β-dependent glomerular apoptosis
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
