label: SIRT1 (resveratrol-activated)
description: Resveratrol-activated endothelial SIRT1 increases eNOS expression and deacetylates and activates it, enhancing nitric-oxide production and promoting vasodilation. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of eNOS activation in the endothelium. Improved NO bioavailability lowers vascular tone, protects against endothelial dysfunction, and reduces platelet aggregation and smooth-muscle proliferation. This underlies resveratrol's cardiovascular and French-paradox associations, and SIRT1's regulation of eNOS is one of its best-established vascular mechanisms, linking sirtuin activity directly to blood-vessel health and blood-pressure control.

label: SIRT1 activation (resveratrol)
description: Through the AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α pathway, resveratrol reduces hepatic steatosis in diet-induced obesity models by enhancing fatty-acid oxidation and mitochondrial function while limiting lipogenesis. Directionally, SIRT1 activation sits upstream of reduced liver fat accumulation. This demonstrates a translational metabolic benefit of sirtuin activation and is consistent with SIRT1s repression of lipogenic transcription factors such as SREBP-1c and PPAR-γ in the liver. By both increasing lipid catabolism and suppressing de novo lipogenesis, the pathway corrects the imbalance that drives non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.

label: Hepatic steatosis (fatty liver)
description: Through the AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α pathway, resveratrol reduces hepatic steatosis in diet-induced obesity models by enhancing fatty-acid oxidation and mitochondrial function while limiting lipogenesis. Directionally, SIRT1 activation sits upstream of reduced liver fat accumulation. This demonstrates a translational metabolic benefit of sirtuin activation and is consistent with SIRT1s repression of lipogenic transcription factors such as SREBP-1c and PPAR-γ in the liver. By both increasing lipid catabolism and suppressing de novo lipogenesis, the pathway corrects the imbalance that drives non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.

label: Hormetic (biphasic) dose-response
description: Resveratrol shows a hormetic, biphasic dose-response: at low-to-moderate doses it acts as a mild stressor that triggers beneficial adaptive responses such as sirtuin activation and antioxidant defense, whereas at very high doses it can produce off-target or pro-oxidant effects. The directionality is dose determining outcome, not simple monotonic benefit. This complicates dosing in therapeutics. It also rationalizes why modest, diet-like exposures may be more effective than pharmacological megadoses.

label: Oral bioavailability
description: Resveratrol undergoes extensive first-pass metabolism, including glucuronidation and sulfation in the gut and liver, yielding very low systemic free concentrations after oral intake. Its plasma half-life is roughly 8-14 minutes. Directionally, oral administration leads to rapid conjugation and poor bioavailability. This undermines many preclinical benefits when translating to humans, because tissue concentrations rarely approach the levels shown to activate SIRT1 in vitro. Formulation strategies, higher doses, and co-administration with absorption enhancers are being explored to overcome these pharmacokinetic limitations.

label: MnSOD (K68, K122)
description: Honokiol-activated SIRT3 deacetylates MnSOD at Lys68 and Lys122, markedly increasing its superoxide-scavenging activity in the mitochondrial matrix. Directionally, SIRT3 enzymatically activates MnSOD. Enhanced MnSOD lowers mitochondrial ROS and protects against oxidative injury in the heart, kidney, and brain. This is a principal mechanism for honokiol's cardiorenal and neuroprotective effects, and it parallels SIRT3's regulation of the same enzyme during caloric restriction and fasting. Because mitochondrial superoxide is a key trigger of damage and inflammasome activation, MnSOD activation by SIRT3 is central to mitochondrial stress resistance.

label: OSCP (ATP synthase subunit)
description: Honokiol-activated SIRT3 deacetylates OSCP, a subunit of the mitochondrial F1Fo-ATP synthase, optimizing coupling of proton flux to ATP synthesis. Directionally, SIRT3 enzymatically tunes ATP synthase function. Improved coupling boosts cellular energy output while limiting proton-leak-associated ROS, enhancing mitochondrial efficiency. This contributes to honokiol's metabolic and cardioprotective actions, and it shows that SIRT3 regulates not only antioxidant enzymes but also the core machinery of ATP production. By improving the efficiency and integrity of oxidative phosphorylation, SIRT3 supports the bioenergetic capacity that declines with age and metabolic disease.

label: Renal tubulointerstitial fibrosis
description: Honokiol suppresses renal tubulointerstitial fibrosis by activating SIRT3, which inhibits the NF-κB/TGF-β1 pathway and limits fibrogenic signaling in kidney tubules. Directionally, honokiol activates SIRT3 to drive antifibrotic transcription. This reduces collagen deposition and inflammatory infiltrate, protecting renal architecture during injury. It illustrates SIRT3's broad tissue-protective role beyond the heart, and it is consistent with the general antifibrotic action of mitochondrial sirtuins. Given that tubulointerstitial fibrosis is the common final pathway of chronic kidney disease, SIRT3 activation represents a promising strategy to slow renal decline.

label: Dihydromyricetin
description: Dihydromyricetin (DHM), a flavonoid from vine tea (Ampelopsis grossedentata), activates SIRT3 mitochondrial deacetylase activity, leading to MnSOD deacetylation and lowered ROS. Directionally, DHM sits upstream of SIRT3 activation. This mitochondrial action underlies DHM's hepatoprotective and metabolic benefits, including protection against alcoholic and metabolic liver injury. DHM also activates AMPK, synergizing with SIRT3 via NAD+ elevation, so its effects reflect coordinated activation of both energy-sensing pathways. The compound is abundant in vine tea, which provides a practical dietary source at therapeutic doses.

label: UBCS039
description: UBCS039, a pyrrolo[1,2-a]quinoxaline, is the first synthetic, selective allosteric activator of SIRT6, binding its distal hydrophobic pocket and stimulating deacetylase activity with an EC50 of approximately 38 micromolar. It preferentially engages the deacetylase function, driving chromatin compaction, glycolysis suppression, and tumor-suppressive programs, and it mitigates fibrosis in models of kidney injury. UBCS039 validated SIRT6 as a druggable longevity target and remains a key chemical tool for probing SIRT6-dependent biology.

label: MDL-801
description: MDL-801 is a potent, cell-permeable synthetic allosteric activator of SIRT6 that binds the hydrophobic pocket and stimulates its deacetylase activity with an EC50 of approximately 10.3 μM. Directionally, MDL-801 sits upstream of SIRT6 activation. It mirrors UBCS039 but with greater potency and cell permeability, and it mitigates kidney fibrosis while suppressing glycolytic, tumor-promoting metabolism. Its improved properties make it a valuable tool for studying SIRT6-dependent pathways in vivo, and it supports the broader thesis that pharmacologic SIRT6 activation can reproduce the metabolic and genome-protective benefits of SIRT6 overexpression.

label: Cyanidin
description: Cyanidin, a natural anthocyanidin from red berries, increases SIRT6 activity by over 50-fold in certain in vitro assays, making it one of the most powerful natural SIRT6 activators identified. Directionally, cyanidin sits upstream of SIRT6 stimulation. Its potency suggests strong binding to the SIRT6 activation pocket, and it is particularly abundant in elderberries, which provide roughly 350-450 mg of cyanidin-3-glucoside per 100 g of fresh fruit. This links berry polyphenols to SIRT6-dependent metabolic and anti-aging effects, and positions dietary anthocyanins as a practical means of engaging SIRT6 biology.

label: H3K9ac and H3K56ac
description: Activated SIRT6 rapidly deacetylates histone H3K9ac and H3K56ac at chromatin, promoting compaction and facilitating DNA-repair and silencing programs. Directionally, SIRT6 enzymatically removes these active marks. Loss of H3K56ac in particular is associated with genome stability and stress resistance, and H3K9ac removal at specific promoters silences glycolytic, inflammatory, and other target genes. This chromatin action underlies SIRT6's roles in longevity and tumor suppression, and it is complemented by SIRT6's mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activity, which recruits repressive complexes to repetitive elements and DNA-damage sites.

label: Glycolysis (Warburg effect)
description: By suppressing glycolysis and pushing tumor cells toward oxidative metabolism or autophagy, SIRT6 activators such as UBCS039 display tumor-suppressive activity. Directionally, SIRT6 activation sits upstream of reduced Warburg glycolysis. This restrains the aerobic-glycolytic phenotype that fuels cancer growth, complementing SIRT6's repression of HIF-1α and c-MYC and its deacetylation of H3K9 at glycolytic promoters. It is a mechanistic rationale for SIRT6 activation in oncology, and SIRT6 deletion in a large fraction of cancer cell lines indicates that restoring SIRT6-dependent metabolic control could constrain tumor metabolism.

label: CPS1 (carbamoyl phosphate synthase 1)
description: SIRT5 desuccinylates and activates carbamoyl phosphate synthase 1 (CPS1), the rate-limiting enzyme of the urea cycle, enhancing ammonia detoxification into urea. Directionally, SIRT5 enzymatically activates CPS1. This is especially important during fasting or high-protein load when nitrogen must be cleared, and SIRT5-deficient mice show elevated ammonia under such conditions. It exemplifies SIRT5's role as a regulator of mitochondrial acyl-metabolism and nitrogen homeostasis, and complements its activation of HMGCS2, fatty-acid oxidation enzymes, and TCA-cycle dehydrogenases, positioning SIRT5 as a coordinator of catabolic flux during nutrient scarcity.

label: SIRT2 overactivity
description: Direct SIRT2 activation is generally avoided therapeutically because overactivity is linked to neurotoxicity in neurodegenerative contexts, where excessive deacetylation may impair microtubule and protein-homeostasis defenses. Directionally, SIRT2 overactivity is associated with neuronal damage. Consequently, SIRT2 inhibitors are pursued for Parkinsons and Huntingtons disease, where preserving α-tubulin acetylation protects neurons from aggregation toxicity. This therapeutic direction contrasts with SIRT2s tumor-suppressive functions in other tissues, illustrating how the same enzyme can be targeted in opposite directions depending on disease context.

label: Neurotoxicity
description: Direct SIRT2 activation is generally avoided therapeutically because overactivity is linked to neurotoxicity in neurodegenerative contexts, where excessive deacetylation may impair microtubule and protein-homeostasis defenses. Directionally, SIRT2 overactivity is associated with neuronal damage. Consequently, SIRT2 inhibitors are pursued for Parkinsons and Huntingtons disease, where preserving α-tubulin acetylation protects neurons from aggregation toxicity. This therapeutic direction contrasts with SIRT2s tumor-suppressive functions in other tissues, illustrating how the same enzyme can be targeted in opposite directions depending on disease context.

label: SIRT2 inhibitors (AGK2, AK-7, SirReal2)
description: Selective SIRT2 inhibitors such as AGK2, AK-7, and SirReal2 are investigated in neurodegenerative disease models because blocking SIRT2 preserves α-tubulin acetylation and protects neurons from aggregation toxicity. Directionally, SIRT2 inhibition promotes microtubule stability and neuroprotection. These agents rescue dopaminergic neurons from α-synuclein toxicity, reduce huntingtin aggregation in models of Huntington's disease, and confer protection in ischemic stroke. The approach exploits the inverse therapeutic logic of SIRT2 versus other sirtuins: while most sirtuin biology supports activation for healthspan, SIRT2 inhibition appears beneficial in specific neurodegenerative contexts.

label: Parkinson's and Huntington's disease
description: Selective SIRT2 inhibitors such as AGK2, AK-7, and SirReal2 are investigated in neurodegenerative disease models because blocking SIRT2 preserves α-tubulin acetylation and protects neurons from aggregation toxicity. Directionally, SIRT2 inhibition promotes microtubule stability and neuroprotection. These agents rescue dopaminergic neurons from α-synuclein toxicity, reduce huntingtin aggregation in models of Huntington's disease, and confer protection in ischemic stroke. The approach exploits the inverse therapeutic logic of SIRT2 versus other sirtuins: while most sirtuin biology supports activation for healthspan, SIRT2 inhibition appears beneficial in specific neurodegenerative contexts.

label: NMN (Nicotinamide Mononucleotide)
description: NMN is a direct NAD+ precursor that, once converted to NAD+, serves as a universal indirect pan-sirtuin activator by supplying the obligate co-substrate for all seven sirtuins. Directionally, NMN is converted to NAD+, which activates sirtuins. It raises NAD+ levels that decline with age, restoring sirtuin function systemically, and NMN repletion in mice reverses mitochondrial dysfunction and features of cellular senescence. NMN, together with NR, is a leading nutraceutical strategy to counteract age-related sirtuin attenuation, and its efficacy is enhanced when combined with agents that prevent NAD+ consumption, such as CD38 inhibitors.

label: Universal indirect pan-sirtuin activator
description: NMN is a direct NAD+ precursor that, once converted to NAD+, serves as a universal indirect pan-sirtuin activator by supplying the obligate co-substrate for all seven sirtuins. Directionally, NMN is converted to NAD+, which activates sirtuins. It raises NAD+ levels that decline with age, restoring sirtuin function systemically, and NMN repletion in mice reverses mitochondrial dysfunction and features of cellular senescence. NMN, together with NR, is a leading nutraceutical strategy to counteract age-related sirtuin attenuation, and its efficacy is enhanced when combined with agents that prevent NAD+ consumption, such as CD38 inhibitors.

label: NR (Nicotinamide Riboside)
description: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) is an NAD+ precursor that raises cellular NAD+ and thereby indirectly activates all seven sirtuins by supplying their shared co-substrate. Directionally, NR is converted to NAD+, leading to pan-sirtuin activation. Like NMN, NR reverses age-related NAD+ decline and restores sirtuin-dependent maintenance, including mitochondrial function and DNA repair. It is a leading nutraceutical approach to broadly engage sirtuin biology, and clinical studies have confirmed NR's ability to raise NAD+ in humans. NR's efficacy is amplified when combined with CD38 inhibitors that prevent precursor consumption by the NADase.

label: NF-κB signaling pathway
description: SIRT1 inhibits NF-κB transcriptional activity by deacetylating the p65/RelA subunit at Lys310, preventing optimal promoter engagement and coactivator recruitment. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of suppressed NF-κB signaling. This lowers chronic inflammation linked to aging, atherosclerosis, and metabolic disease, and is complemented by SIRT6, SIRT2, and SIRT7 actions on the same pathway. It is one of the best-established anti-inflammatory mechanisms of SIRT1, and its decline with age is thought to permit the rise in NF-κB activity and inflammatory cytokine output that characterizes inflammaging.

label: Histone H3K9
description: SIRT6 deacetylates H3K9 at the promoters of NF-κB target genes, reducing their transcription and thereby dampening inflammation. Directionally, SIRT6 enzymatically represses NF-κB-driven loci through chromatin modification. This complements SIRT6's direct promotion of p65 proteasomal degradation and underscores its anti-inflammatory role. Loss of SIRT6 elevates H3K9ac and inflammatory output, contributing to the pro-inflammatory phenotype of SIRT6-deficient tissues. Together with SIRT1, SIRT6 thus provides both chromatin-level and protein-level restraint on the NF-κB pathway that drives chronic inflammation in aging and disease.

label: NF-κB-mediated inflammatory responses
description: SIRT6 overexpression suppresses NF-κB-mediated inflammatory responses, as shown in models such as osteoarthritis development where cytokine production is reduced. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of inhibited NF-κB inflammation. This protection arises from both chromatin deacetylation of NF-κB target genes and promotion of p65 degradation, providing redundant brakes on the pathway. It positions SIRT6 as a nuclear inflammation brake, and its loss derepresses inflammatory gene programs. This anti-inflammatory function is part of SIRT6's broader protective phenotype, alongside its roles in DNA repair, metabolism, and the suppression of age-related pathologies.

label: SIRT7-kidney-specific knockout
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Kidney-specific SIRT7 knockout mice show diminished inflammation with reduced TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 and suppressed nuclear NF-κB p65 accumulation, indicating SIRT7 normally promotes renal NF-κB activation. Directionally, SIRT7 loss leads to less nuclear p65 and lower inflammation. This is somewhat counterintuitive given SIRT7's anti-inflammatory action in other contexts, underscoring the cell-type and context dependence of sirtuin function. It suggests SIRT7 can be pro-inflammatory in specific renal settings, and highlights that the same sirtuin can promote or suppress NF-κB signaling depending on the tissue environment, kinase signaling, and the balance of its interacting partners.

label: spliced X-box binding protein 1
description: SIRT1 deacetylates spliced X-box-binding protein 1 (XBP1s) downstream of an AMPKα-dependent pathway in macrophages, and deacetylated XBP1s then inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome assembly. Directionally, SIRT1 modifies XBP1s, which in turn suppresses NLRP3. This couples endoplasmic-reticulum stress responses to sirtuin control of inflammation, integrating two stress pathways at the intersection of metabolism and immunity. It is a key mechanism in atherosclerotic and metabolic disease, where chronic ER stress and inflammasome activation drive pathology, and it illustrates how SIRT1 coordinates multiple inputs to restrain inflammatory signaling.

label: miR-217
description: The microRNA miR-217 negatively regulates SIRT1 by binding its 3'UTR and repressing translation, thereby diminishing SIRT1's anti-inflammatory and metabolic functions. Directionally, miR-217 sits upstream of lowered SIRT1. Downregulation of miR-217 mitigates inflammatory responses via the SIRT1/AMPK/NF-κB axis, restoring SIRT1-dependent protection. This exemplifies microRNA fine-tuning of sirtuin abundance, and it is part of a larger miRNA network that calibrates sirtuin tone, including miR-543 and miR-378, which similarly repress SIRT1. Understanding how such miRNAs are regulated in aging and disease may offer new routes to modulate sirtuin activity.

label: miR-543
description: miR-543 represses SIRT1 expression post-transcriptionally, and its downregulation reduces inflammation by strengthening the SIRT1/AMPK/NF-κB signaling pathway. Directionally, miR-543 sits upstream of SIRT1 suppression. This places miR-543 among the microRNAs that calibrate inflammatory tone by controlling sirtuin abundance, alongside miR-217 and miR-378. Modulating such microRNAs, through antagomirs or other strategies, is a potential anti-inflammatory approach, and understanding their regulation in aging and disease could reveal new therapeutic targets for restoring SIRT1-dependent protection against chronic inflammation.

label: miR-378
description: miR-378 reduces SIRT1 activity and facilitates NF-κB-TNFα inflammatory signaling, in part by targeting the 5'-AMPK subunit gamma-2. Directionally, miR-378 inhibits SIRT1, which activates NF-κB. This links a metabolic microRNA to sirtuin-controlled inflammation, and it illustrates how microRNA networks gate sirtuin protective effects. Because AMPK and SIRT1 reinforce each other, miR-378's targeting of AMPK indirectly weakens SIRT1 as well, amplifying inflammatory signaling. These findings identify microRNAs as upstream regulators of the SIRT1/AMPK axis, with potential relevance to metabolic and inflammatory disease.

label: MCPIP1
description: MCPIP1 (monocyte chemoattractant protein-induced protein 1), an RNase, alleviates inflammatory responses by promoting SIRT1 expression through modulation of miR-9. Directionally, MCPIP1 sits upstream of increased SIRT1. Higher SIRT1 then suppresses NF-κB-driven inflammation, creating an anti-inflammatory circuit centered on SIRT1 induction. MCPIP1's RNase activity degrades specific microRNAs and mRNAs, and its regulation of the miR-9/SIRT1 axis illustrates how RNA-binding proteins can control sirtuin abundance. This pathway is relevant to chronic inflammation, where MCPIP1 levels are altered in macrophages and other immune cells.

label: p53/miR-22 axis
description: SIRT1 targets the p53/miR-22 axis to suppress inflammation, lowering expression of cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS). Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of repressed p53/miR-22-inflammatory output. This intersects SIRT1's control of p53 with microRNA-mediated gene silencing, broadening SIRT1's anti-inflammatory repertoire beyond NF-κB. By dampening p53-dependent inflammatory signaling, SIRT1 reduces prostaglandin and nitric-oxide production, and this pathway is relevant to inflammatory disease and cancer, where COX-2 and iNOS drive tissue damage and tumor promotion.

label: PTP1B
description: SIRT1 increases insulin sensitivity and lowers blood glucose by downregulating protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTP1B), a key negative regulator of insulin receptor signaling. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of PTP1B suppression. Reduced PTP1B prolongs insulin-receptor phosphorylation and downstream signaling, improving glucose uptake in muscle and fat. This is a direct mechanism for SIRT1's antidiabetic actions, complementing its effects on FOXO1, IRS-2, and adiponectin. Because PTP1B also regulates leptin signaling, SIRT1-dependent PTP1B suppression may contribute to both glucose and energy-balance control.

label: CREB
description: SIRT1 deacetylates CREB (cAMP response element-binding protein) at Lys136, modulating its transcriptional regulation of lipid-metabolism genes downstream of cAMP signaling. Deacetylated CREB alters target-gene programs controlling lipogenesis and energy balance, linking SIRT1 to the cAMP/PKA network including the Epac1 pathway engaged by resveratrol. Because CREB integrates hormonal and nutrient signals, SIRT1-dependent modification of CREB at this specific lysine offers a molecular route by which sirtuin activity shapes metabolic transcription.

label: HNF4α
description: SIRT2 prevents liver steatosis and lipid metabolic disorders by deacetylating hepatocyte nuclear factor 4α (HNF4α), a master regulator of hepatic lipid and drug-metabolizing genes. Directionally, SIRT2 enzymatically activates HNF4α. This maintains lipid homeostasis and protects against fatty liver, with SIRT2 knockdown promoting steatosis and lipid accumulation. It adds a hepatic metabolic function to SIRT2's repertoire, complementing its roles in mitosis and cytoskeletal regulation. The HNF4α connection also links SIRT2 to bile-acid and xenobiotic metabolism, broadening the metabolic consequences of SIRT2 activity in the liver.

label: AMPK/PGC-1α pathway
description: SIRT3 activates the AMPK/PGC-1α pathway, driving mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming toward oxidative phosphorylation and biogenesis. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of AMPK/PGC-1α activation. This enhances energy production and stress resistance while limiting glycolytic reliance, supporting the bioenergetic capacity of muscle, heart, and liver. It is a core mechanism for SIRT3's metabolic and cardioprotective benefits, and it reinforces the reciprocal relationship between sirtuins and AMPK. By promoting oxidative metabolism, SIRT3 helps maintain metabolic flexibility that declines with age and is impaired in obesity and diabetes.

label: Nrf2 signaling
description: Overexpression of SIRT6 in the brain via in vivo gene transfer enhances Nrf2 signaling and reduces oxidative stress, linking SIRT6 to antioxidant transcription. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of Nrf2 pathway activation. This complements SIRT6's AMPK/MnSOD/catalase axis, providing multiple redundant antioxidant mechanisms. It reinforces SIRT6's role in neuronal and systemic antioxidant defense, and suggests that SIRT6 activation could protect the aging brain from oxidative injury. The convergence of SIRT1 and SIRT6 on Nrf2 highlights the importance of this transcription factor in sirtuin-mediated cytoprotection.

label: JAK2/STAT3 pathway
description: SIRT6 inhibits the Janus kinase 2/STAT3 pathway, suppressing growth and survival signaling in gastric cancer. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of JAK2/STAT3 blockade. This restrains STAT3-driven proliferation and is part of SIRT6's tumor-suppressive repertoire, with SIRT6 loss associated with increased STAT3 activity and tumor aggressiveness. It adds a cytokine-receptor-linked mechanism to SIRT6's anti-cancer actions, complementing its repression of HIF-1α, c-MYC, and glycolysis. Because STAT3 integrates multiple growth and inflammatory signals, its suppression by SIRT6 is relevant to both oncology and chronic inflammation.

label: Cervical cancer progression
description: SIRT2 expression is decreased in cervical cancer tissue versus adjacent normal tissue, and higher SIRT2 predicts favorable survival, indicating it suppresses cervical cancer progression. Directionally, SIRT2 loss is associated with, and putatively enables, tumor advancement. Its deacetylase actions on metabolic and mitotic substrates likely enforce differentiation and genome stability, restraining the aggressive features of cervical cancer. This adds to the context-dependent tumor-suppressor face of SIRT2, which can also promote tumors by stabilizing oncogenes such as c-Myc in other settings, underscoring the tissue- and context-specificity of SIRT2's role in cancer.

label: ACC1
description: SIRT3 deacetylates acetyl-CoA carboxylase 1 (ACC1), upregulating its activity and promoting de novo lipogenesis that can fuel invasion and metastasis of cervical cancer cells. Directionally, SIRT3 enzymatically activates ACC1, promoting lipid synthesis. This reveals a tumor-promoting facet of SIRT3 in certain cancers, contrasting with its usual protective role in mitochondrial metabolism and ROS suppression. It highlights that SIRT3's metabolic effects are context-dependent: the same enzyme that protects normal tissues by reducing oxidative stress can supply lipids that support aggressive tumor growth. This dual role must be considered in SIRT3-based therapeutic strategies.

label: LC3
description: SIRT1 promotes autophagy in endothelial and cancer cells by deacetylating LC3, a key autophagy protein required for autophagosome formation and flux. Directionally, SIRT1 modifies LC3 to enhance autophagy. This supports cellular clearance of damaged organelles and proteins, and it is one of several SIRT1 substrates, including Beclin-1, Atg5, Atg7, and ULK1, that license autophagy. By coordinating the core autophagy machinery, SIRT1 links nutrient sensing to cellular quality control, and its decline with age contributes to the accumulation of damaged components that characterizes aging tissue.

label: IGF-Akt signaling
description: SIRT6 blocks IGF-Akt signaling and thereby cardiac hypertrophy development by targeting c-Jun, interrupting a pro-hypertrophic survival pathway. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of IGF-Akt repression. This protects the heart from maladaptive growth, and SIRT6 knockout mice develop cardiac hypertrophy that is abrogated when IGF signaling is inhibited in vivo. It complements SIRT6's anti-fibrotic actions in cardiovascular tissue and illustrates the importance of restraining growth-factor signaling in the heart. SIRT6's co-repression of c-Jun-dependent transcription at the chromatin level links epigenetic control to cardiac remodeling.

label: NFATc2
description: SIRT2 binds and deacetylates the nuclear factor of activated T-cell c2 (NFATc2) transcription factor, regulating its transcriptional activity in immune and cardiovascular contexts. Directionally, SIRT2 enzymatically tunes NFATc2. Because NFATc2 drives interleukin and hypertrophic gene programs, its deacetylation influences inflammation and cardiac remodeling. This links SIRT2 to calcineurin/NFAT signaling, a central pathway in T-cell activation and pathological cardiac growth. By modulating NFATc2, SIRT2 can shape both immune responses and cardiac stress adaptation, illustrating how a cytosolic sirtuin regulates a key inducible transcription factor.

label: Cardiac fibrosis
description: SIRT4 contributes to cardiac fibrosis; global SIRT4 knockout in mice confers resistance to angiotensin-II infusion by suppressing fibrotic deposition. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of profibrotic signaling. This aligns with SIRT4's general tendency to promote pathological remodeling, contrasting with the antifibrotic SIRT1/SIRT3/SIRT6 members. SIRT4's profibrotic action likely reflects its inhibition of mitochondrial oxidative metabolism and promotion of oxidative stress. The opposing roles of SIRT4 versus the protective sirtuins in cardiac fibrosis illustrate the functional antagonism within the sirtuin family and the importance of the SIRT3/SIRT4 balance.

label: SERCA2a
description: Pharmacological activation of SIRT1 restores SERCA2a activity by deacetylating it at Lys492, improving calcium reuptake into the sarcoplasmic reticulum of cardiomyocytes. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically activates SERCA2a. Better SERCA2a function enhances calcium handling and contractility and opposes heart failure, where SERCA2a activity is depressed. This is a direct mechanism for SIRT1's cardioprotection, linking sirtuin activity to excitation-contraction coupling. By restoring SERCA2a-mediated calcium reuptake, SIRT1 activation improves diastolic function and reduces the arrhythmic and energetic burden of failing hearts.

label: Lox-1-mediated foam cell formation
description: SIRT1 activation reduces lectin-like oxidized-LDL receptor-1 (Lox-1)-mediated foam cell formation by suppressing NF-κB signaling in vascular cells. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of inhibited Lox-1 scavenging of oxidized LDL. This limits macrophage lipid loading, a key early step in atherosclerosis, and reduces the inflammatory cascade triggered by ox-LDL uptake. It is a vascular anti-atherogenic action of SIRT1, complementing its activation of eNOS and its regulation of TIMP3. By restraining foam-cell formation, SIRT1 slows the development of atherosclerotic plaques in the vessel wall.

label: VSMC proliferation and migration
description: SIRT7 regulates vascular smooth-muscle cell (VSMC) proliferation and migration through the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway, limiting the neointimal hyperplasia that drives vascular disease. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of VSMC quiescence. By restraining VSMC activation, SIRT7 protects against atherosclerotic and restenotic remodeling after vascular injury. It adds a vascular-stability role to SIRT7, complementing its cardiac functions, and loss of SIRT7 permits excessive VSMC growth and migration. The Wnt/β-catenin pathway is a central driver of VSMC phenotypic switching, and SIRT7's regulation of it links sirtuins to vascular remodeling.

label: MDL-800
description: MDL-800 is a bis-benzenesulfonamide prodrug and potent, selective SIRT6 activator, with an EC50 of 10.3 μM, that stimulates SIRT6 deacetylase activity. Directionally, MDL-800 allosterically activates SIRT6. It mirrors UBCS039 but with greater potency and cell permeability, mitigating kidney fibrosis and tumor glycolysis in preclinical models. It is a lead chemical tool for SIRT6 biology, and its improved potency and selectivity make it well suited for in vivo studies of SIRT6 activation, supporting the therapeutic potential of pharmacologic SIRT6 engagement.

label: EX-527 (Selisistat)
description: EX-527 (Selisistat) is the first known selective, cell-permeable SIRT1 inhibitor, with an IC50 of 0.098 μM and minimal activity against SIRT2 and SIRT3. Directionally, EX-527 blocks SIRT1 catalysis. It is used to dissect SIRT1-dependent phenotypes and was explored clinically for Huntington's disease, where SIRT1 inhibition was hypothesized to be beneficial. As a SIRT1 blocker, its effects contrast with those of STACs such as resveratrol, and it remains the standard tool for confirming whether a cellular effect depends on SIRT1 enzymatic activity rather than other targets.

label: SirReal2
description: SirReal2 is a potent SIRT2 inhibitor, with an IC50 of 0.14 μM and minimal effects on SIRT1 and SIRT3, exploiting a SIRT2-specific binding pocket. Directionally, SirReal2 blocks SIRT2 deacetylase activity. It is a key chemical probe for SIRT2 biology in neurodegeneration and cancer, and its selectivity makes it valuable for isolating SIRT2-specific effects from the broader sirtuin family. Because SIRT2 inhibition protects neurons in Parkinson's and Huntington's models, SirReal2's selectivity positions it as a candidate scaffold for therapeutic development in neurodegenerative disease.

label: Suramin
description: Suramin, a polyanionic urea derivative, inhibits sirtuins with IC50 values of approximately 297 nM, 1150 nM, and 22 μM for SIRT1, SIRT2, and SIRT5 respectively, showing relative selectivity for SIRT5 at higher concentrations. Directionally, suramin blocks sirtuin catalysis. Its broad activity limits specificity, but it remains a tool to probe SIRT5, and it has also been studied as a therapeutic agent. Clinically, suramin is an antiparasitic and anticancer drug with off-target sirtuin effects, and understanding its sirtuin inhibition informs both its pharmacology and the design of more selective inhibitors.

label: TGF-β1-induced apoptosis and fibrosis
description: Overexpression of SIRT1 abolishes TGF-β1-induced apoptosis and fibrosis and suppresses CTGF expression in mouse kidney, protecting renal tissue from TGF-β1 insult. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of suppressed TGF-β1 pathology. This renoprotective action operates via deacetylation of TGF-β pathway components, including the promotion of Smad7 degradation that tempers TGF-β signaling in glomerular cells. It supports SIRT1 activation as a strategy against kidney fibrosis, and it is consistent with SIRT1's broader antifibrotic effects in heart and lung. Preserving SIRT1 in the kidney may slow the progression of chronic kidney disease.

label: TGF-β1-induced fibroblast activation
description: Genetic knockdown and chemical inhibition of SIRT2 attenuate TGF-β1-induced fibroblast activation and MDM2 expression, reducing fibrogenic responses. Directionally, SIRT2 inhibition leads to less TGF-β1 fibroblast activation. This is unusual because it implies SIRT2 can promote, rather than suppress, fibrosis in this context, unlike the antifibrotic SIRT1, SIRT3, and SIRT6. It underscores the context-dependence of sirtuin-fibrosis relationships and suggests that SIRT2 inhibition might be antifibrotic in specific settings. The MDM2 connection links SIRT2 to p53 regulation during fibroblast activation, adding mechanistic depth to the observation.

label: pyruvate dehydrogenase E1α
description: Pyruvate dehydrogenase E1α (PDH E1α) becomes hyperacetylated at Lys385 in tubular epithelial cells after TGF-β1 stimulation and is deacetylated by SIRT3, modulating pyruvate entry into the TCA cycle. Directionally, SIRT3 enzymatically activates PDH. This links mitochondrial metabolism to TGF-β1-driven kidney injury, and loss of SIRT3 leads to PDH hyperacetylation, reduced glucose oxidation, and pyruvate/lactate accumulation. It shows SIRT3 buffering metabolic dysfunction during fibrosis, and connects the metabolic phenotype of injured kidneys to sirtuin-dependent control of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.

label: osteogenic transdifferentiation of VSMCs
description: SIRT6 suppresses osteogenic transdifferentiation of vascular smooth-muscle cells via repression of runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2), limiting vascular calcification. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of inhibited VSMC osteogenesis. This protects against vessel stiffening in atherosclerosis and aging, and it is a vascular-homeostasis function of SIRT6. By preventing VSMCs from adopting an osteoblast-like phenotype, SIRT6 preserves arterial compliance and reduces the calcific burden of aged vessels. The mechanism complements SIRT6's inhibition of NF-κB and inflammatory gene programs in the vasculature.

label: UUO-induced kidney tubulointerstitial inflammation and fibrosis
description: The SIRT6 activator MDL-800 mitigates unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO)-induced kidney tubulointerstitial inflammation and fibrosis, validating SIRT6 activation therapeutically. Directionally, MDL-800 activates SIRT6, which protects the kidney. This complements other evidence that SIRT6 restrains TGF-β/Smad3 fibrogenesis and NF-κB-mediated inflammation. It supports SIRT6 as a target for chronic kidney disease, where tubulointerstitial fibrosis determines outcome. The efficacy of a pharmacologic SIRT6 activator in a standard fibrosis model provides important proof-of-concept for SIRT6-based therapies in renal and fibrotic disease.

label: T helper type 1 cells development
description: Dendritic-cell SIRT1 knockout drives T helper 1 (Th1) cell development and promotes inflammation, indicating SIRT1 normally restrains Th1 polarization. Directionally, DC SIRT1 sits upstream of suppressed Th1 differentiation. This tempers cell-mediated inflammatory responses and promotes regulatory T-cell generation, shaping the balance between immunity and tolerance. It demonstrates SIRT1's immunoregulatory role in antigen presentation and is relevant to autoimmune and inflammatory diseases, where excessive Th1 responses drive pathology. The effect likely reflects SIRT1-dependent control of cytokine and costimulatory molecule expression in dendritic cells.

label: SIRT6 deficiency (macrophages)
description: SIRT6 deficiency in macrophages increases acetylation and stability of FoxO1, leading to sustained FoxO1 protein and an inflammatory state. Directionally, SIRT6 loss leads to hyperacetylated, stabilized FoxO1. Because SIRT6 normally deacetylates FoxO1, its absence prolongs FoxO1 signaling and promotes inflammatory gene expression in macrophages. This reveals a macrophage-intrinsic mechanism linking SIRT6 to inflammation resolution, and it is relevant to atherosclerosis, where macrophage inflammation drives plaque progression. SIRT6's control of FoxO1 stability adds to its chromatin-based regulation of inflammatory genes.

label: GLUT2
description: SIRT6 deacetylates FoxO1 and subsequently increases expression of glucose-dependent transporter 2 (GLUT2) in pancreatic β-cells. Directionally, SIRT6 activates FoxO1, which induces GLUT2. Higher GLUT2 restores glucose sensing and appropriate insulin release, maintaining systemic glucose tolerance. This complements SIRT6's role in β-cell metabolic health and its repression of TXNIP to preserve insulin secretion. By supporting β-cell identity and function, SIRT6 protects against the β-cell failure that characterizes type 2 diabetes, and its actions in β-cells illustrate how a nuclear sirtuin controls nutrient sensing.

label: Preadipocyte differentiation
description: SIRT5 inhibits preadipocyte differentiation and lipid deposition by activating AMPK and repressing MAPK signaling pathways. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of suppressed adipogenesis. This keeps progenitors from becoming lipid-laden fat cells and positions mitochondrial SIRT5 as a negative regulator of fat accumulation. The AMPK arm likely raises NAD+ and reinforces catabolic metabolism, while MAPK repression blocks the mitogenic signaling required for adipocyte maturation. SIRT5's anti-adipogenic function is consistent with the sirtuin family's general opposition to lipid storage and its promotion of oxidative metabolism.

label: Autophagosome-lysosome fusion
description: TFEB is a master transcription factor for lysosomal biogenesis and autophagy that plays a critical role in autophagosome-lysosome fusion and clearance of cargo. Directionally, TFEB sits upstream of autophagic-lysosomal execution. Because SIRT2 stabilizes TFEB mRNA and SIRT1 deacetylates TFEB to promote its nuclear translocation, sirtuins influence TFEB function through multiple mechanisms. This links sirtuins to the terminal degradative step of autophagy, and TFEB's transcriptional program, known as CLEAR, coordinates the lysosomal and autophagic machinery that clears damaged proteins and organelles during stress.

label: LDHB
description: SIRT5-induced deacetylation of lactate dehydrogenase B (LDHB) triggers hyperactivation of autophagy, a process implicated in tumorigenesis. Directionally, SIRT5 modifies LDHB, which promotes autophagic hyperactivation. This connects mitochondrial acyl-metabolism control to lysosomal clearance, and the net effect can be context-dependent in cancer biology, supporting tumor-cell fitness under stress in some settings while potentially contributing to cell death in others. SIRT5's regulation of LDHB, a key enzyme of lactate metabolism, links metabolic enzymes to the autophagic program and illustrates the broad substrate repertoire of the desuccinylase.

label: SIRT5-mediated deacetylation of LDHB
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Deacetylation of LDHB by SIRT5 hyperactivates autophagy, accelerating cellular self-digestion and influencing tumor cell survival and metabolism. Directionally, SIRT5-mediated LDHB deacetylation sits upstream of autophagic hyperactivation. This can support tumor-cell fitness under stress by recycling nutrients, but it may also provoke cell-death programs when excessive. It exemplifies SIRT5's role at the autophagy-metabolism interface, where the same enzyme coordinates both fuel utilization and the clearance of cellular components. Understanding this axis is relevant to cancer therapy, where modulating autophagy can either sensitize or protect tumor cells.

label: Hyperactivation of autophagy
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Deacetylation of LDHB by SIRT5 hyperactivates autophagy, accelerating cellular self-digestion and influencing tumor cell survival and metabolism. Directionally, SIRT5-mediated LDHB deacetylation sits upstream of autophagic hyperactivation. This can support tumor-cell fitness under stress by recycling nutrients, but it may also provoke cell-death programs when excessive. It exemplifies SIRT5's role at the autophagy-metabolism interface, where the same enzyme coordinates both fuel utilization and the clearance of cellular components. Understanding this axis is relevant to cancer therapy, where modulating autophagy can either sensitize or protect tumor cells.

label: Nkx3.2
description: SIRT6 deacetylates histone H3K9 at the promoters of Nkx3.2 and related genes, thereby inhibiting Nkx3.2 transcription. Because Nkx3.2 is itself a repressor of GATA5, this double-negative cascade derepresses GATA5 to prevent endothelial injury and balances vascular protective gene programs. SIRT6 also regulates downstream targets including ERK1/2 through similar H3K9 deacetylation at their promoters, acting as a locus-specific transcriptional regulator. By removing the H3K9ac mark at these loci, SIRT6 silences genes that would otherwise promote pathological programs, a chromatin-based mechanism central to SIRT6's control of endothelial and cardiovascular homeostasis.

label: GATA5
description: SIRT6 induces expression of GATA-binding protein 5 (GATA5) by deacetylating H3K9 at the Nkx3.2 promoter, preventing endothelial injury. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of GATA5 induction. GATA5 supports endothelial integrity and opposes dysfunction, and its induction by SIRT6 protects the vasculature from injury. This is a vascular-protective transcriptional output of SIRT6, achieved through repression of the Nkx3.2 repressor. The SIRT6-Nkx3.2-GATA5 axis exemplifies how SIRT6 controls downstream genes through cascades of transcription factors, and it connects epigenetic regulation to endothelial function and vascular disease.

label: Polyphenol stilbene (3,4',5-trihydroxystilbene)
description: Resveratrol is the polyphenolic stilbene 3,4',5-trihydroxystilbene, a plant defensive compound produced under stress such as pathogen attack or UV exposure. Its chemical structure features three phenolic hydroxyls that confer redox activity and enable binding to sirtuin and phosphodiesterase targets. Directionally, resveratrol acts as the small-molecule upstream activator of SIRT1. Though a weak direct antioxidant compared with vitamin C or cysteine, its biological impact flows mainly through signaling modulation—activating SIRT1, AMPK, and eNOS, and inhibiting PDE4—rather than through stoichiometric scavenging of free radicals.

label: Grape skin
description: Resveratrol is found concentrated in grape skins, where it contributes to the anti-atherosclerotic benefits attributed to red wine consumption. Directionally, dietary resveratrol sits upstream of vascular protection. Skin content is modest and matrix-dependent, influencing how much reaches circulation, and typical red wine contains 1.5-3 mg/L, so a single glass provides only about 0.3 mg. This botanical source motivated the French-paradox hypothesis, and the presence of resveratrol in the skin rather than the flesh explains why wine, not grape juice, carries most of the compound.

label: Traditional East Asian medicine (Veratrum formosanum)
description: Resveratrol-containing plants such as Veratrum formosanum have long been used in traditional East Asian medicine, foreshadowing modern interest in the compound. Directionally, the traditional botanical use precedes and motivates contemporary pharmacological study. This ethnobotanical precedent parallels other stilbene-bearing remedies, and it contributed to the identification of resveratrol as a bioactive compound with cardiovascular and longevity-associated properties. It is historical context rather than a mechanistic claim, but it illustrates how traditional medicine has repeatedly pointed modern pharmacology toward bioactive natural products.

label: Endothelial cells from lipid damage
description: Resveratrol protects endothelial cells from lipid (e.g., oxidized-LDL) damage, helping preserve vascular barrier and nitric-oxide function. Directionally, resveratrol sits upstream of endothelial protection. This action is mediated through SIRT1/eNOS and antioxidant pathways, reducing the injurious effects of oxidized lipoproteins on the endothelium. It is a foundational vascular benefit supporting resveratrol's cardiovascular reputation, and it is consistent with resveratrol's inhibition of Lox-1-mediated foam-cell formation and its promotion of vasodilation. Preserving endothelial integrity is central to preventing the initiation and progression of atherosclerosis.

label: Vasodilation via nitric oxide synthesis modulation
description: Resveratrol promotes vasodilation by modulating nitric-oxide synthesis, principally via SIRT1-mediated activation of eNOS. Directionally, resveratrol sits upstream of NO-dependent relaxation. Improved vasodilation lowers vascular resistance and blood pressure, and enhanced NO bioavailability also reduces platelet aggregation and smooth-muscle proliferation. This is a direct mechanism behind its cardiovascular effects, and it connects resveratrol's SIRT1-activating action to endothelial function. Because endothelial NO is central to vascular health, resveratrol's ability to boost the SIRT1-eNOS axis underlies much of its reported cardiovascular benefit.

label: Platelet aggregation
description: Resveratrol inhibits platelet aggregation, reducing thrombotic risk and complementing its vascular benefits. Directionally, resveratrol sits upstream of suppressed platelet activation. This also creates a bleeding-risk caveat when combined with anticoagulants such as heparin or warfarin, since the anti-platelet effect adds to the anticoagulant's action. It is one of several anti-atherothrombotic actions of the compound, alongside its vasodilatory and anti-inflammatory effects. Clinicians therefore advise caution in anticoagulated patients, and the platelet effect is considered when assessing resveratrol's overall cardiovascular profile.

label: Smooth muscle cell proliferation
description: Resveratrol inhibits vascular smooth-muscle cell proliferation, limiting neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerotic plaque growth. Directionally, resveratrol sits upstream of suppressed VSMC expansion. This restrains the remodeling that narrows vessels after injury, and it complements resveratrol's anti-platelet and vasodilatory effects. The anti-proliferative action likely involves SIRT1, AMPK, and cell-cycle regulation in smooth-muscle cells, and it is relevant to restenosis and the progression of atherosclerosis. By controlling VSMC growth and migration, resveratrol contributes to preserving vascular lumen patency.

label: Coronary relaxation
description: Resveratrol enhances coronary relaxation, reduces ventricular arrhythmias, and inhibits platelet aggregation and smooth-muscle proliferation, collectively protecting the heart. Directionally, resveratrol sits upstream of improved coronary function. These integrated effects support myocardial perfusion under stress and reduce the risk of ischemic events and arrhythmogenesis. They reinforce resveratrol's cardioprotective profile, which is largely attributed to SIRT1, eNOS, and AMPK activation. The combination of improved vasodilation, reduced thrombotic tendency, and restrained vascular remodeling makes resveratrol a multifaceted cardiovascular agent in preclinical models.

label: Ventricular arrhythmias
description: Resveratrol reduces ventricular arrhythmias in preclinical models, likely via antioxidant, ion-channel, and eNOS-modulating actions. Directionally, resveratrol sits upstream of reduced arrhythmogenesis. This adds an electrophysiological benefit to its cardiovascular profile, and it is observed in animal studies with uncertain human translation. The anti-arrhythmic effect may reflect stabilization of cardiac ion channels, reduced oxidative stress, and improved NO signaling in the myocardium. These findings support resveratrol's reputation as a cardioprotective compound, though the relevance to human arrhythmia remains to be established in clinical settings.

label: Glucose metabolism
description: Resveratrol improves glucose metabolism and reduces LDL while elevating HDL, improving the lipid profile in metabolic models. Directionally, resveratrol sits upstream of better glycemic and lipoprotein control. These effects are largely SIRT1/AMPK-dependent, reflecting improved insulin sensitivity, reduced hepatic lipogenesis, and enhanced lipid oxidation. Human outcomes, however, are limited by resveratrol's poor bioavailability and short half-life, so translating these metabolic benefits to patients requires formulations that achieve effective plasma concentrations.

label: Direct antioxidant (weaker than vitamin C)
description: Resveratrol is a relatively poor direct antioxidant, weaker than vitamin C or cysteine at scavenging free radicals in vitro. Directionally, its redox-scavenging capacity is minor. Its biological benefits therefore arise mainly from signaling modulation—activation of SIRT1, AMPK, and eNOS, and inhibition of PDE4—rather than from stoichiometric antioxidant action. This corrects the simplistic antioxidant framing of resveratrol and explains why its effects can persist well after the compound has been metabolized. Understanding resveratrol as a hormetic signaling molecule rather than a direct antioxidant is central to interpreting its pharmacology.

label: Anti-viral effects
description: Resveratrol demonstrates antiviral effects in some experimental systems, though the evidence base is moderate and mechanism-dependent. Directionally, resveratrol sits upstream of viral inhibition in those models. Potential mechanisms include modulation of host stress and inflammatory pathways, inhibition of viral replication enzymes, and effects on cellular signaling that restrict viral spread. Clinical relevance remains preliminary, and the poor bioavailability of resveratrol limits translation. Nonetheless, the antiviral observations contribute to the compound's broad bioactivity profile and warrant further investigation of its role in host defense against specific viruses.

label: Anti-neoplastic effects
description: Resveratrol shows anti-neoplastic effects in preclinical models, including cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis induction, though confidence in human translation is moderate. Directionally, resveratrol sits upstream of suppressed tumor phenotype in those systems. Mechanisms may involve modulation of SIRT1, AMPK, NF-κB, and p53, which together restrain proliferation and promote death of cancer cells. Robust human anticancer efficacy is unproven, and bioavailability remains a major limitation. Nonetheless, the breadth of resveratrol's anti-cancer mechanisms continues to drive interest in its use as an adjunctive agent in oncology research.

label: Vasculature
description: SIRT1 is highly expressed in the vasculature, including endothelial and smooth-muscle cells, positioning it as a central regulator of vascular homeostasis. Directionally, constitutive vascular abundance enables rapid SIRT1 responses to metabolic and shear stress. This expression pattern underlies its roles in vasodilation, inflammation, and atherosclerosis, and loss of vascular SIRT1 promotes endothelial dysfunction. Because the endothelium is constantly exposed to hemodynamic and metabolic signals, SIRT1's abundance in this tissue allows it to integrate nutrient status with vascular function, making it a key determinant of blood-vessel health and disease.

label: Angiogenic activity during vascular remodeling
description: SIRT1 modulates angiogenic activity during vascular remodeling and growth, influencing endothelial sprouting and vessel stability in a context-dependent manner. Directionally, SIRT1 tunes angiogenic signaling. It can either promote or restrain angiogenesis depending on oxygen and metabolic cues, reflecting SIRT1's integration of stress and metabolic inputs in the vessel wall. In some settings SIRT1 supports the neovascularization needed for tissue repair, while in others it limits the pathological angiogenesis that feeds tumors. This context-dependence makes SIRT1 a nuanced regulator of vessel growth, with implications for both regenerative medicine and oncology.

label: Angiotensin II type 1 receptor expression
description: SIRT1 downregulates angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) expression in vascular smooth-muscle cells, reducing angiotensin-II signaling. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of AT1R suppression. Lower AT1R diminishes vasoconstriction and hypertensive signaling, contributing to SIRT1's antihypertensive actions. This is consistent with the observation that resveratrol-driven SIRT1 elevation reduces angiotensin-II-induced hypertension in vivo. By dampening the renin-angiotensin system's most important receptor, SIRT1 provides vascular protection that parallels the effects of AT1R blockers, positioning sirtuin activation as a complementary approach to blood-pressure control.

label: TIMP3 (tissue metalloproteinase 3)
description: SIRT1 regulates tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase 3 (TIMP3), an endogenous inhibitor of matrix metalloproteinases that defends against vascular inflammation and remodeling. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of TIMP3 regulation. By preserving TIMP3, SIRT1 limits extracellular-matrix degradation and inflammatory infiltration in vessels, protecting the vessel wall from pathological remodeling. This adds a matrix-protective dimension to SIRT1's vascular role, complementing its effects on eNOS, AT1R, and NF-κB. TIMP3 also regulates TNF-α signaling, so SIRT1-dependent TIMP3 maintenance connects sirtuins to both matrix homeostasis and inflammatory control.

label: Nuclear SIRT1 (enhanced by resveratrol)
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin System The Holy Grail of Resveratrol?.md
description: Nuclear SIRT1, enhanced by resveratrol, induces superoxide dismutase in cardiomyocytes, an antioxidant enzyme that suppresses cell death under stress. Directionally, nuclear SIRT1 sits upstream of SOD induction. This is a cardiomyoprotective output of resveratrol's SIRT1 activation, reducing oxidative damage and preserving cardiac cell viability during injury. It complements SIRT1's other cardiac actions, including SERCA2a deacetylation and PPARα activation, and it illustrates how resveratrol engages nuclear sirtuin activity to boost endogenous antioxidant defense. The SOD induction is part of the broader FOXO3a-dependent antioxidant program driven by SIRT1.

label: SIRT3-deficient mice
community_name: Severe cardiac hypertrophy and interstitial fibrosis
description: SIRT3-deficient mice develop severe cardiac hypertrophy and interstitial fibrosis when challenged with a hypertrophic stimulus, revealing SIRT3's protective role in the heart. Directionally, SIRT3 loss leads to pathological cardiac remodeling. This is driven by elevated ROS and impaired mitochondrial function, which fuel the hypertrophic and fibrotic response. It mirrors the resistance seen when SIRT3 is overexpressed, confirming a causal protective role. The phenotype highlights the importance of mitochondrial sirtuin activity for cardiac health and supports SIRT3 activation as a therapeutic strategy to prevent maladaptive remodeling in heart disease.

The phenotype highlights the importance of mitochondrial sirtuin activity for cardiac health and supports SIRT3 activation as a therapeutic strategy to prevent maladaptive remodeling in heart disease.

label: SIRT3-overexpressing mice
description: Transgenic mice overexpressing SIRT3 are significantly resistant to stimuli-induced cardiac hypertrophy, the inverse of the SIRT3-null phenotype. Directionally, SIRT3 gain leads to hypertrophy resistance. This protection arises from better mitochondrial ROS control, antioxidant enzyme expression, and metabolic flexibility, which together blunt the growth signals that drive pathological remodeling. It validates SIRT3 as a cardiac therapeutic target and is consistent with SIRT3's regulation of MnSOD, catalase, and mitochondrial Complex I. The complementary loss- and gain-of-function phenotypes firmly establish SIRT3 as a central cardiac protector.

label: Stimuli-induced cardiac hypertrophy
description: Transgenic mice overexpressing SIRT3 are significantly resistant to stimuli-induced cardiac hypertrophy, the inverse of the SIRT3-null phenotype. Directionally, SIRT3 gain leads to hypertrophy resistance. This protection arises from better mitochondrial ROS control, antioxidant enzyme expression, and metabolic flexibility, which together blunt the growth signals that drive pathological remodeling. It validates SIRT3 as a cardiac therapeutic target and is consistent with SIRT3's regulation of MnSOD, catalase, and mitochondrial Complex I. The complementary loss- and gain-of-function phenotypes firmly establish SIRT3 as a central cardiac protector.

label: SIRT7-deficient mice
description: SIRT7-deficient mice show extensive myocardial fibrosis, high basal apoptosis, and cardiomyopathy, reflecting SIRT7's role in maintaining cardiac homeostasis. Directionally, SIRT7 loss leads to fibrotic cardiomyopathy. This contrasts with contexts where SIRT7 promotes fibrosis under stress, indicating that SIRT7 is overall required for myocardial integrity. The phenotype likely reflects SIRT7's contributions to ribosome biogenesis, mitochondrial function, and transcriptional regulation in cardiomyocytes, and it is consistent with SIRT7's deacetylation of GATA4 in stress-induced hypertrophy. SIRT7 thus has both protective and pathological cardiac roles depending on context.

label: Extensive myocardial fibrosis and cardiomyopathy
description: SIRT7-deficient mice show extensive myocardial fibrosis, high basal apoptosis, and cardiomyopathy, reflecting SIRT7's role in maintaining cardiac homeostasis. Directionally, SIRT7 loss leads to fibrotic cardiomyopathy. This contrasts with contexts where SIRT7 promotes fibrosis under stress, indicating that SIRT7 is overall required for myocardial integrity. The phenotype likely reflects SIRT7's contributions to ribosome biogenesis, mitochondrial function, and transcriptional regulation in cardiomyocytes, and it is consistent with SIRT7's deacetylation of GATA4 in stress-induced hypertrophy. SIRT7 thus has both protective and pathological cardiac roles depending on context.

label: Red wine matrix
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin System The Holy Grail of Resveratrol?.md
description: Resveratrol achieves efficacious levels only when ingested within the red-wine matrix, which contains co-constituents that slow its metabolism and improve exposure. Directionally, matrix components sit upstream of better resveratrol bioavailability. This helps resolve discrepancies between in vitro potency and in vivo human trials, and it supports whole-food approaches over isolated-compound supplementation. Quercetin and ethanol in particular may inhibit resveratrol's catabolic enzymes, prolonging its presence. The matrix effect is a key consideration for designing resveratrol formulations and for interpreting epidemiological associations between wine consumption and health.

label: Resveratrol bioavailability
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin System The Holy Grail of Resveratrol?.md

label: ~8–14 minutes
description: Resveratrol has a very short plasma half-life of roughly 8-14 minutes because of rapid conjugation and clearance. Directionally, rapid metabolism sits upstream of low systemic exposure. This severely limits the duration of any SIRT1 activation after a single dose, and it is the central pharmacological obstacle to translating resveratrol's preclinical benefits to humans. Sustained-release formulations, metabolic inhibitors such as quercetin, and delivery within the red-wine matrix are strategies to improve exposure. Understanding the half-life is essential for interpreting both negative clinical trials and claims about resveratrol's efficacy.

label: Cytochrome P450
description: Hepatic cytochrome P450 enzymes contribute to resveratrol catabolism, alongside phase-II conjugation, determining its metabolic fate. Directionally, CYP enzymes sit upstream of resveratrol clearance. This hepatic handling caps bioavailability, and it is relevant to drug-drug interactions and dosing, since resveratrol both is metabolized by and inhibits cytochrome P450 activity. The combination of rapid conjugation and CYP-mediated oxidation explains resveratrol's short half-life. Because resveratrol can both be metabolized by and inhibit CYP enzymes, co-administered drugs may see altered clearance, a clinically important consideration for supplementation.

label: Cytochrome P450 activity
description: Resveratrol both is metabolized by and inhibits cytochrome P450 activity, creating a self-reinforcing effect on its own clearance and on co-administered drugs. Directionally, resveratrol sits upstream of CYP inhibition. This can alter the pharmacokinetics of other medications, since CYP inhibition slows their metabolism, and it also affects resveratrol's own disposition. It is a clinically relevant interaction caveat for supplementation, especially in patients taking drugs with narrow therapeutic windows. Understanding the bidirectional CYP relationship is important for predicting both resveratrol's bioavailability and its potential to influence drug exposure.

label: Quercetin and ethanol
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin System The Holy Grail of Resveratrol?.md
description: Quercetin and ethanol, red-wine constituents, augment resveratrol activity possibly by inhibiting its catabolic enzymes and improving exposure. Directionally, these co-compounds sit upstream of enhanced resveratrol effect. This helps explain the matrix/bioavailability phenomenon, whereby resveratrol shows efficacy within the whole-food matrix but not as an isolated compound. It suggests combination formulations could improve efficacy, and it is consistent with the idea that polyphenols act synergistically. The augmentation is particularly relevant to interpreting the French paradox and to designing resveratrol-based interventions that replicate the wine matrix.

label: French Paradox
description: The French paradox describes lower cardiovascular-disease incidence in some French populations despite high-fat diets, often attributed in part to moderate wine and resveratrol consumption. Directionally, moderate wine intake sits upstream of reduced CVD in this epidemiological observation. Causality is debated, with diet and lifestyle confounders complicating the interpretation, and the wine matrix and polyphenol content may contribute. Resveratrol's vascular actions provide a plausible, but not proven, mechanism, and the concept has driven considerable research into wine polyphenols, sirtuins, and cardiovascular health.

label: Reduced CVD incidence with moderate wine consumption despite high-fat diet
description: The French paradox describes lower cardiovascular-disease incidence in some French populations despite high-fat diets, often attributed in part to moderate wine and resveratrol consumption. Directionally, moderate wine intake sits upstream of reduced CVD in this epidemiological observation. Causality is debated, with diet and lifestyle confounders complicating the interpretation, and the wine matrix and polyphenol content may contribute. Resveratrol's vascular actions provide a plausible, but not proven, mechanism, and the concept has driven considerable research into wine polyphenols, sirtuins, and cardiovascular health.

label: Bleeding risk with concurrent anticoagulant use
description: Because resveratrol inhibits platelet aggregation, concurrent use with anticoagulants such as heparin or warfarin may increase bleeding risk. Directionally, resveratrol combined with anticoagulants sits upstream of heightened bleeding liability. This is a practical safety caveat for supplementation, and clinicians advise caution in anticoagulated patients. The additive anti-platelet and anticoagulant effects raise the risk of hemorrhage, particularly at higher doses. Anyone taking blood thinners should discuss resveratrol supplementation with their healthcare provider, since the interaction is plausible based on resveratrol's pharmacology.

label: SIRT1 downregulation of angiotensin II type 1 receptor
description: SIRT1-mediated downregulation of AT1R expression produces antihypertensive effects; in vivo, resveratrol-driven SIRT1 elevation reduces angiotensin-II-induced hypertension. Directionally, SIRT1-mediated AT1R suppression sits upstream of lower blood pressure. This couples SIRT1 activation to vascular tone control, since reduced AT1R diminishes angiotensin-II-driven vasoconstriction and sodium retention. It is a mechanistic basis for resveratrol's antihypertensive actions, and it parallels the therapeutic strategy of AT1R blockade used clinically. By targeting the same receptor the drugs block, SIRT1 provides an endogenous route to restrain the renin-angiotensin system.

label: Anti-hypertensive effects
description: SIRT1-mediated downregulation of AT1R expression produces antihypertensive effects; in vivo, resveratrol-driven SIRT1 elevation reduces angiotensin-II-induced hypertension. Directionally, SIRT1-mediated AT1R suppression sits upstream of lower blood pressure. This couples SIRT1 activation to vascular tone control, since reduced AT1R diminishes angiotensin-II-driven vasoconstriction and sodium retention. It is a mechanistic basis for resveratrol's antihypertensive actions, and it parallels the therapeutic strategy of AT1R blockade used clinically. By targeting the same receptor the drugs block, SIRT1 provides an endogenous route to restrain the renin-angiotensin system.

label: Beclin1
description: SIRT1 deacetylates Beclin-1 at multiple lysines, promoting its interaction with the class III PI3K Vps34 and enhancing autophagy initiation and flux. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically licenses Beclin-1. This supports autophagosome formation and cellular clearance, and it is a central SIRT1 autophagy substrate alongside LC3, Atg5, Atg7, and ULK1. By deacetylating Beclin-1, SIRT1 promotes the assembly of the autophagy initiation complex and couples nutrient status to cellular quality control. This mechanism contributes to SIRT1's protection against the accumulation of damaged proteins and organelles during aging.

label: FoxO1 (pancreatic β cells)
description: In pancreatic β-cells, SIRT6 deacetylates FoxO1 and increases GLUT2 expression to maintain glucose-sensing ability and systemic glucose tolerance. Directionally, SIRT6 enzymatically activates FoxO1 in β-cells. This preserves insulin-secretory competence under metabolic challenge, since GLUT2 is required for β-cells to sense glucose and respond appropriately. It mirrors SIRT6's broader metabolic-protective phenotype, including its repression of TXNIP to maintain glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. SIRT6's β-cell function is essential for preventing the glucose-intolerant state that characterizes type 2 diabetes.

label: Nrf2 (via Keap1 modification)
description: SIRT1 activates Nrf2 by modifying Keap1 structure, leading to Nrf2 nuclear translocation and expression of antioxidant genes. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of Nrf2 activation. This is a canonical cytoprotective axis against oxidative and electrophilic insult, and it complements SIRT1's direct antioxidant substrate actions through FOXO and PGC-1α. Because Nrf2 coordinates the expression of hundreds of detoxifying and antioxidant enzymes, SIRT1-dependent Nrf2 activation provides broad protection against cellular stress. This pathway is relevant to aging, where declining Nrf2 activity contributes to the accumulation of oxidative damage.

label: NLRP3 inflammasome (via AMPKα/XBP1)
description: SIRT1 protects against inflammation by deacetylating and attenuating NLRP3 activity via the AMPKα/XBP1 pathway in macrophages. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically suppresses NLRP3 through XBP1s. This couples endoplasmic-reticulum stress responses to innate immune regulation, and it is a refined mechanistic view of SIRT1's anti-inflammasome action. By deacetylating XBP1s downstream of AMPK, SIRT1 prevents NLRP3 assembly and the subsequent maturation of IL-1β. This pathway is relevant to atherosclerotic and metabolic disease, where inflammasome-driven inflammation contributes to tissue damage and insulin resistance.

label: Heart failure (via SERCA2a deacetylation)
description: SIRT1 deacetylates SERCA2a at Lys492, restoring its activity and improving cardiac contractility in heart failure. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically rescues SERCA2a function. Better calcium handling opposes the systolic dysfunction of failing hearts, since SERCA2a-mediated calcium reuptake is depressed in heart failure. This is a direct mechanistic rationale for SIRT1 activation in cardiomyopathy, and it complements SIRT1's effects on PPARα, antioxidant genes, and cardiac metabolism. By restoring the molecular pump that controls cardiac relaxation, SIRT1 addresses a fundamental defect in the failing myocardium.

label: TGF-β1/Smad3 signaling
description: SIRT6 prevents TGF-β1-induced lung myofibroblast differentiation by inactivating TGF-β1/Smad3 signaling, limiting fibrogenesis. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of TGF-β1/Smad3 blockade. This complements SIRT6's other antifibrotic actions in heart and kidney, and it positions SIRT6 as a broad suppressor of Smad3-driven fibrosis. By blocking myofibroblast differentiation, SIRT6 prevents the accumulation of contractile, matrix-producing cells that drive tissue scarring. SIRT6 activation therefore represents a potential strategy for pulmonary fibrosis and other fibrotic diseases where TGF-β signaling is central.

label: MFN2 (at K655, K662)
description: SIRT1 deacetylates mitofusin 2 (MFN2) at Lys655 and Lys662, regulating mitochondrial fusion and quality control; loss of SIRT1 causes defective autophagy linked to impaired MFN2 function. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically modifies MFN2. This connects sirtuin activity to mitochondrial dynamics and mitophagy, and it is relevant to neurodegenerative and metabolic disease where fusion is perturbed. By modulating MFN2, SIRT1 influences the balance between mitochondrial fusion and fission that determines mitochondrial network health. This regulation links SIRT1's pro-autophagy and mitophagy functions to the machinery that maintains mitochondrial integrity.

label: p53 at Lys379
description: SIRT1 deacetylates p53 specifically at Lys379, inhibiting p53-dependent apoptosis and promoting cell survival under genotoxic stress. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically inactivates p53 at this site. This is one of several lysines, including Lys317 and Lys370, targeted by SIRT1, and the net effect is cytoprotection that can be oncogenic in established tumors. By dampening p53-mediated apoptosis, SIRT1 biases cells toward repair and survival after DNA damage. The p53-SIRT1 axis is thus a double-edged sword, protecting normal tissues but also potentially shielding cancer cells from death signals.

label: AMPK (preadipocyte differentiation)
description: SIRT5 inhibits preadipocyte differentiation by activating AMPK and repressing MAPK signaling, analogous to its broader adipogenesis-blocking role. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of AMPK activation in adipogenic progenitors. Activated AMPK shifts cells away from lipogenesis and toward catabolism, while MAPK repression blocks the proliferative signals needed for adipocyte maturation. It reaffirms SIRT5 as a negative regulator of fat formation, and it is consistent with the general anti-adipogenic theme across sirtuins. By restraining adipocyte differentiation, SIRT5 contributes to the maintenance of metabolic flexibility and the prevention of excessive fat accumulation.

label: Nicotinamide to NMN
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: NAMPT condenses nicotinamide with 5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP) to form NMN, the rate-limiting step of the NAD+ salvage pathway. Directionally, NAMPT sits upstream of NMN and NAD+ biosynthesis. This recovers nicotinamide that would otherwise feedback-inhibit sirtuins, and AMPK and SIRT1 both induce NAMPT, creating a positive loop for NAD+ and sirtuin activity. Because NAMPT is rate-limiting, its regulation largely determines NAD+ availability in most tissues. Preserving or inducing NAMPT is thus a central strategy for maintaining sirtuin function and NAD+-dependent metabolism.

label: TGF-beta1
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: TGF-β1 binds the type II receptor (TβRII), which recruits and phosphorylates the type I receptor (TβRI), leading to phosphorylation and nuclear translocation of SMAD2/3 to drive fibrotic transcription. Directionally, TGF-β1 sits upstream of SMAD3 activation. This canonical pathway is the main driver of pathological fibrosis across organs, inducing collagen, fibronectin, and other matrix genes. Sirtuins such as SIRT6 and SIRT7 intersect this axis at multiple points, either by deacetylating SMAD3 or by repressing SMAD3-dependent transcription. Understanding the TGF-β/SMAD cascade is essential for interpreting sirtuin effects on fibrosis.

label: SMAD3
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: TGF-β1 binds the type II receptor (TβRII), which recruits and phosphorylates the type I receptor (TβRI), leading to phosphorylation and nuclear translocation of SMAD2/3 to drive fibrotic transcription. Directionally, TGF-β1 sits upstream of SMAD3 activation. This canonical pathway is the main driver of pathological fibrosis across organs, inducing collagen, fibronectin, and other matrix genes. Sirtuins such as SIRT6 and SIRT7 intersect this axis at multiple points, either by deacetylating SMAD3 or by repressing SMAD3-dependent transcription. Understanding the TGF-β/SMAD cascade is essential for interpreting sirtuin effects on fibrosis.

label: Pathological fibrosis
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: TGF-β1 activates SMAD3-dependent transcription of pro-fibrotic genes including COL1A1, COL3A1, FN1, ACTA2, and TIMP1, driving collagen deposition and tissue scarring in multiple organs. Directionally, TGF-β1 sits upstream of fibrogenesis. This makes TGF-β1 a central target in fibrosis therapeutics, and sirtuins that inhibit SMAD3 signaling, such as SIRT6 and SIRT7, are antifibrotic. Because fibrosis is the common final pathway of chronic organ injury, understanding the TGF-β1/SMAD3 axis is central to developing treatments for heart, lung, kidney, and liver fibrosis. Sirtuin activation is emerging as one such strategy.

label: BRCA1
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: BRCA1 is recruited to DNA double-strand breaks by the MRN complex, promotes end resection, and facilitates RAD51 loading via PALB2 and BRCA2 to execute homologous recombination repair. Directionally, BRCA1 sits upstream of high-fidelity double-strand-break repair. Loss of BRCA1 cripples homologous recombination, increasing mutation and cancer risk, particularly in breast and ovarian tissue. Sirtuins such as SIRT2 support BRCA1 localization to damage sites, linking sirtuin activity to genome stability. The BRCA1 pathway is also the basis for synthetic lethality with PARP inhibitors in BRCA-deficient cancers.

label: Homologous recombination repair
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: BRCA1 is recruited to DNA double-strand breaks by the MRN complex, promotes end resection, and facilitates RAD51 loading via PALB2 and BRCA2 to execute homologous recombination repair.
