label: BRCA1 deficiency
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Loss of BRCA1 triggers increased autophagy as a compensatory survival mechanism in breast and ovarian cancers, buffering the viability impact of defective homologous recombination. Directionally, BRCA1 deficiency sits upstream of autophagic upregulation. This metabolic rewiring can be co-opted by tumors to survive despite genome instability, and it connects genome-maintenance failure to lysosomal clearance pathways. Because autophagy supports the survival of BRCA-deficient cells, combining PARP inhibitors with autophagy inhibitors is being explored as a therapeutic strategy. The compensatory autophagy illustrates how cancer cells adapt to DNA-repair defects.

label: Compensatory autophagy
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Loss of BRCA1 triggers increased autophagy as a compensatory survival mechanism in breast and ovarian cancers, buffering the viability impact of defective homologous recombination. Directionally, BRCA1 deficiency sits upstream of autophagic upregulation. label: BRCA1 mutation
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: BRCA1-deficient tumors are exquisitely sensitive to PARP inhibitors because blocking base-excision (PARP) repair in the setting of defective homologous recombination causes catastrophic, lethal DNA damage through synthetic lethality. Directionally, BRCA1 mutation sits upstream of PARP-inhibitor vulnerability. This is a cornerstone of precision oncology, targeting the specific repair defect of the tumor. It illustrates how repair-pathway context determines therapeutic selectivity, and it has transformed the treatment of BRCA-mutated breast and ovarian cancer. Sirtuins that modulate repair pathways may influence sensitivity to such agents.

label: PARP inhibitors (synthetic lethality)
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: BRCA1-deficient tumors are exquisitely sensitive to PARP inhibitors because blocking base-excision (PARP) repair in the setting of defective homologous recombination causes catastrophic, lethal DNA damage through synthetic lethality. Directionally, BRCA1 mutation sits upstream of PARP-inhibitor vulnerability. This is a cornerstone of precision oncology, targeting the specific repair defect of the tumor. It illustrates how repair-pathway context determines therapeutic selectivity, and it has transformed the treatment of BRCA-mutated breast and ovarian cancer. Sirtuins that modulate repair pathways may influence sensitivity to such agents.

label: Caspase-3 (at Ser150)
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: p38 MAPK phosphorylates caspase-3 at Ser150, suppressing its proteolytic activity; this inhibition is reversed by the phosphatase PP2A. Directionally, p38 sits upstream of caspase-3 inhibition. This provides a survival signal that tempers apoptosis under certain stresses, and it shows that stress kinases can directly restrain executioner caspases. By phosphorylating pro-caspase-3, p38 reduces the pool available for proteolytic activation, blunting the death response. This regulatory layer illustrates how the balance between kinases and phosphatases determines the threshold for apoptotic commitment under stress.

label: ULK1, ATG13, FIP200, ATG101
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: ULK1 functions within a stable initiation complex containing ATG13, FIP200 (RB1CC1), and ATG101, which nucleates autophagosome formation in response to nutrient status. Directionally, the complex sits upstream of autophagy initiation. SIRT1 deacetylates and activates ULK1 within this complex, positioning sirtuins at the top of the autophagic machinery. The ULK1 complex integrates signals from AMPK and mTORC1, which either activate or inhibit it depending on energy and nutrient state. This makes the initiation complex the central decision point for whether autophagy proceeds.

label: ULK1 (at Ser757)
description: Under nutrient-rich conditions, mTORC1 phosphorylates ULK1 at Ser757, disrupting its interaction with AMPK and suppressing autophagy. Directionally, mTORC1 sits upstream of ULK1 inhibition. This couples nutrient abundance to autophagic restraint, and it is the basis for rapamycin's autophagy-promoting effects. Sirtuin and AMPK activation opposes mTORC1 to relicense ULK1, connecting sirtuin biology to the nutrient-sensing control of autophagy. The AMPK-mTORC1-ULK1 network is a central regulatory circuit that determines autophagic flux in response to energy and growth signals.

label: STRAD and MO25 for activity
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: LKB1 requires binding to STRAD and MO25 to exit the nucleus and gain full kinase activity; without this scaffold it remains inactive. Directionally, STRAD and MO25 sit upstream of LKB1 activation. This gating is essential for LKB1's role as the master upstream AMPK kinase, and SIRT1 and AMPK deacetylate and phosphorylate LKB1 to modulate its localization. The STRAD/MO25 scaffold both stabilizes LKB1 and directs it to the cytoplasm where it can activate AMPK. Mutations in LKB1, as in Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, disrupt this pathway and predispose to cancer.

label: Thr172
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: LKB1 is the primary upstream kinase phosphorylating AMPK at Thr172 in the activation loop, increasing AMPK activity over a hundred-fold. Directionally, LKB1 sits upstream of AMPK activation. This couples energy sensing to metabolic reprogramming, since activated AMPK promotes catabolism and inhibits anabolism. Sirtuins feed into this node via LKB1 deacetylation and AMPK-dependent NAD+ elevation, creating a self-reinforcing circuit. The LKB1-AMPK pathway is a central regulator of cellular energy homeostasis, and its dysregulation contributes to metabolic disease and cancer.

label: LKB1 deficiency
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Germline loss-of-function mutations in STK11 (LKB1) cause Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, characterized by hamartomatous polyps and elevated cancer risk. Directionally, LKB1 deficiency sits upstream of this cancer predisposition. This highlights LKB1 as a critical tumor suppressor and metabolic regulator, and its connection to AMPK and sirtuin axes explains the metabolic features of the syndrome. Because LKB1 loss compromises AMPK activation, cells fail to properly sense energy stress, promoting growth and genomic instability. The syndrome illustrates the clinical importance of the LKB1-AMPK-sirtuin network.

label: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Germline loss-of-function mutations in STK11 (LKB1) cause Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, characterized by hamartomatous polyps and elevated cancer risk. Directionally, LKB1 deficiency sits upstream of this cancer predisposition. This highlights LKB1 as a critical tumor suppressor and metabolic regulator, and its connection to AMPK and sirtuin axes explains the metabolic features of the syndrome. Because LKB1 loss compromises AMPK activation, cells fail to properly sense energy stress, promoting growth and genomic instability. label: Beclin1 BH3 domain
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: The BH3 domain of Beclin1 binds anti-apoptotic Bcl-2/Bcl-xL proteins, which sequester it and inhibit autophagy, linking apoptosis and autophagy regulation. Directionally, Bcl-2 sits upstream of Beclin1 sequestration. SIRT1 deacetylation of Beclin1 modulates this interaction, illustrating the molecular crosstalk between cell-death and clearance pathways. When Bcl-2 sequesters Beclin1, autophagy is suppressed, but under stress signals that release Beclin1, autophagy proceeds. This interplay determines whether cells commit to apoptosis or to autophagic survival, and it is central to both normal physiology and cancer cell fate decisions.

label: Bcl-2 anti-apoptotic proteins
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: The BH3 domain of Beclin1 binds anti-apoptotic Bcl-2/Bcl-xL proteins, which sequester it and inhibit autophagy, linking apoptosis and autophagy regulation. Directionally, Bcl-2 sits upstream of Beclin1 sequestration. SIRT1 deacetylation of Beclin1 modulates this interaction, illustrating the molecular crosstalk between cell-death and clearance pathways. When Bcl-2 sequesters Beclin1, autophagy is suppressed, but under stress signals that release Beclin1, autophagy proceeds. label: Four distinct class III PI3K complexes
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Beclin1 scaffolds four class III PI3K complexes (I/Atg14L, II/UVRAG, III/UVRAG+Rubicon, IV/Bif-1) that regulate autophagy at initiation, nucleation, and maturation stages. Directionally, Beclin1 sits upstream of autophagosome machinery assembly. SIRT1 deacetylates Beclin1 to enhance Vps34 activity, making Beclin1 a hub integrating sirtuin signals into autophagy. The distinct complexes direct autophagosome nucleation, membrane expansion, and fusion with lysosomes, and their composition determines whether autophagy proceeds or is restrained. Beclin1's central scaffolding role makes it a critical control point for autophagic flux.

label: Tumour suppressor (glutamine metabolism)
description: SIRT4 acts as a tumor suppressor by inhibiting GDH and restricting glutamine-derived anaplerosis into the TCA cycle, starving cancer cells of carbon for proliferation. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of suppressed glutamine metabolism. This limits the glutamine addiction of tumors, which rely on glutamine for both energy and biosynthesis, and it is a context where SIRT4 opposes rather than promotes growth. By restraining glutamine utilization, SIRT4 reduces the metabolic support for rapid proliferation, and its loss in some cancers relieves this brake. SIRT4's tumor-suppressive role is thus tied to its regulation of mitochondrial metabolism.

label: MTPα (fatty acid oxidation)
description: SIRT4 suppresses fatty-acid oxidation in liver by inhibiting the mitochondrial trifunctional protein α subunit (MTPα), promoting lipid accumulation under nutrient-replete conditions. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of reduced β-oxidation. This contrasts with SIRT3 and SIRT5, which support fat oxidation, and it positions SIRT4 as a mitochondrial anabolic brake that conserves lipids when nutrients are abundant. The inhibition of MTPα and of PPARα signaling shifts metabolism away from mitochondrial fatty-acid utilization toward lipid storage. SIRT4's opposition to oxidative metabolism is central to the antagonistic SIRT3/SIRT4 balance.

label: H3K18ac
description: SIRT7 possesses NAD+-dependent deacetylase activity with high selectivity for histone H3 lysine 18 acetylation (H3K18ac), a mark of active transcription at rDNA and elsewhere. Directionally, SIRT7 enzymatically removes H3K18ac. Deacetylation at pericentric heterochromatin maintains genomic stability and silences repetitive elements, and the selectivity of SIRT7 for this mark distinguishes it from other sirtuins. This substrate specificity underlies SIRT7's roles in ribosome biogenesis and chromatin integrity, and its dysregulation contributes to genomic instability and disease. SIRT7's H3K18ac control is thus central to its nuclear functions.

label: Replicative lifespan
description: Overexpression of SIRT7 extends the replicative lifespan of primary human cells by maintaining rDNA stability and reducing mitochondrial dysfunction. Directionally, SIRT7 gain sits upstream of prolonged cellular lifespan. This mirrors the pro-longevity roles of other sirtuins and supports a broadly conserved lifespan-promoting function for the family. The mechanism likely involves preservation of ribosomal DNA repeats, maintenance of heterochromatin, and support of mitochondrial gene expression through GABPβ1. SIRT7's ability to extend replicative lifespan is consistent with the theme that sirtuin activity generally counteracts cellular senescence.

label: 1.5 to 3 mg per liter
description: Typical red wine contains 1.5-3 mg/L trans-resveratrol, up to about 5.8 mg/L in some cool-climate wines, with a 5-ounce glass providing only about 0.3 mg. Directionally, wine content sits upstream of modest resveratrol intake. This low dose highlights why drinking alone may not reach pharmacologic exposures, and it contextualizes the French-paradox and matrix-bioavailability discussion. Because red wine's co-constituents, including quercetin and ethanol, may improve resveratrol's bioavailability, the whole-matrix effect matters for interpreting epidemiological associations with wine consumption.

label: 0.15 to 1.3 mg per 100g
description: Raw red grapes contain roughly 0.15-1.3 mg resveratrol per 100 g, mostly in the skins, making dietary intake from fruit modest. Directionally, grape content sits upstream of limited resveratrol exposure. Skin concentration explains why wine, not flesh, carries most of the compound, and it reinforces that supplementation, rather than diet alone, reaches high doses. Even so, grape-derived resveratrol contributes to the polyphenol intake associated with Mediterranean-style diets. Understanding the natural abundance of resveratrol is important for interpreting both dietary and supplement-based research.

label: Vine Tea (Ampelopsis grossedentata)
description: Vine tea (Ampelopsis grossedentata) leaves contain 20-30% dihydromyricetin (DHM) by weight, so 1-1.5 g of dry leaf suffices for roughly a 300 mg therapeutic dose. Directionally, the botanical source sits upstream of DHM availability. DHM is a potent SIRT3 and AMPK activator, and this makes vine tea a practical natural source of the compound. The high DHM content distinguishes vine tea from most other botanical sources and supports its traditional use as a metabolic tonic. This abundance is a key practical advantage for studying and using DHM clinically.

label: Cyanidin-3-glucoside
description: Black elderberries provide roughly 350-450 mg cyanidin-3-glucoside per 100 g of fresh fruit, with about 70-85 g reaching a 300 mg therapeutic dose. Directionally, berry content sits upstream of anthocyanin intake. Cyanidin is a powerful natural SIRT6 activator, and this positions elderberry as a dietary SIRT6-modulating food. The high anthocyanin content makes elderberry one of the richest natural sources of cyanidin, and its traditional use for immune support is consistent with the bioactivity of these compounds. Understanding the dose achievable from food is essential for interpreting dietary studies.

label: 350 to 450 mg per 100g
description: Black elderberries provide roughly 350-450 mg cyanidin-3-glucoside per 100 g of fresh fruit, with about 70-85 g reaching a 300 mg therapeutic dose. Directionally, berry content sits upstream of anthocyanin intake. Cyanidin is a powerful natural SIRT6 activator, and this positions elderberry as a dietary SIRT6-modulating food. The high anthocyanin content makes elderberry one of the richest natural sources of cyanidin, and its traditional use for immune support is consistent with the bioactivity of these compounds. Understanding the dose achievable from food is essential for interpreting dietary studies.

label: Water
description: Honokiol is highly lipophilic with very poor water solubility, so hot-water tea extraction is inefficient and ethanol tinctures or supercritical CO2 extracts are needed for therapeutic dosing. Directionally, the physicochemical property sits upstream of formulation requirement. Its lipophilicity also aids cell and mitochondrial membrane penetration, supporting SIRT3 engagement and explaining its potency despite poor aqueous solubility. This is a practical caveat for honokiol use, since the delivery vehicle determines both absorption and bioavailability. Nanoparticle and other advanced formulations are being explored to improve honokiol's pharmacokinetics.

label: Dual mechanism (direct + indirect)
description: Resveratrol activates SIRT1 through both direct allosteric binding at the N-terminal domain (Glu230) and an indirect cascade via PDE4/cAMP/Epac1/Ca2+/CaMKKβ/AMPK/NAMPT/NAD+. Directionally, resveratrol sits upstream of dual SIRT1 activation. The indirect limb raises NAD+ to fuel SIRT1, amplifying the direct effect, and this dual mechanism explains resveratrol's robust pleiotropic metabolic benefits. Because the two arms are complementary, blocking either reduces but does not eliminate SIRT1 activation. This layered regulation is a defining feature of resveratrol as a sirtuin-activating compound.

label: Tenovin-6
description: Tenovin-6 inhibits SIRT2 with an IC50 of 10 μM, making SIRT2 its more potent sirtuin target compared with SIRT1. Directionally, Tenovin-6 blocks SIRT2 catalysis. By inhibiting SIRT2 deacetylation, it can protect neurons and reactivate p53, and it also inhibits SIRT3 with an IC50 of 67 μM, so its effects span multiple sirtuins. It is a chemical probe distinguishing SIRT2 from other sirtuins, and its p53-reactivation activity underlies its anticancer phenotype. The moderate potency and limited selectivity require careful interpretation of Tenovin-6 studies.

label: Tenovins
description: By inhibiting SIRT1/SIRT2-mediated deacetylation, Tenovins promote p53 hyperacetylation and reactivation of p53-dependent transcriptional networks. Directionally, Tenovin-mediated sirtuin inhibition sits upstream of p53 activation. This restores p53 tumor-suppressive function in cells where sirtuins silence it, and it is the basis for Tenovins' anticancer activity. Because p53 is a central tumor suppressor, its reactivation by sirtuin inhibition represents a compelling strategy for p53-wild-type tumors. The hyperacetylation increases p53 stability and transcriptional potency, driving cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis.

label: p53 (via hyperacetylation)
description: By inhibiting SIRT1/SIRT2-mediated deacetylation, Tenovins promote p53 hyperacetylation and reactivation of p53-dependent transcriptional networks. Directionally, Tenovin-mediated sirtuin inhibition sits upstream of p53 activation. This restores p53 tumor-suppressive function in cells where sirtuins silence it, and it is the basis for Tenovins' anticancer activity. Because p53 is a central tumor suppressor, its reactivation by sirtuin inhibition represents a compelling strategy for p53-wild-type tumors. The hyperacetylation increases p53 stability and transcriptional potency, driving cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis.

label: Xenograft models
description: Tenovin-1 and Tenovin-6 significantly delay tumor growth in human cancer mouse xenografts at single-digit micromolar concentrations. Directionally, Tenovin treatment sits upstream of reduced tumor growth. This effect is attributed to p53 reactivation and sirtuin inhibition, and it validates sirtuin inhibition as an anticancer strategy in p53-wild-type tumors. The xenograft data demonstrate that sirtuin inhibitors can exert anti-tumor efficacy in vivo, complementing the extensive in vitro evidence. These results support the continued development of sirtuin inhibitors for oncology, particularly in combination with DNA-damaging agents.

label: Splitomicin
description: Splitomicin inhibits human SIRT1 with an IC50 of 96 μM in vitro by blocking NAD+-dependent deacetylation. Directionally, Splitomicin sits upstream of SIRT1 inhibition. It is an early-tool sirtuin inhibitor used to probe SIRT1 phenotypes, though its moderate potency limits in vivo utility. Splitomicin also inhibits SIRT2 with an IC50 of 113 μM, and its effects on NF-κB acetylation and inflammation are consistent with sirtuin inhibition. As a first-generation inhibitor, Splitomicin helped establish the concept that sirtuin blockade can be achieved pharmacologically.

label: NF-κB p65
description: Splitomicin reduces intracellular deacetylase activity, causing hyperacetylation and enhanced nuclear translocation of NF-κB p65, amplifying inflammatory transcription. Directionally, Splitomicin-mediated sirtuin inhibition sits upstream of increased NF-κB signaling. This demonstrates the converse of SIRT1's normal anti-inflammatory action and shows experimentally that sirtuin tone sets inflammatory set-points. By inhibiting SIRT1 and SIRT2, Splitomicin permits p65 hyperacetylation and nuclear accumulation, driving cytokine expression. This inverse relationship is important evidence that sirtuins restrain NF-κB and that their loss is pro-inflammatory.

label: Ischemic preconditioning cardioprotection
description: In ischemic-preconditioning models, Splitomicin reverses protective lysine deacetylation and abolishes preconditioning-induced cardioprotection. Directionally, Splitomicin-mediated sirtuin inhibition sits upstream of lost cardiac protection. This indicates that sirtuin deacetylase activity is required for ischemic tolerance, and it argues that sirtuin activation, not inhibition, protects the heart. The cardioprotective effect of preconditioning is thought to involve SIRT1-dependent stress adaptation, and its loss upon sirtuin inhibition confirms this mechanism. These findings support the development of sirtuin activators for ischemic heart disease.

label: Cambinol
description: Cambinol inhibits human SIRT1 with an IC50 of 56 μM by blocking access to both NAD+ and acetyl-lysine substrate-binding regions. Directionally, Cambinol sits upstream of SIRT1 inhibition. It also inhibits SIRT2 with an IC50 of 59 μM, with minimal activity against SIRT3 or class I/II HDACs, and it sensitizes cancer cells to chemotherapy and suppresses invasion. By targeting the catalytic pocket, Cambinol prevents both substrate binding and NAD+ utilization. Its dual SIRT1/2 inhibition reactivates pro-apoptotic programs in cancer cells.

label: Cancer cell migration and invasion
description: In hepatocellular and lung cancer cells, Cambinol impairs migration and invasion in a dose-dependent manner, consistent with sirtuin inhibition reducing metastatic behaviors. Directionally, Cambinol sits upstream of suppressed motility. This suggests sirtuin blockers may limit metastasis, complementing Cambinol's chemotherapy-sensitizing effects. By inhibiting SIRT1 and SIRT2, Cambinol disrupts the survival and migration programs that cancer cells depend on. The anti-migratory effect adds a metastatic dimension to the anticancer profile of sirtuin inhibitors, supporting their evaluation as anti-metastatic agents.

label: Cancer cells to chemotherapy
description: Cambinol combination with chemotherapeutic agents dramatically sensitizes cancer cells to chemotherapy-induced apoptosis. Directionally, Cambinol sits upstream of enhanced chemosensitivity. By inhibiting SIRT1 and SIRT2, it removes survival signals that protect tumor cells from drug-induced death, and this supports sirtuin inhibition as a chemosensitization strategy. The effect is particularly relevant in p53-wild-type tumors, where sirtuin inhibition reactivates p53-dependent apoptosis. Combination regimens of sirtuin inhibitors with conventional chemotherapy are therefore of significant clinical interest.

label: Salermide
description: Salermide is a potent synthetic sirtuin inhibitor with improved potency against SIRT1 relative to the parent compound sirtinol. Directionally, Salermide blocks SIRT1 deacetylase activity. This reactivates proapoptotic genes silenced by SIRT1 in cancer, and it is a research and anticancer chemical probe. Salermide also potently inhibits SIRT2, broadening its sirtuin-blocking profile, and its improved potency made it a widely used tool for studying the consequences of SIRT1/2 inhibition in cancer biology. The compound's effects on apoptosis and senescence are attributed to its dual sirtuin inhibition.

label: Proapoptotic genes (via H4K16ac)
description: Salermide inhibits SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of H4K16, leading to epigenetic reactivation of proapoptotic genes aberrantly repressed in cancer cells. Directionally, Salermide promotes H4K16 hyperacetylation, which drives apoptosis gene expression. This removes a chromatin-based survival brake and is a mechanistic rationale for sirtuin-inhibitor cancer therapy. By restoring H4K16ac at the promoters of pro-apoptotic genes, Salermide reverses the epigenetic silencing imposed by SIRT1. This illustrates how sirtuin inhibitors can act as epigenetic modulators to restore tumor-suppressive transcription.

label: Cancer cell lines (MOLT4, MDA-MB-231, RKO)
description: Salermide induces robust apoptosis in leukemia (MOLT4), breast (MDA-MB-231), and colon (RKO) cancer cells, validating broad antitumor activity. Directionally, Salermide treatment sits upstream of cancer-cell death. This is consistent with SIRT1/2 inhibition removing survival signaling, and it supports sirtuin blockers as anticancer agents. The activity across diverse cancer cell lines indicates that SIRT1/2 inhibition engages a general pro-apoptotic program rather than a tumor-type-specific mechanism. These results provided key evidence for the anticancer potential of sirtuin inhibitors.

label: Colorectal cancer stem cells
description: Salermide inhibits colorectal carcinoma cancer-stem-cell self-renewal and reduces tumorigenesis, targeting the resilient stem-cell fraction. Directionally, Salermide sits upstream of stem-cell suppression. This is important because cancer stem cells drive relapse and resistance, and extending sirtuin-inhibitor effects to the tumor-initiation compartment has therapeutic significance. By suppressing self-renewal, Salermide reduces the population of cells capable of regenerating tumors. These findings suggest that sirtuin inhibitors may be effective against the most refractory cancer cell populations.

label: Sirtinol
description: Sirtinol inhibits SIRT1 with an IC50 of approximately 131 μM, preventing deacetylation of histones and non-histone targets. Directionally, Sirtinol sits upstream of SIRT1 inhibition. It is the parent compound of salermide and a classic sirtuin research tool, and its weaker potency spurred development of more active derivatives. Sirtinol also inhibits SIRT2 with an IC50 of about 38-68 μM, showing comparable or stronger activity against SIRT2 than SIRT1. Its use established the sirtuin-inhibitor chemical scaffold on which more selective and potent compounds were later built.

label: Senescence-like growth arrest
description: Sirtinol induces senescence-like growth arrest in human lung cancer H1299 cells, consistent with sirtuin inhibition engaging tumor-suppressive programs. Directionally, Sirtinol sits upstream of growth arrest. This phenotype mirrors aspects of SIRT1 loss and suggests that sirtuin blockers can blunt proliferation. The senescence-like arrest likely reflects reactivation of p53 and other tumor suppressors that sirtuins normally restrain. By demonstrating that sirtuin inhibition can induce growth arrest, sirtinol provided early evidence for the anticancer potential of sirtuin blockers.

label: Apoptotic and autophagic cell death (MCF-7)
description: In MCF-7 breast cancer cells, sirtinol triggers both apoptotic and autophagic programmed cell death, reflecting disrupted survival homeostasis. Directionally, Sirtinol sits upstream of dual cell-death activation. This is attributed to SIRT1/2 inhibition removing anti-apoptotic deacetylation, and it illustrates the pleiotropic anticancer potential of sirtuin blockers. The simultaneous engagement of apoptosis and autophagy suggests that sirtuin inhibition disrupts multiple survival pathways in cancer cells. This dual death response makes sirtinol an informative tool for studying how sirtuins support cancer-cell survival.

label: CD38 inhibitor 78c
description: 78c is a highly potent, selective, orally bioavailable small-molecule inhibitor of CD38 NAD+-glycohydrolase activity. Directionally, 78c sits upstream of CD38 blockade. By stopping NAD+ consumption, it spares the co-substrate for sirtuins and other NAD+-dependent enzymes, and it is a leading age-reversal NAD+-preservation strategy. 78c's potency and oral bioavailability make it suitable for chronic in vivo studies, and its administration to aged mice restores NAD+ levels and sirtuin activity. These properties positioned 78c as the key pharmacological tool for validating CD38 as a longevity target.

label: CD38 (NAD+-glycohydrolase)
description: 78c is a highly potent, selective, orally bioavailable small-molecule inhibitor of CD38 NAD+-glycohydrolase activity. Directionally, 78c sits upstream of CD38 blockade. By stopping NAD+ consumption, it spares the co-substrate for sirtuins and other NAD+-dependent enzymes, and it is a leading age-reversal NAD+-preservation strategy. 78c's potency and oral bioavailability make it suitable for chronic in vivo studies, and its administration to aged mice restores NAD+ levels and sirtuin activity. These properties positioned 78c as the key pharmacological tool for validating CD38 as a longevity target.

label: NAD+ levels
description: By selectively inhibiting CD38, 78c prevents age-related NAD+ degradation, keeping cellular pools high in aged animals. Directionally, CD38 inhibition sits upstream of preserved NAD+. Higher NAD+ then fuels sirtuin and other NAD+-dependent enzymes, reversing a hallmark of aging. Because CD38 expression rises with age, its inhibition becomes increasingly important for maintaining NAD+ homeostasis in older organisms. 78c's NAD+-preserving effect underlies its ability to restore sirtuin activity and extend lifespan, and it established the concept that pharmacologically limiting NAD+ consumption can counteract age-related decline.

label: Sirtuin activity (SIRT1, SIRT3)
description: 78c indirectly boosts SIRT1 and SIRT3 by maintaining NAD+ co-substrate availability, restoring their deacetylase function in aged tissue. Directionally, NAD+ preservation sits upstream of sirtuin reactivation. This is an indirect pan-sirtuin approach distinct from direct STACs, and it links CD38 pharmacology to longevity pathways. By preventing NAD+ consumption, 78c ensures that sirtuins have the co-substrate they require, effectively restoring the NAD+-dependent regulation that declines with age. This strategy is complementary to NAD+ precursor supplementation, and the two approaches are often combined.

Administration of 78c to naturally aged male mice yields about a 14% lifespan extension, demonstrating in vivo geroprotective efficacy. Directionally, CD38 inhibition sits upstream of prolonged lifespan. This effect is attributed to restored NAD+ and sirtuin function, and it validates CD38 as a longevity drug target. The lifespan benefit in naturally aged animals, rather than in accelerated-aging models, provides particularly strong evidence for translational relevance. 78c's efficacy, combined with its NAD+-sparing mechanism, established CD38 inhibition as a leading pharmacological strategy in geroscience.

label: NMN and NR
description: 78c enhances the efficacy of NAD+ precursors NMN and NR by preventing their rapid CD38-mediated degradation, combining supply and preservation. Directionally, 78c combined with precursors sits upstream of amplified NAD+ and sirtuin activation. This synergy is a rational anti-aging combination, overcoming the limited durability of precursors alone, and it is one of the most promising strategies for restoring NAD+ in aging. Because CD38 consumes both NAD+ and its precursors, inhibiting CD38 while supplying precursors maximizes the NAD+ pool available to sirtuins. This combination approach is now central to NAD+ restoration research.

label: Fucoidan
description: Fucoidan, notably Fucoidan-FV, activates SIRT6 by increasing its protein abundance and preferentially stimulating its mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activity rather than its deacetylase activity. This selectively recruits KAP1 and HP1alpha to silence LINE-1 retrotransposons, yielding antifibrotic and genome-stabilizing effects, and demonstrates that SIRT6's functions can be pharmacologically separated. Fucoidan extends healthspan and lifespan in aged mice, making it a natural SIRT6-targeted intervention of considerable geroscience interest.

label: LINE-1 expression (HGPS fibroblasts)
description: Fucoidan-FV (50-100 μg/mL) reduces LINE-1 ORF1p and ORF2p protein levels in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria (HGPS) patient-derived fibroblasts, indicating suppressed retrotransposition. Directionally, fucoidan/SIRT6 sits upstream of LINE-1 silencing. This addresses a progeria-associated chromatin defect and supports SIRT6's role in repetitive-element control. By restoring SIRT6-mediated silencing of LINE-1 elements, fucoidan mitigates a key feature of progeria biology, and AAV-mediated centenarian-SIRT6 delivery produces a similar reduction. These findings link fucoidan and SIRT6 to the maintenance of genome integrity in premature-aging syndromes.

label: Healthspan and lifespan (aged mice)
description: SIRT6-activating fucoidan extends healthspan and lifespan in aged wild-type mice, confirming in vivo geroprotection. Directionally, fucoidan sits upstream of improved survival and function. This mirrors the longevity association of centenarian SIRT6 variants and positions fucoidan as a natural SIRT6-targeted intervention. The benefit in naturally aged mice suggests that SIRT6 activation can counteract age-related decline even when initiated late in life. Fucoidan's dual activation of SIRT6 protein and ADP-ribosyltransferase activity is thought to mediate its healthspan effects.

label: ML385
description: ML385 binds the NRF2 bZIP domain, blocking its heterodimerization with small Maf proteins and preventing ARE-driven antioxidant transcription. Directionally, ML385 sits upstream of NRF2 inhibition. Because SIRT1 activates NRF2, ML385 can be used to disrupt that axis experimentally, and it is a tool to dissect NRF2-dependent cytoprotection. By preventing NRF2 from binding antioxidant-response elements, ML385 reduces the expression of the protective enzyme battery. Its selectivity for NRF2 over other bZIP factors makes it a valuable pharmacological probe in oxidative-stress research.

label: AGK2
description: AGK2 is a highly selective SIRT2 inhibitor with an IC50 of 3.5 μM and over 10-fold selectivity over SIRT1 and SIRT3. Directionally, AGK2 blocks SIRT2. Its selectivity makes it the preferred probe for SIRT2-specific biology, and it rescues neurons in Parkinson's models, supporting SIRT2 inhibition therapeutically. By preserving α-tubulin acetylation, AGK2 protects microtubule stability and neuronal viability. AGK2's potency and selectivity established it as the reference SIRT2 inhibitor and a key tool for studying SIRT2's roles in neurodegeneration and cancer.

label: α-synuclein-mediated toxicity
description: AGK2-mediated SIRT2 inhibition prevents deacetylation of α-tubulin and microtubule elements, suppressing aggregation and protecting dopaminergic neuron viability in Parkinson's models. Directionally, AGK2/SIRT2 inhibition sits upstream of neuronal rescue. This targets the microtubule instability underlying synuclein toxicity, and it is a leading SIRT2-inhibition neurodegenerative strategy. By maintaining the acetylated, stable state of tubulin, AGK2 helps neurons withstand α-synuclein aggregates. These results provided some of the strongest evidence that SIRT2 inhibition, rather than activation, is neuroprotective.

label: Ischemic stroke
description: AGK2 confers neuroprotection under ischemic and hypoxic conditions by suppressing phospho-JNK and FOXO3a and preventing caspase-3 cleavage. Directionally, AGK2/SIRT2 inhibition sits upstream of reduced neuronal death. This broadens AGK2's neuroprotective utility beyond proteinopathy, and it reinforces the inverse therapeutic logic for SIRT2. By blunting JNK and FOXO3a death signaling and preventing effector-caspase activation, AGK2 protects neurons in ischemic stroke models. These findings support SIRT2 inhibition as a candidate strategy across diverse forms of acute and chronic neurodegeneration.

label: SIRT6 centenarian variants (N308K/A313S)
description: Centenarian-associated SIRT6 variants (N308K/A313S) elevate endogenous SIRT6 protein through a weakened interaction with vimentin, independent of mRNA changes. Directionally, the variant reduces vimentin binding, which raises SIRT6. This suggests protein stability, not expression, drives the longevity phenotype, and it links a human genetic finding to SIRT6 abundance. By escaping vimentin-mediated degradation, variant SIRT6 accumulates to higher levels in cells. This mechanism explains how a subtle coding change can increase SIRT6 output and is consistent with the variants' association with exceptional longevity.

label: SIRT6 protein levels
description: Centenarian-associated SIRT6 variants (N308K/A313S) elevate endogenous SIRT6 protein through a weakened interaction with vimentin, independent of mRNA changes. Directionally, the variant reduces vimentin binding, which raises SIRT6. This suggests protein stability, not expression, drives the longevity phenotype, and it links a human genetic finding to SIRT6 abundance. By escaping vimentin-mediated degradation, variant SIRT6 accumulates to higher levels in cells. This mechanism explains how a subtle coding change can increase SIRT6 output and is consistent with the variants' association with exceptional longevity.

label: SIRT6 N308K mutation
description: The N308K substitution selectively reduces SIRT6-vimentin interaction, which normally promotes SIRT6 degradation, thereby increasing SIRT6 protein levels. Directionally, N308K sits upstream of weakened vimentin binding. This stabilizes SIRT6 and enhances its functional output, and it is the molecular explanation for the centenarian variant phenotype. Because vimentin normally targets SIRT6 for proteasomal degradation, the N308K variant escapes this turnover. This post-translational stabilization, rather than transcriptional upregulation, underlies the increased SIRT6 abundance seen in carriers of the longevity-associated variant.

label: Vimentin
description: The N308K substitution selectively reduces SIRT6-vimentin interaction, which normally promotes SIRT6 degradation, thereby increasing SIRT6 protein levels. Directionally, N308K sits upstream of weakened vimentin binding. This stabilizes SIRT6 and enhances its functional output, and it is the molecular explanation for the centenarian variant phenotype. Because vimentin normally targets SIRT6 for proteasomal degradation, the N308K variant escapes this turnover. This post-translational stabilization, rather than transcriptional upregulation, underlies the increased SIRT6 abundance seen in carriers of the longevity-associated variant.

label: SIRT6 deacetylase activity
description: Despite higher SIRT6 protein, centenarian hMSCs show increased histone acetylation at H3K9, H3K18, and H3K27, confirming reduced deacetylase activity. Directionally, the variant sits upstream of weaker deacetylation. This indicates that the longevity benefit may hinge more on the ADP-ribosyltransferase than on the deacetylase function of SIRT6, and it reframes how active SIRT6 should be interpreted. The dissociation between increased protein abundance and reduced deacetylation highlights that SIRT6's two enzymatic activities are independently regulated. These findings are central to understanding the molecular basis of SIRT6's longevity association.

label: Replicative senescence (hMSCs)
description: At late passages, centenarian-variant hMSCs show more Ki67-positive proliferating cells and fewer SA-β-gal-positive senescent cells, demonstrating delayed replicative senescence. Directionally, CentSIRT6 sits upstream of senescence delay. This is a cellular correlate of exceptional human longevity, and it supports SIRT6 as a senescence-modulating factor. By delaying the entry into replicative senescence, the variant maintains the proliferative capacity and regenerative potential of stem cells. These observations connect the centenarian SIRT6 genotype to measurable cellular phenotypes associated with longevity.

label: Progerin-induced stress
description: Centenarian SIRT6 variants ameliorate multiple aging phenotypes in progerin-expressing hMSCs, including higher Ki67, reduced SA-β-gal, decreased p16/p21, reduced IL-6, and increased Lamin B1. Directionally, CentSIRT6 sits upstream of progerin-stress resistance. This shows the variant buffers premature-aging pathology and ties SIRT6 to laminopathy resilience. By maintaining proliferation, reducing senescence markers, and lowering inflammatory output in progerin-stressed cells, the variants counteract key features of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria. These findings support SIRT6-boosting strategies for laminopathy and related premature-aging conditions.

label: LINE-1 derepression (under progerin stress)
description: Under progerin-induced stress, centenarian-variant hMSCs better maintain LINE-1 repression, with reduced ORF1p and ORF2p proteins. Directionally, CentSIRT6 sits upstream of continued LINE-1 silencing. This protects genome integrity against retrotransposition, and it connects the ADP-ribosyltransferase gain to repetitive-element control. By preserving heterochromatic silencing of LINE-1 elements during progerin stress, the variant maintains a key genome-defense mechanism. These results link the enhanced ADP-ribosylation activity of centenarian SIRT6 to the suppression of retroelement expression that destabilizes aging genomes.

label: AAV-CentSIRT6
description: AAV-mediated delivery of centenarian SIRT6 reduces LINE-1 ORF1p and ORF2p protein levels in HGPS patient-derived fibroblasts, validating the variant's silencing function in progeria. Directionally, CentSIRT6 expression sits upstream of LINE-1 reduction. This is a proof-of-concept gene-therapy approach to laminopathy, and it extends the SIRT6/LINE-1 axis to a treatable model. By restoring SIRT6 function in progeria cells through gene delivery, the approach reproduces the LINE-1-suppressing effect of the centenarian variant. These results support the feasibility of SIRT6-based gene therapy for progeroid syndromes.

label: LINE-1 in HGPS fibroblasts
description: AAV-mediated delivery of centenarian SIRT6 reduces LINE-1 ORF1p and ORF2p protein levels in HGPS patient-derived fibroblasts, validating the variant's silencing function in progeria. Directionally, CentSIRT6 expression sits upstream of LINE-1 reduction. This is a proof-of-concept gene-therapy approach to laminopathy, and it extends the SIRT6/LINE-1 axis to a treatable model. By restoring SIRT6 function in progeria cells through gene delivery, the approach reproduces the LINE-1-suppressing effect of the centenarian variant. These results support the feasibility of SIRT6-based gene therapy for progeroid syndromes.

label: KAP1
description: SIRT6 mono-ADP-ribosylates KAP1 (a transcriptional corepressor), a modification that licenses recruitment of heterochromatin protein HP1α to repetitive DNA. Directionally, SIRT6 enzymatically ADP-ribosylates KAP1. This is distinct from its deacetylase action and is selectively enhanced by fucoidan and centenarian variants, and it is a key chromatin-silencing mechanism. By ADP-ribosylating KAP1, SIRT6 initiates the deposition of HP1α that packages LINE-1 retrotransposons into heterochromatin. This pathway is central to SIRT6's suppression of repetitive elements and genome stability.

label: SIRT6/KAP1
description: SIRT6-mediated mono-ADP-ribosylation of KAP1 recruits HP1α to package LINE-1 retrotransposons into heterochromatin, silencing their expression. Directionally, SIRT6/KAP1 sits upstream of HP1α tethering. This protects genome stability by containing mobile elements, and it explains how SIRT6 loss derepresses LINE-1. By maintaining heterochromatic silencing of retrotransposons, SIRT6 prevents the insertional mutations and genomic instability caused by active LINE-1 elements. The KAP1-HP1α axis is thus a critical effector of SIRT6's genome-protective function, and its disruption contributes to the instability seen in SIRT6-deficient cells.

label: HP1alpha (to LINE-1 heterochromatin)
description: SIRT6-mediated mono-ADP-ribosylation of KAP1 recruits HP1α to package LINE-1 retrotransposons into heterochromatin, silencing their expression. Directionally, SIRT6/KAP1 sits upstream of HP1α tethering. This protects genome stability by containing mobile elements, and it explains how SIRT6 loss derepresses LINE-1. By maintaining heterochromatic silencing of retrotransposons, SIRT6 prevents the insertional mutations and genomic instability caused by active LINE-1 elements. The KAP1-HP1α axis is thus a critical effector of SIRT6's genome-protective function, and its disruption contributes to the instability seen in SIRT6-deficient cells.

label: TFEB (at K116)
description: SIRT1 deacetylates TFEB at Lys116, enhancing its nuclear translocation and transcriptional activity to drive the CLEAR autophagic/lysosomal gene program. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically activates TFEB. This promotes lysosomal biogenesis and autophagic flux, and it links SIRT1 to the terminal degradative arm of autophagy alongside ULK1 and Beclin-1. By promoting TFEB nuclear translocation, SIRT1 coordinates the expression of lysosomal enzymes and autophagy machinery. This regulation ensures that sirtuin-dependent quality control extends to the final steps of cargo degradation, and its decline with age impairs cellular clearance.

label: BMAL1
description: SIRT1 deacetylates BMAL1, a core circadian transcription factor, gating circadian NAD+ oscillations and coupling metabolic state to clock-gene expression. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically tunes BMAL1. This places sirtuins at the interface of circadian rhythm and metabolism, and it explains how NAD+ rhythms drive daily transcriptional programs. Because BMAL1/CLOCK regulate NAMPT, the circadian system controls NAD+ production, which in turn activates SIRT1, which deacetylates BMAL1 to feed back on the clock. This SIRT1-BMAL1-NAMPT loop couples daily rhythms to cellular energy metabolism.

label: Atg5
description: SIRT1 deacetylates Atg5, enhancing autophagosome formation as part of its autophagy-promoting function. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically activates Atg5. Atg5 is essential for LC3 lipidation and autophagosome elongation, so this modification supports the core autophagic machinery. SIRT1's deacetylation of Atg5 adds to its coordinated regulation of ULK1, Beclin-1, Atg7, and LC3, placing SIRT1 at multiple steps of the autophagy pathway. This broad control links sirtuin activity to the clearance of damaged organelles and proteins, contributing to SIRT1's cytoprotective and longevity-associated functions.

label: Atg7
description: SIRT1 deacetylates Atg7, promoting autophagy initiation and autophagosome formation. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically activates Atg7, the E1-like enzyme that conjugates LC3 to phosphatidylethanolamine. This reinforces SIRT1's broad control of the autophagic machinery, and it complements SIRT1 actions on ULK1, Beclin-1, Atg5, and LC3. By enhancing the lipidation of LC3, SIRT1-dependent Atg7 activation supports autophagosome membrane elongation. This coordinated regulation across multiple autophagy components is a hallmark of SIRT1's role in cellular quality control.

label: LXR (Liver X Receptor)
description: SIRT1 deacetylates the liver X receptor (LXR), a nuclear receptor that regulates cholesterol metabolism and efflux. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically modulates LXR. This influences reverse cholesterol transport and lipid homeostasis, expanding SIRT1's role in cardiovascular and metabolic regulation. By deacetylating LXR, SIRT1 can alter the expression of cholesterol-efflux genes, connecting sirtuin activity to lipid handling. This regulation is relevant to atherosclerosis and metabolic disease, where cholesterol homeostasis is central, and it complements SIRT1's actions on PPARs and other nuclear receptors.

label: PML-mediated premature senescence
description: In mouse embryonic fibroblasts, SIRT1 rescues cells from PML-mediated premature senescence by deacetylating and inhibiting p53, relieving the senescence program. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of senescence rescue. This requires the PML-p53-SIRT1 nuclear-body axis, and it shows SIRT1 can oppose proliferative arrest when appropriately engaged. By deacetylating p53 within PML nuclear bodies, SIRT1 dampens the p53-dependent senescence checkpoint. This dual role—promoting survival in normal cells but potentially enabling cancer-cell proliferation—illustrates the context-dependence of SIRT1's functions.

label: ROCK1 (neurons)
description: SIRT1 downregulates ROCK1 expression in neurons, which induces α-secretase (ADAM10) activity relevant to amyloid precursor processing and Alzheimer's prevention under caloric restriction. Directionally, SIRT1 suppresses ROCK1, which induces α-secretase. This shifts APP cleavage away from the amyloidogenic β-secretase pathway, reducing β-amyloid production. By promoting the non-amyloidogenic processing of APP through ADAM10, SIRT1 protects against amyloid pathology in Alzheimer's models. This mechanism is induced by caloric restriction and links sirtuin activity to the prevention of Alzheimer's disease.

label: DNA double-strand breaks (RCM)
description: During DNA repair, SIRT1 relocalizes to double-strand breaks where it deacetylates repair factors, a central mechanism of the Information Theory of Aging (RCM) framework. Directionally, DNA damage sits upstream of SIRT1 relocalization. This consumes NAD+ and redistributes chromatin modifiers, proposed to drive epigenetic drift, and it is a key node in Sinclair's model of aging. By moving to sites of damage, SIRT1 is thought to abandon its normal genomic loci, causing loss of epigenetic information. This redistribution model is the basis for the ICE-Mouse experiments linking DNA repair to epigenetic aging.

label: FOXO3a (to induce SOD2, Catalase)
description: SIRT1 deacetylates FOXO3a, which then transcriptionally induces SOD2, catalase, and glutathione-biosynthesis genes, protecting cells against oxidative stress. Directionally, SIRT1 activates FOXO3a, which drives antioxidant enzyme induction. This is a canonical longevity-associated stress-resistance program, and it underlies much of SIRT1's cytoprotective reputation. By biasing FOXO3a target selection toward antioxidant and repair genes, SIRT1 reduces oxidative damage and supports cellular resilience. This axis is central to the beneficial effects of caloric restriction and NAD+ repletion on redox homeostasis.

label: CDC14B
description: The phosphatase CDC14B dephosphorylates SIRT2, triggering its ubiquitination and 26S proteasomal degradation, which promotes exit from mitosis. Directionally, CDC14B sits upstream of SIRT2 destabilization. This couples SIRT2 turnover to cell-cycle progression, and it ensures SIRT2 levels fall as cells complete division. By dephosphorylating SIRT2 at mitotic exit, CDC14B inactivates and degrades the enzyme that was active during G2/M. This regulatory circuit links SIRT2 abundance to the cell cycle and explains the oscillation of SIRT2 levels during division.

label: OPA1 (at Lys926, Lys931)
description: SIRT3 deacetylates OPA1 at Lys926 and Lys931 within its GTPase domain, raising OPA1 GTPase activity and enhancing mitochondrial fusion during stress. Directionally, SIRT3 enzymatically activates OPA1. This preserves mitochondrial network integrity under damage, and it links SIRT3 to mitochondrial dynamics and quality control. By promoting fusion, SIRT3 helps mitochondria share membrane potential, dilute damage, and maintain respiratory function. This regulation is particularly important in the heart and during oxidative stress, where maintaining a connected mitochondrial network protects against fragmentation and bioenergetic collapse.

label: Mitochondrial fusion (via OPA1)
description: Through OPA1 deacetylation, SIRT3 enhances mitochondrial fusion during stress, maintaining a connected, healthy mitochondrial network. Directionally, SIRT3 activates OPA1, which promotes fusion. Fused mitochondria better share membrane potential and dilute damage, and this protects against fragmentation and bioenergetic collapse. By supporting the fusion arm of mitochondrial dynamics, SIRT3 preserves respiratory efficiency and quality control under conditions that would otherwise fragment the network. This is a key mechanism by which SIRT3 maintains mitochondrial health and supports cardiac and neuronal function.

label: Obese mouse BAT
description: Brown adipose tissue of obese mice shows reduced SIRT3 protein and decreased mitochondrial protein expression, linking obesity to impaired thermogenic capacity. Directionally, obesity sits upstream of lower SIRT3. This blunts cold-induced and basal mitochondrial function, and it connects metabolic disease to sirtuin attenuation. By reducing SIRT3, obesity impairs the mitochondrial biogenesis and oxidative capacity required for thermogenesis. This observation supports the concept that restoring SIRT3, through fasting or pharmacological activation, could improve the metabolic and thermogenic dysfunction associated with obesity.

label: Phylogenetic Class II (evolutionarily ancient)
description: SIRT4 is classified in phylogenetic Class II, which includes sirtuins from bacteria, insects, nematodes, mould, and protozoa—among the most ancient sirtuin lineages. Directionally, this is an evolutionary placement rather than a causal pathway. This antiquity implies conserved mitochondrial metabolic roles, and it situates SIRT4 early in sirtuin evolution. Because Class II sirtuins predate the divergence of major eukaryotic lineages, SIRT4's mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase function likely represents an ancestral enzymatic activity. Understanding SIRT4's phylogenetic position helps contextualize its metabolic-brake functions relative to the more derived deacetylases.

label: HMGCS2 (ketogenesis)
description: SIRT5 desuccinylates and activates HMGCS2 (3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA synthase 2), the rate-limiting enzyme of ketone-body synthesis, supporting energy production during fasting. Directionally, SIRT5 enzymatically activates HMGCS2. This promotes ketogenesis when carbohydrate is scarce, and it is a fasting-adaptive function of SIRT5. By enabling ketone-body production from acetyl-CoA, SIRT5 supports the brain and other tissues during prolonged fasting. This regulation complements SIRT5's activation of urea-cycle and fatty-acid-oxidation enzymes, positioning SIRT5 as a coordinator of catabolic metabolism.

label: LCAD and ACADS (fatty acid β-oxidation)
description: SIRT5 desuccinylates multiple fatty-acid β-oxidation enzymes including LCAD and ACADS, coordinating mitochondrial lipid catabolism. Directionally, SIRT5 enzymatically activates these acyl-CoA dehydrogenases. This supports energy harvest from fat, and it exemplifies SIRT5's broad desuccinylase control of metabolism. By activating the enzymes of β-oxidation, SIRT5 promotes the use of fatty acids as fuel, particularly during fasting. This catabolic role aligns SIRT5 with SIRT3 in supporting lipid oxidation, in contrast to SIRT4's inhibition of the same pathways.

label: IDH2 and SDHA (TCA cycle)
description: SIRT5 desuccinylates TCA-cycle enzymes IDH2 and SDHA, tuning their activity and coordinating mitochondrial energy metabolism. Directionally, SIRT5 enzymatically modulates TCA flux. This helps match oxidation to demand during fasting or stress, and it reinforces SIRT5's role as a central mitochondrial metabolic regulator. By adjusting the activity of key TCA-cycle enzymes, SIRT5 balances carbon entry, ATP production, and the supply of reducing equivalents. This regulation supports the metabolic flexibility that allows cells to adapt fuel utilization to nutrient availability.

label: SOD1 (via desuccinylation)
description: SIRT5 activates superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1) through desuccinylation, enhancing NADPH production and glutathione recycling for ROS detoxification. Directionally, SIRT5 enzymatically activates SOD1. This bolsters cytosolic antioxidant capacity, and it extends SIRT5's protective actions beyond the mitochondria's own enzymes. By promoting NADPH generation and glutathione recycling, SOD1 activation supports the detoxification of superoxide and the maintenance of redox balance. This antioxidant function complements SIRT5's metabolic roles and contributes to cellular protection against oxidative stress.

label: IDH2 (via desuccinylation)
description: SIRT5 activates IDH2 through desuccinylation, enhancing its NADPH-producing activity and thereby supporting glutathione reduction and ROS scavenging. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of IDH2-dependent redox buffering. This complements SOD1 activation in antioxidant defense, and it shows SIRT5's desuccinylation broadly strengthens reductive capacity. By boosting NADPH production, SIRT5 ensures sufficient reducing equivalents for glutathione and thioredoxin systems. This regulation links SIRT5 to both energy metabolism and redox homeostasis, particularly during fasting when oxidative stress rises.

label: Phylogenetic Class III (prokaryotic origin)
description: SIRT5 is the sole mammalian member of phylogenetic Class III, a group distributed widely across prokaryotes, marking it as one of the most ancient mammalian sirtuins. Directionally, this is an evolutionary classification. Its prokaryotic origin aligns with SIRT5's fundamental mitochondrial metabolic functions, and this situates SIRT5 at the root of sirtuin biology. Because Class III sirtuins predate the eukaryotic sirtuins, SIRT5's desuccinylase activity may represent an ancestral enzymatic function retained through evolution. SIRT5's phylogenetic position helps explain its resistance to nicotinamide inhibition and its distinct substrate preferences.

label: MTPα (mitochondrial trifunctional protein α)
description: SIRT4 suppresses fatty-acid oxidation in liver by inhibiting the mitochondrial trifunctional protein α subunit (MTPα), promoting lipid accumulation under nutrient-replete conditions. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of reduced β-oxidation. This contrasts with SIRT3 and SIRT5, which support fat oxidation, and it positions SIRT4 as a mitochondrial anabolic brake. By inhibiting MTPα, SIRT4 conserves fatty acids for storage when nutrients are abundant. This opposition to oxidative metabolism is central to the antagonistic SIRT3/SIRT4 balance that determines mitochondrial metabolic state.

label: ICE Mouse
description: The ICE (Induced Changes in Epigenetics) Mouse uses inducible I-PpoI expression to introduce targeted double-strand breaks that are repaired without introducing mutations. Directionally, I-PpoI sits upstream of controlled double-strand-break formation. This lets researchers trigger DNA damage alone, isolating epigenetic from mutational effects, and it is the experimental engine of the RCM model. By using sequence-specific breaks that are repaired faithfully, the ICE Mouse creates pure DNA-repair events. This design is central to testing whether DNA damage drives aging through epigenetic information loss.

label: I-PpoI endonuclease
description: The ICE (Induced Changes in Epigenetics) Mouse uses inducible I-PpoI expression to introduce targeted double-strand breaks that are repaired without introducing mutations. Directionally, I-PpoI sits upstream of controlled double-strand-break formation. This lets researchers trigger DNA damage alone, isolating epigenetic from mutational effects, and it is the experimental engine of the RCM model. By using sequence-specific breaks that are repaired faithfully, the ICE Mouse creates pure DNA-repair events. This design is central to testing whether DNA damage drives aging through epigenetic information loss.

label: RCM-driven epigenetic aging
description: Induction of double-strand breaks in the ICE Mouse, followed by repair, produces accelerated epigenetic aging and physiological decline without mutagenesis, supporting the RCM hypothesis. Directionally, double-strand-break repair sits upstream of epigenetic aging. This argues that aging can arise from information loss rather than just genetic damage, and it is a cornerstone experiment for the Information Theory of Aging. Because the phenotype occurs without mutations, it is attributed to loss of epigenetic information during repair. These results reframe aging as a software problem and motivate NAD+/sirtuin-based interventions.

label: Information Theory of Aging
description: Because the ICE Mouse phenotype occurs without mutations, it is attributed to loss of epigenetic information rather than hardware damage, supporting the Information Theory of Aging. Directionally, mutation-free double-strand-break repair sits upstream of information loss. This reframes aging as a software, not hardware, failure, and it is a foundational claim of Sinclair's theory. By showing that repair of faithful breaks still accelerates aging, the ICE Mouse separates epigenetic information loss from genetic mutation. This has profound implications for aging research, suggesting that age-related decline may be reversible by restoring epigenetic information.

label: I-PpoI
description: I-PpoI recognizes and cleaves a specific 15-20 base-pair sequence within rRNA gene repeats, generating sequence-specific double-strand breaks. Directionally, I-PpoI sits upstream of targeted double-strand-break formation. Its specificity makes it ideal for the ICE Mouse's controlled damage, and this enables reproducible epigenetic-aging studies. Because I-PpoI cleaves at a defined sequence, researchers can induce breaks at known genomic loci in a controlled manner. This precision distinguishes the ICE Mouse from treatments that cause random DNA damage, allowing the isolation of repair-driven effects.

label: Sequence-specific double-strand breaks
description: I-PpoI recognizes and cleaves a specific 15-20 base-pair sequence within rRNA gene repeats, generating sequence-specific double-strand breaks. Directionally, I-PpoI sits upstream of targeted double-strand-break formation. Its specificity makes it ideal for the ICE Mouse's controlled damage, and this enables reproducible epigenetic-aging studies. Because I-PpoI cleaves at a defined sequence, researchers can induce breaks at known genomic loci in a controlled manner. This precision distinguishes the ICE Mouse from treatments that cause random DNA damage, allowing the isolation of repair-driven effects.

label: David Sinclair
description: David Sinclair identified SIRT1 as a mediator of caloric-restriction benefits and, in a landmark 2003 study, discovered resveratrol as a sirtuin-activating compound (STAC). Directionally, the discovery establishes SIRT1/STAC centrality to longevity research. This launched the modern sirtuin field, and it connects basic yeast findings to mammalian therapeutics. By showing that resveratrol extends yeast lifespan through Sir2, Sinclair bridged the caloric-restriction and sirtuin fields. This work catalyzed decades of sirtuin-drug development and made SIRT1 a central target in geroscience.

label: SIRT1 as CR mediator
description: David Sinclair identified SIRT1 as a mediator of caloric-restriction benefits and, in a landmark 2003 study, discovered resveratrol as a sirtuin-activating compound (STAC). Directionally, the discovery establishes SIRT1/STAC centrality to longevity research. This launched the modern sirtuin field, and it connects basic yeast findings to mammalian therapeutics. By showing that resveratrol extends yeast lifespan through Sir2, Sinclair bridged the caloric-restriction and sirtuin fields. This work catalyzed decades of sirtuin-drug development and made SIRT1 a central target in geroscience.

label: Resveratrol as STAC
description: In 2003, Sinclair showed resveratrol extends yeast lifespan via Sir2 and later demonstrated parallel effects in higher organisms, discovering it as the first STAC. Directionally, the discovery sits upstream of the STAC concept. This catalyzed decades of sirtuin-drug development, and it remains a seminal finding in geroscience. By identifying a natural compound that activates sirtuins, Sinclair provided the prototype for pharmacologically engaging longevity pathways. The STAC concept has since driven the search for more potent and specific sirtuin activators for therapeutic use.

label: Sirtris Pharmaceuticals
description: Sinclair co-founded Sirtris Pharmaceuticals (later acquired by GlaxoSmithKline) to develop STACs such as SRT1720 and SRT2104 as therapeutics. Directionally, the academic discovery was translated into a company. This drove clinical translation of sirtuin activators, and it illustrates the bench-to-bedside path of sirtuin research. By commercializing STACs, Sirtris aimed to develop drugs that reproduce the metabolic benefits of caloric restriction. Although clinical outcomes were mixed, the company's formation validated sirtuins as a druggable target class and stimulated industrial interest in longevity biology.

label: ICE Mouse model
description: The Sinclair lab developed the ICE Mouse to test the RCM hypothesis using mutation-free double-strand breaks. Directionally, the model enables tests of epigenetic aging. This provided key evidence for the Information Theory of Aging, and it is a methodological contribution alongside the theoretical framework. By engineering a system to induce faithful DNA breaks, Sinclair created a tool to separate epigenetic from genetic contributions to aging. The ICE Mouse's results have made it a centerpiece of the argument that aging results from loss of epigenetic information.

label: SIRT1 (via Hes1 deacetylation)
description: SIRT1 directly regulates BDNF transcription by deacetylating and repressing Hes1, a transcriptional repressor of BDNF, thereby relieving inhibition and promoting neuronal survival. Directionally, SIRT1 deacetylates Hes1, which induces BDNF. This links sirtuin activity to neurotrophic support, and it is a mechanism for SIRT1's neuroprotective and cognitive benefits. By removing the Hes1 brake on the BDNF promoter, SIRT1 increases BDNF expression in the brain. This regulation is engaged by caloric restriction and exercise, both of which elevate BDNF through SIRT1-dependent pathways.

label: SIRT1/PGC-1α
description: SIRT1 activates PGC-1α, which co-activates the BDNF promoter, linking mitochondrial biogenesis to neurotrophic support. Directionally, SIRT1/PGC-1α sits upstream of BDNF transcription. This couples energy metabolism to neuronal growth-factor expression, and it reinforces the metabolic-neurotrophic axis of SIRT1. By coordinating the activation of PGC-1α and the expression of BDNF, SIRT1 links mitochondrial function to neuronal survival and plasticity. This connection helps explain how sirtuin activation and caloric restriction benefit brain health.

label: BDNF promoter
description: SIRT1 activates PGC-1α, which co-activates the BDNF promoter, linking mitochondrial biogenesis to neurotrophic support. Directionally, SIRT1/PGC-1α sits upstream of BDNF transcription. This couples energy metabolism to neuronal growth-factor expression, and it reinforces the metabolic-neurotrophic axis of SIRT1. By coordinating the activation of PGC-1α and the expression of BDNF, SIRT1 links mitochondrial function to neuronal survival and plasticity. This connection helps explain how sirtuin activation and caloric restriction benefit brain health.

label: BDNF and NAD+ levels
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Exercise raises both BDNF and NAD+ levels, and SIRT1 may mediate exercise-induced BDNF upregulation in the hippocampus. Directionally, exercise sits upstream of BDNF and NAD+ elevation. Higher NAD+ fuels SIRT1, which then supports BDNF, and this provides a mechanistic bridge between physical activity, sirtuins, and brain health. By raising NAD+, exercise engages the sirtuin pathway that promotes BDNF expression and mitochondrial function. This axis is central to the well-established cognitive benefits of exercise and to the geroscience concept of exercise as medicine.

label: BDNF (via SIRT1/FoxO)
description: Caloric restriction and intermittent fasting elevate BDNF through SIRT1/FoxO-dependent pathways, contributing to cognitive resilience against aging. Directionally, caloric restriction sits upstream of BDNF elevation via SIRT1/FoxO. This neuroprotective adaptation complements CR's systemic benefits, and it motivates CR and fasting for brain health. By raising BDNF through sirtuin-dependent mechanisms, caloric restriction supports synaptic plasticity, neurogenesis, and neuronal survival. These effects contribute to the protection of cognitive function during aging.

label: PCAF
description: SIRT1 physically interacts with and deacetylates PCAF (p300/CBP-associated factor), a histone acetyltransferase, within regulatory complexes at muscle-gene promoters. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically inhibits PCAF. This counterbalances acetylation during myogenic regulation, and it shows SIRT1 tuning acetyltransferase partners, not only substrates. By deacetylating PCAF, SIRT1 reduces its HAT activity and its contribution to muscle-gene activation. This regulation is part of SIRT1's broader control of the acetylation-deacetylation balance that shapes transcriptional programs.

label: PCAF/GCN5
description: The positive histone acetyltransferases PCAF and GCN5 acetylate the myogenic transcription factor MyoD, enhancing its DNA-binding and recruitment of transcriptional machinery. Directionally, PCAF/GCN5 sits upstream of MyoD activation. This promotes muscle differentiation, and SIRT1 opposes this by deacetylating both PCAF and MyoD. By acetylating MyoD, these HATs support the expression of muscle-specific genes during differentiation. The balance between PCAF/GCN5 acetylation and sirtuin deacetylation determines the timing and extent of myogenic commitment.

label: MyoD
description: The positive histone acetyltransferases PCAF and GCN5 acetylate the myogenic transcription factor MyoD, enhancing its DNA-binding and recruitment of transcriptional machinery. Directionally, PCAF/GCN5 sits upstream of MyoD activation. This promotes muscle differentiation, and SIRT1 opposes this by deacetylating both PCAF and MyoD. By acetylating MyoD, these HATs support the expression of muscle-specific genes during differentiation. The balance between PCAF/GCN5 acetylation and sirtuin deacetylation determines the timing and extent of myogenic commitment.

label: MEF2D (at Lys424)
description: HDAC4 possesses SUMO E3 ligase activity and sumoylates MEF2D at Lys424, locking it into an inactive, transcription-repressing state. Directionally, HDAC4 sits upstream of MEF2D inactivation. This regulates muscle-gene expression independently of sirtuins, and it is included as a parallel chromatin regulatory mechanism contextualizing SIRT1's muscle actions. By sumoylating MEF2D, HDAC4 represses its transcriptional activity and the muscle genes it controls. This regulation is distinct from the acetylation-deacetylation balance that sirtuins influence, illustrating the diversity of muscle-gene control.

label: PML-IV
community_name: p53 and SIRT1 to nuclear bodies
description: Upon oncogenic stress, the PML-IV isoform recruits both p53 and SIRT1 into PML nuclear bodies, assembling a stress-responsive regulatory hub. Directionally, PML-IV sits upstream of p53/SIRT1 compartmentalization. Within these bodies, SIRT1 deacetylates p53 to shape the senescence/apoptosis decision, and it connects PML bodies to sirtuin-mediated tumor suppression. By concentrating p53 and SIRT1 at nuclear bodies, PML-IV ensures that stress responses are locally integrated. This compartmentalization is central to the tumor-suppressive functions of the PML pathway.

label: p53 and SIRT1 to nuclear bodies
community_name: p53 and SIRT1 to nuclear bodies
description: Upon oncogenic stress, the PML-IV isoform recruits both p53 and SIRT1 into PML nuclear bodies, assembling a stress-responsive regulatory hub. Directionally, PML-IV sits upstream of p53/SIRT1 compartmentalization. Within these bodies, SIRT1 deacetylates p53 to shape the senescence/apoptosis decision, and it connects PML bodies to sirtuin-mediated tumor suppression. By concentrating p53 and SIRT1 at nuclear bodies, PML-IV ensures that stress responses are locally integrated. This compartmentalization is central to the tumor-suppressive functions of the PML pathway.

label: PML
description: PML-IV overexpression is sufficient to induce p53-dependent premature senescence, and loss of PML accelerates tumorigenesis, establishing PML as a tumor suppressor. Directionally, PML sits upstream of senescence. This process engages SIRT1 and p53 at PML nuclear bodies, and it contextualizes SIRT1's role in proliferation arrest. By activating p53-dependent senescence, PML restricts uncontrolled proliferation and prevents tumor formation. The PML-SIRT1-p53 axis illustrates how a nuclear body can coordinate the decision between senescence, apoptosis, and proliferation.

label: Premature cellular senescence
description: PML-IV overexpression is sufficient to induce p53-dependent premature senescence, and loss of PML accelerates tumorigenesis, establishing PML as a tumor suppressor. Directionally, PML sits upstream of senescence. This process engages SIRT1 and p53 at PML nuclear bodies, and it contextualizes SIRT1's role in proliferation arrest. By activating p53-dependent senescence, PML restricts uncontrolled proliferation and prevents tumor formation. The PML-SIRT1-p53 axis illustrates how a nuclear body can coordinate the decision between senescence, apoptosis, and proliferation.

label: Mediterranean Diet
description: The PREDIMED trial showed that a Mediterranean diet supplemented with olive oil or nuts significantly reduced major cardiovascular events. Directionally, the dietary pattern sits upstream of lower CVD incidence. Polyphenols including resveratrol may engage SIRT1, but the effect is multifactorial, and it is a clinically validated dietary intervention. The trial provides the strongest evidence that a Mediterranean dietary pattern reduces cardiovascular risk. Its success supports the concept that whole-diet approaches, engaging multiple pathways including sirtuins, are effective for cardiovascular prevention.

label: SIRT1 (via resveratrol)
description: The Mediterranean Diet's resveratrol content is proposed to activate SIRT1, linking the dietary pattern to longevity pathways. Directionally, diet-derived resveratrol sits upstream of SIRT1 activation. This is one of several polyphenol-mediated mechanisms of the diet, though human causality is inferential rather than proven. The Mediterranean Diet also provides other polyphenols and healthy fats that may act through SIRT1 and AMPK. This dietary association has motivated research into how whole-food polyphenol patterns, rather than isolated compounds, influence sirtuin biology.

label: Cardiovascular Disease risk
description: The PREDIMED trial showed that a Mediterranean diet supplemented with olive oil or nuts significantly reduced major cardiovascular events. Directionally, the dietary pattern sits upstream of lower CVD incidence. Polyphenols including resveratrol may engage SIRT1, but the effect is multifactorial, and it is a clinically validated dietary intervention. The trial provides the strongest evidence that a Mediterranean dietary pattern reduces cardiovascular risk. Its success supports the concept that whole-diet approaches, engaging multiple pathways including sirtuins, are effective for cardiovascular prevention.

label: Lipid profile (raises HDL, reduces LDL oxidation)
description: The Mediterranean Diet raises HDL while reducing LDL oxidation through its polyphenol-rich components, improving the overall lipid profile. Directionally, the diet sits upstream of favorable lipid changes. This contributes to its cardiovascular protection, and resveratrol and other polyphenols are putative SIRT1-engaging contributors. By combining healthy fats with antioxidant polyphenols, the diet improves both the quantity and quality of circulating lipoproteins. These lipid effects are part of the broader cardiovascular benefit demonstrated in clinical trials of the Mediterranean diet.

label: SIRT3/SIRT4 ratio
description: The SIRT3/SIRT4 ratio defines the hormetic window—the dose range over which mitochondrial stress triggers adaptive responses rather than damage. Directionally, the ratio sits upstream of the adaptive-versus-harmful threshold. Because SIRT3 is protective and SIRT4 is detrimental, a high ratio broadens resilience, and caloric restriction and youth raise this ratio while aging lowers it. By setting the balance between mitochondrial protection and oxidant stress, the SIRT3/SIRT4 ratio determines how cells respond to stress. Maintaining a high ratio is a proposed strategy for preserving mitochondrial health during aging.

label: SIRT3 (and downregulates SIRT4)
description: Caloric restriction upregulates SIRT3 and downregulates SIRT4, shifting the SIRT3/SIRT4 ratio toward a protective, oxidative-phosphorylation-promoting state. Directionally, caloric restriction sits upstream of the ratio shift. This counters the age-related pattern of declining SIRT3 and rising SIRT4, and it is a core mechanism of CR's metabolic benefits. By biasing the balance toward SIRT3, caloric restriction promotes mitochondrial oxidation, antioxidant defense, and metabolic flexibility. This ratio shift is a key molecular readout of the beneficial effects of dietary restriction.

label: Declining SIRT3 and rising SIRT4
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Aging is associated with declining SIRT3 activity and rising SIRT4, which narrows the hormetic window and increases vulnerability to mitochondrial stressors. Directionally, aging sits upstream of the altered ratio. This shift favors oxidant stress and metabolic inflexibility, and restoring the ratio, for example via caloric restriction or NAD+ precursors, is a proposed anti-aging strategy. By reducing the protective SIRT3/SIRT4 balance, aging impairs mitochondrial quality control and stress adaptation. This association links mitochondrial sirtuin biology to the functional decline of aging tissues.

label: STACs
description: Sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs) such as resveratrol lower the Km of SIRT1 for its peptide and NAD+ substrates, amplifying deacetylation efficiency. Directionally, STAC binding sits upstream of enhanced catalytic rate. This allosteric effect is the defining action of a STAC, and it underlies the metabolic and longevity benefits attributed to these molecules. By increasing substrate affinity, STACs allow SIRT1 to deacetylate targets even at low NAD+ concentrations. This mechanism distinguishes true STACs from indirect NAD+-raising compounds, and it is central to STAC pharmacology.

label: SIRT1 KM for substrates
