label: NAD+ in tumor microenvironment
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins (overview, CD38 KO risks, cancer therapies).md
description: CD38 enzymatic activity depletes NAD+ in the tumor microenvironment and generates adenosine, suppressing anti-tumor T-cell and NK-cell responses. Directionally, CD38 sits upstream of NAD+ depletion and immunosuppression. This links CD38 to cancer immune evasion, and anti-CD38 antibodies both target myeloma and reshape the tumor microenvironment. By consuming NAD+ and producing immunosuppressive adenosine, CD38 on tumor and immune cells dampens anti-tumor immunity. This dual role makes CD38 both a therapeutic target and a mechanism of immune escape in cancer.

label: Anti-CD38 mAbs
description: Anti-CD38 monoclonal antibodies eliminate CD38+ Tregs and MDSCs and reduce adenosine-mediated immunosuppression, restoring T- and NK-cell function in the tumor microenvironment. Directionally, anti-CD38 therapy sits upstream of tumor-microenvironment reprogramming. This is both an anticancer action and a means to spare NAD+ for sirtuins, and it illustrates the dual therapeutic logic of CD38 targeting. By depleting immunosuppressive cells and reducing adenosine, these antibodies restore effector immune responses. The resulting reshaping of the tumor microenvironment contributes to the efficacy of anti-CD38 antibodies in multiple myeloma and other cancers.

label: FOXO3a (to induce BNIP3 mitophagy)
description: SIRT1 deacetylates FOXO3a, which transcriptionally induces BNIP3, forming the NAD+-SIRT1-FOXO3a-BNIP3 mitophagy axis that clears damaged mitochondria. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of BNIP3-dependent mitophagy. This protects cells from mitochondrial dysfunction and ROS, and it is a refined mitophagic branch of the SIRT1-FOXO3a program. By inducing BNIP3, FOXO3a promotes the selective removal of damaged mitochondria. This axis connects sirtuin-mediated NAD+ sensing to the quality control of the mitochondrial network.

label: HIF-2α
description: SIRT7 inhibits HIF-2α, similar to its HIF-1α opposition.

label: Retinoblastoma Protein (Rb)
description: SIRT1 deacetylates the retinoblastoma protein (Rb) as part of its cell-cycle regulatory functions, influencing Rb's interaction with E2F and cell-cycle control. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically modifies Rb. This adds a cell-cycle dimension to SIRT1 beyond p53/E2F, and the evidence carries moderate confidence reflecting incomplete mechanistic detail. By deacetylating Rb, SIRT1 may modulate its ability to restrain E2F-dependent transcription and cell-cycle progression. This regulation connects SIRT1 to the G1/S checkpoint and to the control of proliferation in normal and cancer cells.

label: SIRT1/AMPK
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT1 and AMPK form a reciprocal regulatory loop in which each can activate the other, jointly promoting energy homeostasis and autophagic flux. Directionally, the interaction is bidirectional: SIRT1 deacetylates and activates LKB1 and PGC-1α while AMPK phosphorylates and activates SIRT1. This creates a self-reinforcing metabolic circuit, and it is a central node integrating nutrient sensing and clearance. By activating each other, SIRT1 and AMPK amplify catabolic and protective programs, including mitochondrial biogenesis and autophagy. This loop is a key target for interventions that aim to restore metabolic health in aging.

label: Energy homeostasis and autophagy
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

This creates a self-reinforcing metabolic circuit, and it is a central node integrating nutrient sensing and clearance. By activating each other, SIRT1 and AMPK amplify catabolic and protective programs, including mitochondrial biogenesis and autophagy. This loop is a key target for interventions that aim to restore metabolic health in aging.

label: SIRT1 (Ser27, Thr344)
description: Under low-energy conditions, AMPK directly phosphorylates SIRT1 at Ser27 and Thr344, enhancing its deacetylase activity and coupling energy deficit to sirtuin function. Directionally, AMPK sits upstream of SIRT1 activation. This closes the reciprocal loop with SIRT1, and it ensures sirtuin responses track cellular AMP/ATP state. By phosphorylating SIRT1, AMPK links the energy-sensing kinase network to sirtuin-dependent gene regulation. This mechanism explains how fasting, exercise, and caloric restriction, which activate AMPK, also engage SIRT1-dependent programs.

label: p73
description: SIRT1 deacetylates p73, suppressing its transcriptional activity and inhibiting apoptosis, analogous to its regulation of the related p53 family member. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically inactivates p73. This promotes cell survival under stress but can be tumor-promoting, and it extends SIRT1's control over the p53 family. By deacetylating p73, SIRT1 dampens its ability to activate pro-apoptotic and cell-cycle-checkpoint genes. This regulation is relevant to both normal tissue protection and cancer, where p73 suppression by SIRT1 may reduce tumor-suppressive responses.

label: SIRT1 deacetylation of FOXO4
description: FOXO4 deacetylation by SIRT1 enhances expression of GADD45 and suppresses caspase-3/7 activity, promoting DNA repair over apoptosis. Directionally, SIRT1 activates FOXO4, which induces GADD45. This biases cells toward damage repair rather than death, and it is a further example of SIRT1 steering stress responses toward survival and genome maintenance. By inducing GADD45, FOXO4 supports nucleotide-excision repair and cell-cycle arrest, giving cells time to repair damage. This survival-oriented program is central to SIRT1's cytoprotective functions.

label: GADD45 expression
description: FOXO4 deacetylation by SIRT1 enhances expression of GADD45 and suppresses caspase-3/7 activity, promoting DNA repair over apoptosis. Directionally, SIRT1 activates FOXO4, which induces GADD45. This biases cells toward damage repair rather than death, and it is a further example of SIRT1 steering stress responses toward survival and genome maintenance. By inducing GADD45, FOXO4 supports nucleotide-excision repair and cell-cycle arrest, giving cells time to repair damage. This survival-oriented program is central to SIRT1's cytoprotective functions.

label: OX2R
description: In BRASTO mice, hypothalamic SIRT1 deacetylates the transcription factor NKX2-1, which drives expression of the orexin type 2 receptor (OX2R); increased OX2R in DMH/LH raises neural activity, physical activity, and energy expenditure, underpinning the approximately 11% lifespan extension. This positions the SIRT1-to-NKX2-1-to-OX2R pathway as a hypothalamic longevity axis that mimics calorie restriction. By increasing physical activity and energy expenditure through orexin signaling, SIRT1 promotes a CR-like metabolic state. This brain-centered mechanism demonstrates that sirtuin effects on lifespan can be mediated through neural control of energy balance.

label: NKX2-1
description: NKX2-1 (Nk2 homeobox 1) is deacetylated by SIRT1 in hypothalamic DMH/LH neurons; deacetylated NKX2-1 activates transcription of OX2R, the orexin receptor whose increased signaling recapitulates calorie restriction and extends lifespan in BRASTO mice. Thus NKX2-1 is the direct transcriptional relay between SIRT1 and OX2R. By linking SIRT1 activity to orexin-receptor expression, NKX2-1 connects sirtuin signaling to the neural circuits controlling arousal, activity, and energy expenditure. This pathway illustrates how a single transcription factor can mediate the longevity effects of sirtuin activation in the brain.

label: IGF-1 signaling
description: Male SIRT6 transgenics have lower serum IGF-1 and reduced downstream insulin/IGF-1-like signaling (AKT, pAKT); reduced insulin/IGF-1-like signaling is strongly associated with increased longevity in model organisms, providing the leading explanation for SIRT6's male-specific lifespan extension. Directionally, SIRT6-mediated inhibition of IGF-1 signaling sits upstream of lifespan extension. By suppressing the growth-promoting IGF-AKT axis, SIRT6 may recapitulate the longevity benefits of reduced insulin/IGF signaling. This mechanism connects SIRT6 to one of the most conserved longevity pathways across species.

label: CtIP
description: SIRT6 deacetylates CtIP (RBBP8), a key factor in DNA double-strand-break end resection and homologous recombination repair; this is one of the three best-characterized direct SIRT6 substrates (with H3K9ac/H3K56ac and GCN5). By promoting end resection, CtIP enables homologous recombination, and its regulation by SIRT6 connects sirtuin activity to high-fidelity DNA repair, genome stability, and tumor suppression. Loss of SIRT6 impairs this repair, contributing to genomic instability and cancer.

label: ADAM10
description: SIRT1 induces expression of ADAM10, the principal alpha-secretase that cleaves APP away from amyloidogenic beta-secretase (BACE1) processing, reducing beta-amyloid production; this underlies SIRT1's protective role in Alzheimer's disease models. Directionally, SIRT1 upregulates ADAM10 to promote non-amyloidogenic APP processing. By shifting APP cleavage away from the amyloidogenic pathway, SIRT1 reduces the production of toxic beta-amyloid peptides. This mechanism, together with SIRT1's anti-inflammatory and antioxidant actions, underlies its protection in Alzheimer's models and supports the idea that sirtuin activation could delay amyloid pathology.

label: Metabolic Syndrome
description: A nonsynonymous SIRT3 SNP reducing recombinant catalytic activity by about 34% is associated with metabolic syndrome in NAFLD patients and the Finnish Metabolic Syndrome in Men cohort, implicating lowered SIRT3 activity in human metabolic disease susceptibility. Directionally, reduced SIRT3 catalytic activity is associated with metabolic syndrome. This genetic evidence connects impaired mitochondrial sirtuin function to human metabolic disease, and it complements the animal studies showing that SIRT3 loss causes metabolic dysfunction. These findings support SIRT3 as a therapeutic target for metabolic syndrome.

label: Extrachromosomal rDNA Circles (ERCs)
description: Sir2p protects yeast from toxic accumulation of self-replicating extrachromosomal rDNA circles (ERCs); deletion of the replication-fork-blocking protein Fob1p rescues the short lifespan of sir2 mutants, establishing ERC suppression as the first mechanistic explanation for Sir2's longevity effect. Directionally, Sir2p suppresses ERC accumulation to extend lifespan. By preventing the toxic buildup of these circular DNA molecules, Sir2 preserves genome stability and replicative capacity. This was the first molecular mechanism linking Sir2 to longevity and remains a foundational finding in sirtuin research.

label: Mother cell
description: Sir2p maintains cellular polarity so that oxidized proteins, misfolded aggregates, and dysfunctional mitochondria are retained in the mother cell, allowing daughter cells to begin life undamaged; this asymmetric segregation extends daughter-cell lifespan at the mother's expense. Directionally, Sir2p promotes asymmetric segregation of damage to the mother cell. By ensuring that daughters are born free of damage, this mechanism supports the longevity of the lineage. It illustrates how sirtuins contribute to cellular rejuvenation, a concept that has influenced thinking about asymmetric cell division and aging.

label: Sas2p
description: A more recent epigenetic mechanism: Sir2p and the HAT Sas2p regulate H4K16 acetylation at the telomere-euchromatin boundary; Sir2p levels decline with age as H4K16Ac rises, and constitutive H4K16 acetylation shortens lifespan, linking subtelomeric silencing to yeast longevity. Directionally, the Sir2/Sas2 balance at telomeres determines lifespan. By maintaining H4K16 deacetylation at subtelomeric regions, Sir2 preserves the silenced state that supports longevity. This mechanism extends the sirtuin-longevity link beyond ERC suppression and highlights the importance of chromatin state in aging.

label: IRS-2
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: SIRT1 deacetylates insulin receptor substrate-2 (IRS-2), a key adaptor in insulin and insulin-like growth factor signaling. This deacetylation enables efficient tyrosine phosphorylation of IRS-2 and downstream activation of the PI3K-Akt cascade, improving insulin signal transduction in peripheral tissues. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatic activity sits upstream of enhanced insulin signaling. By reinforcing this pathway, SIRT1 helps counter insulin resistance and hyperglycemia in type 2 diabetes. The regulation illustrates how a single sirtuin can tune insulin sensitivity, and it positions SIRT1 activators as potential metabolic therapeutics alongside lifestyle interventions that raise NAD+.

label: CRTC2
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: SIRT1 deacetylates CREB-regulated transcriptional coactivator 2 (CRTC2), an important regulator of hepatic gluconeogenesis. CRTC2 deacetylation occurs as part of SIRT1's dynamic, fasting-coupled control of glucose production in the liver, complementing its actions on FOXO1 and PGC-1alpha. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of CRTC2-dependent transcriptional programs. Together these branches fine-tune when and how much glucose the liver releases, balancing gluconeogenic output against the body's energy needs. The coordination of CRTC2, FOXO1 and PGC-1alpha shows that SIRT1 integrates multiple transcriptional nodes to achieve homeostatic glucose control during fasting and refeeding.

label: Akt phosphorylation
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: SIRT6 negatively regulates the insulin-signaling cascade by suppressing upstream signaling through the insulin receptor and insulin receptor substrates. This restraint reduces downstream Akt phosphorylation, preventing excessive glucose uptake and helping to maintain metabolic balance in peripheral tissues. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of dampened insulin-PI3K-Akt signaling. Loss of SIRT6 elevates this signaling, contributing to insulin resistance and metabolic dysfunction. By toning down insulin-driven anabolic responses, SIRT6 protects cells from nutrient overload and supports the metabolic flexibility that is lost in obesity and type 2 diabetes.

label: SREBP2
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: SIRT6 limits cholesterol and lipid accumulation in the liver by repressing the sterol-regulatory transcription factor SREBP2. Suppression of SREBP2 restrains the expression of cholesterol-biosynthetic genes, contributing to SIRT6's protection against hepatic steatosis and systemic metabolic dysfunction. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of SREBP2-dependent cholesterol synthesis. This complements SIRT6's repression of SREBP-1c-mediated fatty-acid synthesis, giving SIRT6 broad control over hepatic lipid homeostasis.

label: ATGL
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: SIRT6 enhances adipose tissue lipolysis and prevents lipotoxic insulin resistance by inducing expression of adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL), the rate-limiting enzyme of triglyceride breakdown. This induction is dependent on the transcription factor FOXO1, which SIRT6 engages to drive ATGL gene expression. Directionally, SIRT6 promotes fat mobilization through FOXO1-dependent ATGL induction. By mobilizing stored fat, this pathway supplies fuel during fasting and prevents the accumulation of lipid intermediates that impair insulin signaling. The regulation supports SIRT6's role in metabolic flexibility, balancing lipid storage against oxidation according to systemic energy demands.

label: XBP1
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: SIRT6 alleviates endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress by regulating the transcription factor XBP1, a central mediator of the unfolded-protein response. By modulating XBP1, SIRT6 limits the inflammatory and metabolic dysfunction that arises from chronic ER stress in the liver. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of XBP1-dependent stress resolution. This action complements SIRT6's H3K9 deacetylation at glycolytic gene promoters, giving it coordinated control over hepatic metabolism and stress signaling. In this way SIRT6 couples chromatin regulation to the unfolded-protein response, protecting hepatocytes from the damage that drives fatty liver disease and metabolic decline.

label: PCSK9
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: SIRT6 regulates systemic lipid homeostasis in part through PCSK9, a secreted protein that controls LDL receptor degradation and thereby plasma LDL-cholesterol levels. Deficiency of SIRT6 accelerates atherosclerosis through dysregulation of PCSK9 and impaired LDL metabolism, indicating that SIRT6 normally constrains PCSK9-driven LDL accumulation. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of PCSK9 and LDL handling. By restraining this axis, SIRT6 limits the lipid burden on the vascular wall and protects against atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. This places SIRT6 among the chromatin-regulatory proteins that influence cardiovascular risk through systemic cholesterol control.

label: GABPβ1
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: SIRT7 deacetylates GA-binding protein beta1 (GABPbeta1), a subunit of the GABP transcription factor complex that controls expression of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial genes. Deacetylation facilitates GABP complex formation and transcriptional activation of these genes, supporting mitochondrial biogenesis and function. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of GABP-dependent mitochondrial gene expression. SIRT7 deficiency accordingly causes systemic mitochondrial dysfunction, manifesting as lactate accumulation and cardiac abnormalities.

label: Pyruvate Dehydrogenase
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: Beyond its well-known mono-ADP-ribosylation of glutamate dehydrogenase, SIRT4 also functions as a lipoamidase that regulates the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex. By removing lipoate modifications, SIRT4 can influence pyruvate dehydrogenase activity and thereby control entry of glucose-derived carbon into the tricarboxylic acid cycle. Directionally, SIRT4's lipoamidase activity sits upstream of pyruvate dehydrogenase regulation. This broadens SIRT4's control of mitochondrial substrate oxidation and adds to its role in metabolic flexibility.

label: NNMT
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: Nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT) methylates nicotinamide to 1-methylnicotinamide, diverting this precursor away from the NAMPT-dependent salvage pathway. By withdrawing nicotinamide from NAD+ regeneration, NNMT activity limits NAD+ biosynthesis and indirectly modulates the activity of NAD+-dependent sirtuins. Directionally, NNMT sits upstream of reduced NAD+ availability. This makes NNMT a metabolic competitor with the salvage pathway, and elevated NNMT in obesity and certain cancers contributes to NAD+ depletion and metabolic dysfunction. Modulating NNMT is therefore of interest as a strategy to preserve NAD+ pools and support sirtuin activity in disease states.

label: Brown Adipose Tissue
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: SIRT6 supports thermogenesis in brown and beige adipose tissue, which is induced under cold exposure, thereby contributing to energy expenditure and protection from obesity. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of thermogenic gene programs in brown adipose tissue. This pro-thermogenic role opposes SIRT7, which suppresses brown-adipose function, illustrating opposing actions within the sirtuin family on energy expenditure. By maintaining the capacity of brown and beige fat to burn calories, SIRT6 helps the body dissipate energy as heat rather than store it. Supporting SIRT6 activity is therefore considered a potential approach for counteracting weight gain and metabolic disease.

label: UCP1
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: SIRT3 controls thermogenesis in brown adipose tissue by deacetylating regulatory targets upstream of the uncoupling protein UCP1, maintaining the mitochondrial function required for adaptive heat production. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of UCP1-dependent thermogenic capacity. By preserving mitochondrial oxidative function and reducing oxidative stress in brown fat, SIRT3 ensures that mitochondria can sustain the proton leak through UCP1 that generates heat. This makes SIRT3 important for cold-induced thermogenesis and overall energy balance.

label: mTOR signaling
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: Nutrient abundance activates the mTOR pathway, which promotes anabolic processes such as protein synthesis and lipid accumulation while suppressing autophagy. Sirtuins counterbalance this anabolic state by favoring catabolic pathways that restore metabolic equilibrium. Directionally, sirtuins and mTOR act as opposed nutrient-sensing axes. This opposition is most evident during caloric restriction or fasting, when falling nutrient signals dampen mTOR while NAD+-sensitive sirtuins drive fatty-acid oxidation, mitochondrial maintenance, and autophagy.

label: WAT browning
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: SIRT1 deacetylates PPARgamma at lysine residues K268 and K293, and this modification promotes exchange of cofactors within the PPARgamma transcriptional complex. The resulting change in cofactor recruitment enhances browning of white adipose tissue, increasing thermogenesis, mitochondrial biogenesis, and PGC-1alpha-dependent oxidative programs. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatic modification of PPARgamma sits upstream of beige adipocyte induction. Because PPARgamma is a master regulator of adipocyte biology, its deacetylation by SIRT1 can shift adipose tissue from a fat-storing toward a fat-burning phenotype.

label: FoxO1 deacetylation
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: SIRT2 suppresses adipocyte differentiation through deacetylation of the transcription factor FoxO1, which reinforces FoxO1-mediated repression of PPARgamma. Consistent with this, reduced SIRT1 and SIRT2 expression in visceral adipose stem cells from obese individuals correlates with enhanced adipogenic capacity and visceral fat expansion. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of FoxO1-dependent anti-adipogenic programs. By keeping FoxO1 active in repressing PPARgamma, SIRT2 restrains the conversion of precursor cells into mature adipocytes.

label: LCAD (fatty acid β-oxidation)
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: Fasting induces SIRT3 activation, which in turn enhances fatty acid oxidation through deacetylation and activation of long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (LCAD), a key enzyme of mitochondrial beta-oxidation. Directionally, SIRT3 enzymatic activation of LCAD sits upstream of enhanced lipid catabolism. This promotes the harvest of energy from fat stores during fasting and caloric restriction, when glucose is scarce. By supporting efficient beta-oxidation, SIRT3 helps maintain ATP production while limiting the accumulation of damaging lipid intermediates.

label: Pyruvate Dehydrogenase (PDH)
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: SIRT3 maintains the activity of pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) by preventing its hyperacetylation, thereby coupling glycolysis-derived carbon to mitochondrial oxidation. Loss of SIRT3 leads to PDH hyperacetylation, reduced glucose oxidation, and accumulation of pyruvate and lactate, impairing metabolic flexibility in skeletal muscle. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of PDH-dependent glucose oxidation. By protecting PDH, SIRT3 ensures that glucose can be oxidized in mitochondria rather than being diverted to lactate, preserving energy efficiency during exercise and metabolic stress. This function is central to SIRT3's role in supporting muscle performance and whole-body glucose handling.

label: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: In hepatocytes, SIRT4 represses PPARalpha signaling and inhibits malonyl-CoA decarboxylase, shifting liver metabolism away from mitochondrial fatty-acid utilization and toward anabolic lipid conservation. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of suppressed fatty acid oxidation. This metabolic brake counterbalances SIRT3, which promotes beta-oxidation, so the relative activity of the two mitochondrial sirtuins determines whether the liver oxidizes or stores fat. Under chronic nutrient surplus, sustained SIRT4 activity contributes to hepatic steatosis, whereas conditions that shift the SIRT3/SIRT4 balance toward SIRT3 favor fat burning.

label: VLCAD, LCAD, MCAD, ECHA (fatty acid oxidation)
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: SIRT5 activates multiple fatty acid beta-oxidation enzymes through desuccinylation, including very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (VLCAD), long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (LCAD), medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (MCAD), and the alpha subunit of enoyl-CoA hydratase (ECHA). Directionally, SIRT5 enzymatic activation of these enzymes sits upstream of enhanced lipid catabolism. Deficiency of SIRT5 compromises fatty acid metabolism, leading to acylcarnitine accumulation and decreased ATP production.

label: Telomeric chromatin
source_file: _document_ - SIRT1 Protein roles at the nexus of health, disease, and therapeutics.md
description: SIRT1's histone deacetylase activity is directly associated with regulation of telomeric chromatin, gene expression, and the dynamic association of DNA repair factors with chromatin. Telomere shortening occurs over the lifespan and has been linked to the concomitant decrease in SIRT1 expression with age. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of telomeric chromatin maintenance. By preserving the integrity of telomere-associated chromatin and facilitating repair factor access, SIRT1 helps stabilize the chromosome ends whose erosion is a hallmark of aging.

label: 40 substrates
source_file: _document_ - SIRT1 Protein roles at the nexus of health, disease, and therapeutics.md
description: SIRT1 functions as a deacetylase that modulates more than forty known substrates involved in inflammation, stress resistance, mitochondrial biogenesis, fatty acid metabolism, insulin secretion, glucose production, and lipid homeostasis. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatic activity sits upstream of a broad network of cellular processes. This extraordinary substrate diversity explains why SIRT1 participates in metabolism, stress resistance, inflammation, and longevity across many tissues. The wide substrate range also means SIRT1's effects are highly context-dependent, with outcomes shaped by the tissue, the nutrient state, and the specific substrates engaged.

label: N-Myc and c-Myc
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT2 enhances the protein stability of the oncogenic transcription factors N-Myc and c-Myc, promoting cancer cell proliferation. This represents an oncogenic function of SIRT2 that is distinct from its tumor-suppressive roles in other cellular contexts. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of Myc stabilization and enhanced proliferation. By protecting these potent oncogenes from degradation, SIRT2 can support the growth of Myc-driven tumors, complicating the simple view of sirtuins as universal tumor suppressors.

label: AKR1C1 (inhibiting STAT3 transactivation)
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT2 deacetylates aldo-keto reductase family 1 member C1 (AKR1C1), and this modification inhibits transactivation of STAT3 target genes, suppressing migration of non-small-cell lung cancer cells both in vitro and in xenograft models. Directionally, SIRT2 enzymatic modification of AKR1C1 sits upstream of reduced STAT3-driven metastasis. By restraining STAT3 transcriptional activity, SIRT2 limits the invasive and migratory phenotype that contributes to lung cancer progression. This tumor-suppressive axis contrasts with SIRT2's pro-tumorigenic stabilization of Myc in other settings, reinforcing the context-dependence of sirtuin biology in oncology.

label: IDH1 (repressing CRC migration)
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: In human colorectal cancer, SIRT2-dependent deacetylation of the metabolic enzyme IDH1 represses cancer cell migration and invasion both in vitro and in vivo. This regulation of IDH1 influences cellular metabolism and inhibits the formation of liver metastases. Directionally, SIRT2 enzymatic modification of IDH1 sits upstream of suppressed colorectal cancer metastasis. By modulating IDH1 and the metabolic state of the tumor cell, SIRT2 limits the invasive capacity that drives metastatic spread. This positions SIRT2 as a suppressor of colorectal cancer progression and indicates that preserving SIRT2 activity, or mimicking its effects, could restrain metastasis in this malignancy.

label: E-cadherin promotion
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT4 suppresses epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) by promoting expression of the epithelial marker E-cadherin in gastric cancer cells. This maintains an epithelial phenotype and inhibits cancer cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of maintained epithelial phenotype and suppressed metastasis. By preventing the loss of E-cadherin that characterizes EMT, SIRT4 blocks a key step in the acquisition of invasive and migratory behavior. This supports SIRT4's role as a tumor suppressor in gastric cancer, where its downregulation may allow tumors to progress toward metastatic disease.

label: Snail-dependent KLF4 repression
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT6 drives epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and metastasis in non-small-cell lung cancer through Snail-dependent transrepression of the transcription factor KLF4. This represents an oncogenic function of SIRT6 that contrasts sharply with its tumor-suppressive roles in other cancers. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of EMT induction and metastatic progression in this context. By repressing KLF4, an epithelial-fate factor, SIRT6 allows Snail to drive the mesenchymal program that promotes invasion and spread.

label: BRCA1 deacetylation
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT2 promotes BRCA1-BARD1 heterodimerization through deacetylation of BRCA1, facilitating assembly of the repair complex required for homologous recombination. This supports genome maintenance and tumor suppression by enabling high-fidelity repair of DNA double-strand breaks. Directionally, SIRT2 enzymatic licensing of BRCA1 sits upstream of repair complex formation. By promoting homologous recombination, SIRT2 helps cells repair potentially oncogenic DNA damage accurately rather than through error-prone pathways. This links SIRT2 to DNA repair fidelity and explains part of its tumor-suppressive activity.

label: Slug (EMT transcription factor)
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: In basal-like breast cancer, SIRT2 maintains the protein stability of Slug, an epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) transcription factor, through deacetylation. Stabilized Slug contributes to the robust tumorigenic activity of basal-like breast cancer, along with its enhanced invasive and metastatic capabilities. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of Slug-dependent EMT and tumor progression. By protecting Slug from degradation, SIRT2 sustains the mesenchymal program that drives invasion and metastasis in this aggressive breast cancer subtype.

label: SIRT1 (via glutamine metabolism)
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT4 exerts tumor-suppressive activity in breast cancer by negatively regulating expression of SIRT1, and this suppression occurs through repression of glutamine metabolism. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of reduced SIRT1 expression via metabolic regulation. This reveals cross-talk between mitochondrial and nuclear sirtuin proteins in cancer progression, where mitochondrial SIRT4 restrains nuclear SIRT1-dependent growth programs. By limiting glutamine utilization and, consequently, SIRT1 levels, SIRT4 curbs the metabolic and survival advantages that SIRT1 confers on tumor cells.

label: FoxO1/MDR2 upregulation
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT1 causes tamoxifen resistance in ER-alpha-positive breast cancer cells through upregulation of multidrug resistance protein 2 (MDR2), an effect mediated by deacetylation of the transcription factor FoxO1. Inhibition of SIRT1 impairs nuclear FoxO1 accumulation and MDR2 expression and augments the cytotoxic effects of paclitaxel and doxorubicin in tamoxifen-resistant cells. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of FoxO1- and MDR2-mediated chemoresistance. By driving drug-efflux capacity in resistant cells, SIRT1 reduces the efficacy of endocrine therapy and other agents.

label: VEGF-A elevation
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT1 promotes cisplatin resistance in non-small-cell lung cancer cells by elevating expression of vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A). SIRT1 is upregulated in cisplatin-resistant tumor tissues and cells compared with cisplatin-sensitive groups, correlating with the resistant phenotype. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of VEGF-A-mediated chemoresistance. By enhancing VEGF-A, SIRT1 may support tumor survival and adaptive responses that blunt the cytotoxic effects of cisplatin. This identifies SIRT1 as a potential target for overcoming chemotherapy resistance in lung cancer, since inhibiting SIRT1 could lower VEGF-A and re-sensitize resistant tumors to platinum-based treatment.

label: ATM-Chk2 DNA damage repair
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT3 promotes DNA damage repair and radioresistance through the ataxia telangiectasia mutated (ATM)-Chk2 pathway in non-small-cell lung cancer cells. By supporting this DNA-damage-response branch, SIRT3 enables cancer cells to survive ionizing radiation more effectively. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of enhanced DNA repair and radiation resistance. This has therapeutic implications, because combining SIRT3 inhibition with radiotherapy could impair the repair of radiation-induced damage and thereby improve treatment efficacy.

label: p16 and p21
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT4 upregulates expression of the cell-cycle inhibitor genes p16 and p21, while suppressing CyclinB1/Cdc2 and Cdc25c, and this cell-cycle blockade induces apoptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma cells. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis induction. By enforcing these checkpoints, SIRT4 functions as a tumor suppressor in liver cancer, limiting proliferation and promoting death of transformed cells. The coordinated upregulation of p16 and p21 with suppression of cell-cycle drivers reflects SIRT4's broad influence on the machinery that governs entry into mitosis. This supports interest in SIRT4 as a therapeutic target for hepatocellular carcinoma.

label: Glutathione S-transferase π1
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT3 downregulates both the mRNA and protein levels of glutathione S-transferase pi 1 (GSTP1), a phase II detoxification enzyme involved in the metabolism of chemotherapeutic agents. SIRT3 overexpression promotes sorafenib-induced apoptosis and thereby enhances the drug sensitivity of hepatocellular carcinoma cells. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of reduced GSTP1 and enhanced drug responsiveness. By lowering the capacity of cancer cells to detoxify sorafenib, SIRT3 restores sensitivity to this agent. This suggests that SIRT3 expression status could predict sorafenib response in liver cancer, and that boosting SIRT3 may help overcome drug resistance in this malignancy.

label: JAK2/STAT3 inhibition
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT6 suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma cell growth through induction of apoptosis, inhibition of oxidative stress, and blockade of the JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of JAK2/STAT3 blockade and tumor suppression. By restraining this oncogenic signaling axis, SIRT6 limits the proliferative and survival signals that drive liver cancer progression. The combination of apoptosis induction and oxidative-stress suppression reflects SIRT6's multi-pronged tumor-suppressive activity. This positions SIRT6 as a promising target for hepatocellular carcinoma, where restoring or enhancing SIRT6 function could complement existing treatments.

label: eNOS activation
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Endothelial-cell-specific overexpression of SIRT1 protects against atherosclerosis in apolipoprotein E-deficient mice, and this protection is associated with inhibition of endothelial cell apoptosis through activation of eNOS expression. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of eNOS-dependent vascular protection. By maintaining nitric oxide production and limiting endothelial cell death, SIRT1 preserves endothelial function and resists the progression of atherosclerotic lesions. This positions SIRT1 as an atheroprotective factor in the vasculature and supports efforts to activate SIRT1 as a strategy against cardiovascular disease.

label: Macrophage polarization
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT2 decreases atherosclerotic plaque formation in LDL receptor-deficient mice by regulating macrophage polarization. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of anti-atherogenic macrophage phenotypes. By steering macrophages toward less inflammatory states, SIRT2 reduces the foam-cell accumulation and chronic inflammation that drive plaque development. This links SIRT2 to innate immune modulation in vascular disease, complementing the anti-inflammatory actions of other sirtuins. Because macrophages are central to atherosclerosis, interventions that preserve SIRT2 activity in these cells could help limit plaque burden and stabilize existing lesions, reducing the risk of cardiovascular events.

label: COPD development
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Reduced SIRT6 expression is associated with COPD development through enhancement of cellular senescence that arises from insufficient autophagy during cigarette smoke exposure. SIRT6 deficiency impairs autophagy and promotes premature senescence in lung cells. Directionally, SIRT6 deficiency sits upstream of impaired autophagy and accelerated cellular aging in the lung. By failing to clear damaged components, cells accumulate and enter senescence, contributing to the structural remodeling and functional decline characteristic of COPD.

label: SIRT3 deficiency
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT3 deficiency in the aging murine lung promotes a fibrotic response mediated by TGF-beta1 and augments mitochondrial DNA damage and apoptosis in alveolar epithelial cells. Conversely, SIRT3 overexpression can ameliorate asbestos-induced pulmonary fibrosis. Directionally, SIRT3 deficiency sits upstream of enhanced TGF-beta1-driven fibrosis, because by weakening mitochondrial antioxidant defenses it renders alveolar epithelial cells vulnerable to the damage that fuels the fibrotic program. Restoring SIRT3 could therefore protect against pulmonary fibrosis, making mitochondrial sirtuin activity an important determinant of lung resilience to environmental and aging-related fibrotic injury.

label: Lung fibrosis via TGF-β1
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT3 deficiency in the aging murine lung promotes a fibrotic response mediated by TGF-beta1 and augments mitochondrial DNA damage and apoptosis in alveolar epithelial cells. label: Th2 responses and macrophage polarization
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT2 enhances allergic asthmatic inflammation by upregulating T-helper type 2 responses and macrophage polarization. Pharmacologic ablation of SIRT2 attenuates, while genetic SIRT2 overexpression exaggerates, the allergic asthmatic phenotype. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of Th2-driven allergic inflammation. By promoting the type 2 immune response characteristic of asthma, SIRT2 amplifies airway inflammation and the associated pathology. This makes SIRT2 inhibition a candidate therapeutic approach for allergic asthma, since reducing SIRT2 activity could dampen Th2 responses and macrophage-mediated inflammation, providing a potential strategy to modulate the severity of the disease.

label: Unbalanced p53/SIRT1 axis
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: The unbalanced p53/SIRT1 axis may impact lymphocyte homeostasis in COVID-19 patients. COVID-19 is characterized by increased p53 transcription in circulating lymphocytes and a persistently activated form of p53, possibly due to low SIRT1 levels. Directionally, low SIRT1 and elevated p53 activity sit upstream of disturbed lymphocyte homeostasis. Because SIRT1 normally deacetylates p53 and restrains its pro-apoptotic activity, its deficiency could leave lymphocytes vulnerable to p53-driven apoptosis and contribute to the lymphopenia seen in severe disease. Increased SIRT1 expression might therefore help alleviate COVID-19 pathogenesis by restoring the balance of this axis.

label: SIRT3 levels
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Serum SIRT3 levels are markedly lower in severe COVID-19 patients compared with those with mild or moderate disease, indicating a positive role of SIRT3 in alleviating COVID-19. Directionally, SIRT3 levels sit upstream of clinical outcome and prognosis. Because SIRT3 supports mitochondrial antioxidant defense and dampens inflammation, its reduction in severe cases may permit greater oxidative stress and inflammatory damage. SIRT3 levels therefore serve as an indicator of disease severity and associate with prognosis.

label: Metabolic switch in cardiac hypertrophy
description: SIRT1 interacts with and activates PPARalpha to prevent the metabolic switch from fatty acid oxidation to glycolysis that occurs in cardiac hypertrophy. By promoting fatty acid oxidation gene expression and inactivating NF-kappaB, SIRT1 preserves the adult heart's preferred fuel preference. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of PPARalpha-dependent metabolic preservation. Maintaining fatty acid oxidation prevents the maladaptive glycolytic shift that accompanies hypertrophic growth and heart failure.

label: SOD2 and Catalase
description: SIRT3 protects against cardiac hypertrophy by inducing expression of the antioxidant proteins SOD2 and catalase. The SIRT3-mediated reduction in reactive oxygen species inhibits AKT signaling and the downstream gene expression associated with hypertrophy induction. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of antioxidant defense and hypertrophy suppression, since by lowering mitochondrial oxidative stress it removes a key stimulus for the growth signaling that drives pathological cardiac enlargement. This places mitochondrial sirtuin activity at the center of the redox control governing cardiac stress responses.

label: c-Jun (cardiac hypertrophy)
description: SIRT6 functions as a negative regulator of cardiac hypertrophy by co-repressing c-Jun-dependent transcription at the chromatin level, thereby inhibiting downstream IGF-AKT signaling. In vivo inhibition of IGF signaling in SIRT6 knockout mice abrogates the hypertrophic response. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of suppressed c-Jun transcription and IGF-AKT signaling. By restraining this growth-promoting axis, SIRT6 limits the pathological growth signals that drive cardiac hypertrophy. The observation that blocking IGF signaling rescues the hypertrophic phenotype confirms that this pathway mediates the effect.

label: SIRT3 gene
description: The human SIRT3 gene is deleted in up to 20% of all human cancers analyzed overall, and in up to 40% of breast and ovarian cancers. This frequent deletion establishes SIRT3 as a tumor suppressor that acts through reactive oxygen species suppression and metabolic regulation. Directionally, SIRT3 loss sits upstream of increased tumorigenesis susceptibility. By removing mitochondrial antioxidant protection, deletion of SIRT3 raises oxidative stress that can drive oncogenic signaling and genomic damage. The high deletion frequency, especially in breast and ovarian cancer, suggests SIRT3 status is an important determinant of cancer risk and may have prognostic value.

label: 20% of human cancers
description: The human SIRT3 gene is deleted in up to 20% of all human cancers analyzed overall, and in up to 40% of breast and ovarian cancers. label: SIRT6 locus
description: A survey of approximately one thousand human cancer cell lines revealed that the SIRT6 locus was deleted in 35% of the samples. This high deletion frequency supports SIRT6's role as a tumor suppressor that acts through repression of HIF-1alpha and c-MYC and suppression of glycolytic metabolic reprogramming. Directionally, SIRT6 loss sits upstream of enhanced oncogenic metabolism and tumor growth. Without SIRT6, the brakes on aerobic glycolysis and proliferation are released, promoting the metabolic phenotype that sustains cancer. The prevalence of SIRT6 deletion across diverse cancer cell lines underscores its broad importance in restraining malignancy.

label: 35% of cancer cell lines

This high deletion frequency supports SIRT6's role as a tumor suppressor that acts through repression of HIF-1alpha and c-MYC and suppression of glycolytic metabolic reprogramming. label: ATM-p53/p73 pathway
description: Ectopic SIRT6 overexpression results in increased p53- and p73-dependent apoptosis through the ataxia telangiectasia mutated (ATM) kinase, and this effect requires SIRT6's mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activity. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of ATM-dependent activation of p53 and p73. This reveals a deacetylation-independent tumor-suppressive mechanism of SIRT6, in which its enzymatic transfer of ADP-ribose rather than histone deacetylation triggers the cell-death program. By engaging the p53 family, SIRT6 can eliminate stressed or transformed cells before they become established tumors. This expands our understanding of sirtuin catalytic diversity in cancer suppression.

label: Aging (depleting NAD+)
description: CD38, the major NADase in many mouse tissues, increases with age and depletes cellular NAD+ pools, thereby compromising sirtuin function. Mice lacking CD38 show elevated NAD+ levels and increased SIRT1 activity, coupled with protection from diet-induced obesity. Directionally, age-related CD38 upregulation sits upstream of NAD+ depletion and reduced sirtuin activity. Because sirtuins depend on NAD+ as a co-substrate, the rising NAD+ consumption by CD38 during aging starves sirtuin enzymes of their fuel. This makes CD38 a key target for NAD+-restoring interventions, and CD38 inhibition is being explored as a way to preserve NAD+ and support sirtuin function during aging.

label: PARP1 and PARP2
source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
description: PARP1 and PARP2 are major NAD+-consuming enzymes whose activity can deplete cellular NAD+ pools and compromise sirtuin function, creating competition for the same limited co-substrate. Directionally, PARP activity sits upstream of NAD+ consumption and reduced sirtuin availability. This competition is especially relevant during DNA damage, when PARP activation surges and rapidly consumes NAD+ to synthesize ADP-ribose polymers. Because both PARPs and sirtuins are essential for genome maintenance and stress responses, their shared dependence on NAD+ creates an intrinsic trade-off.

label: NAMPT/NAD+ cycle
source_file: _document_ - SIRT1 Protein roles at the nexus of health, disease, and therapeutics.md
description: SIRT1 deacetylates PGC-1alpha and amplifies expression of the circadian transcription factors BMAL1 and CLOCK. A key target of the BMAL1-CLOCK complex is NAMPT, establishing a circadian NAD+ biosynthesis cycle that rhythmically activates and deactivates SIRT1 in alignment with the daily cycle. Directionally, the NAMPT-NAD+ cycle sits upstream of rhythmic SIRT1 activity. Because SIRT1 feeds back to regulate clock components, this forms a stable oscillator coupling metabolism to circadian time. Disruption of this loop, as seen with aging and shift work, impairs both circadian function and metabolic health.

label: CHD4 (chromatin remodeler)
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT6 can coordinate with the chromatin remodeler chromodomain-helicase-DNA-binding 4 (CHD4) to promote chromatin relaxation and DNA repair, exerting an anticarcinogenic role in lung cancer. Directionally, SIRT6 and CHD4 cooperation sits upstream of enhanced DNA repair capacity. By opening chromatin at sites of damage, the pair facilitates access of repair machinery and promotes accurate repair of DNA lesions. This reduces the genomic instability that drives cancer initiation and progression. The finding highlights how sirtuins partner with chromatin remodelers to maintain genome integrity, and it supports SIRT6 as a relevant target in lung cancer prevention and therapy.

label: SIRT6 silencing
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT6 silencing can overcome sorafenib resistance by promoting ferroptosis in gastric cancer, suggesting a therapeutic strategy for resistant malignancies. Directionally, SIRT6 loss sits upstream of ferroptotic cell death and restored drug sensitivity. By triggering this iron-dependent form of cell death, SIRT6 depletion bypasses the resistance mechanisms that allow gastric cancer cells to survive sorafenib treatment. This reveals an unexpected pro-survival role for SIRT6 in this context, where its activity protects cells from ferroptosis.

label: Twist downregulation
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT3 overexpression dramatically suppresses the metastatic capability of ovarian cancer cells by inhibiting epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition through downregulation of Twist, a key EMT transcription factor. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of Twist suppression and maintenance of an epithelial phenotype. By reducing Twist, SIRT3 blocks the switch that confers migratory and invasive behavior on tumor cells. This restrains the metastatic spread that is the main cause of ovarian cancer mortality. The finding positions SIRT3 as a suppressor of ovarian cancer metastasis and suggests that maintaining SIRT3 activity could help limit disease dissemination.

label: Nrf2/HO-1 pathway (ovarian cancer)
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT5 promotes cisplatin resistance in ovarian cancer by suppressing DNA damage in a ROS-dependent manner through regulation of the Nrf2/Heme Oxygenase-1 pathway. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of Nrf2-mediated chemoresistance. By activating this antioxidant program, SIRT5 helps cancer cells neutralize the reactive oxygen species that contribute to cisplatin-induced DNA damage. This reduces the genotoxic burden of the drug and blunts its cytotoxicity, allowing tumor cells to survive treatment. Inhibiting SIRT5, therefore, could re-sensitize ovarian cancer cells to cisplatin by dismantling their antioxidant defenses.

label: SIRT1-mediated PAK1 deacetylation at K420
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of p21-activated kinase 1 (PAK1) at lysine 420 hinders autophagy and glioblastoma growth, establishing SIRT1 as a tumor suppressor in this context. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatic inhibition of PAK1 sits upstream of suppressed glioblastoma progression. By restraining PAK1 activity, SIRT1 limits the autophagy that glioblastoma cells rely on to survive under metabolic stress. This impairs tumor growth and positions SIRT1 as a brake on an aggressive brain malignancy. The finding illustrates that the same sirtuin can exert opposite effects in different cancers, and it suggests SIRT1 activation as a therapeutic direction for glioblastoma.

label: Glioblastoma growth
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of p21-activated kinase 1 (PAK1) at lysine 420 hinders autophagy and glioblastoma growth, establishing SIRT1 as a tumor suppressor in this context. label: Ku70-Bax
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT3 stabilizes the interaction between Ku70 and Bax to enhance the viability of glioma cells, representing an oncogenic function in this cancer type that contrasts with its tumor-suppressive roles elsewhere. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of enhanced glioma cell survival. By keeping Bax sequestered by Ku70, SIRT3 prevents the pro-apoptotic protein from triggering mitochondrial cell death, allowing glioma cells to evade apoptosis. This oncogenic facet complicates the picture of SIRT3 as a universal tumor suppressor and underscores that its net effect depends on cellular context. In gliomas, SIRT3 inhibition might be a strategy to promote tumor cell death.

label: ERK and STAT3 signaling
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT7 affects the malignancy of glioma cells mainly by promoting glioma proliferation and invasion through the ERK and STAT3 signaling pathways. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of ERK- and STAT3-driven glioma progression. By sustaining these proliferative and invasive signaling cascades, SIRT7 supports the aggressive growth and spread characteristic of glioma. This identifies SIRT7 as a pro-tumorigenic factor in this brain cancer and suggests that SIRT7 inhibition could suppress glioma progression. The finding adds to the emerging picture of SIRT7 as an oncogenic sirtuin in certain malignancies, where its functions diverge from the longevity-promoting roles of other family members.

label: p27/CDK2 deacetylation
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT1 promotes the progression of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia by regulating the phosphorylation and degradation of the cell-cycle inhibitor p27 through deacetylation of cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2). Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of CDK2-dependent cell-cycle progression in leukemia. By licensing CDK2 activity, SIRT1 promotes the degradation of p27 and thereby removes a brake on cell-cycle entry, fueling leukemic proliferation. This makes SIRT1 a promoter of T-ALL progression and identifies SIRT1 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy to restore p27-mediated cell-cycle control and suppress leukemic growth.

label: SIRT2 inhibition
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Inhibition of SIRT2 suppresses the in vitro growth and in vivo engraftment of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia cells through diminished deacetylation of LIM domain only 2 (LMO2). Directionally, SIRT2 inhibition sits upstream of LMO2-dependent leukemia suppression. LMO2 is a key oncogenic transcription factor in T-ALL, and its activity depends on deacetylation by SIRT2. Blocking SIRT2 reduces LMO2 function, impairing both the expansion of leukemic cells in culture and their ability to engraft in vivo. This identifies SIRT2 inhibition as a promising approach for T-ALL therapy, targeting a central oncogenic driver in this disease.

label: LMO2 deacetylation
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Inhibition of SIRT2 suppresses the in vitro growth and in vivo engraftment of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia cells through diminished deacetylation of LIM domain only 2 (LMO2). Directionally, SIRT2 inhibition sits upstream of LMO2-dependent leukemia suppression. LMO2 is a key oncogenic transcription factor in T-ALL, and its activity depends on deacetylation by SIRT2. Blocking SIRT2 reduces LMO2 function, impairing both the expansion of leukemic cells in culture and their ability to engraft in vivo. label: Sepsis-induced inflammatory lung injury
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Overall SIRT1 knockout mice are highly susceptible to sepsis-induced inflammatory lung injury due to activation of the proinflammatory transcription factor NF-kappaB. Directionally, SIRT1 loss sits upstream of heightened inflammatory lung damage. Because SIRT1 normally deacetylates and restrains NF-kappaB, its absence removes a key brake on inflammatory gene expression during sepsis. This unleashes an exaggerated inflammatory response that damages the lung, illustrating SIRT1's protective role in acute inflammatory injury. Restoring SIRT1 activity may therefore help dampen the excessive inflammation that complicates sepsis and contributes to acute respiratory failure.

label: Hyperoxia-induced acute lung injury
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT3 promotes the expression of manganese superoxide dismutase (MnSOD), and this regulation is crucial for the protective effect of SIRT3 on hyperoxia-induced acute lung injury. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of MnSOD-dependent lung protection. By maintaining MnSOD, SIRT3 supports mitochondrial antioxidant defense against the oxidative stress generated by high oxygen exposure. This shields lung tissue from the reactive oxygen species that drive injury during hyperoxia. The finding highlights SIRT3 as a mitochondrial antioxidant guardian in the lung and suggests that strategies to enhance SIRT3 or MnSOD could protect against oxygen-induced lung damage in clinical settings.

label: ARDS (acute respiratory distress syndrome)
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT6 regulates macrophage polarization to alleviate sepsis-induced acute respiratory distress syndrome via dual mechanisms that are both dependent on and independent of autophagy. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of anti-inflammatory macrophage phenotypes in lung injury. By steering macrophages away from proinflammatory states, SIRT6 dampens the excessive inflammatory response that drives ARDS, while its autophagy-related actions support cellular quality control. This coordinated regulation helps limit lung damage during sepsis.

label: SNHG10
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: The long noncoding RNA SNHG10 upregulates the tumor-suppressive sirtuin SIRT1 in non-small-cell lung cancer by sponging miR-543, relieving microRNA-mediated repression of SIRT1 expression. Directionally, SNHG10 acts upstream of SIRT1 abundance in the NSCLC ceRNA network. By sequestering miR-543, SNHG10 raises SIRT1 levels, and this upregulation underlies the lncRNA's tumor-suppressive activity in lung cancer. The finding highlights how noncoding RNAs can tune sirtuin expression and thereby influence the balance between tumor suppression and tumor promotion in specific cancer contexts.

label: NSCLC cell proliferation
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT1, when upregulated by the long noncoding RNA SNHG10, suppresses proliferation of non-small-cell lung cancer cells, acting as a tumor suppressor in this context. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of restrained NSCLC growth. This tumor-suppressive role of SIRT1 in lung cancer contrasts with the oncogenic functions SIRT1 displays in other settings, underscoring the strong context dependence of sirtuin biology. The finding implicates SIRT1 as a mediator of SNHG10's anti-proliferative effects and suggests that sustaining SIRT1 expression may limit NSCLC cell expansion.

label: circ_0001946
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: The circular RNA circ_0001946 upregulates SIRT1, and the resulting SIRT1 activity promotes cell growth in lung adenocarcinoma by activating the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. Directionally, circ_0001946 sits upstream of SIRT1 upregulation, which in turn drives oncogenic Wnt signaling. This represents a tumor-promoting axis in lung adenocarcinoma that is opposite to the tumor-suppressive SIRT1 effect mediated by SNHG10 in NSCLC, illustrating how different noncoding RNAs can direct SIRT1 toward opposing outcomes in the same tissue.

label: Wnt/β-catenin signaling in lung adenocarcinoma
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT1, upregulated by circ_0001946, promotes cell growth in lung adenocarcinoma by activating the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of β-catenin-driven proliferation in this lung cancer subtype. This oncogenic SIRT1 function contrasts with the tumor-suppressive anti-proliferative effect SIRT1 exerts in non-small-cell lung cancer when induced by SNHG10, demonstrating that SIRT1's role in lung cancer depends on the tumor subtype and the signaling context.

label: osteopontin-induced NF-κB p65 acetylation and EMT
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Overexpression of SIRT1 protects non-small-cell lung cancer cells against osteopontin-induced NF-κB p65 acetylation and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, thereby attenuating osteopontin-driven cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of dampened NF-κB signaling and EMT in response to the pro-metastatic cytokine osteopontin. By deacetylating p65 and restraining EMT, SIRT1 limits the invasive and proliferative program that osteopontin triggers in NSCLC cells, supporting a tumor-suppressive role in this context.

label: phosphoglycerate mutase (K100)
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT2 deacetylates the K100 residue of the glycolytic enzyme phosphoglycerate mutase and facilitates its activation, which results in enhanced NADPH production and accelerated tumor growth in non-small-cell lung cancer cells. Directionally, SIRT2 enzymatic modification of phosphoglycerate mutase sits upstream of increased glycolytic flux and anabolic support for tumor growth. This oncogenic action of SIRT2 in lung cancer contrasts with its tumor-suppressive deacetylation of AKR1C1 in the same disease, illustrating the context dependence of SIRT2's cancer-related functions.

label: SIRT1 silencing
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Silencing of SIRT1 enhances the cisplatin sensitivity of H1299/cisplatin non-small-cell lung cancer cells by suppressing autophagy. Directionally, SIRT1 loss sits upstream of reduced autophagic survival signaling and increased susceptibility to cisplatin. Because autophagy can protect cancer cells from chemotherapy-induced damage, its suppression re-sensitizes resistant NSCLC cells to cisplatin. This identifies SIRT1 inhibition as a potential strategy to overcome platinum resistance in lung cancer.

label: cisplatin sensitivity via autophagy suppression
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Silencing of SIRT1 enhances the cisplatin sensitivity of H1299/cisplatin non-small-cell lung cancer cells by suppressing autophagy. Directionally, SIRT1 loss sits upstream of reduced autophagic survival signaling and increased susceptibility to cisplatin. Because autophagy can protect cancer cells from chemotherapy-induced damage, its suppression re-sensitizes resistant NSCLC cells to cisplatin. This identifies SIRT1 inhibition as a potential strategy to overcome platinum resistance in lung cancer.

label: SIRT2 upregulation
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Upregulation of SIRT2 in non-small-cell lung cancer cells increases their sensitivity to cisplatin treatment, while the opposite modulation reduces responsiveness. Directionally, SIRT2 levels sit upstream of platinum chemosensitivity in NSCLC. Higher SIRT2 expression renders tumor cells more vulnerable to cisplatin-induced killing, suggesting that SIRT2 activity could be exploited to improve the efficacy of platinum-based therapy in lung cancer.

label: cisplatin sensitivity in NSCLC
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Upregulation of SIRT2 in non-small-cell lung cancer cells increases their sensitivity to cisplatin treatment, while the opposite modulation reduces responsiveness. Directionally, SIRT2 levels sit upstream of platinum chemosensitivity in NSCLC. Higher SIRT2 expression renders tumor cells more vulnerable to cisplatin-induced killing, suggesting that SIRT2 activity could be exploited to improve the efficacy of platinum-based therapy in lung cancer.

label: cisplatin resistance in lung cancer
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT3 reduces cisplatin resistance in lung cancer by modulating the FoxO3/Cdc10-dependent transcript 1 protein axis. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of restored platinum sensitivity in drug-resistant lung cancer cells. By acting through the FoxO3/CDT1 pathway, SIRT3 counteracts the survival adaptations that underlie cisplatin resistance, making SIRT3 activation a candidate strategy to re-sensitize resistant lung tumors to platinum-based chemotherapy.

label: Serum SIRT3
community_name: lung cancer patients from healthy individuals
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Serum SIRT3 distinguishes lung cancer patients from healthy individuals with an area under the curve of 0.918, an optimal cutoff value of 3.12, a sensitivity of 86.4%, and a specificity of 94%. Directionally, serum SIRT3 levels serve as a diagnostic biomarker for lung cancer. The high accuracy of SIRT3 in discriminating cancer patients supports its use as a blood-based marker for lung cancer screening or early detection, complementing SIRT expression differences observed between tumor and non-tumor lung tissue.

label: bile acid metabolism orchestration
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT5 prevents tumor immune evasion and suppresses the development of hepatocellular carcinoma by orchestrating bile acid metabolism. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of anti-tumor immunity and restrained HCC growth. By shaping the bile acid milieu, SIRT5 influences the immune microenvironment of the liver tumor, reducing the ability of HCC to evade immune destruction. This tumor-suppressive metabolic function contrasts with SIRT5's glycolysis-reprogramming role that can promote HCC growth, reflecting SIRT5's context-dependent effects in liver cancer.

label: HCC growth and metastasis via glycolysis reprogramming
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Activation of mitochondrial SIRT5 promotes the growth and metastasis of hepatocellular carcinoma cells via glucose metabolism reprogramming from oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of the glycolytic switch that fuels liver cancer progression. By favoring glycolysis, SIRT5 supplies the biosynthetic and bioenergetic demands of rapidly growing HCC cells, supporting tumor aggressiveness. This oncogenic role is opposed by SIRT5's bile-acid-metabolism-mediated suppression of HCC, underscoring the dual, context-dependent functions of SIRT5 in liver cancer.

label: SIRT1 and SIRT6
community_name: hnRNP A1 to suppress glycolysis and growth in HCC
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT1 and SIRT6 deacetylate the RNA-binding protein hnRNP A1 to suppress glycolysis and growth in hepatocellular carcinoma. Directionally, SIRT1 and SIRT6 sit upstream of hnRNP A1 deacetylation, which curtails glycolytic gene expression and tumor growth. By restraining the glycolytic program through hnRNP A1, these nuclear sirtuins act as metabolic tumor suppressors in HCC, opposing the aerobic glycolysis that supports cancer cell proliferation.

label: hnRNP A1 to suppress glycolysis and growth in HCC
community_name: hnRNP A1 to suppress glycolysis and growth in HCC
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT1 and SIRT6 deacetylate the RNA-binding protein hnRNP A1 to suppress glycolysis and growth in hepatocellular carcinoma. Directionally, SIRT1 and SIRT6 sit upstream of hnRNP A1 deacetylation, which curtails glycolytic gene expression and tumor growth. By restraining the glycolytic program through hnRNP A1, these nuclear sirtuins act as metabolic tumor suppressors in HCC, opposing the aerobic glycolysis that supports cancer cell proliferation.

label: stabilized by USP48
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT6, stabilized by the deubiquitinase USP48, attenuates glycolysis in hepatocellular carcinoma and impedes metabolic reprogramming, thereby hampering HCC malignancy. Directionally, USP48-dependent stabilization of SIRT6 sits upstream of suppressed glycolytic metabolism and reduced tumor aggressiveness. By maintaining SIRT6 protein levels, USP48 sustains SIRT6-mediated repression of glycolysis, preventing the metabolic shift that fuels liver cancer growth. This identifies the USP48-SIRT6 axis as a potential therapeutic node in HCC.

label: colorectal cancer via glutamine metabolism and apoptosis
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT1 affects colorectal cancer in a dose-dependent manner by regulating glutamine metabolism and apoptotic pathways. Heterozygous deletion of SIRT1 induces c-Myc expression, enhancing glutamine metabolism, proliferation, autophagy, and cancer formation, whereas homozygous deletion triggers apoptosis, increases cell death, diminishes autophagy, and reduces cancer formation. Directionally, SIRT1 expression level sits upstream of opposing metabolic and survival outcomes in CRC, explaining the dual roles of SIRT1 in colorectal tumorigenesis.

label: SOD2 and PGC-1α regulation
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: Overexpression of SIRT3 improves the resistance of colorectal cancer cells to anticancer drugs through regulation of superoxide dismutase 2 and PGC-1α. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of SOD2- and PGC-1α-dependent protective responses in CRC. By enhancing antioxidant and mitochondrial programs, SIRT3 reduces the vulnerability of CRC cells to chemotherapeutic agents, contributing to drug resistance. This resistance-promoting role should be weighed when considering SIRT3-targeted cancer therapy.

label: 5-fluorouracil by inhibiting the cell cycle
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT4 increases the sensitivity of colorectal cancer cells to the chemotherapeutic drug 5-fluorouracil by inhibiting the cell cycle. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of cell-cycle arrest, which primes CRC cells for 5-fluorouracil-induced killing. By restraining proliferation, SIRT4 enhances the cytotoxic effect of the drug, suggesting that SIRT4 expression status could predict or improve responses to 5-fluorouracil-based therapy in colorectal cancer.

label: SIRT1 upregulation
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: FoxQ1-mediated SIRT1 upregulation augments the expression and nuclear translocation of β-catenin and benefits CRC-related intestinal pathological bacteria, thereby enhancing the radioresistance of colorectal cancer cells. Directionally, SIRT1 upregulation sits upstream of β-catenin-driven survival and radiation resistance in CRC. By promoting β-catenin signaling, SIRT1 helps colorectal cancer cells survive ionizing radiation, which has implications for combining SIRT1 inhibition with radiotherapy to improve treatment outcomes.

label: CRC radioresistance via β-catenin
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: FoxQ1-mediated SIRT1 upregulation augments the expression and nuclear translocation of β-catenin and benefits CRC-related intestinal pathological bacteria, thereby enhancing the radioresistance of colorectal cancer cells. Directionally, SIRT1 upregulation sits upstream of β-catenin-driven survival and radiation resistance in CRC. By promoting β-catenin signaling, SIRT1 helps colorectal cancer cells survive ionizing radiation, which has implications for combining SIRT1 inhibition with radiotherapy to improve treatment outcomes.

label: SIRT1 depletion
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT1 depletion promotes gastric cancer progression through activation of the STAT3/MMP-13 signaling pathway. Directionally, SIRT1 loss sits upstream of STAT3- and MMP-13-driven tumor progression in gastric cancer. Because SIRT1 normally restrains this pathway, its depletion unleashes STAT3 activation and MMP-13 expression, accelerating GC growth and invasion. This positions SIRT1 as a tumor suppressor in gastric cancer and identifies STAT3/MMP-13 signaling as a downstream mediator of SIRT1's protective effect.

label: gastric cancer progression via STAT3/MMP-13
source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
description: SIRT1 depletion promotes gastric cancer progression through activation of the STAT3/MMP-13 signaling pathway.
