The non-peptide substrates broaden the assay chemistry available for studying SIRT1 and its modulators.

label: JGB1741
source_file: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md
description: JGB1741 is a small-molecule SIRT1 inhibitor developed on the sirtinol structure and identified with other sirtinol analogues through sirtuin fluorimetric activity assays. As a sirtinol derivative, it is expected to block SIRT1 deacetylase activity, promoting hyperacetylation of substrates such as p53. Directionally, JGB1741 engages the SIRT1 catalytic site to inhibit deacetylation. Its derivation from the sirtinol scaffold places it within the beta-naphthol family of sirtuin inhibitors, whose anticancer activities derive substantially from p53 reactivation.

label: Tubulin deacetylase
source_file: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md
description: SIRT2 is the predominantly cytoplasmic sirtuin that functions as a tubulin deacetylase, removing acetyl groups from alpha-tubulin to regulate microtubule dynamics and mitotic fidelity. Because it deacetylates tubulin and other mitotic regulators, SIRT2 loss impairs the control that normally keeps Aurora-A and Aurora-B in check during division, leading to aneuploidy and mitotic cell death. Directionally, SIRT2's tubulin deacetylase activity is an upstream determinant of normal chromosome segregation, linking sirtuin biology to mitotic stability and tumor suppression.

label: ETS transcription factor
source_file: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md
description: ELK4 (SAP-1) belongs to the ETS-domain ternary complex factor (TCF) subfamily of transcription factors, defined by a conserved ETS DNA-binding domain. Within sirtuin biology, ELK4 is notable for interacting with SIRT7 and stabilizing the deacetylase at target gene promoters, where SIRT7 deacetylates lysine 18 of histone H3 and represses tumor suppressor genes. Directionally, ELK4's identity as an ETS factor underlies its promoter-targeting function. This links the ETS transcription factor family to the pro-oncogenic SIRT7-H3K18ac axis in cancer.

label: ELK1
source_file: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md
description: ELK1 is the founding member of the ternary complex factor subfamily of ETS-domain transcription factors, alongside ELK3 and ELK4 (SAP-1), and is a major nuclear target of the RAS-MAPK/ERK cascade that controls immediate-early gene expression. In the context of sirtuin biology it serves as the canonical reference for the ETS-TCF family whose member ELK4 stabilizes SIRT7 at target promoters. Directionally, ELK1's ETS DNA-binding domain and SRF-coupling architecture are shared by the TCF family, informing how ELK4 anchors SIRT7 to chromatin for H3K18 deacetylation.

label: ETS
source_file: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md
description: ETS is a large family of eukaryotic transcription factors sharing a conserved winged helix-turn-helix DNA-binding ETS domain that recognizes purine-rich GGAA/T core motifs and regulates proliferation, differentiation, and oncogenesis. The ETS-family member ELK4 plays a central role in sirtuin biology by stabilizing SIRT7 at target gene promoters, enabling H3K18 deacetylation and repression of tumor suppressor genes. Directionally, the ETS family provides the DNA-binding and promoter-targeting mechanisms that members such as ELK4 use to recruit chromatin-modifying enzymes such as SIRT7.

label: Transcription factor family
source_file: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md
description: ETS is a large family of eukaryotic transcription factors sharing a conserved winged helix-turn-helix DNA-binding ETS domain that recognizes purine-rich GGAA/T core motifs and regulates proliferation, differentiation, and oncogenesis. The ETS-family member ELK4 plays a central role in sirtuin biology by stabilizing SIRT7 at target gene promoters, enabling H3K18 deacetylation and repression of tumor suppressor genes. Directionally, the ETS family provides the DNA-binding and promoter-targeting mechanisms that members such as ELK4 use to recruit chromatin-modifying enzymes such as SIRT7.

label: Adenosine-binding site with kinases
source_file: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md
description: Sirtuins and protein kinases both contain an adenosine-binding pocket in their catalytic machinery, an overlap that allowed screening of known kinase inhibitors against SIRT2. This shared scaffold led to the discovery that bisindolylmaleimides such as Ro31-8220 and indolinones such as GW5074 inhibit SIRT1 and SIRT2 in the low micromolar range. Directionally, the shared adenosine site is the molecular basis for cross-inhibition between kinase inhibitors and sirtuins, but it also means these compounds retain kinase activity, complicating the attribution of cellular effects to sirtuin inhibition alone.

label: Polyphenol STAC
source_file: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md
description: Butein is a chalcone polyphenol that belongs to the first generation of natural sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs), reported to activate SIRT1 together with resveratrol, piceatannol, quercetin, and myricetin. These polyphenolic activators established the concept of pharmacological SIRT1 activation and served as the basis for later, more potent synthetic STACs such as SRT1460, SRT1720, and SRT2183. Directionally, butein's identification as a polyphenol STAC initiated the activator chemistry that progressed to synthetic scaffolds, though the direct activation mechanism remains controversial due to fluorescent-substrate artifacts.

label: Synthetic STAC
source_file: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md
description: SRT1460 is a second-generation synthetic sirtuin-activating compound (STAC) of the imidazothiazole class, developed with SRT1720 and SRT2183 as chemically diverse and more potent activators than the initial polyphenolic STACs. These compounds were reported to have anticancer activity, but their mechanism is controversial: activation could frequently only be demonstrated with fluorescently tagged substrates, and in vivo effects may be indirect (e.g., via the cAMP-Epac1-AMPK pathway) rather than direct SIRT1 binding. Directionally, SRT1460 belongs to the synthetic STAC class whose biology underlies the ongoing debate about STAC-mediated SIRT1 activation.

label: Kinase-inhibitor scaffold
source_file: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md
description: Ro31-8220 is a bisindolylmaleimide compound originally developed as a protein kinase C inhibitor; its adenosine-binding scaffold allowed it to be repurposed as an inhibitor of SIRT1 and SIRT2 in the low micromolar range. It belongs to the kinase-inhibitor scaffolds identified by screening known kinase inhibitors against sirtuins, sharing this property with the indolinone GW5074. Directionally, Ro31-8220's identity as a kinase-inhibitor scaffold underlies its cross-reactivity with sirtuins through the shared adenosine-binding site. Because it retains potent kinase activity, cellular effects cannot be attributed solely to sirtuin inhibition.

label: SIRT1-selective inhibitor
source_file: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md
description: NF675 is a suramin-derived small molecule that is the most potent and selective compound in its scaffold series, showing a 20-fold selectivity ratio for SIRT1 over SIRT2. It was obtained through optimization of the suramin scaffold, which itself is a nanomolar inhibitor of SIRT1/SIRT2. Directionally, NF675's identity as a suramin-derived, SIRT1-selective inhibitor illustrates scaffold engineering for isoform selectivity within the sirtuin inhibitor field. Its modest drug-likeness, stemming from high molecular weight and anionic character, limits therapeutic application despite good potency and selectivity.

label: Kinase-inhibitor scaffolds
source_file: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md
description: SIRT2 is inhibited by kinase-inhibitor scaffolds identified by screening known kinase inhibitors against the enzyme on the rationale that sirtuins and protein kinases share an adenosine-binding site. The bisindolylmaleimide Ro31-8220 and the indolinone GW5074 showed SIRT1/SIRT2 inhibitory properties in the low micromolar range, alongside the general Kinase enzyme family that shares the adenosine pocket. Directionally, the shared adenosine-binding site of SIRT2 and protein kinases underlies this cross-inhibition. Because these scaffolds retain kinase activity, their cellular effects reflect a combination of kinase and sirtuin blockade.

label: Kinase
source_file: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md
description: Protein kinases share an adenosine-binding site with sirtuins such as SIRT2, an overlap exploited by screening known kinase inhibitors against sirtuins as a drug-discovery strategy. This shared adenosine pocket allows scaffolds like the bisindolylmaleimide Ro31-8220 and the indolinone GW5074 to engage both families, inhibiting SIRT1 and SIRT2 in the low micromolar range while retaining kinase activity. Directionally, the enzyme superfamily of Kinase proteins and sirtuin deacetylases both rely on an adenosine-binding pocket, explaining the cross-reactivity between kinase-inhibitor scaffolds and sirtuins. This structural convergence frames interpretation of kinase-inhibitor effects in sirtuin biology.

label: Adenosine-binding site with SIRT2
source_file: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md
description: Protein kinases share an adenosine-binding site with sirtuins such as SIRT2, an overlap exploited by screening known kinase inhibitors against sirtuins as a drug-discovery strategy. This shared adenosine pocket allows scaffolds like the bisindolylmaleimide Ro31-8220 and the indolinone GW5074 to engage both families, inhibiting SIRT1 and SIRT2 in the low micromolar range while retaining kinase activity. This structural convergence frames interpretation of kinase-inhibitor effects in sirtuin biology.

label: Curcumin
source_file: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process
description: The review highlights natural compounds, especially curcumin, as candidates to activate or otherwise regulate sirtuins, positioning them as low-toxicity anti-ageing interventions. Directionally, curcumin is upstream as a putative sirtuin modulator. A caveat is that the review frames this as a hope/area of active research rather than established clinical efficacy, and sirtuin activation by curcumin remains less mechanistically defined than for resveratrol.

label: miR-34a
source_file: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process
description: The 3'UTR of the SIRT1 transcript contains a miR-34a-responsive element; active miR-34a represses SIRT1 translation. Directionally, miR-34a sits upstream to lower SIRT1 protein. Because SIRT1 deacetylates and inhibits p53, this repression is part of a negative feedback loop that helps explain the drop in SIRT1 observed during senescence.

label: Mus musculus
source_file: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process
description: P66shc knockout mice live about 30% longer than wild-type controls and show enhanced resistance to oxidative stress and age-related pathologies, indicating P66shc is a negative regulator of longevity. Directionally, loss of P66shc extends lifespan. This makes P66shc an attractive node, with SIRT1 as an upstream suppressor, for longevity interventions.

label: SOD1
source_file: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process
description: SIRT5 desuccinylates superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1), increasing its activity and thereby enhancing cytosolic antioxidant defense. Directionally, SIRT5 enzymatically activates SOD1. This extends sirtuin control of antioxidant enzymes beyond SIRT3's activation of mitochondrial MnSOD/IDH2.

label: Histone H3
source_file: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process
description: SIRT7 deacetylates histone H3 at K18 (and H2A/H2B), an activity associated with repression of tumor-suppressor genes; SIRT7 thereby helps sustain the cancer phenotype without driving transformation. Directionally, SIRT7 enzymatically remodels chromatin to favor oncogenic transcription. This links nucleolar SIRT7 to tumor biology.

label: Oocyte
source_file: _document_ - Sirtuins, a promising target in slowing down the ageing process
description: In mouse oocytes aged in vivo or in vitro, expression of SIRT1, SIRT2 and SIRT3 is dramatically reduced; prolonged expression of these sirtuins reduces postovulatory oocyte ageing. Directionally, loss of SIRT3 (with SIRT1/2) accompanies oocyte ageing. SIRT1 and SIRT3 act as redox sensors in oocytes, implicating them in female fertility and age-related reproductive decline.

label: IDH2
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: SIRT3 deacetylates and activates mitochondrial isocitrate dehydrogenase 2 (IDH2) at Lys413 (Yu 2012 PMID 22416140), boosting NADPH biosynthesis. Under caloric restriction and dietary restriction, SIRT3-mediated IDH2 deacetylation elevates NADPH, regenerating glutathione and lowering mitochondrial ROS; loss of SIRT3 abolishes this DR-dependent antioxidant response and exacerbates metabolic disease. The resulting NADPH fuels antioxidant regeneration and prevents electron transport chain overload, curbing ROS and potentiating mitochondrial antioxidant capacity. This SIRT3-IDH2-NADPH axis couples nutrient sensing to mitochondrial redox homeostasis and preserves cochlear hair cells under caloric restriction.

label: Succinate Dehydrogenase
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: SIRT3 regulates succinate dehydrogenase (SDH, complex II), described as a critical acetylation node within the mitochondrial matrix that mediates crosstalk between metabolic flux control and mitochondrial energy transduction systems. Through modulation of SDH enzymatic activity, SIRT3 fine-tunes substrate utilization efficiency while maintaining electron transfer chain synchronization, preserving metabolic homeostasis across the TCA cycle and oxidative phosphorylation interface.

label: Histone Crotonylation eraser activity
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: Beyond canonical deacetylase activity, SIRT3 possesses substantial lysine decrotonylase capacity, selectively removing crotonyl groups from specific histone substrates. This dynamic regulation of histone crotonylation adds a new dimension to SIRT3's epigenetic repertoire, modulating gene expression plasticity under both homeostatic and stress conditions. The review positions this decrotonylase activity alongside SIRT3's roles in heterochromatin maintenance and double-strand break repair as a nuclear epigenetic function of the mitochondrial deacetylase.

label: H3K27 crotonylation at ETS1 loci
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: SIRT3 decreases H3K27 crotonylation at metastasis-associated loci such as the ETS1 promoter, effectively constraining neoplastic dissemination. Mechanistically, the long noncoding RNA LINC00922 can decoy SIRT3 away from the ETS1 promoter, upregulating local H3K27 crotonylation and driving colorectal cancer metastasis. This places SIRT3's lysine decrotonylase activity at the interface of histone acylation state and oncogenic transcription.

label: Non-homologous End Joining
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: SIRT3 facilitates DNA double-strand break repair by enhancing the recruitment of 53BP1, thereby promoting the efficiency of non-homologous end joining (NHEJ). It also promotes H3K56 deacetylation to enhance NHEJ fidelity, and interacts with critical DNA repair proteins such as PARP1, Ku70/80, XRCC1, and DNA ligase 4 to repair mitochondrial and genomic DNA damage. This nuclear DNA-repair program complements SIRT3's mitochondrial antioxidant function in maintaining genomic stability and preventing cellular senescence (Fig. 1B).

label: GSK3beta at Lys15
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: SIRT3 mediates its anti-fibrotic effect through targeted deacetylation of glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta (GSK3beta) at Lys15, effectively preventing Smad3 transcriptional complex formation and subsequent fibrogenic programming. Genetic deletion of SIRT3 increases GSK3beta acetylation and hyperactivates TGF-beta signaling, culminating in enhanced transcription of ECM-related genes. This mechanism operates across peritoneal, cardiac, pulmonary, and hepatic fibrosis models.

label: FOS/AP-1 and STAT3/NFATc2 signaling
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: In cardiomyocytes, SIRT3 attenuates fibrosis by inhibiting the FOS/AP-1 and STAT3/NFATc2 signaling pathways, complementing its GSK3beta Lys15 deacetylation that blocks Smad3 complexes. Together these transcriptional suppressions reduce ECM gene expression and pathological cardiac remodeling, establishing SIRT3 as a master anti-fibrotic node acting on multiple pro-fibrotic pathways simultaneously.

label: MIP-2 expression
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: SIRT3 activation consistently correlates with reduced expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNF-alpha, IL-6, and MIP-2 (CXCL2), as well as diminished polymorphonuclear leukocyte infiltration in various preclinical models. These anti-inflammatory effects are sustained even after discontinuation of dietary interventions, indicating durable transcriptional reprogramming via NF-kappaB and STAT3 suppression.

label: AMPK/mTOR autophagy axis
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: SIRT3 regulates autophagic flux through the AMPK/mTOR and FOXO3a pathways, facilitating mitochondrial quality control via AMPK/ULK1 phosphorylation while antagonizing mTOR-mediated autophagic repression. Genetic ablation of SIRT3 impairs autophagic signaling with paradoxical activation of glutathione peroxidase 4 activity that suppresses autophagy initiation. A positive feedback loop exists in which autophagy induces SIRT3 via FOXO3a, restoring hematopoietic stem cell repopulation through enhanced clearance of damaged mitochondria.

label: PINK1/Parkin mitophagy
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: SIRT3 promotes PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy, which reduces mitochondrial ROS and restores hematopoietic stem cell repopulation efficiency through lysosomal clearance of damaged mitochondria. In the aging brain, the PINK1/Parkin pathway clears damaged mitochondria in Alzheimer's disease models, mitigating amyloidogenesis and tau pathology, and in osteoarthritis models SIRT3 promotes mitophagy to maintain chondrocyte health. Mitophagy is thus a core mitochondrial quality-control arm of SIRT3's cytoprotective program.

label: p53 at Lys320
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: In Alzheimer's disease, SIRT3 enhances mitochondrial bioenergetics disrupted by amyloid-beta toxicity, partially through deacetylation of mitochondrial p53 at Lys320, a modification crucial for maintaining energy homeostasis and neuronal survival. SIRT3 mRNA expression declines progressively in AD clinical specimens and rodent models, and SIRT3 levels inversely associate with tau protein deposition, supporting SIRT3 as a mitochondrial checkpoint and candidate biomarker in AD.

label: PGC-1alpha transcriptional programs
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: SIRT3 governs mitochondrial biogenesis by activating PGC-1alpha transcriptional programs, which maintain mitochondrial DNA integrity in Parkinson's disease models, and promotes PGC-1alpha-dependent transcription to sustain redox homeostasis and neuronal energy metabolism in Huntington's disease. In diabetic nephropathy, the PGC-1alpha/SIRT3 axis activated by meteorin-like protein stimulates AMPK at Thr172 and UCP1-dependent proton leak, preserving mitochondrial ultrastructure.

label: Alpha-synuclein aggregates
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: Beyond mitochondrial homeostasis, SIRT3 contributes to the clearance of misfolded alpha-synuclein aggregates, a pathological hallmark of Parkinson's disease, and mitigates neuroinflammation by suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation. These converging actions highlight the translational potential of targeting SIRT3 in PD therapy, though whether SIRT3 alterations precede dopaminergic neurodegeneration remains unclear.

label: DRP1/Fis1 mitochondrial fission
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: In Huntington's disease, SIRT3 maintains mitochondrial dynamics by suppressing fission regulators such as Fis1 and Drp1, preserving mitochondrial morphology and promoting efficient axonal transport. In Drosophila HD models, transgenic expression of the SIRT3 ortholog dSirt2 significantly attenuates neuropil degeneration and prolongs organismal longevity, reinforcing conserved neuroprotective functions of SIRT3 across species.

label: VDAC1/GRP75/IP3R complex
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: Chronic hyperglycemia suppresses SIRT3 expression in the hippocampus, contributing to cognitive deficits through mitochondrial Ca2+ overload and neuronal apoptosis. SIRT3 overexpression mitigates neuronal injury by inhibiting the VDAC1/GRP75/IP3R complex, thereby reducing mitochondria-associated endoplasmic reticulum membrane (MAM) formation and protecting neurons from metabolic stress-induced apoptosis in diabetic encephalopathy.

label: Irisin osteoprotection
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: In diabetic periodontitis models, irisin exerts antioxidative and osteoprotective effects that are strictly dependent on SIRT3: lentivirus-mediated SIRT3 silencing abolishes irisin's osteoprotective efficacy against osteoclastic alveolar bone resorption and ROS overproduction. SIRT3 is therefore the obligatory signaling node for irisin-mediated redox homeostasis and bone preservation in the diabetic periodontium.

label: chemoresistance in CLL
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: In chronic lymphocytic leukemia, SIRT3 enables metabolic adaptation that confers chemoresistance via ROS buffering. This tumor-supportive role contrasts with SIRT3's tumor-suppressive actions in other contexts (Warburg suppression via HIF-1alpha destabilization, OGG1-mediated DNA repair, H3K56 deacetylation for NHEJ fidelity), exemplifying the dualistic, context-dependent behavior of SIRT3 in cancer biology.

label: HIF-1alpha
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: SIRT3 destabilizes hypoxia-inducible factor 1alpha (HIF-1alpha), thereby attenuating the Warburg effect, a characteristic metabolic adaptation of rapidly proliferating tumors. Transcriptomic profiling in castration-resistant prostate cancer reveals that SIRT3 also suppresses aconitase 2 activation, disrupting glutamine-driven lipogenesis, supporting SIRT3's predominantly tumor-suppressive metabolic role in early oncogenic transformation.

label: Acute Kidney Injury
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: SIRT3 is a pivotal coordinator of renal bioenergetics maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis, enhancing antioxidant defenses, and modulating ECM dynamics; its expression is reduced across nephropathies and negatively correlated with histological injury severity. SIRT3 overexpression alleviates AKI and CKD progression in multiple preclinical models, via Nrf2 pathway upregulation, NF-kappaB suppression through IkappaBalpha stabilization, and inhibition of NLRP3 inflammasome activation.

label: SENP1
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: Pharmacological AMPK activation using metformin promotes SENP1-mediated deSUMOylation of SIRT3, enhancing its mitochondrial localization and functional activity, which in turn reduces tubular cell apoptosis under metabolic stress in AKI models. The AMPK/SENP1/SIRT3 axis also governs mitochondrial apoptosis via SOD2 deacetylation, mitigating oxidative stress-induced apoptosis across renal and other tissues.

label: Beta-catenin
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: SIRT3 deacetylates beta-catenin, a pivotal transcriptional coactivator in fibroblast activation, facilitating the expression of MMP-7 and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1, two mediators implicated in ECM remodeling via EMT induction. In CKD, this complements SIRT3's FOXO3a-dependent EMT suppression. Independently, poricoic acid A upregulates SIRT3 and promotes beta-catenin K49 deacetylation to attenuate renal fibroblast activation and interstitial fibrosis.

label: soluble epoxide hydrolase
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: A regulatory axis exists in which soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH) modulates SIRT3 turnover via proteolytic degradation, with sEH deficiency preserving SIRT3 bioavailability to fulfill bioenergetic demands and impede renal vascular calcification progression. sEH inhibition or deficiency therefore acts as an indirect SIRT3-stabilizing strategy in advanced CKD-associated vascular calcification.

label: caloric restriction protection in cochlea
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: Caloric restriction alleviates age-related hearing loss by reducing oxidative damage in cochlear cells, but this protective effect is abolished in SIRT3-deficient mice, highlighting SIRT3's indispensable role in CR-induced auditory resilience. Mechanistically, SIRT3 enhances IDH2 activity under CR, boosting mitochondrial NADPH production and ROS clearance, preserving cochlear hair cell integrity and delaying hearing loss progression.

label: miR-494-3p
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: Oxidative stress-induced upregulation of microRNA-494-3p leads to decreased SIRT3 levels, establishing a feedback loop that further exacerbates senescence. In COPD, miR-494-3p directly targets SIRT3 in small airway epithelial cells, leading to SIRT3 downregulation, increased p27 expression, and accelerated cellular senescence contributing to COPD pathophysiology.

label: Honokiol effects
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: Honokiol (HKL), a bisphenolic lignan from Magnolia officinalis, upregulates SIRT3 while augmenting its enzymatic activity, and shRNA-induced SIRT3 knockdown significantly attenuates HKL's cytoprotective effects on mitochondrial biogenesis, OXPHOS capacity, and bioenergetic output. HKL protects the brain from ischemia-reperfusion injury, ameliorates intracerebral hemorrhage-induced apoptosis and mitochondrial fission, and inhibits ferroptosis, all via SIRT3 activation.

label: 2-APQC
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: 2-APQC (2-acetylphenolquinone congener) is a novel pharmacological agonist of SIRT3 that significantly alleviates isoproterenol-induced pathological cardiac hypertrophy and fibrotic progression, with efficacy completely lost in SIRT3-knockout models and markedly attenuated by the SIRT3 inhibitor nicotinamide, confirming SIRT3 as its primary molecular target. Mechanistically it suppresses AKT/mTOR/p70S6K and JNK/TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling.

label: Liquiritigenin
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: The licorice-derived compound liquiritigenin induces Nrf2 translocation, thereby potentiating SIRT3 activity and facilitating mitochondrial biogenesis while simultaneously suppressing apoptosis in acute kidney injury models. This dual action mitigates oxidative stress injury and cell death, highlighting liquiritigenin's therapeutic value in AKI and related redox-driven pathologies.

label: Poricoic acid A
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: Poria cocos-derived poricoic acid A upregulates SIRT3 and promotes beta-catenin K49 deacetylation, effectively attenuating renal fibroblast activation and renal interstitial fibrosis in vivo and in vitro. The compound thereby exemplifies phytochemical engagement of the SIRT3-beta-catenin axis as a disease-modifying strategy for tubulointerstitial fibrosis in chronic kidney disease.

label: Stanniocalcin-1
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: Stanniocalcin-1, a glycoprotein hormone, orchestrates a hormetic AMPK/SIRT3 axis that mitigates oxidative stress and apoptosis, and inhibits BNIP3 expression through the AMPK/SIRT3 pathway to ameliorate renal injury in diabetic murine models. The hormetic description reflects STC1's pattern of effect: mild mitochondrial stress engages AMPK, supporting SIRT3-dependent mitochondrial quality control.

label: Intermedin
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: Intermedin (adrenomedullin 2) enhances mitochondrial bioenergetic capacity via AMPK/SIRT3-mediated cristae remodeling in vascular calcification models. Because vascular calcification, a hallmark of advanced CKD, is driven by mitochondrial dysfunction and osteogenic transdifferentiation of vascular smooth muscle cells, intermedin's SIRT3-dependent improvement of cristae architecture opposes the calcific phenotype.

label: Meteorin-like protein
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: Meteorin-like protein activates the PGC-1alpha/SIRT3 axis, which stimulates AMPK at Thr172 and increases UCP1-dependent proton leak, thereby preserving mitochondrial ultrastructural integrity and regulating energy metabolism, particularly in diabetic nephropathy. The cascade links an exercise-induced myokine to mitochondrial quality control through the PGC-1alpha/SIRT3/AMPK/UCP1 pathway.

label: Ac2-26
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: The annexin A1-derived tripeptide Ac2-26 transcriptionally upregulates SIRT3, concurrently reducing oxidative damage while promoting mitochondrial biogenesis and mitophagy. In models of ischemic kidney injury, Ac2-26 increases SIRT3 and augments mitochondrial function to limit injury, linking pro-resolving inflammation biology to mitochondrial quality control.

label: AGO2/cytochrome b axis
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: In diabetic cardiomyopathy, SIRT3 activation improves mitochondrial respiratory capacity and suppresses oxidative stress primarily through modulation of the AGO2/cytochrome b (CYTB) signaling pathway, uncoupling excessive glucose levels from electron transport chain dysfunction. SIRT3 downregulation leads to breakdown of this axis, resulting in impaired ETC activity and accelerated DCM progression.

label: Withaferin A anti-fibrotic effect
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: In hepatic fibrosis models, SIRT3 has been implicated in mediating the anti-fibrotic effects of withaferin A, an effect that is abolished in SIRT3-knockout mice. This finding reinforces SIRT3's role as an indispensable molecular effector of pharmacological anti-fibrotic agents, consistent with its central suppressive function across hepatic, pulmonary, cardiac, and renal fibrosis models.

label: TFAM at Lys154
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: Melatonin's orchestration of sequential mitophagy processes depends on SIRT3-mediated deacetylation of TFAM at Lys154, the pivotal molecular switch promoting mitophagic flux. In vascular calcification, SIRT3 also deacetylates proteins within the PGC-1alpha/TFAM pathway, promoting mitochondrial biogenesis while attenuating vascular smooth muscle cell calcification.

label: Vascular Calcification
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: SIRT3 counteracts vascular calcification via mitochondrial function preservation and oxidative stress mitigation, deacetylating proteins in the PGC-1alpha/TFAM pathway to promote mitochondrial biogenesis while attenuating vascular smooth muscle cell calcification. AMPK/SIRT3 axis activation attenuated mineralization through mitochondrial functional restoration, and sEH deficiency preserves SIRT3 bioavailability to impede VC progression.

label: OPA1 deacetylation
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: SIRT3 contributes to maintaining mitochondrial morphology through optic atrophy 1 (OPA1) deacetylation, maintaining cristae structure and preventing inflammasome activation in cardiac fibroblasts. Matrine engages protective effects against cisplatin-induced AKI by modulating mitochondrial membrane dynamics through the SIRT3/OPA1 pathway, combining antioxidant and anti-inflammatory mechanisms to preserve renal function.

label: PDH E1alpha
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: SIRT3 regulates pyruvate dehydrogenase E1alpha deacetylation, bridging glycolysis and the TCA cycle in tubular epithelial cells during the progression of renal fibrosis. Honokiol-activated SIRT3 upregulates mitochondrial GPX4 and decreases its acetylation, inhibiting neuronal ferroptosis and mitigating perioperative neurocognitive disorders, illustrating SIRT3's metabolic-enzyme control across glycolysis-TCA coupling.

label: SUMOylation
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: Epigenetic modifications can impair SIRT3 function, such as through SUMOylation-mediated inhibition, exacerbating mitochondrial dysfunction and cartilage degeneration in osteoarthritis. SENP1-mediated deSUMOylation of SIRT3 (promoted by AMPK activation with metformin) enhances its mitochondrial localization and functional activity, reducing tubular cell apoptosis under metabolic stress.

label: Chondrocytes
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: In osteoarthritis, SIRT3 preserves mitochondrial integrity by deacetylating cytochrome c oxidase subunit 4 isoform 2, and its deletion correlates with OA exacerbation in animal and human models. SIRT3 promotes mitophagy via the PINK1/Parkin axis, maintains mitochondrial health by regulating FOXO3a hyperacetylation, inhibits chondrocyte apoptosis through PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling, facilitates mitochondrial fusion for mtDNA complementation, and enhances cartilage resilience.

label: Intervertebral Disc Degeneration
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: SIRT3 expression is significantly reduced in degenerated intervertebral discs, and its knockdown further exacerbates deterioration of nucleus pulposus cells under oxidative stress. Lactate downregulates SIRT3, increasing ACSL4 lactylation and promoting ferroptosis, while SIRT3 overexpression alleviates IDD severity in vivo, and hydrogel microspheres upregulating both SIRT3 and SOD2 maintain NPC viability.

label: healthspan outcomes
source_file: _document_ - Roles of SIRT3 in aging and aging-related diseases.md
description: The conclusion of the review positions SIRT3 as a pleiotropic regulatory hub in cellular senescence and geropathology, a critical determinant across cardiovascular diseases, neurodegenerative conditions, metabolic syndrome, cancer, kidney diseases, COPD, and degenerative spine and joint diseases. It highlights SIRT3's regulation of the mitochondrial acetylome and its profound effect on chromatin remodeling and genome stability, making SIRT3 agonism a promising translational strategy in geroscience.

label: Histone Crotonylation
description: Histone crotonylation (Kcr) is deposited from crotonyl-CoA and generally marks active transcription. SIRT3 possesses substantial lysine decrotonylase capacity, selectively removing crotonyl groups from specific histone substrates, and decreases H3K27 crotonylation at metastasis-associated loci such as ETS1 to constrain neoplastic dissemination.

label: ETS1
description: SIRT3 decreases H3K27 crotonylation at the ETS1 promoter, constraining neoplastic dissemination. The lncRNA LINC00922 decoys SIRT3 from the ETS1 promoter, upregulating H3K27 crotonylation and driving colorectal cancer metastasis (Liao et al., Mol Cancer 2023).

label: SIRT3 via H3K27 crotonylation
description: SIRT3 decreases H3K27 crotonylation at the ETS1 promoter, constraining neoplastic dissemination. The lncRNA LINC00922 decoys SIRT3 from the ETS1 promoter, upregulating H3K27 crotonylation and driving colorectal cancer metastasis (Liao et al., Mol Cancer 2023).

label: FOS
description: FOS (c-Fos) is an immediate-early bZIP transcription factor that heterodimerizes with JUN family members to form AP-1 complexes regulating proliferation, inflammation, and matrix remodeling genes. SIRT3 attenuates fibrosis in cardiomyocytes by inhibiting FOS/AP-1 (and STAT3/NFATc2) signaling, restraining pathological cardiac remodeling.

label: AP-1 complex
description: FOS (c-Fos) is an immediate-early bZIP transcription factor that heterodimerizes with JUN family members to form AP-1 complexes regulating proliferation, inflammation, and matrix remodeling genes. SIRT3 attenuates fibrosis in cardiomyocytes by inhibiting FOS/AP-1 (and STAT3/NFATc2) signaling, restraining pathological cardiac remodeling.

label: MIP-2
description: MIP-2 (CXCL2) is a CXC chemokine recruiting neutrophils via CXCR2. SIRT3 activation consistently correlates with reduced MIP-2 expression alongside TNF-alpha and IL-6, and diminished polymorphonuclear leukocyte infiltration in preclinical models, via NF-kappaB suppression.

label: Withaferin A
description: Withaferin A, a withanolide from Withania somnifera, mediates anti-fibrotic effects in hepatic fibrosis models through SIRT3; this effect is abolished in SIRT3-knockout mice, positioning SIRT3 as the indispensable molecular effector of this pharmacological anti-fibrotic agent.

label: SIRT3 for anti-fibrotic effect
description: Withaferin A, a withanolide from Withania somnifera, mediates anti-fibrotic effects in hepatic fibrosis models through SIRT3; this effect is abolished in SIRT3-knockout mice, positioning SIRT3 as the indispensable molecular effector of this pharmacological anti-fibrotic agent.

label: Irisin
description: Irisin, the exercise-induced FNDC5 cleavage product, exerts antioxidative and osteoprotective effects in diabetic periodontitis models that require SIRT3: lentiviral SIRT3 silencing abolishes its protection against osteoclastic alveolar bone resorption and ROS overproduction, establishing SIRT3 as the obligatory signaling node.

label: SIRT3 for osteoprotection
description: Irisin, the exercise-induced FNDC5 cleavage product, exerts antioxidative and osteoprotective effects in diabetic periodontitis models that require SIRT3: lentiviral SIRT3 silencing abolishes its protection against osteoclastic alveolar bone resorption and ROS overproduction, establishing SIRT3 as the obligatory signaling node.

label: Periodontitis
description: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease of tooth-supporting tissues driven by dysbiotic biofilm and host responses, with diabetes as a major risk modifier. In diabetic periodontitis models, irisin's SIRT3-dependent osteoprotection prevents alveolar bone resorption, identifying SIRT3 as a host-modulatory target.

label: Irisin via SIRT3
description: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease of tooth-supporting tissues driven by dysbiotic biofilm and host responses, with diabetes as a major risk modifier. In diabetic periodontitis models, irisin's SIRT3-dependent osteoprotection prevents alveolar bone resorption, identifying SIRT3 as a host-modulatory target.

label: GRP75
description: GRP75 (mortalin/HSPA9) links the ER IP3R to the mitochondrial VDAC1 channel at mitochondria-associated ER membranes, gating calcium transfer. SIRT3 overexpression inhibits the VDAC1/GRP75/IP3R complex, reducing MAM formation and protecting hippocampal neurons from hyperglycemia-induced mitochondrial calcium overload and apoptosis.

label: VDAC1 and IP3R at MAMs
description: GRP75 (mortalin/HSPA9) links the ER IP3R to the mitochondrial VDAC1 channel at mitochondria-associated ER membranes, gating calcium transfer. SIRT3 overexpression inhibits the VDAC1/GRP75/IP3R complex, reducing MAM formation and protecting hippocampal neurons from hyperglycemia-induced mitochondrial calcium overload and apoptosis.

label: Indole-3-propionic acid
description: Indole-3-propionic acid is a gut microbiota-derived tryptophan metabolite. It potentiates SIRT3 to enhance myocardial bioenergetics and improve diastolic function in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, representing a microbiota-mitochondria axis with translational potential.

label: COL1A1
description: COL1A1 encodes the alpha-1 chain of type I collagen, the principal ECM fibrillar collagen in myocardium. SIRT3 suppresses myocardial fibrosis through deacetylation of pro-fibrotic genes including COL1A1 and TGF-beta1, reducing ECM deposition in pressure-overloaded cardiomyocytes.

label: MMP-7
description: MMP-7 (matrilysin) is a secreted metalloproteinase that degrades ECM components and mediates EMT and tissue remodeling. SIRT3 deacetylates beta-catenin, influencing MMP-7 and PAI-1 expression, two mediators implicated in ECM remodeling via EMT induction in renal fibrosis.

label: beta-catenin deacetylation
description: MMP-7 (matrilysin) is a secreted metalloproteinase that degrades ECM components and mediates EMT and tissue remodeling. SIRT3 deacetylates beta-catenin, influencing MMP-7 and PAI-1 expression, two mediators implicated in ECM remodeling via EMT induction in renal fibrosis.

label: SIRT3 proteolytic degradation
description: Soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH/EPHX2) hydrolyzes epoxy-fatty acids and modulates SIRT3 turnover via proteolytic degradation. sEH deficiency preserves SIRT3 bioavailability to fulfill bioenergetic demands and impedes renal vascular calcification progression, linking lipid-epoxide biology to SIRT3 stability.

label: Hair Cells
description: Cochlear hair cells are mechanosensory receptors that cannot regenerate once lost. Under caloric restriction, SIRT3-driven IDH2 activation boosts mitochondrial NADPH and ROS clearance, preserving cochlear hair cell integrity — protection completely lost in SIRT3-deficient mice.

label: SIRT3-IDH2-NADPH axis
description: Cochlear hair cells are mechanosensory receptors that cannot regenerate once lost. Under caloric restriction, SIRT3-driven IDH2 activation boosts mitochondrial NADPH and ROS clearance, preserving cochlear hair cell integrity — protection completely lost in SIRT3-deficient mice.

label: Cochlea
description: The cochlea is the auditory organ where cumulative oxidative damage drives age-related hearing loss. Caloric restriction reduces oxidative damage in cochlear cells, but this protection is abolished in SIRT3-deficient mice, making SIRT3 indispensable for CR-induced auditory resilience and a candidate therapeutic target in AHL.

label: SIRT3 under caloric restriction
description: The cochlea is the auditory organ where cumulative oxidative damage drives age-related hearing loss. Caloric restriction reduces oxidative damage in cochlear cells, but this protection is abolished in SIRT3-deficient mice, making SIRT3 indispensable for CR-induced auditory resilience and a candidate therapeutic target in AHL.

label: Mst1
description: Mst1 (STK4) is a Hippo-pathway kinase that promotes apoptosis and suppresses protective autophagy. In diabetic cardiomyopathy, melatonin counteracts adverse left-ventricle remodeling by inhibiting Mst1 phosphorylation and upregulating SIRT3, promoting autophagy, reducing apoptosis, and mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction.

label: Melatonin in DCM
description: Mst1 (STK4) is a Hippo-pathway kinase that promotes apoptosis and suppresses protective autophagy. In diabetic cardiomyopathy, melatonin counteracts adverse left-ventricle remodeling by inhibiting Mst1 phosphorylation and upregulating SIRT3, promoting autophagy, reducing apoptosis, and mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction.

label: Silybin
description: Silybin is the principal flavonolignan of milk thistle. It attenuates cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity by preserving renal tubular integrity and mitochondrial bioenergetics, likely via SIRT3-mediated mechanisms, placing it among natural compounds engaging the mitochondrial deacetylase axis in kidney injury.

label: cisplatin nephrotoxicity
description: Silybin is the principal flavonolignan of milk thistle. It attenuates cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity by preserving renal tubular integrity and mitochondrial bioenergetics, likely via SIRT3-mediated mechanisms, placing it among natural compounds engaging the mitochondrial deacetylase axis in kidney injury.

label: Matrine
description: Matrine is a quinolizidine alkaloid from Sophora flavescens. It protects against cisplatin-induced AKI by modulating mitochondrial membrane dynamics through the SIRT3/OPA1 pathway and confers cardiovascular benefits via the SIRT3/AMPK pathway, preserving cardiomyocyte viability and limiting cell death.

label: SIRT3/OPA1 pathway
description: Matrine is a quinolizidine alkaloid from Sophora flavescens. It protects against cisplatin-induced AKI by modulating mitochondrial membrane dynamics through the SIRT3/OPA1 pathway and confers cardiovascular benefits via the SIRT3/AMPK pathway, preserving cardiomyocyte viability and limiting cell death.

label: SIRT3 via Nrf2
description: Liquiritigenin is a licorice-derived flavanone that induces Nrf2 translocation, thereby potentiating SIRT3 activity and facilitating mitochondrial biogenesis while suppressing apoptosis in acute kidney injury models, mitigating oxidative stress injury and cell death.

label: AMPK/SIRT3 hormetic axis
description: Stanniocalcin-1 is a glycoprotein hormone orchestrating a hormetic AMPK/SIRT3 axis that mitigates oxidative stress and apoptosis. It inhibits BNIP3 expression through the AMPK/SIRT3 pathway, ameliorating renal injury in diabetic murine models.

label: mitochondrial bioenergetics
description: Intermedin (adrenomedullin 2) enhances mitochondrial bioenergetic capacity via AMPK/SIRT3-mediated cristae remodeling in vascular calcification models, opposing the calcific phenotype driven by mitochondrial dysfunction in advanced chronic kidney disease.

label: PGC-1alpha/SIRT3 axis
description: Meteorin-like (Metrnl) activates the PGC-1alpha/SIRT3 axis, stimulating AMPK at Thr172 and increasing UCP1-dependent proton leak, preserving mitochondrial ultrastructural integrity and regulating energy metabolism in diabetic nephropathy.

label: DNA Ligase IV
description: DNA ligase IV (LIG4) catalyzes the final phosphodiester-bond sealing step of non-homologous end joining with XRCC4/XLF. SIRT3 promotes NHEJ efficiency via 53BP1 recruitment and H3K56 deacetylation and interacts with DNA repair proteins including DNA ligase 4 to repair mtDNA damage.

label: double-strand breaks in NHEJ
description: DNA ligase IV (LIG4) catalyzes the final phosphodiester-bond sealing step of non-homologous end joining with XRCC4/XLF. SIRT3 promotes NHEJ efficiency via 53BP1 recruitment and H3K56 deacetylation and interacts with DNA repair proteins including DNA ligase 4 to repair mtDNA damage.

label: lncRNA DACH1
description: A long noncoding RNA at the DACH1 locus interacts with SIRT3 to regulate mitochondrial oxidative damage and cell death in heart failure, representing a noncoding-RNA arm of SIRT3's cardioprotective network that couples nuclear gene regulation to mitochondrial integrity.

label: Lactylation
description: Lysine lactylation is a lactate-derived post-translational modification coupling metabolic state to protein function. Lactate downregulates SIRT3, increasing ACSL4 lactylation, promoting ferroptosis and accelerating nucleus pulposus cell decline in intervertebral disc degeneration.

label: Ferroptosis in IDD
description: Nucleus pulposus cells decline in intervertebral disc degeneration, exacerbated by SIRT3 knockdown under oxidative stress. Lactate downregulates SIRT3, increasing ACSL4 lactylation and promoting ferroptosis that accelerates NPC functional decline; SIRT3 overexpression alleviates IDD severity in vivo.

label: AGO2
description: AGO2 (Argonaute 2) is the catalytic core of RISC executing microRNA-guided silencing. In diabetic cardiomyopathy, SIRT3 activation improves mitochondrial respiratory capacity through modulation of the AGO2/cytochrome b (CYTB) signaling pathway; SIRT3 loss breaks this axis, impairing ETC activity and accelerating DCM progression.

label: microRNA silencing
description: AGO2 (Argonaute 2) is the catalytic core of RISC executing microRNA-guided silencing. In diabetic cardiomyopathy, SIRT3 activation improves mitochondrial respiratory capacity through modulation of the AGO2/cytochrome b (CYTB) signaling pathway; SIRT3 loss breaks this axis, impairing ETC activity and accelerating DCM progression.

label: Type 2 Diabetes
description: SIRT3 is consistently downregulated in clinical diabetic tissues, with deficiency correlating with insulin resistance and disturbed systemic energy homeostasis. In skeletal muscle, SIRT3 deficiency impairs insulin-stimulated glucose translocation, aggravating peripheral insulin resistance and contributing to type 2 diabetes pathophysiology.

label: Diabetic Cardiomyopathy
description: SIRT3 activation improves mitochondrial respiratory capacity and suppresses oxidative stress in DCM primarily through the AGO2/cytochrome b (CYTB) signaling pathway. SIRT3 downregulation breaks this axis, impairing ETC activity and accelerating DCM progression; melatonin protects via Mst1 inhibition and SIRT3 upregulation.

label: SIRT3 loss
description: SIRT3 activation improves mitochondrial respiratory capacity and suppresses oxidative stress in DCM primarily through the AGO2/cytochrome b (CYTB) signaling pathway. SIRT3 downregulation breaks this axis, impairing ETC activity and accelerating DCM progression; melatonin protects via Mst1 inhibition and SIRT3 upregulation.

label: Nucleus Pulposus
description: Nucleus pulposus cells decline in intervertebral disc degeneration, exacerbated by SIRT3 knockdown under oxidative stress. Lactate downregulates SIRT3, increasing ACSL4 lactylation and promoting ferroptosis that accelerates NPC functional decline; SIRT3 overexpression alleviates IDD severity in vivo.

label: Age-related Hearing Loss
description: AHL is the most prevalent auditory impairment in older adults, tightly correlated with cumulative oxidative stress. Caloric restriction alleviates AHL by reducing oxidative damage in cochlear cells, but this protection is abolished in SIRT3-deficient mice; SIRT3-driven IDH2/NADPH activity preserves cochlear hair cells.

label: SIRT3-dependent CR protection
description: AHL is the most prevalent auditory impairment in older adults, tightly correlated with cumulative oxidative stress. Caloric restriction alleviates AHL by reducing oxidative damage in cochlear cells, but this protection is abolished in SIRT3-deficient mice; SIRT3-driven IDH2/NADPH activity preserves cochlear hair cells.

label: ASAH1
description: Acid ceramidase (ACase, aCDase) is encoded by ASAH1. It is a lysosomal hydrolase that cleaves ceramide into sphingosine and a free fatty acid.

label: Carmofur
description: Carmofur has IC50 29 nM against acid ceramidase, is clinically approved in Japan, crosses the BBB, and is a repurposing candidate for senolytic therapy.

label: NF-kappaB
description: SIRT1 deacetylates RelA/p65 at Lys310, inhibiting NF-κB-dependent pro-inflammatory gene expression (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β). This is an established anti-inflammatory mechanism.

label: CXCL5
description: AP-1 transactivates CXCL5 (a SASP chemokine), which feeds inflammaging. Caloric restriction suppresses inflammaging and activates autophagy via mTOR/AMPK.

label: Hydroxychloroquine
description: HCQ blocks cytoprotective autophagy in cancer cells and is combined with chemotherapy in clinical trials. Results have been modest and inconsistent across cancer types.

label: p62
description: SQSTM1/p62-mediated selective autophagy directly degrades p16 and p21 (independent of UPS), reversing the senescent phenotype in canine MMVD valve cells.

label: TRIAD
description: TRIAD (Test of Rapamycin In Aging Dogs) is a parallel-group, double-masked, randomized, placebo-controlled trial testing rapamycin's effect on lifespan and healthspan in companion dogs.

label: PAK2
description: PAK2 directly binds and phosphorylates Caspase-7 at Ser30, Thr173, and Ser239, neutralizing its effector function and promoting survival in breast cancer.

label: Pin1
description: Pin1 binding to phosphorylated BAX (Thr167) catalyzes a conformational change that locks Bax in an inactive state, preventing mitochondrial translocation and MOMP.

label: PTPN5
description: PTPN5 (STEP), along with PTPN2 and PTPN23, dephosphorylates BAK at Tyr108, licensing it for mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization and apoptosis.

label: K-RAS
description: In K-RAS mutated cancers, hyperactive ERK1/2 phosphorylates and inactivates PTPN5, locking BAK in its inactive phosphorylated state and providing resistance to apoptosis.

label: Geraldol
description: Fisetin is metabolized by COMT to geraldol (3'-O-methylfisetin). This metabolic activation is concentration-dependent and consumes SAMe, generating SAH.

label: Cardiolipin
description: Cardiolipin stimulates DRP1 GTPase activity for fission AND is required for OPA1-mediated fusion — it has dual pro-fusion and pro-fission roles depending on context.

label: Mice
description: Male transgenic mice overexpressing SIRT6 show ~30% lifespan extension. SIRT6 KO mice die within ~4 weeks with dramatic progeroid phenotype. [ESTABLISHED: animal data]

label: PDE4
description: Resveratrol acts as a competitive inhibitor of cAMP phosphodiesterases (PDE4), leading to cAMP accumulation, Epac1 activation, Ca2+ release, and AMPK activation.

label: CDK5
description: CDK5 phosphorylates NOXA at Ser13, causing inactivation in metabolically regulated T-cell leukemia cells.

label: Trehalose
description: Trehalose activates TFEB via inhibiting Akt, increasing clearance of proteolipid aggregates in Batten disease and reducing cardiac hypertrophy/fibrosis in chronic MI models.

label: Celastrol
description: Celastrol activates TFEB via inhibiting mTORC1, reducing insoluble phosphorylated Tau aggregates and improving memory deficiency in Alzheimer's disease models.

label: Bleomycin
description: Bleomycin induces premature senescence via DNA breaks, activating p53-p21 and p16 pathways with SASP secretion.

label: Sodium Butyrate
description: Sodium butyrate (HDAC inhibitor) induces senescence-like state via p21 upregulation, which can be both p53-dependent and independent.

label: Lands cycle
description: The Lands cycle exchanges fatty acids into the sn-2 position of membrane phospholipids. ACase-liberated fatty acids enter this cycle, enriching PUFA-containing species.

label: Phospholipid
description: The Lands cycle exchanges fatty acids into the sn-2 position of membrane phospholipids. ACase-liberated fatty acids enter this cycle, enriching PUFA-containing species.

label: Sphingosine-1-phosphate
description: ACase overexpression raises sphingosine/S1P levels, which is classically anti-apoptotic and helps senescent cells resist apoptosis via SCAP pathways.

label: Huntingtin
description: Mutant huntingtin (mHTT) uncouples fission from degradation while disrupting autophagic flux. Broad-spectrum autophagy activators like rapamycin may be insufficient if downstream transport remains blocked.

label: PLK3
description: PLK3 phosphorylates BCL-XL at Ser49, causing cell cycle G2 arrest in lymphoma cells.

label: RSK
description: RSK phosphorylates APAF-1 at Ser268, causing inhibition in prostate cancer cells.

label: Hepatocellular Carcinoma
description: SIRT3 expression is lower in HCC tissue than in adjacent tissue. Modulating SIRT3 enhances sorafenib therapy, and SIRT3 downregulates GST-pi1 to enhance chemo- and sorafenib-induced apoptosis. Its loss therefore correlates with tumor aggressiveness and reduced treatment efficacy in hepatocellular carcinoma.

label: Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury
description: SIRT1 protects against myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury: knockout increases infarct size while overexpression upregulates FoxO1 and MnSOD and downregulates caspase-3 and Bax. Signaling upstream of SIRT1 includes miR-132 inhibition leading to PGC-1alpha/Nrf2, and lncRNA Oip5-as1 acting through the SIRT1/AMPK/PGC-1alpha axis. SIRT1 is thus an endogenous cardioprotective factor against reperfusion damage.

label: ChREBP
description: SIRT6 deacetylates ChREBP and SREBP-1c to suppress hepatic lipogenesis, and hepatocyte-specific SIRT6 knockout elevates fibrosis and oxidative stress in NASH mice. SIRT6 also antagonizes liver fibrosis by blocking hepatic stellate cell activation. These actions position SIRT6 as a protective metabolic regulator in NAFLD and NASH.

label: Liver Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury
description: SIRT3 protects against liver ischemia-reperfusion injury: systemic GPCR5 knockout suppresses SIRT3, driving proinflammatory macrophages and exacerbated injury. As the dominant mitochondrial sirtuin, SIRT3 sustains mitochondrial function in hepatocytes during reperfusion stress. This protective role parallels SIRT3's cardioprotective function in myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury.

label: Hepatitis B Virus
description: SIRT3 is downregulated in HBV-positive patients and inhibits HBV replication via H3K9 deacetylation on cccDNA. This epigenetic silencing of the viral genome at the chromatin level provides a mitochondrial-to-nuclear link in antiviral defense. SIRT6 exerts an analogous H3K9-deacetylation-mediated suppression of HBV on cccDNA.

label: Peroxiredoxin 3
description: SIRT3 alleviates mitochondrial oxidative damage and apoptosis in intestinal ischemia-reperfusion injury by deacetylating peroxiredoxin 3. Deacetylation restores peroxiredoxin 3's antioxidant activity within mitochondria, limiting the oxidative burst on reperfusion. This is a canonical example of SIRT3's mitochondrial quality-control function protecting the intestine.

label: Pancreatitis
description: SIRT1 is protective in acute pancreatitis via deacetylation of p53 and HSF1, dampening acinar-cell damage. In chronic pancreatitis, however, SIRT1 is upregulated and drives inflammation-induced EMT through the miR-278 axis, illustrating a context-dependent switch from protection to pathogenesis within the same organ.

label: Huntington's Disease
description: Brain-specific SIRT1 knockout exacerbates Huntington's disease, while SIRT1 overexpression rescues CREB-CRTC1 interaction to restore BDNF transcription. SIRT1 therefore supports neuronal survival and transcriptional resilience in HD. SIRT2 inhibition also achieves neuroprotection in HD models by mimicking the beneficial effects of sterol-biosynthesis manipulation.

label: Kidney Fibrosis
description: SIRT1 overexpression abolishes TGF-beta1-induced apoptosis and fibrosis through CTGF suppression, and SRT1720 attenuates UUO fibrosis, while SIRT1 represses HIF2alpha. However, SIRT1 downregulation may also inhibit fibroblast activation via EGFR/PDGFR-beta, creating therapeutic ambiguity. The dominant role is renoprotective, opposing tubulointerstitial fibrosis.

label: Osteoporosis
description: SIRT1 is protective in osteoporosis: SIRT1 knockout mice have low bone mass, SIRT1 increases osteoblast osteogenesis via FoxO3a, and it deacetylates sclerostin to promote Wnt/beta-catenin signaling. Resveratrol restores alkaline phosphatase and osteocalcin via NF-kB. SIRT1 thus supports bone formation and opposes age-related bone loss.

label: Tamoxifen
description: SIRT1 causes tamoxifen resistance in ER-alpha-positive breast cancer by upregulating multidrug resistance protein 2 (MRP2) through FoxO1 deacetylation. SIRT1 inhibition therefore augments paclitaxel and doxorubicin cytotoxicity, while SIRT4 enhances tamoxifen sensitivity via STAT3 inhibition. This makes SIRT1 status a determinant of endocrine-therapy response in breast cancer.

label: AKR1C1
description: SIRT2 suppresses NSCLC migration by deacetylating AKR1C1 and inhibiting STAT3. In a counteracting oncogenic axis SIRT2 deacetylates phosphoglycerate mutase at K100 to generate NADPH and accelerate tumor growth, giving SIRT2 a context-dependent dual role in lung cancer.

label: E-cadherin
description: SIRT4 upregulates E-cadherin in colorectal cancer while suppressing proliferation, migration, and invasion via glutamine-metabolism inhibition. SIRT4 also increases sensitivity to 5-fluorouracil by inhibiting the cell cycle, cementing its tumor-suppressive role in CRC.

label: Glutaminolysis
description: SIRT5 enhances glutaminolysis in colorectal cancer in a deglutarylation-dependent manner to drive colorectal carcinogenesis, and it deacetylates lactate dehydrogenase B to induce hyperactive autophagy and tumorigenesis. SIRT5 overexpression is associated with poor prognosis in CRC, contrasting with protective SIRT6.

label: Gastric Cancer
description: SIRT6 is downregulated in gastric cancer where low expression negatively correlates with tumor size and pathological grade and predicts poor prognosis. It inhibits the JAK2/STAT3 pathway to suppress growth, and SIRT6 silencing overcomes sorafenib resistance by promoting ferroptosis.

label: AIM2
description: SIRT1 is overexpressed in HPV-infected cervical cancer cells and nullifies AIM2 inflammasome-mediated immunity, correlating with poor clinical outcomes. This immunosuppressive action allows cervical cancer cells to evade inflammasome-driven clearance, positioning SIRT1 as an oncogenic factor in HPV-driven cervical cancer.

label: Coronary Artery Disease
description: Genetic SIRT1 polymorphisms are associated with coronary artery disease risk, and SIRT1 expression is reduced in CAD patients where its downregulation is linked to acetylated p53 in CAD monocytes. The lncRNA C2dat1 promotes SIRT1 to suppress miR-34a, driving VSMC proliferation and migration in the vessel wall.

label: Rspo1
description: SIRT6 preserves Rspo1 expression to confer intestinal epithelium injury resistance in inflammatory bowel disease, and SIRT6 deletion promotes inflammation via NF-kB. SIRT2 similarly inhibits Wnt/beta-catenin to maintain gut homeostasis, while SIRT3, SIRT5, and SIRT7 knockout mice are susceptible to colitis.

label: Intestinal Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury
description: SIRT1 suppresses intestinal epithelial ROS accumulation and apoptosis after ischemia-reperfusion, and resveratrol protects through the SIRT1-NF-kB-iNOS-NO pathway. SIRT3 alleviates mitochondrial oxidative damage and apoptosis via peroxiredoxin 3 deacetylation, while SIRT6 downregulation by miR-351-5p aggravates intestinal IRI injury.

label: GKRP
description: SIRT2 promotes glucose-dependent hepatic glucose uptake by deacetylating GKRP at K126, and its downregulation ameliorates reduced Akt activity while increasing insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in insulin-resistant neuro-2a cells. SIRT1 overexpression improves insulin sensitivity, but hepatic SIRT1 knockdown prevents fasting hyperglycemia by increasing hepatic insulin responsiveness, illustrating SIRT1's dual role in diabetes.

label: Diabetic Retinopathy
description: SIRT1 overexpression prevents capillary cell apoptosis and degenerative capillary formation in diabetic retinopathy, reduces DM-induced retinal inflammation, and improves visual function. In diabetic cardiomyopathy SIRT1 activation inhibits ROS-induced oxidative stress and fibrosis, while SIRT3 regulates fibrosis, inflammation, apoptosis, and oxidative stress in the diabetic myocardium.

label: Kidney Stones
description: SIRT3 is downregulated in kidney stone patients and protects via the Nrf2/heme oxygenase-1 pathway, while suppressing SIRT1 promotes calcium oxalate crystal-cell adhesion and exacerbates injury. SIRT1 also protects against aging-induced kidney injury through HIF-1alpha deacetylation of tubulointerstitial damage.

label: Sclerostin
description: SIRT1 deacetylates sclerostin to activate Wnt/beta-catenin signaling and increase bone anabolism, and SIRT1 knockout mice have a low bone-mass phenotype while SIRT1 overexpression increases osteoblast osteogenesis via FoxO3a. SIRT6 inhibits age-related bone loss by stabilizing estrogen receptor alpha in preosteoblastic cells.

label: Melanoma
description: Oncogene-induced senescence (OIS) is the permanent cell-cycle arrest triggered in cells carrying BRAF/RAS/MYC mutations. The benign melanocytic nevus (mole) is the in-vivo embodiment of OIS and prevents melanoma; bypass of OIS via p53/PTEN loss or TERT activation is required for malignancy. Capped, arrested growth is therefore tumor-suppressive.

label: Benign Tumor
description: Benign tumors are dual-natured: OIS-type arrested lesions (nevi) are longevity-positive cancer barriers, whereas growth-signal-driven benign growths such as TSC1/TSC2-loss mTORC1 hamartomas are themselves disease (Tuberous Sclerosis, angiomyolipoma, epilepsy). Arrested growth is good; ongoing growth is bad.

label: Hamartoma
description: Benign tumors are dual-natured: OIS-type arrested lesions (nevi) are longevity-positive cancer barriers, whereas growth-signal-driven benign growths such as TSC1/TSC2-loss mTORC1 hamartomas are themselves disease (Tuberous Sclerosis, angiomyolipoma, epilepsy). Arrested growth is good; ongoing growth is bad.

label: TSC1
description: Loss of TSC1 or TSC2 removes the GAP that restrains Rheb, causing constitutive mTORC1 hyperactivation that drives benign hamartomas (Tuberous Sclerosis, renal angiomyolipoma, epilepsy, autism). Here benign growth is itself the disease, contrasting with the protective OIS-type benign lesion.

label: Hyperfunction Theory of Aging
description: The hyperfunction theory of aging holds that aging is the quasi-programmed continuation of developmental growth signaling; mTOR is the engine of aging and Rapamycin extends lifespan by suppressing mTOR. This frames the key distinction that arrested growth (OIS) is protective while ongoing, unopposed growth signaling is pathogenic.

label: Ribosome Biogenesis
description: SIRT7 drives ribosome biogenesis by activating RNA Pol I at rDNA and suppresses p21 via H3K18 deacetylation, fueling the biosynthetic capacity tumors need; it is overexpressed in breast, thyroid, and HCC. This proliferative, biosynthetic driver role makes SIRT7 an oncogenic sirtuin.

label: Phosphoglycerate Mutase
description: SIRT2 promotes tumor glycolysis in some settings by deacetylating phosphoglycerate mutase at Lys100, channeling carbon into NADPH production and accelerating tumor growth in lung cancer. This illustrates SIRT2's context-dependent, often harmful, metabolic face versus the protective SIRT1/3/6 axis.

label: N-Acetylcysteine
description: In C. elegans, glucose restriction normally raises mitochondrial respiration and ROS, inducing catalase and extending lifespan; NAC pre-treatment completely abolished both the ROS rise and the longevity benefit. NAC is the strongest direct evidence that scavenging the ROS signal blocks mitohormesis.

label: Endogenous Antioxidant Upregulation
description: Exogenous antioxidants prevent the upregulation of endogenous defense enzymes (SOD, GPx) that exercise normally induces via NRF2. The Ristow 2009 study showed antioxidant-supplemented subjects failed to upregulate endogenous SOD/GPx and lost the insulin-sensitizing benefit of exercise.

label: NF-kB
description: PAK1 facilitates NF-kB nuclear activation; ivermectin's PAK1 degradation therefore dampens NF-kB signaling. Because NF-kB is the master transcriptional regulator of the SASP, this overlaps with the senomorphic strategy — targeting SASP production without killing senescent cells.
